Beyond reconstruction quality, the structural clarity and computational efficiency of PLANING make it well suited for a broad range of downstream applications, such as enabling large-scale scene modeling and simulation-ready environments for embodied AI. Project page: https://city-super.github.io/PLANING/

papers.title: Quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for the magnetic Schödinger operator with unbounded electrical potential
papers.abstract: The first author established in [8] a quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for the Schrödinger operator with unbounded potential. In the present work, we extend the results in [8] to the magnetic Schrödinger operator. We discuss both the isotropic and anisotropic cases. We establish Hölder stability inequalities of determining the electrical potential or magnetic field from the corresponding boundary spectral data.

papers.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
papers.abstract: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. In the MAGNDATA database, 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. With the $k$ index fixed to its experimental value, about nine structures are generated per material on average. We perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. The characteristic energy scale among oriented SSA structures is only approximately 0.29 meV per magnetic atom, about 300 times smaller than that of distinct SSA structures. These results demonstrate that oriented SSG-based enumeration, combined with the two-step calculations for SSA and oriented SSA structures, provides an efficient and robust route for large-scale magnetic-structure prediction.

papers.title: Fractional Besov-Sobolev Spaces on Chord-arc Curves
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a bounded rectifiable Jordan curve with interior and exterior domains $Ω_i$ and $Ω_e$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$, we study harmonic functions $u$ on either domain $Ω$ with finite weighted energy $\int_Ω|\nabla u(z)|^p \operatorname{dist}(z,Γ)^{(1-s)p-1} dA(z)$. On the unit circle, the interior and exterior trace spaces both coincide with the fractional Besov-Sobolev space $B^s_{p,p}(Γ)$. We ask which rough curves preserve this trace identity and the corresponding seminorm estimates. For radial-Lipschitz curves, we prove that both trace spaces coincide with $B^s_{p,p}(Γ)$, with equivalent seminorms, in the following ranges: $1/p-1/2\le s<1$ for $1<p<2$; $0<s<1$ for $p=2$; and $0<s\le 1/p+1/2$ for $2<p<\infty$. For arbitrary chord-arc curves, the same conclusion holds when $1/p\le s<1/2+1/(2p)$. Taking $s=1-1/p$ yields an almost-Dirichlet principle on radial-Lipschitz domains: for $4/3\le p\le 4$, the unweighted $p$-energy of the harmonic extension is bounded by a constant times that of any extension with the same boundary values. Neither endpoint can be improved over this class. We also obtain a sharp endpoint counterpart of Brennan's integrability conclusion: every Riemann map $g$ from a bounded radial-Lipschitz domain $Ω_i$ onto the unit disk satisfies $g'\in L^4(Ω_i)$, and no exponent greater than $4$ works for all such domains.

papers.title: Multi-Dimensional Prompt Chaining to Improve Open-Domain Dialogue Generation
papers.abstract: Small language models (SLMs) offer significant deployment advantages but often struggle to match the dialogue quality of larger models in open-domain settings. In this paper, we propose a multi-dimensional prompt-chaining framework that integrates Naturalness, Coherence, and Engagingness dimensions to enhance human-likeness in open-domain dialogue generation. We apply the framework to two SLMs, TinyLlama and Llama-2-7B, and benchmark their performance against responses generated by substantially larger models, including Llama-2-70B and GPT-3.5 Turbo. We then employ automatic and human evaluation to assess the responses based on diversity, contextual coherence, as well as overall quality. Results show that the full framework improves response diversity by up to 29%, contextual coherence by up to 28%, and engagingness as well as naturalness by up to 29%. Notably, Llama-2-7B achieves performance comparable to substantially larger models, including Llama-2-70B and GPT-3.5 Turbo. Overall, the findings demonstrate that carefully designed prompt-based strategies provide an effective and resource-efficient pathway to improving open-domain dialogue quality in SLMs.

papers.title: Energy-Guided Generative Modeling for Low-Energy Molecular Structure Discovery
papers.abstract: Exploring molecular energy landscapes and identifying ground-state conformations are central challenges in computational chemistry. However, generating diverse low-energy conformers from molecular graphs remains expensive with traditional physics-based pipelines. Existing learning-based approaches remain fragmented: generative models capture conformational diversity but often lack reliable energy calibration, whereas deterministic predictors focus on a single structure and fail to represent ensemble variability. Here we introduce EnFlow, to our knowledge, the first energy-guided generative framework that couples flow-based conformer generation with explicit energy landscape modeling for joint conformational ensemble generation and ground-state identification. By integrating generative dynamics with a learned energy model, EnFlow guides sampling toward low-energy regions of the conformational landscape, improving structural fidelity under extremely few sampling steps while enabling energy-based ranking of generated conformations. Experiments on GEOM-QM9 and GEOM-Drugs show that EnFlow achieves strong performance in conformer generation and ground-state identification while requiring only 1-2 ordinary differential equation (ODE) sampling steps. Single-point GFN2-xTB evaluations further show that the learned energy scores preserve physically meaningful energetic rankings of generated conformations. These results support explicit energy landscape modeling as an effective strategy for low-energy molecular structure discovery through joint modeling of conformational ensembles and their associated energies.

papers.title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonlinear Estimation with Convex Models
papers.abstract: A linear functional of an object from a convex symmetric set can be optimally estimated, in a worst-case sense, by a linear functional of observations made on the object. This well-known fact is extended here to a nonlinear setting: other simple functionals of the object can be optimally estimated by functionals of the observations that share a similar simple structure. This is established for the maximum of several linear functionals and even for the $\ell$th largest among them. Proving the latter requires an unusual variation of the analytical Hahn--Banach theorem. The existence results are accompanied by practical recipes relying on convex optimization to construct the desired functionals, thereby justifying the term of estimation algorithms.

papers.title: Modular Neural Image Signal Processing
papers.abstract: Neural image signal processing (ISP) pipelines have largely abandoned the modular design of classical ISPs in favor of black-box networks, gaining expressiveness but losing interpretability, controllability, and the ability to swap or extend stages. Reintroducing modularity exposes a tradeoff: pipelines built from fixed operators or fixed neural proxies preserve interpretability but limit expressiveness, while jointly optimizing the proxies recovers expressiveness but often entangles functional roles across stages. We present a practical role-preserving and yet expressive neural ISP built on a two-level training strategy. At the module level, components with available ground truth are optimized separately to preserve functional decomposition. At the operator level, where intermediate ground truth is impractical to obtain, operators are trained jointly under final-image supervision but kept aligned with their roles via architectural design and role specific losses. The resulting framework is simultaneously interpretable, controllable, and expressive, enabling operator-level adjustment, targeted debugging, multi-style extension without full-pipeline retraining, and rendering of raw images from unseen cameras by swapping the camera specific modules. Lightweight at 0.5-3.9M parameters, our ISP achieves state-of-the-art results on most S24 picture styles and competitive performance on MIT-Adobe FiveK at a fraction of the parameter count of the closest neural ISPs. Code and the photo-editing tool are available at https://github.com/mahmoudnafifi/modular_neural_isp.

papers.title: An improved bound on the Overfull Conjecture for graphs with small minimum degree and large maximum degree
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph with order $n$, maximum degree $Δ(G)$, minimum degree $δ(G)$, and chromatic index $χ'(G)$. A graph $G$ is called $Δ$-critical if $χ'(G)=Δ(G)+1$ and $χ'(H) < χ'(G)$ for every proper subgraph $H$ of $G$, and $G$ is overfull if $\left|E(G)\right|>Δ(G)\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor$. In 1986, Chetwynd and Hilton proposed the Overfull Conjecture, which is equivalent to the following $Δ$-critical form: Every $Δ$-critical graph $G$ with $Δ(G) > \frac{n}{3}$ is overfull. The Overfull Conjecture has many implications. For example, it implies a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index of graphs $G$ with $Δ(G) > \frac{n}{3}$, and implies several longstanding conjectures in the area of graph edge coloring. Recently, Cao, Chen, Jing, and Shan (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2022) verified the Overfull Conjecture for $Δ$-critical graphs $G$ when $Δ(G)-\frac{7δ(G)}{4}\ge \frac{3n-17}{4}$. In this paper, we establish the required bound $Δ(G)-\frac{5δ(G)}{3}\ge\frac{2n-7}{3}$.

papers.title: EditThinker: Enhancing Image Editors via Iterative Reasoning with a Plug-and-Play VLM
papers.abstract: Image editors can produce realistic images while still failing to satisfy the requested changes. Improving their instruction following requires identifying these failures and translating visual feedback into instructions that the editor can execute. We introduce EditThinker, an 8B vision-language model (VLM) that enhances existing image editors through iterative reasoning while keeping their weights fixed. EditThinker jointly critiques semantic consistency and visual quality, reasons about editing failures, and refines the instruction in a structured response. It interacts with the editor through a Critique-Refine-Repeat loop, providing a plug-and-play interface for feedback-driven editing. Learning effective refinements requires more than imitating plausible expert suggestions: the instructions must work with the capabilities of the underlying editor. We therefore combine supervised fine-tuning on expert demonstrations with reinforcement learning from executed editing outcomes, using format, critic, and edit rewards. To support this training, we construct ThinkEdit-167k, a dataset of 167k step-wise samples with unified supervision for critique, reasoning, and instruction refinement. Across four tested editors, EditThinker improves overall scores on GEdit-Bench-EN, ImgEdit-Bench, RISE-Bench, and KRIS-Bench. Ablations examine the joint model design, data allocation, and training across VLM backbones. In our GEdit round-budget study, refinement achieves higher scores with fewer editor calls than best-of-N selection. We will release our data construction framework, datasets, and models.

papers.title: A Note on Emergent Behavior in Multi-agent Systems Enabled by Neuro-spike Communication
papers.abstract: In this note, we show emergent behavior can arise even when the agents interact solely through spikes. Rather than exchanging real-valued states, each agent encodes its own state by bio-inspired neuromorphic amplifiers and transmits signed spikes, so that each firing carries a single bit and the traffic is intermittent and asynchronous. We model the resulting network as a hybrid system and introduce a coordinate that is invariant under the spike-induced jumps, which reduces the convergence analysis to a flow dynamics without jumps. On this coordinate, we prove that the agents practically synchronize and collectively follow the blended dynamics that characterizes an emergent behavior, and we derive explicit ultimate error bounds for synchronization and for the expected behavior. The bound reveals a certified accuracy--threshold trade-off and yields closed-form tuning rules under a minimum-threshold or prescribed-accuracy constraints. A distributed median solver is tested using neuro-spike communication.

papers.title: BEAVER: An Efficient Deterministic LLM Verifier
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) transition from research prototypes to production systems, practitioners need reliable ways to verify model outputs before they are deployed. While sampling-based estimates provide an ad-hoc intuition of model behavior, they offer no sound guarantees. We present BEAVER, the first practical framework for computing deterministic, sound bounds on the probability that an LLM's response to a prompt satisfies a property. Given a prompt and an oracle, BEAVER systematically explores the model's output distribution using a *token trie* and a *frontier*, maintaining provably sound bounds at every iteration. We formalize the LLM verification problem, prove that BEAVER's bounds are sound and that its selection strategy Max-$μ$ is optimal for verification upto any tolerance. On 3 important safety tasks across 5 popular LLMs, BEAVER certifies up to $7.6\times$ more prompts as risky than a sampling-based verifier while using fewer forward passes, and its per-prompt bounds extend to statistical certificates over distributions of prompts.

papers.title: Dynamics and Statistics of Dissipative Nonlinear Systems: A Study via 2D CGLE by Contact Geometry
papers.abstract: A unified description of dynamics and statistics is fundamental to understanding dissipative nonlinear systems. This paper develops one using the contact geometry of complex stochastic vector bundles. The first theorem establishes the least-constraint principle for complex vector bundles. It uniquely determines the characteristic field, whose integral curves obey the contact Hamilton equations and preserve the contact form exactly, leading to the dissipative contact Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The second theorem constructs a probability measure from the same contact structure. Applied to the two-dimensional cubic--quintic complex Ginzburg--Landau equation, the contact Hamilton--Jacobi equation admits closed-form travelling waves in reciprocal Jacobi-elliptic form. The induced measure yields a heavy-tailed intensity law $I^{-3/2}$ with non-extensive index $q=5/3$, anomalous structure-function scaling, an on-shell bifurcation between extended waves and localised solitons with square-root onset, and an equilibrium crossover converging in the thermodynamic limit.

papers.title: MemVerse: Multimodal Memory for Lifelong Learning Agents
papers.abstract: Despite the remarkable advancements in multimodal large language models across various domains, AI agents still lack the ability to retain past information. Without reliable memory, agents struggle to leverage historical context, impairing long-horizon reasoning and coherent interactions in dynamic environments. In this paper, we introduce MemVerse, a model-agnostic, plug-and-play memory framework that combines fast parametric recall with hierarchical retrieval, enabling scalable and adaptive multimodal intelligence. MemVerse maintains short-term memory for recent context while transforming raw experiences into structured long-term memory graphs, empowering continuous learning and autonomous knowledge evolution. To meet real-time demands, we introduce a periodic distillation mechanism that compresses essential knowledge from the cognitive graph into the parametric model, providing fast and differentiable recall while preserving interpretability. Extensive experiments show that MemVerse boosts multimodal reasoning with superior efficiency, allowing agents to maintain coherence and adapt seamlessly throughout extended interactions. Our code is available at https://github.com/KnowledgeXLab/MemVerse.

papers.title: From n-systems to Lie and Courant algebroids
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method for constructing pure algebroids, dull algebroids, and Lie algebroids. The construction relies on what we call $n$-systems on vector bundles, and we provide explicit formulas for all resulting structure maps. Analogously, metric $n$-systems defined on metric vector bundles allow us to construct metric algebroids, pre-Courant algebroids, and Courant algebroids.

papers.title: ChroniUXMag: A Persona-Driven Framework for Inclusive mHealth Requirements Engineering
papers.abstract: Context: Mobile health (mHealth) applications for chronic disease management present challenges in accessibility, inclusivity, usability, and sustained engagement. Clinical context, caregiver involvement, trust, and long-term use create domain-specific requirements engineering (RE) challenges. Objective: This study introduces ChroniUXMag, a framework for eliciting and analysing inclusivity requirements in mHealth design, building on InclusiveMag and GenderMag. Method: ChroniUXMag was developed using the Scope and Derive stages of InclusiveMag. Evidence came from a systematic literature review, focus groups, interviews, and an online survey. Candidate inclusivity facets were identified from literature and empirical data, organised into personas representing diverse health situations, attitudes, and digital practices, and integrated into an adapted cognitive walkthrough form. Results: Thirteen qualitative categories were consolidated into six facets: health situation, health attitude, cultural differences, level of dependency, trust in mHealth apps, and users' involvement with the app. These facets support structured, persona-driven evaluations that reveal inclusivity barriers often missed by traditional usability assessments. Conclusion: ChroniUXMag provides an empirically grounded, facet-driven framework and persona-based artefacts for representing inclusivity concerns during requirements elicitation and early analysis. Its utility in professional RE practice remains to be evaluated with practitioners. Future work will extend the Apply stage through practitioner-led evaluation in real-world design contexts.

papers.title: Observation of topological phases without crystalline counterparts
papers.abstract: The center-of-mass position of a nonlinear soliton in a lattice is commonly attributed to the interplay between nonlinearity and lattice confinement. Here, we reveal its geometric origin by establishing an exact relation between the soliton position and an intrinsic Zak phase. Unlike the Zak phase of a linear Bloch band, this intrinsic Zak phase arises from the nonlinear self-consistent band of the lattice reconstructed by the soliton density. We construct a composite periodic function to define this phase and demonstrate that its topological winding during nonlinear Thouless pumping dictates the quantized soliton displacement. Our results establish band geometry as a fundamental descriptor of nonlinear soliton position in a lattice and provide a geometric framework for their topological transport.

papers.title: Hierarchical Deep Research for Physically Grounded System-Level Materials Design
papers.abstract: Designing multicomponent materials systems requires evidence on composition, interfaces, processing and deviceoperation that is scattered across the literature. Language-model research agents can collect this evidence, but their reports are seldom tested against physics. Here we show that Deep Tree of Research, a hierarchical multi-agent system built on locally deployable open-weight language models, ranks first among 47 agents in blinded evaluationacross 27 nanomaterials and device topics. Candidates from local agents outperform those from the best commercial systems on nine of ten first-principles simulation metrics across five design tasks. In a sensing case study, the agent nominated a fluorinated silver-nanoparticle/MXene architecture for the short-chain pollutant perfluoropentanoic acid; after an expert replaced the anchor with an amine, fabricated sensors respond selectively and reproduciblyintap water, consistent with interfacial calculations. Hierarchical research agents can therefore turn dispersed literatureinto experimentally testable materials hypotheses under human supervision.

papers.title: Nowcast3D for effective precipitation nowcasting
papers.abstract: The evolution of extreme precipitation depends on height-varying wind fields and coupled physical processes, underscoring the importance of three-dimensional information for precipitation nowcasting. Radar volume scans provide such an observational basis. Most learning-based systems, however, either compress these scans into two-dimensional products, losing vertical information needed for height-dependent storm evolution, or rely on purely data-driven mappings that inadequately represent the physical evolution of extreme precipitation. We introduce Nowcast3D, a gray-box learning framework for 3D radar-volume nowcasting, which integrates physically structured neural operators with a conditional diffusion model. The neural operators produce a physics-guided forecast via 3D advection, local diffusion and microphysics processes. Conditioned on this forecast, the diffusion model generates uncertainty-quantified ensembles. Trained on provincial-scale radar volumes covering a $10.24^\circ \times 10.24^\circ$ region and fine-tuned on a $2.56^\circ \times 2.56^\circ$ city-scale region ($0.01^\circ \approx 1$ km), Nowcast3D produces effective near-real-time reflectivity forecasts up to 3 hours ahead. It consistently outperforms competitive baselines in both cross-region and temporal-out-of-sample evaluations, and its inferred motion fields show good consistency with collocated wind-profiler observations. In a blind evaluation with 160 meteorologists, Nowcast3D ranked first and was preferred in 57% of post-hoc assessments, compared with 27% for the leading baseline. These results highlight its operational potential for effective nowcasting of extreme precipitation events.

papers.title: Lexical tableaux and quasisymmetric functions
papers.abstract: We introduce dual lexical functions, which we construct as an iterated strict-minimum restricted product on Frobenius characteristics of the trivial representation of the cyclic group induced to the symmetric group, generalizing Grinberg's construction of the dual immaculate functions. To model these combinatorially, we introduce lexical tableaux, a generalization of immaculate tableaux in which each row is lexicographically minimal among its cyclic shifts. For a fixed shape, standard lexical tableaux can be counted by a hook length formula with a q-analogue, while summing over all shapes with a fixed size and number of rows gives the (q-)Stirling numbers of the first kind. The dual lexical functions are then the generating functions of lexical tableaux, and they form a basis of the quasisymmetric functions. The dual lexical functions have a positive expansion into the fundamental basis, with coefficients counting another new family of tableaux defined by conditions on the major index values of their rows. We also introduce column-strict lexical tableaux and their respective quasisymmetric functions. We show that standard column-strict lexical tableaux are in bijection with multidimensional Kreweras-type lattice paths.

papers.title: The Gatekeeping Expert's Dilemma
papers.abstract: This paper studies how experts with veto power---gatekeeping experts---influence agents through communication. Their expertise informs agents' decisions, while veto power provides discipline. Gatekeepers face a dilemma: transparent communication can invite gaming, while opacity wastes expertise. How can gatekeeping experts guide behavior without being gamed? Many economic settings feature this tradeoff, including bank stress tests, environmental regulations, and financial auditing. Using financial auditing as the primary setting, I show that strategic vagueness resolves this dilemma: by revealing just enough to prevent the manager from inflating the report, the auditor guides the manager while minimizing opportunities for manipulation. This theoretical lens provides a novel rationale for why auditors predominantly accept clients' financial reports. Comparative statics reveal that greater gatekeeper independence or expertise sometimes dampens communication. This paper offers insights into why gatekeepers who lack direct control can still be effective.

papers.title: Intrinsic spin accumulation in the magnetic spin Hall effect
papers.abstract: The magnetic spin Hall effect is a time-reversal-odd phenomenon in which spin current is induced by the charge current. In the presence of a spin-orbit coupling and/or noncolinear magnetism, however, spin current is not uniquely defined. Instead, we study an intrinsic response of spin to an electric field gradient that describes the spin accumulation at the boundaries of magnetic systems. We derive a generic formula expressed by Bloch wave functions and apply it to a minimal model for representative altermagnets, RuO$_{2}$ and MnF$_{2}$. Our results show that the intrinsic spin accumulation can be nonzero in magnetic insulators in sharp contrast to the magnetic spin Hall conductivity.

papers.title: Rethinking Multiplication in Neural Networks with Hadamard Transform-Assisted Operators
papers.abstract: Multiplication-avoiding neural operators are attractive for compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures, but directly replacing conventional convolutions often causes accuracy degradation. We investigate whether this limitation arises from multiplication avoidance itself or from the representation on which the operator acts. In this work, we introduce Hadamard Transform-assisted multiplication-avoiding (HMA) operators that combine Walsh--Hadamard transform features with multiplication-avoiding channel mixing. To identify where conventional multiplication remains necessary, we employ a gated formulation in which conventional and HMA operators compete through learned layer-wise coefficients. ResNet-18 experiments show that intermediate convolutional layers assign greater weight to HMA, whereas the earliest layers and final classifier retain greater contribution from conventional computation. Guided by this observation, we construct a compact hybrid HMA network and train it using knowledge distillation from a conventional teacher. On CIFAR-10, the resulting ResNet-18 student achieves 91.2\% accuracy compared with 90.4\% for the corresponding conventional baseline while reducing parameters by 68.25\%, conventional MACs by 85.71\%, and general multiplications by 85.54\%. Across ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and MobileNetV2 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet, HMA with knowledge distillation matches or improves the conventional models. These results show that Hadamard-domain feature restructuring can improve the accuracy--complexity tradeoff of multiplication-avoiding networks and provide a practical path toward efficient CIM inference.

papers.title: Hidden universality in large-deformation soft contact
papers.abstract: Large-deformation soft contact mediates how biological and robotic systems interact with their environments, underpinning embodied intelligence, wearables, human-machine interactions and tactile sensing. The same coupling between contact area and remaining thickness shapes the response of physical interaction interfaces in wearable sensors and soft robots. Yet predictive theories remain confined to small strains or specific geometries, and a general law for nonlinear soft contact has remained elusive. Here we reveal hidden universality in large-deformation soft-body contact: after normalization by a simple geometric correction, diverse force-displacement responses collapse onto a master curve. By extending the method of dimensionality reduction into the nonlinear regime, the framework yields analytical solutions for contact force and radius. Finite element analyses and experiments across canonical geometries, non-axisymmetric structures and irregular gummy candies validate the scaling law up to 50% compression. These results establish a universal principle for nonlinear soft contact and a mechanics-guided route to wearable devices, tactile systems and soft robotics interactions beyond empirical calibration.

papers.title: Conditional Deep Levy Models for Exotic Derivatives: History-Aware Path Generation and P-Q Payoff Diagnostics
papers.abstract: We develop a history-aware equity-index path generator based on Denoising Levy Probabilistic Models (DLPMs) and evaluate its predictive distributions through path-dependent derivative payoffs. A conditional U-Net combines contract state, index identity, 60- and 252-day return histories, and financial regularization with coordinate-wise stable mixing. A matched experiment holds initialization, training data, batch order, objective, computational budget and evaluation checkpoint fixed while comparing $α=1.9$ with the Gaussian limit $α=2$. On 6,824 chronological windows from eight Chinese and U.S. indices, terminal CRPS falls from 0.050585 to 0.048031, a 5.05% reduction, and path energy improves by 4.03%. The paired 60-calendar-day CRPS interval is [-0.004022, -0.001298]. Coverage rises from 56.68% to 71.00% while the proper 90% interval score improves by 20.30%. Empirical references remain competitive: the full-pool terminal control attains CRPS 0.047566. A common P-Q protocol translates the forecasts into vanilla, Asian and floating-strike lookback outcomes against an independent martingale-corrected Student-t GARCH benchmark. With quote-error filtering and a fixed-state initial Delta hedge, the matched Lookback difference is 0.285% of initial spot, with a 60-day interval [0.061%, 0.489%]. The evaluation also applies the same recorded ensembles to accumulator and snowball scenarios. These contracts expose different responses of early termination and downside cashflows to the noise specification. The study connects conditional historical path generation, a controlled stability-parameter comparison, empirical forecasting references, and payoff-sensitive derivative evaluation.

papers.title: Patient-Zero: Scaling Synthetic Patient Agents to Real-World Distributions without Real Patient Data
papers.abstract: Synthetic data generation with Large Language Models (LLMs) has emerged as a promising solution in the medical domain to mitigate data scarcity and privacy constraints. However, existing approaches remain constrained by their derivative nature, relying on real-world records, which pose privacy risks and distribution biases. Furthermore, current patient agents face the Stability-Plasticity Dilemma, struggling to maintain clinical consistency during dynamic inquiries. To address these challenges, we introduce Patient-Zero, a novel framework for ab initio patient simulation that requires no real medical records. Our Medically-Aligned Hierarchical Synthesis framework generates comprehensive and diverse patient records from medical knowledge via stratified attribute permutation. To support rigorous clinical interaction, we design a Dual-Track Cognitive Memory System to enable agents dynamically update memory while preserving logical consistency and persona adherence. Extensive evaluations show that Patient-Zero outperforms baselines in both data quality and interaction fidelity. In physician evaluations, our records obtain the highest mean diversity, consistency, and completeness ratings. Downstream medical reasoning model trained on our synthetic dataset shows substantial performance gains (MedQA +24.0%; MMLU +14.5%), demonstrating the practical utility of our framework.

papers.title: Follow-Bench: A Unified Motion Planning Benchmark for Socially-Aware Robot Person Following
papers.abstract: Robot person following (RPF)---mobile robots that follow and assist a specific person---has emerging applications in personal assistance, security patrols, eldercare, and logistics. To be effective, such robots must follow the target while ensuring safety and comfort for both the target and surrounding people. In this work, we present the first comprehensive study of RPF, which (i) surveys representative scenarios, motion-planning methods, and evaluation metrics with a focus on safety and comfort; (ii) introduces Follow-Bench, a unified benchmark simulating diverse scenarios, including various target trajectory patterns, crowd dynamics, and environmental layouts; and (iii) re-implements eight representative RPF planners, ensuring that both safety and comfort are systematically considered. Extensive simulation experiments provide a quantitative study of safety- and comfort-related physical indicators, while real-world trials of two MPC-based implementations on a differential-drive robot illustrate deployment feasibility and practical following behaviors. These results reveal open challenges and future research directions.

papers.title: A Higgs category for the cluster variety of triples of flags
papers.abstract: The cluster variety of triples of flags (associated with a split simple Lie group of Dynkin type Delta) plays a key role in higher Teichmuller theory as developed by Fock-Goncharov, Jiarui Fei, Ian Le, ... and Goncharov-Shen. We refer to it as the basic triangle associated with Delta. In this paper, for simply laced Delta, we construct and study a Higgs category (in the sense of Yilin Wu) which we expect to categorify the basic triangle. This category is a certain exact dg category (in the sense of Xiaofa Chen) which is Frobenius and stably 2-Calabi-Yau. We show that it has indeed the expected cyclic group symmetry and that its derived category has the expected braid group symmetry. A key ingredient in our construction is a conjecture by Merlin Christ, whose proof occupies most of this paper. The proof is based on a new description of the Higgs category in terms of Gorenstein projective dg modules. Our techniques are in the spirit of Orlov in his work on triangulated categories of graded B-branes.

papers.title: Optimal control of SDEs with merely measurable drift: an HJB approach
papers.abstract: We investigate an optimal control problem for a diffusion whose drift and running cost are merely measurable in the state variable. Such low regularity rules out the use of Pontryagin's maximum principle and also invalidates the standard proof of the Bellman principle of optimality. We address these difficulties by analyzing the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Working in a weak formulation of admissible controls, we first establish the state-equation solvability and Krylov estimates needed to make the control problem well defined. Using PDE techniques together with a policy iteration scheme, we prove that the HJB equation admits a unique strong solution, and this solution coincides with the value function of the control problem. Based on this identification, we establish a verification theorem and recover the Bellman optimality principle without imposing any additional smoothness assumptions. We further investigate a mollification scheme depending on a parameter $\varepsilon > 0$. It turns out that the smoothed value functions $V_{\varepsilon}$ may fail to converge to the original value function $V$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, and we provide an explicit counterexample. To resolve this, we identify a structural condition on the control set. When the control set is countable, convergence $V_{\varepsilon} \to V$ holds locally uniformly.

papers.title: EEG-MedRAG: Enhancing EEG-based Clinical Decision-Making via Hierarchical Hypergraph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: With the widespread application of electroencephalography (EEG) in neuroscience and clinical practice, efficiently retrieving and semantically interpreting large-scale, multi-source, heterogeneous EEG data has become a pressing challenge. EEG-MedRAG addresses this challenge through a three-layer hypergraph-based retrieval-augmented generation framework that unifies EEG domain knowledge, individual patient cases, and large-scale EEG recordings into a traversable n-ary relational hypergraph, enabling joint semantic-temporal retrieval and evidence-grounded clinical reasoning. The accompanying benchmark is the first to pair EEG questions about the same clinical fact across five user roles. Its 700 questions span seven clinical domains and support direct comparisons of answer consistency across roles. Across three LLM backbones, EEG-MedRAG outperforms all four baselines in both overall answer correctness and token-level F1. It achieves up to 86.14% answer correctness on the full benchmark and 97.32% on non-EEG questions, with 97.41% evidence coverage on knowledge questions. In EEG retrieval, EEG-MedRAG improves top-five label agreement by 8.58 percentage points over the time-series baseline. The code is available at https://github.com/li-zan/EEG-MedRAG.

papers.title: TimeMachine: Fine-Grained Facial Age Editing with Identity Preservation
papers.abstract: With the advancement of generative models, facial image editing has made significant progress. However, achieving fine-grained age editing while preserving personal identity remains a challenging task. In this paper, we propose TimeMachine, a unified diffusion-based framework for accurate facial age editing with identity preservation. TimeMachine employs fine-grained age conditions and a Multi-Cross-Attention module to decouple the dedicated age and identity conditions. This branch-wise design enables controllable age transformation while maintaining identity consistency. Furthermore, we introduce an Age Classifier Guidance (ACG) module that predicts age embeddings from latent denoising features without reconstructing images during training. This lightweight training-only predictor provides additional age-related supervision and is removed during inference. To support large-scale training, we construct HFFA (High-quality Fine-grained Facial-Age), a million-scale collection of high-resolution face images annotated with captions, identity embeddings, MiVOLO-estimated numerical ages, and age embeddings. Extensive experiments across five public face datasets demonstrate that TimeMachine achieves superior age accuracy and identity preservation relative to the evaluated baselines, with consistent conclusions across five age estimators.

papers.title: Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs: resilience and approximate decompositions
papers.abstract: Dirac's classical theorem asserts that, for $n\ge 3$, any $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $\frac{n}{2}$ is Hamiltonian. Furthermore, if we additionally assume that such graphs are regular and sufficiently large, then, by the breakthrough work of Csaba, Kühn, Lo, Osthus, and Treglown, they admit a decomposition into Hamilton cycles and at most one perfect matching, solving the well-known Nash-Williams conjecture. In the pseudorandom setting, it has long been conjectured that similar results hold in much sparser graphs. We prove two overarching theorems for graphs that exclude excessively dense subgraphs, which yield asymptotically optimal resilience and Hamilton-decomposition results in sparse pseudorandom graphs. First, our results imply that for every fixed $γ>0$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that if $G$ is a spanning subgraph of an $(n,d,λ)$-graph satisfying $δ(G)\ge\bigl(\tfrac12+γ\bigr)d$ and $ d/λ\ge C,$ then $G$ must contain a Hamilton cycle. Second, we show that for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $C>0$ so that any $(n,d,λ)$-graph $G$ with $d/λ\ge C$ contains at least $\bigl(1-\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, and, finally, we prove that the entire edge set of $G$ can be covered by no more than $\bigl(1+\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ such cycles. All bounds are asymptotically optimal and significantly improve earlier results on Hamiltonian resilience, packing, and covering in sparse pseudorandom graphs.

papers.title: Iwasawa Theory of Elliptic Curves in Quadratic Twist Families
papers.abstract: In this article, we use two different approaches -- one algebraic and the other analytic -- to study the variation of Iwasawa invariants of rational elliptic curves in some quadratic twist families. The analytic approach involves a thorough investigation of half-integral weight modular forms. On the other hand, the algebraic proof requires studying the BDP-Selmer groups and the fine Selmer groups.

papers.title: A2Mamba: Attention-augmented State Space Models for Visual Recognition
papers.abstract: Transformers and Mamba, initially invented for natural language processing, have inspired backbone architectures for visual recognition. Recent studies integrated Local Attention Transformers with Mamba to capture both local details and global contexts. Despite competitive performance, these methods are limited to simple stacking of Transformer and Mamba layers without any interaction mechanism between them. Thus, deep integration between Transformer and Mamba layers remains an open problem. We address this problem by proposing A2Mamba, a powerful Transformer-Mamba hybrid network architecture, featuring a new token mixer termed Multi-scale Attention-augmented State Space Model (MASS), where multi-scale attention maps are integrated into an attention-augmented SSM (A2SSM). A key step of A2SSM performs a variant of cross-attention by spatially aggregating the SSM's hidden states using the multi-scale attention maps, which enhances spatial dependencies pertaining to a two-dimensional space while improving the dynamic modeling capabilities of SSMs. Our A2Mamba outperforms all previous ConvNet-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based architectures in visual recognition tasks. For instance, A2Mamba-L achieves an impressive 86.1% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K. In semantic segmentation, A2Mamba-B exceeds CAFormer-S36 by 2.5% in mIoU, while exhibiting higher efficiency. In object detection and instance segmentation with Cascade Mask R-CNN, A2Mamba-S surpasses MambaVision-B by 1.2%/0.9% in AP^b/AP^m, while having 40% fewer parameters. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/LMMMEng/A2Mamba.

papers.title: Reducing Pipeline Bubbles in Message-Efficient State Machine Replication
papers.abstract: Round-based pipelining in state machine replication (SMR) protocols reduces amortized bottleneck message complexity to $O(1)$, but waiting for network propagation and accommodating timing variation create pipeline bubbles that can erase this benefit. We present Chora, a message-efficient SMR protocol co-designed with a network runtime to minimize these bubbles under common-case synchrony. Chora introduces a new round construct that decouples propagation delay from round length. It then builds a carefully engineered runtime that minimizes variation in processing jitter. The co-designed protocol leverages strong synchrony to achieve $O(1)$ amortized bottleneck message complexity with high resource utilization, and maintains safety and liveness when timing predictability degrades. Evaluation shows that Chora reaches 3.92 million operations per second with five RDMA replicas, achieving 2.87$\times$ throughput of the state-of-the-art, while maintaining comparable latency. Even on this single-hop RDMA network that favors conventional rounds, Chora reduces time lost to pipeline bubbles, leaving more CPU time for protocol processing. Across three to seven replicas, the CPU utilization rate for protocol processing increases by 211%--421% and throughput improves by 5.3--6.6$\times$ over conventional rounds.

papers.title: Time arrow in open-boundary one-dimensional stochastic dynamics: effects of discrete thermal kicks over temperature interface
papers.abstract: Does nonequilibrium characteristics exhibit in one-dimensional open-boundary stochastic systems? We introduce a discrete-timestep stochastic model, where the particle dynamics follows a discrete overdamped stochastic equation, and thermal kicks are presented over discrete timesteps. These thermal kicks are derived from a position-dependent temperature profile with a sharp interface. The discrete characteristic and the Itô-type stochastic scheme make our model distinct from the conventional discussions of an overdamped colloidal model. Under the open-boundary condition, one cannot observe any net probability current in the nonequilibrium steady state (NESS). On the other hand, the nonequilibrium nature of this system can be extracted through the asymmetry in forward and backward transition probabilities, as is reported in this work through the simulation and theoretic analysis. In particular, our result shows prominent time irreversibility near the temperature interface. We propose a hidden-gyration scenario that demonstrates the source of irreversibility, while the collapse of gyrations on the one-dimensional coordinate accounts for the absence of probability current.

papers.title: A full-rank subgroup of Bloch Groups of CM Fields
papers.abstract: This article generalizes the result of Burns et al (2022), to find an algorithm to find some elements generating a full-rank subgroup of the torsion-free part of Bloch group of a certain CM number field, and compute the rank of it.

papers.title: Spin Current Generation Controlled by the Néel State in a Compensated Ferrimagnet
papers.abstract: Compensated ferrimagnets, which break sublattice and time-reversal symmetries in the ground state, exhibit an isotropic ferromagnet-like spin splitting despite a vanishing net magnetization, in contrast to altermagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting. We investigate how isotropic spin splitting manifests in spin transport by analyzing the spin Seebeck effect and spin pumping in a junction between a compensated ferrimagnet and a normal metal. We show that compensated ferrimagnets generate a sizable spin Seebeck signal, with a sign that can be reversed by switching between the two Néel states. Furthermore, we demonstrate that spin pumping exhibits a Néel-state-dependent resonance splitting, which is absent in conventional antiferromagnets. These results identify spin pumping as a natural readout mechanism for compensated ferrimagnets and establish them as promising magnetization-free building blocks for spintronic memory devices.

papers.title: Degenerate symplectic fixed points and Gromov-Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between Gromov--Witten invariants and the number of fixed points of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on closed rational symplectic manifolds, without assuming nondegeneracy, via deformed Hamiltonian spectral invariants. We obtain a Hamiltonian fixed point estimate involving Gromov--Witten invariants with one point insertion under an explicit minimum-area hypothesis. We propose three conjectures about Hamiltonian fixed point estimate and prove them for every generalized flag manifold $X=G/P$ equipped with a rational Kähler form. We extend Schwarz's quantum cuplength to deformed quantum cuplength for symplectic periods and use it to obtain estimates on monotone symplectic manifolds admitting nonzero mixed Gromov--Witten invariants. We use the quantum-factorization estimate to recover the Fano toric case of Givental's symplectic fixed-point theorem. Finally, a graded spectral-carrier argument gives uniform fixed-point bounds on negatively monotone manifolds.

papers.title: Text-to-Image Prompt Optimization for Unseen Rewards
papers.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) prompt optimization rewrites user prompts to improve the quality of generated images under a target reward. Existing methods typically assume a known reward, relying on reward-specific training or handcrafted instructions. We instead study prompt optimization for unseen rewards, which are unknown at design time and accessible only through scores at test time. We observe that removing reward-specific guidance substantially reduces the search efficiency of LLM-based optimizers, even though their optimization histories contain evidence of what the reward favors. To address this challenge, we introduce RATTPO (Reward-Adaptive Test-Time Prompt Optimization), a reward-generic method that turns this implicit evidence into explicit search guidance. At each round, RATTPO contrasts high- and low-scoring prompts to infer competing hypotheses about promising rewriting directions, then generates and evaluates candidates under each hypothesis. Across four reward families, RATTPO consistently outperforms reward-generic baselines at equal budgets and achieves performance comparable to reward-tailored optimizers without any reward-specific adjustment.

papers.title: To collapse or not to collapse: Halo evolution with self-interacting dark matter mass segregation
papers.abstract: Surprisingly compact substructures in galaxies and galaxy clusters, but also field halos, have been observed by gravitational lensing. They could be difficult to explain with collisionless dark matter (DM). To explain those objects, recent studies focused on the gravothermal collapse that halos consisting of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) can undergo. However, simple models of elastic scattering could face problems explaining those compact objects during very later stages of the collapse and the post-collapse phase, where a black hole may have formed from DM. We aim to explain compact halos while avoiding the gravothermal catastrophe to which typical SIDM models are subject. Therefore, we investigate the evolution of a DM halo for an SIDM model consisting of two species with unequal masses, which features only interactions between the different species but not within themselves. Employing $N$-body simulations, we study the effect of unequal-mass SIDM models on the evolution of an isolated DM halo. In particular, the late stages of its evolution with high central densities are simulated. We find that our two-species SIDM models can produce density cores with their size depending on the mass ratio of the two species. Moreover, mass segregation caused by the unequal particle masses leads to a finite final density state or at least a slowly growing density, which depends on the mass ratio and the mass fraction of the two DM species. SIDM models consisting of two DM species can simultaneously explain DM halos with density cores, as well as systems that are denser in their centre than expected from collisionless DM, while avoiding the gravothermal catastrophe. They are a compelling alternative to single-species models, offering a rich phenomenology.

papers.title: Boundedness of complements for fibered Fano threefolds in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a canonical bundle formula for Fano type fibrations and Shokurov's conjecture on boundedness of complements for Fano type threefold pairs $(X,B)$ with fibration structures in large characteristics. In particular, we prove the conjecture when $-(K_X+B)\not\equiv 0$ is nef and not big in large characteristics.

papers.title: Fortune: Formula-Driven Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning over Complex Tables
papers.abstract: Tables are a fundamental medium for organizing and analyzing data, making table reasoning an essential capability for intelligent systems. Although large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong general reasoning abilities, they still struggle with accurate numerical reasoning over tabular data, particularly in complex table settings that require more than simple relational lookup. Spreadsheet formulas provide a powerful and expressive interface for executable symbolic operations, enabling sophisticated reasoning patterns that remain largely underexplored by existing LLMs. In this paper, we introduce Formula Tuning (Fortune), a formula-driven reinforcement learning (RL) framework that trains LLMs to generate executable spreadsheet formulas for question answering over tabular data, using execution success and answer correctness as reward signals. Building upon Fortune, we train Formula-R1 and evaluate its performance across seven table reasoning benchmarks, demonstrating competitive performance, particularly on tasks involving complex tables and multi-step numerical computation. Furthermore, Formula-R1-Plus, which integrates textual and formula-based reasoning, achieves further performance improvements. Beyond these empirical results, we provide insights into the roles of reinforcement learning and executable formula representations in table reasoning, highlighting the broader potential of symbolic RL to enhance the reasoning capabilities of LLMs.

papers.title: Hardware-tailored logical Clifford circuits for stabilizer codes
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction is the art of protecting fragile quantum information through suitable encoding and active interventions. However, it is notoriously difficult to manipulate encoded quantum data without causing uncorrectable errors. Here, we introduce a mathematical framework for constructing hardware-tailored circuits that implement any desired Clifford unitary on the logical level of any given stabilizer code. We formulate this task as a discrete optimization problem that minimizes the number of CZ gates while naturally incorporating a parameterization of all Clifford stabilizers. Despite the intrinsic difficulty of the circuit compilation problem, our methods scale to at least $16$ physical qubits. Because our circuits require very few CZ gates, they provide excellent starting points for constructing fault-tolerant implementations using flag gadgets. Using a brute-force search, we develop several such flag gadgets, including weakly fault-tolerant logical Hadamard circuits for the $[[8,3,2]]$ code that require an unprecedentedly small number of physical two-qubit gates. Our work introduces both the mathematics and software for compiling hardware-tailored logical Clifford circuits. From a broader perspective, we turn away from the standard generator decomposition and instead focus on the holistic compilation of entire logical circuits, leading to significant savings in practice.

papers.title: VFRTok: Variable Frame Rates Video Tokenizer with Duration-Proportional Information Assumption
papers.abstract: Modern video generation frameworks based on Latent Diffusion Models suffer from inefficiencies in tokenization due to the Frame-Proportional Information Assumption. Existing tokenizers provide fixed temporal compression rates, causing the computational cost of the diffusion model to scale linearly with the frame rate. The paper proposes the Duration-Proportional Information Assumption: the upper bound on the information capacity of a video is proportional to the duration rather than the number of frames. Based on this insight, the paper introduces VFRTok, a Transformer-based video tokenizer, that enables variable frame rate encoding and decoding through asymmetric frame rate training between the encoder and decoder. Furthermore, the paper proposes Partial Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) to decouple position and content modeling, which groups correlated patches into unified tokens. The Partial RoPE effectively improves content-awareness, enhancing the video generation capability. Benefiting from the compact and continuous spatio-temporal representation, VFRTok achieves competitive reconstruction quality and state-of-the-art generation fidelity while using only 1/8 tokens compared to existing tokenizers. The code and weights are released at: https://github.com/KwaiVGI/VFRTok.

papers.title: Adaptive Linear Networks for Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting in Big Data Systems
papers.abstract: Large-scale sensing, clinical, transportation, energy, and climate systems often produce irregular multivariate time series with sparse observations, heterogeneous sampling intervals, and asynchronous variables. Forecasting at externally supplied future query coordinates requires a model to accommodate variable observation lengths and time locations while retaining efficient variable interaction. We present AiT (Adaptive inverted Transformer), whose ALinear (Adaptive Linear) module generates sample-adaptive temporal weights from observation or query coordinates. More precisely, ALinear is time-conditioned attention pooling without value projection. Available observation or query coordinates generate the corresponding keys or queries, the fixed-shape counterpart may use learned default slots, and the unprojected inputs serve as values. The name "Linear" therefore denotes only the final weighted-sum output form and not equivalence to an unrestricted affine layer or to DLinear. AiT uses ALinear to encode variable-length histories and decode query-conditioned forecasts, and applies Transformer blocks over the resulting variable tokens to model cross-variable relationships. The evaluation on four public irregular forecasting datasets examines prediction accuracy and computational efficiency, while controlled protocols are specified for temporal-design, scalability, missingness, and statistical analyses.

papers.title: Topological phases of coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger wires
papers.abstract: The global half-filled phase diagrams of an arbitrary number $N_{\text{w}}$ of diagonally and perpendicularly coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger wires are identified. The diagonally coupled wires exhibit rich topological phase diagrams with insulating phases characterized by winding numbers $0\leq w \leq N_{\text{w}}$ and topological critical lines. They also exhibit completely flat bands at specific values of the model parameters, indicated by lines in the phase diagrams. An even number of perpendicularly coupled wires exhibits either gapless or topologically trivial phases. An odd number of perpendicularly coupled wires additionally exhibits nontrivial topological phases with winding number $w=1$. For $δ<0$, their gapless regions contain a topologically nontrivial effective SSH sector supporting localized single-particle edge modes. They also reveal confined coherent correlations in the odd-indexed wires at strong inter-wire coupling away from the gapless regions.

papers.title: VideoMark: Training-Free Watermarking for 2D-VAE Video Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This work presents \textbf{VideoMark}, a training-free watermarking framework for video diffusion models with frame-aligned 2D VAEs. VideoMark embeds pseudorandom error-correcting (PRC) codewords by modulating the signs of Gaussian initialization noise without model retraining. Under a joint pseudorandomness assumption on the instantiated PRC encoder, the resulting initialization tensor is computationally indistinguishable from the Gaussian reference; exact distributional equality holds for the ideal independent uniform-sign construction. To support temporally structured video watermarking, we introduce a frame-wise message design together with a Temporal Matching Module (TMM), which recovers frame correspondence under temporal reordering without requiring length-specific watermark layouts. Experiments on ModelScope and I2VGen-XL show that VideoMark achieves accurate watermark extraction on clean generations while maintaining video quality comparable to watermark-free generation. The proposed temporal matching mechanism further improves recovery under frame reordering and enables systematic evaluation under a range of temporal and compression perturbations. We additionally analyze the computational characteristics and practical operating conditions of inversion-based extraction. Overall, VideoMark provides a simple training-free construction for studying pseudorandom watermarking in videos generated by frame-aligned 2D-VAE diffusion models, and establishes a foundation for extending structured noise watermarking to broader video-generation architectures.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Causal Inference with Spillover and Carryover Effects: Airstrikes and Insurgent Violence in Vietnam and Afghanistan
papers.abstract: Do airstrikes suppress insurgent violence or provoke it? Answering such questions requires methods that preserve the spatial and temporal structure of airstrikes and insurgent retaliation. Yet nearly all microlevel research aggregates fine-grained data into panels built on large administrative units and long time intervals. This practice forecloses direct tests of causal mechanisms and imposes restrictive assumptions about spillover and carryover that bias estimates. We develop a practical framework for spatiotemporal causal inference in which treatment, mediator, and outcome all retain their precise locations and timing. Applying it to declassified airstrike data from Vietnam and Afghanistan, we find that bombing displaces, but does not suppress, insurgent violence. Insurgent retaliation follows predictable patterns, concentrating near rebel-controlled hamlets (Vietnam) and U.S. bases (Afghanistan) and emerging about a week later. Civilian harm does not mediate this response. Post-airstrike insurgent violence appears less about avenging aggrieved civilians than demonstrating resolve by imposing costs on counterinsurgents.

papers.title: Mamba-3D as Masked Autoencoders for Accurate and Data-Efficient Analysis of Medical Ultrasound Videos
papers.abstract: Ultrasound videos are an important form of clinical imaging data, and deep learning-based automated analysis can improve diagnostic accuracy and clinical efficiency. However, the scarcity of labeled data and the inherent challenges of video analysis have impeded the advancement of related methods. In this work, we introduce E-ViM$^3$, a data-efficient Vision Mamba network that preserves the 3D structure of video data, enhancing long-range dependencies and inductive biases to better model space-time correlations. With our design of Enclosure Global Tokens (EGT), the model captures and aggregates global features more effectively than competing methods. To further improve data efficiency, we employ masked video modeling for self-supervised pre-training, with the proposed Spatial-Temporal Chained (STC) masking strategy designed to adapt to various video scenarios. Experiments demonstrate that E-ViM$^3$ performs as the state-of-the-art in two high-level semantic analysis tasks across four datasets of varying sizes: EchoNet-Dynamic, CAMUS, MICCAI-BUV, and WHBUS. Furthermore, our model achieves competitive performance with limited labels, highlighting its potential impact on real-world clinical applications.

papers.title: Local patch analysis of ACT DR6 convergence map using morphological statistics
papers.abstract: We perform a hierarchical, multi-scale morphological analysis to search for anomalous behavior in the large-scale matter distribution using the Atacama Cosmology Telescope Data Release 6 (ACT DR6) convergence map. Employing Minkowski functionals, contour Minkowski tensors, and Betti numbers, we measure their deviations from ensemble expectations and median values obtained from isotropic $Λ$CDM simulations provided by ACT. To assess statistical significance, we develop a general methodology based on the persistence of anomalies across threshold ranges and spatial resolutions, accounting for correlations among the statistics. Analyzing both the full dataset and hemispherical subregions reveals overall consistency with isotropic $Λ$CDM expectations. Because localized deviations may be diluted over larger areas, we further examine individual sky patches, identifying several regions with statistically significant deviations that we designate as anomalous. In particular, positive density fluctuations near the CMB Cold Spot are anomalous, exceeding the 99% confidence level, and overlap with a previously reported anomalous southern spot in Planck CMB temperature data. Analysis of the corresponding null map indicates potential contamination from residual foregrounds or instrumental systematics. Comparing the anomalous patches in ACT with those from a previous Planck convergence map analysis reveals no overlapping regions, suggesting that the Planck anomalies are likely attributable to noise. Further investigation of these atypical patches, considering residual foregrounds, instrumental systematics, reconstruction noise, and independent large-scale structure surveys, is warranted to determine their physical origin.

papers.title: On the $\mathcal{D}^+_J$ operator on higher-dimensional almost Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth exact $J$-invariant two-form on a closed almost Kähler manifold admits a unique scalar potential, and that the associated generalized Monge-Ampère equation has at most one solution. In real dimension four, \textcolor{black}{we establish} local existence and uniqueness for nearby volume forms with the same total volume under the condition $h_J^-=b^+-1$. We also construct a nonintegrable almost Kähler four-torus and volume forms on it that cannot be realized by cohomologous $J$-compatible forms. These volume forms have the same total volume as the original volume form and can be chosen arbitrarily close to it. Finally, we relate the resulting trace potential to existing \textcolor{black}{a priori} estimates.

papers.title: Extending van der Geer and Hirzebruch's generalization of Construction A
papers.abstract: This paper discusses a generalization of Construction A and its application to root lattices of type $A_n, D_n,$ and $E_n$. While the classical Construction A provides a correspondence between binary codes and lattices, and its extension to cyclotomic fields relates $p$-ary codes to lattices over the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)$, we further extend this framework to a broader class of even root lattices. Specifically, for a given lattice $Λ$ of type $A_n, D_n,$ or $E_n$, we define a surjective mapping $ρ$ from the dual lattice $Λ^*$ to a finite ring $R$ isomorphic to the quotient $Λ^*/Λ$. We then characterize the conditions under which the resulting lattice $(ρ^{\oplus m})^{-1}(C)$, constructed from an $R$-code $C$ of length $m$, becomes an even unimodular lattice. Furthermore, we apply our generalized Construction A to the algebraic lattices of type $D_4$ and $E_6$ realized as fractional ideals of cyclotomic fields. Consequently, we show that the theta functions associated with these lattices can be expressed via the weight enumerators of the corresponding codes, proving that they are Hilbert modular forms over totally real fields.

papers.title: A Steerable Deep Network for Model-Free Diffusion MRI Registration
papers.abstract: Nonrigid registration is vital to medical image analysis but remains challenging for diffusion MRI (dMRI) due to its high-dimensional, spatio-angular dependence. We present a novel, geometric deep learning framework for model-free, nonrigid registration of raw dMRI data. We formulate registration in the native spatio-angular acquisition space under the joint action of 3D roto-translations, $\mathrm{SE}(3)$. Central to our framework is the equivalence between equivariant spatio-angular convolutions and 3D steerable convolutions on spherical-harmonic coefficient fields, which we exploit to construct an $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant U-Net. A by-product of this design choice is freedom from having to augment the data with roto-translated versions of itself. We also formulate a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss between water-displacement distributions, evaluated in Fourier space as a weighted sum of squared signal differences, and extend it with a local contrast correction that reduces to a local correlation. In controlled comparisons, including a known deformation of real tissue, the raw signal yields markedly more accurate alignment than fractional anisotropy under the same optimizer. On held-out HCP subjects and on a held-out clinical-grade cohort (AOMIC) from a different scanner, our method improves anatomical overlap over ANTs SyN on fractional anisotropy, mrregister on fODFs, DDMReg and SynthMorph, without estimating any derived representation, and the steerable network matches a conventional U-Net with fewer parameters while being unaffected by grid rotations of its inputs. This work establishes a foundation for data-driven, geometry-aware dMRI registration directly in the acquisition space.

papers.title: Rethinking domain generalization in medical image segmentation: One image as one domain
papers.abstract: Domain shifts in medical image segmentation, particularly when data comes from different centers, pose significant challenges. Intra-center variability, such as differences in scanner models or imaging protocols, can cause domain shifts as large as, or even larger than, those between centers. To address this, we propose the "one image as one domain" (OIOD) hypothesis, which treats each image as a unique domain, enabling flexible and robust domain generalization. Based on this hypothesis, we develop a unified disentanglement-based domain generalization (UniDDG) framework, which simultaneously handles both multi-source and single-source domain generalization without requiring explicit domain labels. This approach simplifies training with a fixed architecture, independent of the number of source domains, reducing complexity and enhancing scalability. We decouple each input image into content representation and style code, then exchange and combine these within the batch for segmentation, reconstruction, and further disentanglement. By maintaining distinct style codes for each image, our model ensures thorough decoupling of content representations and style codes, improving domain invariance of the content representations. Additionally, we enhance generalization with expansion mask attention (EMA) for boundary preservation and style augmentation (SA) to simulate diverse image styles, improving robustness to domain shifts. Extensive experiments show that our method achieves Dice scores of 84.43% and 88.91% for multi-source to single-center and single-center generalization in optic disc and optic cup segmentation, respectively, and 86.96% and 88.56% for prostate segmentation, outperforming current state-of-the-art domain generalization methods, offering superior performance and adaptability across clinical settings.

papers.title: MMGenBench: An Automated Pipeline for Evaluating LMMs from a Text-to-Image Generation Perspective
papers.abstract: Existing benchmarks often rely on predefined questions or reference captions, limiting their flexibility for evaluating detailed descriptions on new image collections. We present MMGenBench, an automated benchmark framework for evaluating Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) from raw images without per-image questions or reference captions. The pipeline generates descriptions, reconstructs images with a frozen text-to-image model, and compares the original and reconstructed images using a frozen image encoder. It produces reusable per-image scores and inspectable reconstructions, supporting both model comparison and diagnosis of reconstructible visual information. We construct MMGenBench-Domain with 10,000 generated images and MMGenBench-Test with 1,284 images spanning 13 overlapping visual patterns. Evaluation of 68 LMMs reveals pattern-specific differences in reconstruction quality that overall scores can obscure. On 1,000 human-labeled caption pairs from six models, the default score achieves 90.00\% sample-level agreement. Factual perturbations and component analyses characterize the score's sensitivity under the evaluated pipeline, while a COCO study provides initial validation on natural photographs. MMGenBench complements existing benchmarks by linking automated comparisons to visual evidence of the information preserved in LMM descriptions. Project page: https://github.com/lerogo/MMGenBench.

papers.title: Revisiting Out-of-Distribution Detection in Semantic Difference Space
papers.abstract: The primary goal of most existing out-of-distribution (OOD) detection works is to identify inputs with "Semantic Shifts". However, the existing definition of "Semantic Shift" in previous studies remains vague, resulting in controversial choices of OOD samples in many benchmarks. Consequently, some benchmarks are too trivial for evaluating OOD detection, whereas others include OOD instances that are practically undetectable. In this paper, we propose a formal definition of "Semantic Difference Space", which reflects the scope of a model's OOD detection capability after training convergence. The definition is grounded in an analysis of how the loss-based optimization shapes the model's perceptual toward OOD inputs, offering theoretical explanations for the controversies regarding the selection of OOD samples across existing benchmarks. To validate the correctness of our analysis, we construct multiple datasets, primarily in the context of image classification, and we find that compared to different OOD detection methods, different OOD settings play a more decisive role in the detection results. Finally, we propose a simple yet effective OOD Separability Probe (OSP) method to evaluate whether the existing OOD detection benchmarks are reasonable, identifying issues in some benchmarks and highlighting a few that are worth further exploration.

papers.title: On Cone Restriction Estimates in Higher Dimensions
papers.abstract: We revisit the Ou-Wang's approach to the cone restriction problem via polynomial partitioning. By recasting their inductive scheme as a recursive algorithm and incorporating the nested polynomial Wolff axioms, we obtain improved bounds for cone restriction estimates in higher dimensions.

papers.title: ProFL: Performative Robust Optimal Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Performative prediction is a framework that captures distribution shifts that occur during the training of machine learning models due to their deployment. As the trained model is used, the induced data distribution evolves, leading to deviations from the original data distribution. The impact of such model-induced distribution shifts in federated learning (FL) is increasingly likely to transpire in real-life use cases. A recently proposed approach extends performative prediction to FL with the resulting model converging to a performative stable point, which may be far from the performative optimal point. Earlier research in centralized settings has shown that the performative optimal point can be achieved under model-induced distribution shifts, but these approaches require the performative risk to be convex and the training data to be noiseless. These assumptions are often violated in realistic FL systems. This paper addresses these limitations and proposes Performative Robust Optimal Federated Learning (ProFL), an algorithm that targets the performative optimal point in FL while mitigating the effects of noisy and contaminated local data. We present a neighborhood-convergence analysis under the Polyak--Lojasiewicz condition, which applies to non-convex objectives. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the advantage of Robust Optimal Federated Learning over the state-of-the-art.

papers.title: Grammatical Error Correction for Low-Resource Languages: The Case of Zarma
papers.abstract: Grammatical error correction (GEC) aims to improve text quality and readability. Previous work on the task focused primarily on high-resource languages, while low-resource languages lack robust tools. To address this shortcoming, we present a study on GEC for Zarma, a language spoken by over five million people in West Africa. We compare three approaches: rule-based methods, machine translation (MT) models, and large language models (LLMs). We evaluated GEC models using a dataset of more than 250,000 examples, including synthetic and human-annotated data. Our results showed that the MT-based approach using M2M100 outperforms others, with a detection rate of 95.82% and a suggestion accuracy of 78.90% in automatic evaluations (AE) and an average score of 3.0 out of 5.0 in manual evaluation (ME) from native speakers for grammar and logical corrections. The rule-based method was effective for spelling errors but failed on complex context-level errors. LLMs -- Gemma 2b and MT5-small -- showed moderate performance. Our work supports use of MT models to enhance GEC in low-resource settings, and we validated these results with Bambara, another West African language.

papers.title: Asymmetry Amplification by a Nonadiabatic Passage through a Critical Point
papers.abstract: We propose and solve a minimal model of dynamic passage through a second-order phase transition in the presence of symmetry breaking interactions and no dissipation. Our model generalizes the Hamiltonian dynamics of the Painleve'-2 equation to the case with many degrees of freedom, while maintaining the integrability property. The evolution eventually leads to a highly asymmetric state, no matter how weak the symmetry breaking parameter of the Hamiltonian is. This suggests a potential mechanism for strong asymmetry in the production of quasi-particles with nearly identical characteristics. The model's integrability also yields exact exponents for the scaling of the density of the nonadiabatically excited quasi-particles.

papers.title: Feriji: A French-Zarma Parallel Corpus, Glossary & Translator
papers.abstract: Machine translation (MT) is a rapidly expanding field that has experienced significant advancements in recent years with the development of models capable of translating multiple languages with remarkable accuracy. However, the representation of African languages in this field still needs to improve due to linguistic complexities and limited resources. This applies to the Zarma language, a dialect of Songhay (of the Nilo-Saharan language family) spoken by over 5 million people across Niger and neighboring countries \cite{lewis2016ethnologue}. This paper introduces Feriji, the first robust French-Zarma parallel corpus and glossary designed for MT. The corpus, containing 61,085 sentences in Zarma and 42,789 in French, and a glossary of 4,062 words represent a significant step in addressing the need for more resources for Zarma.
