papers.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables language models to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations, but repeatedly including multiple examples increases context length and inference cost. Many existing implicit ICL methods encode demonstrations as fixed vectors, limiting adaptation of the intervention to individual queries and token positions. We propose Attention-Patching, an implicit ICL method that models contextual changes in self-attention outputs through task-specific updates to attention output projections. Using query-answer pairs processed with and without a fixed demonstration set, Attention-Patching fits layer-wise affine transformations from non-contextual attention representations to the demonstration-induced output changes. Across 12 classification benchmarks and four model families, Attention-Patching achieves higher average accuracy than the evaluated implicit ICL baselines while maintaining performance comparable to explicit ICL at near zero-shot inference cost. Further experiments on diverse generation tasks demonstrate its applicability to autoregressive multi-token generation.

papers.title: Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Operators: Strict Monotonicity and Asymptotic Behavior
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the properties of the generalized principal eigenvalue for a coupled local/nonlocal operator. First, we establish sufficient conditions to guarantee strict monotonicity properties, obtaining weaker hypotheses than those currently available in the literature for nonlocal operators. Next, we establish several results concerning the asymptotic behavior of this generalized eigenvalue, along with the convergence of the corresponding eigenfunctions. These results are very useful for the study of nonlinear problems. Our findings reveal novel phenomena that are not present in purely local or purely nonlocal cases. The main mathematical difficulty lies in the fact that the generalized eigenvalue does not always admit an eigenfunction, in addition to the inherent technicalities of the considered coupling.

papers.title: The effect of isotopically-enriched 70Ge on the Raman scattering in Cr2Ge2Te6
papers.abstract: The highest-energy A5g Raman-active vibrational mode in chromium germanium telluride (Cr2Ge2Te6, CGT) exhibits a unique lineshape comprising a series of remarkably narrow peaks. While this multiplet was attributed to the natural isotope distribution of germanium affecting Ge-Ge pseudo-molecular vibrations, direct evidence has been lacking. Here, we present a Raman spectroscopy study of CGT isotopically enriched with 70Ge to validate this hypothesis. Upon isotopic enrichment, both the E5g and A5g modes exhibit a pronounced blue-shift. At room temperature, the A5g peak undergoes significant narrowing, while low-temperature measurements reveal a single, well-defined line instead of the previously observed multiplet. These observations align precisely with density functional theory calculations, confirming that the multi-line profile originates from Ge isotope distribution. Our findings demonstrate that similar isotope-induced Raman splitting may occur in other structurally analogous layered tellurides containing Ge or Si.

papers.title: Statistics of Fundamental Fourier Coefficients of Cusp Forms
papers.abstract: We study sign changes of Fourier coefficients of elliptic and Siegel modular forms in considerable generality. For any $N \geq 1$ and an arbitrary non-zero elliptic cusp form $f\in S_κ(Γ_1(N))$ ($κ\in \frac{1}{2} \mathbb{Z}$) with real Fourier coefficients, we show that a positive proportion of its non-zero Fourier coefficients change sign if $κ\geq 1$ is integral. If $κ\geq 1/2$ is half-integral, we get an almost optimal result. As applications, we establish quantitative sign-change results for `fundamental' Fourier coefficients of Siegel cusp forms of arbitrary degree $n$. These improve the previous best known results on the number of non-zero fundamental Fourier coefficients, even in degree $n=1$.

papers.title: On the Unique Identification of Finitely Many Radial Heat Sources
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate an inverse source problem for the heat equation in $\R^d$ ($d\geq1$), in which the source is a finite positive linear combination of translates of a known real-valued radial Schwartz profile with nonzero total mass. Both the locations and strengths of the sources are to be identified from the observations of time traces at finitely many spatial points over an arbitrary nonempty open positive-time interval. For $d\geq2$, we prove that the sharp universal measurement threshold is $dN+1$: every set of $dN+1$ measurement points in affine general position uniquely identifies every source configuration with at most $N$ locations. For $d=1$, we prove that two distinct measurement points uniquely identify every finite source configuration, independently of the number of sources, and that this count is sharp. The analysis relies on an equivalence between equality of heat traces and equality of weighted distance measures, and then employs perpendicular-bisector hyperplanes to resolve geometric ambiguities. We also establish identification guarantees using $d+1$ measurement points: clustered designs under a reference-distance separation condition, adaptive designs for arbitrary configurations, and any fixed affinely independent design for almost every location configuration, uniformly over all positive strengths.

papers.title: How Many Parameters Does Forecasting Need? A Survey and Code-Level Audit of Lightweight Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Long-term time series forecasting supports decisions in energy, transportation, weather and finance, where forecasts are produced continuously and often on constrained hardware. Recent work has moved in two directions. One scales Transformers and pre-trained foundation models to millions or hundreds of millions of parameters. The other shows that models with only hundreds to tens of thousands of parameters remain competitive on the standard benchmarks. Existing surveys organize forecasting models by backbone and treat efficiency as a side topic, so the reasons these small models work, and the way their sizes are reported, remain unexamined. This survey focuses on lightweight long-term forecasting. It provides a taxonomy of about thirty-five models in six families, with a common notation and an architecture diagram for each core model. It offers a structured-linear view in which the smallest models are linear maps restricted by frequency truncation or period folding, and it tests each restriction in closed form on eight benchmarks. It complements the literature review with an audit of sixteen official code repositories, which reproduces published parameter counts and reveals reporting gaps of up to 289 times. Finally, it gives practical guidance on model selection and reporting, and summarizes open problems.

papers.title: Positivity and multivariate extensions of two-parameter Askey-Wilson moments
papers.abstract: Kim and Stanton showed that certain specialized Askey--Wilson moments are polynomials with integer coefficients after normalization, and conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative. We refine this into the conjecture for the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments and prove the refinement by establishing a manifestly positive recurrence. We also construct a combinatorial model that expresses the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments as weighted sums of decorated partial matchings. This model specializes to the partial matching model for the mixed moments of continuous $q$-Hermite polynomials. Finally, we consider the corresponding multivariate moments and prove that their minimal numerators have nonnegative coefficients up to an explicit sign.

papers.title: Stay or Switch? Metric Distortion with Online Candidate Arrivals
papers.abstract: We study metric distortion in sequential elections with online candidate arrivals. In each round, a newly arriving challenger competes against the incumbent, and a voting rule must select one of the two based on voters' pairwise preferences. Our goal is to guarantee low metric distortion at every round, relative to the best candidate among all those that have arrived so far. For deterministic rules, we establish an asymptotically optimal bound of $Θ(\sqrt{t})$ at round $t$, achieved by a threshold rule favoring the incumbent. In contrast, randomization allows constant distortion. We show that persistent randomized dictatorship achieves optimal distortion of $5$ against adaptive adversaries, which observe previous winners, and $3$ against oblivious adversaries, which do not. Finally, we generalize the model along two dimensions, the available information and the action space, and establish distortion guarantees for each setting.

papers.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
papers.abstract: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $ζ_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.

papers.title: Strain-induced non-trivial band topology and large magnetoresistance in epitaxial SrTaO$_3$ thin films
papers.abstract: Epitaxial thin films of complex transition metal oxides constitute an ideal platform for realizing correlated topological phases through strain engineering of crystal symmetry and band topology. Here, we investigate the electronic transport properties and the band structure of the 5$d^1$ paramagnetic metal SrTaO$_3$ thin film under epitaxial compressive strain. The film exhibits a large non-saturating quasi-quadratic magnetoresistance (MR) and a nonlinear Hall effect characteristic of two-band transport, together with the field induced re-entrant metallic behavior. The violation of Kohler's scaling further corroborates the scattering from multiple bands. Semiclassical two-band analysis yields carrier densities and mobilities of the order $\sim 10^{21}~\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and $\sim 10^{4}~\mathrm{cm^2 V^{-1} s^{-1}}$, respectively. The observed large mobility and unsaturated MR, indicates the presence of a non-trivial band structure. Consistent with this, results from density functional theory calculations and tight binding model studies reveal that the stable structure has an octahedral rotation $a^0a^0c^+$, where the non-symmorphic symmetry ensures the presence of topological nodal lines yielding finite Berry curvature in the vicinity of the Fermi level. Besides the nodal line, trivial electron and hole pockets exist near the Fermi level, contributing to electron transport. These findings establish that epitaxial strain drives SrTaO$_3$ into a nontrivial topological semimetal, a phase inaccessible in the bulk counterpart.

papers.title: Coherence transfer under bounded channel capacity
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum coherence transfer between two parties whose local reference bases are misaligned, under a constraint on the capacity of the quantum communication channel. Within the resource theory of coherence, we formulate the task as maximizing the coherence received by Bob when Alice is restricted to Maximally Incoherent Operations (MIO) in her local basis. We first analyze two single-shot protocols, based on direct and locally entangled transmission, and derive their phase-optimized coherence yields. We further investigate their performance when Bob's reference basis is unknown, averaging over uniformly distributed basis configurations. In the asymptotic regime, we exploit the reversibility of coherence under MIO to characterize achievable transfer rates in terms of Alice's initial coherence. For single-qubit transmission, we derive an analytical lower bound using pure-state conversions and identify a regime in which the optimal yield saturates the channel capacity.

papers.title: Equivalence of Cohen generics is hyperfinite
papers.abstract: It is shown that the equivalence relation on Cohen generic reals over a countable model of set theory, where two are equivalent if they produce the same generic extension, is hyperfinite, answering a question of the author. The proof uses asymptotic separation and is a digestion of an argument originally produced by GPT-6.

papers.title: Power-Swing Blocking and Out-of-Step Tripping Scheme Using the Swing Center Voltage in Systems With Inverter-Based Resources
papers.abstract: Misoperation of power-swing blocking (PSB) and out-of-step tripping (OST) schemes in distance relays is a critical concern in power systems with increasing penetration levels of inverter-based resources (IBRs). Recently, several papers have studied the impact of IBRs on conventional dual-blinder PSB/OST schemes. They highlight interoperability issues concerning fast power swings and unconventional impedance trajectories, and propose revised relay settings in attempts to deal with the problems. However, the blinder-based PSB methodology suffers from being dependent on the speed of the apparent impedance just as it crosses between the blinders. It is therefore important to consider alternative methods. This paper thoroughly analyzes the characteristics of the swing center voltage (SCV) and the impacts of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) inverters on its local estimation. Then, an SCV-based PSB/OST scheme is proposed, where the main PSB criterion can be tuned from simple system parameters. This is made possible by a separate PSB activation function. The OST scheme uses only one setting and is motivated from the analytical analysis of the SCV with IBRs. Extensive PSCAD/EMTDC simulations verify the performance of the proposed SCV-based PSB/OST scheme and how it overcomes limitations of blinder-based schemes with GFM and GFL inverters.

papers.title: On $k$-very ample line bundles on blowups of surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article we study the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow ups of some smooth surfaces. We begin by investigating the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow-ups of smooth surfaces with Picard number $1$, extending the previously known cases of uniform line bundles to arbitrary line bundles, under certain restrictions. We then show that for blowups of smooth surfaces with trivial canonical divisor, $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles implies the $k$-very ampleness of arbitrary line bundles. In view of the above, we study $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles on blow ups of certain $K3$-surfaces $(K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X)$. Finally, we provide a result concerning the $k$ very ampleness of certain uniform line bundles on the general blow up of product of curves $(K_X \not\cong \mathcal{O}_X)$.

papers.title: THeatA: Transport- and Heating-aware QEC simulation with Cooling Strategies for QCCD Trapped-Ion Systems
papers.abstract: The quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) architecture is a promising approach to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing, enabling flexible qubit interactions by transporting ions between dedicated trap zones. Programs for such systems require operations beyond conventional circuit primitives: ion shuttling, physical SWAPs, trap splitting and merging, and cooling. Motional excitation accumulated during transport increases the mean phonon number of ions and degrades the fidelity of the two-qubit Molmer-Sorensen gates. However, existing quantum error correction (QEC) simulation frameworks do not jointly track per-ion motional excitation and explicitly schedule cooling operations with their transport time and heating costs. We develop a full-stack software framework for QEC experiments and simulations on linear QCCD systems with a single ion species, comprising an intermediate representation (IR) supporting QCCD-native operations, a compiler that translates syndrome-extraction circuits into the IR, and a heating-aware noise-injection pipeline that generates noisy Stim circuits. The compiler updates the mean phonon number of each ion throughout the schedule, and the pipeline derives gate-dependent error rates from the tracked phonon states and per-ion timing, enabling the evaluation of finite-size logical-error scaling of the rotated surface code under transport- and heating-aware noise. We show that transport-induced heating prevents logical error rates from decreasing with increasing code distance under the evaluated conditions, and that indirectly cooling the ion pairs involved in two-qubit gates, by merging them with precooled coolant ions immediately before each gate, restores this decrease. By sweeping the duration and post-cooling mean phonon number of an abstract cooling instruction, we characterize their trade-off and identify the region in which logical-error scaling is maintained.

papers.title: Empirical Margin Sensitivity: An Interventional Neuron-Level Probe of Post-Trained Medical LLMs
papers.abstract: Medical post-training raises benchmark accuracy, but accuracy does not show which internal components a model's decisions depend on, or whether components that support one benchmark also support another. We apply the weight-space intervention paradigm of ROME and MEMIT at the granularity of one MLP down-projection column. Our measurement, Empirical Margin Sensitivity (EMS), replaces each coordinate magnitude of a column by its mean while preserving the column's sign pattern and L1 scale, and records the resulting change in the logit margin between the correct option and its hardest-wrong competitor. This isolates the margin's dependence on a column's fine-grained coordinate structure while the column stays in place. We discover high-EMS columns (anchors) on MedQA in ten public checkpoints (four general-purpose bases and six medical post-trained variants) across the Gemma, Llama, Qwen, and AFM families, and measure the same columns on MedMCQA and PubMedQA. Mean-ablating each discovered anchor set lowers MedQA accuracy in all six post-trained models, by 6 to 28 points. In the two pure-SFT checkpoints, crushing anchors raises the PubMedQA margin on correctly answered items (negative EMS), and anchors with this property sit significantly deeper than the same model's other anchors; the four checkpoints trained with RL or mixed recipes show positive PubMedQA EMS and no significant depth shift. The depth association recurs in each of three held-out checkpoints. Because the checkpoints differ in data and pipeline as well as objective, we report these as per-checkpoint observations.

papers.title: The user who is not there: genealogy and critique of simulated users built with generative AI in UX testing
papers.abstract: Usability testing depends on people, and people's time does not speed up at the pace that software production demands. Large language models (LLMs) now promise to remove people from testing by generating simulated users that browse websites, answer questionnaires and give interviews. This paper examines how academic research understands that promise. It combines a critical literature review with a genealogical reading that follows the simulated user from the cognitive models of the 1980s to current generative agents. The paper makes four claims. First, testing without the user is an old aim of human-computer interaction (HCI), and cost has always justified it. Second, the validity criterion for user models shifted from predictive precision to believability, and recent studies that return to precision report weak results. Third, simulated participants conflict with the values of academic research and with methods that treat participation as a political right, with Participatory Design as the limit case. Fourth, the Latin American literature found in this review uses generative AI to support expert inspection and contains no study of synthetic users. That gap leaves open questions about who gets represented and about research ethics regulation in Brazil. The paper closes with an agenda of open problems. As part of its method, it reports that the review itself used an LLM as research assistant, and it discusses what that implies.

papers.title: Uncovering Hidden Behaviours in Language Models via Limited-Parameter Finetuning
papers.abstract: Large language models can have behaviours which only arise in hard-to-anticipate contexts. These hidden behaviours pose a challenge to alignment audits, which seek to uncover problematic model behaviour but are limited by the scenarios the auditor can anticipate. To address this challenge, we explore limited-parameter finetuning (LPF) on examples of a target behaviour. While training 3-25% of LoRA parameters, LPF reveals whether the model has a hidden behaviour, even when standard behavioural evaluations cannot. LPF succeeds on a suite of model organisms with hidden behaviours (8-14B parameters), and also surfaces naturally occurring hidden behaviours in open-weight models (27-35B parameters). LPF can thus distinguish between models which appear behaviourally identical to an auditor, and does not require the context in which the hidden behaviour surfaces. LPF provides a novel affordance that may be useful for auditing frontier AI models. However, we do not evaluate LPF against baselines in a realistic auditing setting, so further work is needed to determine its practicality.

papers.title: DriveDreamer-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Driving Perception and Agentic Data Generation
papers.abstract: Controllable generation can expand training data for driving perception, but visual realism alone does not ensure learning gains. Effective generation must adapt both what data to generate and how to construct them as the perception model evolves. In this paper, we present DriveDreamer-RSI, a framework for recursive self-improvement of driving perception and agentic data generation through feedback between perception learning and data construction. Its outer loop implements Gap-Guided Target Adaptation, generating labeled videos from current perception gaps and updating targets after training. Its inner loop uses a vision-language agent to iteratively edit scenes through observation and execution feedback. Across rounds, Learning-Feedback-Driven Strategy Refinement derives reusable construction advice from execution experience and downstream learning outcomes. On the nuScenes validation set, DriveDreamer-RSI surpasses the dataset-replay baseline by 4.09 mAP and 4.13 NDS points using approximately half the synthetic frames.

papers.title: Beyond the Black Box: A Diagnosis-Driven Agent for Interpretable MIP Solver Tuning
papers.abstract: Tuning a mixed-integer programming (MIP) solver is an instance-specific problem, where a poor configuration can increase solving time by orders of magnitude. Existing Bayesian optimization tuners treat solver tuning as a black-box optimization problem: each evaluation returns a single score, allowing the tuner to learn which configuration is faster, but not why. Inspired by the use of profilers in GPU-kernel optimization, we introduce APEC (Agent for Per-instance Explainable Configuration), a log-grounded tuning agent for MIP solvers. APEC has three layers: a deterministic layer that profiles each log, an interpretation layer that guides hypothesis-driven diagnosis, and a system layer that controls evaluation, enabling more reliable and interpretable solver tuning. On the full MIPLIB 2017 benchmark set, APEC achieves a 1.58X improvement over the default configuration with over 38% fewer parameter changes than the baselines, making the results easier to read.

papers.title: Identifying the conformal window by chiral phase boundaries
papers.abstract: Once the number of massless fermion flavours reaches a critical value $N_f^*$, many-flavour QCD enters the conformal window, where chiral symmetry remains unbroken in the vacuum. At non-zero quark mass, chiral symmetry is explicitly broken, and thermal chiral crossovers can also occur for $N_f\geq N_f^*$. Their presence alone therefore does not distinguish a QCD-like theory from a mass-deformed conformal theory. They differ, however, in whether a thermal transition persists in the continuum chiral limit. To address this, we map out the chiral phase boundaries of unimproved staggered fermions in the bare lattice parameter space $(N_τ,β,am,N_f)$, comparing $N_f=7$ and $N_f=8$. Our results indicate that the thermal chiral transition persists in the continuum chiral limit for $N_f=7$, whereas the massless continuum theory with $N_f=8$ remains chirally symmetric in the vacuum. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the pseudo-critical surface for eight flavours observed for finite quark masses is consistent with conformal hyperscaling, providing further evidence that eight-flavour QCD lies within the conformal window and suggesting $7<N_f^*\leq8$.

papers.title: Cold CCH and warm CH3CCH: complementary tracers in the massive star-forming complex RCW122 (NE & SW)
papers.abstract: AIMS: By combining CH3CCH and CCH, we present a first multi-transition analysis of the RCW122-NE and RCW122-SW regions in the massive star-forming complex RCW 122. The aim is to investigate and to constrain the nature, chemistry, and evolutionary stage of each region. METHODS: We performed observations with the Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX). The analysis is based on 39 CH3CCH lines with J=10-9 to 20-19 (170.8-341.8 GHz) and four hyperfine components of the CCH N=4-3 transition (349.1-349.6 GHz). We estimated excitation conditions using both local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and non-LTE methods, with rotational-diagram analysis and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) calculations. Gas-grain chemical models were performed with the Nautilus code to reproduce the observed abundances over timescales characteristic of high-mass YSO evolution. RESULTS: The excitation analysis of CH3CCH indicates two physical components suggestive of a thermal gradient. The NE region yields T~41-61 K and N_tot~1x10^{16} cm^{-2}, while SW exhibits T~33-48 K and N_tot~7x10^{15} cm^{-2}. In both regions, CCH traces cold gas below 15 K with an H_2 density of 0.5-4x10^6 cm^{-3}. The detection of the ^{13}C isotopologues of CCH indicates that C^{13}CH is more abundant than ^{13}CCH. Chemical models at various evolutionary stages, with cosmic rays as a key parameter, reproduce the observed CCH and CH3CCH abundances, although the two species form through chemically distinct routes. CONCLUSIONS: We provide a coherent scenario in which CCH traces colder gas at an early evolutionary stage, whereas CH3CCH traces a region characterized by a warmer temperature gradient, associated with chemically more evolved gas at a later stage. These results constrain the conditions governing the origin and survival of interstellar species in a thermally and chemically stratified medium.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Compositional Continual Learning for Robot Manipulation with Gated Low-Rank Experts
papers.abstract: General-purpose manipulation robots must acquire new skills over time without forgetting prior ones or retraining from scratch. We present a continual learning framework that represents each skill as a dedicated expert sub- network in a Progressive Neural Network (PNN). New tasks reuse prior knowledge through low-rank adaptation (LoRA) modules on lateral connections controlled by learnable per-parent gates, enabling explicit attenuation of individual transfer paths while reducing the parameter cost of dense PNN laterals. For long-horizon deployment, a frozen local large language model decomposes natural-language instructions into sub-tasks, routes them to suitable experts, and requests a new expert only when the library is insufficient. Using a shared task-space action interface, we evaluate the framework on twelve MetaWorld tasks and in a Sawyer-to-Panda-to-UR5e cross-embodiment transfer experiment, showing improved task success relative to learning from scratch when demonstrations are limited. Real-robot manipulation experiments further demonstrate that the proposed framework supports compositional execution and expert orchestration.

papers.title: Zhengrong: World Models with Pole-Based Action-Response Factorization for Direct Visual Planning
papers.abstract: Direct visual world models predict the effects of candidate action sequences without recursive latent rollout, yet they leave the temporal structure of action effects unspecified. We introduce Zhengrong (Zhengrong-PoleWM), a world model that decomposes a latent trajectory into an initial-condition anchor, a free response, and delayed responses to action innovations. Nonlinear networks map visual history and causal action prefixes to response coefficients. A shared bank of stable conjugate poles determines how each response evolves with elapsed time. This factorization preserves nonlinear interactions across actions, anchors predictions exactly at the initial state, prevents future actions from affecting earlier predictions, and yields bounded responses to finite control plans. We derive an exact re-anchoring identity that identifies the additional basis direction $Ψ_κ(s)$ needed to represent shifted trajectory tails. Across four offline image-goal control benchmarks (Cube, TwoRoom, PushT, and Reacher), Zhengrong-PoleWM achieves $90.83\% \pm 0.47\%$ macro-average success over two training seeds at epoch 20, exceeding the strongest baseline (QQWorld) by 6.08 percentage points. Selecting checkpoints by validation loss yields $91.21\% \pm 1.00\%$. In a controlled first-epoch Cube study without restart regularization, neural and pole response heads outperform a generic direct predictor by 20.67 and 23.34 percentage points, respectively. On an NVIDIA A100 GPU, median latency for a full 30-iteration cross-entropy method search ranges from 74 to 87 ms across the four tasks. The mean of these medians is 77.5 ms, a 15.8% latency reduction relative to Fast-LeWM and a $7.1\times$ speedup over autoregressive LeWM.

papers.title: Microlocal and global smoothing effect of variable coefficient ZK-type operators
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the smoothing effect of a class of Zakharov-Kuznetsov (ZK) equations, which generalize the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation to higher dimensions. Specifically, we consider linear evolution equations generated by ZK-type operators with variable coefficients, and we study both their microlocal and global smoothing effects under suitable conditions on the coefficients of the operator. Our analysis requires a detailed study of the geometric properties of the Hamiltonian flow associated with the operator under consideration. These properties allow us to prove a dispersive and a strong smoothing effect associated with the Cauchy problem in question: under suitable moment conditions on the initial datum, the solution becomes smooth in space for positive times in a finite time interval.

papers.title: The cost functional for hyperbolic systems of conservation laws
papers.abstract: For hyperbolic systems of conservation laws (without any genuine nonlinearity of linear degeneracy assumption on the flux) we construct a quadratic interaction functional, which controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions and it is local in time. This extends the analysis of [3] from scalar conservation laws to $n \times n$ systems.

papers.title: A local-in-time quadratic functional for scalar conservation laws
papers.abstract: We construct a Glimm-type functional for scalar conservation laws, which is quadratic (w.r.t. the total variation of the initial datum), it controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions, and, differently than functionals with similar properties already present in the literature, it is purely local in time, meaning that it depends only on the present profile of the (approximate) solution (and not on its past or future evolution).

papers.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
papers.abstract: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Our training pipeline begins with two-stage continued pre-training that progressively raises the proportion of e-commerce data within a diverse multimodal data mixture, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training that combines on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning to support both non-thinking and thinking modes. For evaluation, we construct a comprehensive suite of 28 e-commerce benchmarks (23 in-house and five open-source) covering eight business scenarios and complement it with 64 public general-purpose benchmarks. On the e-commerce suite, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B surpasses substantially larger open-source flagship models, including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, HY4, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. On the general-purpose suite, every WeMM-Ecom model surpasses its similarly sized Qwen3.5 counterpart, with the lightweight variants (e.g., WeMM-Ecom-2B) showing clear advantages over leading lightweight models such as Qwen3.5-2B, MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B, and LFM3-VL-2B. Beyond benchmarks, WeMM-Ecom now powers hundreds of production use cases in WeChat, including catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce, serving billion-scale requests per day. We publicly release all model weights and detail our data curation, training recipe, and benchmark construction to facilitate future work on domain-specialized multimodal models. We have released the model weights and code to facilitate future research at https://github.com/Tencent/WeMM-Ecom.

papers.title: Reconstructing the depth of first interaction in extensive air showers from fluorescence detector profiles with a physics-motivated neural network
papers.abstract: We present a physics-motivated neural network that reconstructs, event by event, the depth of the first interaction of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays from longitudinal profiles measured by fluorescence detectors. The network couples a convolutional encoder to a decoder that implements the Gaisser-Hillas function and predicts quantiles of the target, providing a per-event uncertainty estimate. It is trained and evaluated on four million proton- and iron-induced showers between $10^{18}$ and $10^{20}$ eV, simulated with the hadronic interaction models EPOS LHC-R and Sibyll 2.3d and processed by an end-to-end simulation of the fluorescence detector response. Despite detector effects, the reconstruction retains useful information for protons, achieving a mean absolute error of about 21 g$\,$cm$^{-2}$ for primary energies around $10^{19}$ eV, whereas for iron most of the information is lost. The reconstructed distributions preserve the exponential shape of the true ones, so the proton-air interaction length can be recovered from their tail with a model-related systematic uncertainty of approximately 4%. This value is limited mainly by the choice of the hadronic interaction model and is nearly insensitive to iron contamination. These results show that the depth of the first interaction can be reconstructed under realistic detection conditions, offering a complementary route to measurements of the proton-air cross section and mass-composition studies.

papers.title: Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells
papers.abstract: We derive and analyze a phase-field model describing the formation of the active layer of organic solar cells. The process combines phase separation of an electron donor (polymer) and an electron acceptor (non-fullerene acceptor) with evaporation of a solvent. Taking the macroscopic motion of the fluid into account, this results in a coupled system of incompressible Navier--Stokes, degenerate multispecies Cahn--Hilliard, and Allen--Cahn equations with cross-diffusion terms. We give a thermodynamically consistent derivation of the system and prove the existence of global-in-time weak solutions without any size constraints on the data. The solutions dissipate the total energy and require an ad-hoc variational formulation of the definition of the diffusion fluxes, which is made necessary by the degeneracy of the mobility matrix.

papers.title: ActField: Learning Action Effects as Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics
papers.abstract: Learning how actions change visual states is essential for prediction and decision-making in embodied tasks. Existing action-conditioned JEPA world models typically predict future representations at discrete observation intervals, leaving the temporal evolution of action effects implicit. We introduce ActField, a continuous-time JEPA world model that explicitly models latent state evolution through an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time. ActField separates action-independent evolution from action-induced changes, with the latter modulated by the latent context. A reference-conditioned representation and multi-step dynamics loss further support accurate long-horizon prediction. Together, these components provide a structured and temporally continuous formulation for predicting action-conditioned visual dynamics. Experiments across LIBERO, DROID, and BEHAVIOR demonstrate improved visual prediction fidelity and more accurate action-induced motion prediction over existing world models. Further evaluations on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the utility of ActField in improving downstream policy planning through VLM-guided action selection.

papers.title: Active Observation for Robust Visual Servoing in Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robust visual servoing during robotic grasping remains challenging, as approach-phase occlusion frequently disrupts closed-loop control. To address this, we present an active observation framework in which one arm of an existing dual-arm platform carries an RGB-D camera as an active observer while the other executes grasping. The observer repositions to maintain or recover a shared target-gripper view within the feasible shared-view workspace. Occlusion during the final approach is particularly acute: fixed eye-to-hand lacks an active recovery mechanism once the target is hidden, while eye-in-hand can suffer from self-occlusion and sensitivity to hand-eye calibration. The observer first uses an active two-phase viewpoint strategy to align high-precision RGB-D axes with task-relevant error components. If visibility later degrades, an occlusion-triggered exploration module pauses the worker arm and scores candidate viewpoints by observation quality to recover a shared target-gripper view. Because both objects are detected in a single RGB-D image, the resulting Relative Servo Error avoids differencing two independently transformed target and gripper estimates. We evaluate the system on a dual 6-DoF Piper platform using an open-vocabulary detector with text prompts, without task-specific fine-tuning or demonstrations. Across 50 randomized trials per object, the system achieves 94% grasp success versus 76% for a reactive viewpoint baseline and 64% for a fixed camera. On triggered severe-occlusion trials, recovery takes $1.8 \pm 0.6$ s on average.

papers.title: Computational Complexity and Energy Landscapes of Coulomb Crystals
papers.abstract: Simulated annealing is widely used to search for ground states of trapped-ion Coulomb crystals and of charges on a sphere (the Thomson problem). Elementary nonuniform bounds clarify the role of the input encoding. For identical ions in a fixed trap, unary ion count and a binary energy threshold define a decision problem in P/poly; NP-hardness would imply a collapse of the polynomial hierarchy. The same holds on the unit sphere. With unary ion count and logarithmic precision parameter, approximate configuration search on the sphere and in a fixed positive-definite harmonic trap admits a solution function in FP/poly. These advice bounds provide no uniform search algorithm. In simulations of up to 100 ions, the number of distinct minima found and the time to reach the best-known minimum both grow approximately exponentially. When ions are pinned to prescribed candidate sites, choosing which sites to occupy to minimize the Coulomb energy is NP-hard in two and three dimensions; a finite-precision promise version is NP-complete. All ions are identical, the interaction is bare Coulomb repulsion, and the hardness is carried by the site positions alone. We extend a previous inverse-square reduction to the Coulomb interaction by deriving its angular law, including the quartic field term, and sharpening two estimates. The construction is an array of quadrupoles whose common monopole term cancels from energy differences between legal configurations. Its energy landscapes exhibit large barriers between nearly degenerate minima. Barrier trees resolve this structure, and simulated annealing becomes trapped above the ground state in the cube example. At laboratory parameters, with individually tunable well depths, the encoding survives numerically on a half-filled square lattice. For Doppler-cooled strontium ions, this requires stiff wells a few to tens of micrometers apart, as in electrode trap arrays.

papers.title: Quantifying superposition via coherence by stochastic orthogonalization
papers.abstract: Here we present an approach to quantifying superposition of nonorthogonal reference states through quantum coherence. No change of basis achieves this: every orthonormal basis makes some superposition-free states appear coherent. We show that orthogonalization succeeds instead as a measurement mapping every reference state onto a multiple of a basis vector in each outcome; such measurements are exactly the free operations that convert superposition into coherence. The largest average coherence they extract from a state, which we call its degree of superposition, turns every coherence measure into a superposition measure with the same operational meaning. An interference term becomes coherence at most with the probability of unambiguously discriminating its two reference states, a bound attained when there are no others and, for positive coefficients and nonnegative overlaps, exactly when the overlaps are probabilities of a random grouping. Maximal degree means conversion into a maximally coherent state with certainty, possible for up to three reference states but not in general. Each coherence measure gives its own degree; when two degrees order two superpositions oppositely, neither converts into the other with certainty, and we find such pairs already for two reference states, unlike in qubit coherence. For equal positive overlaps, in-phase superpositions are rigid: deterministic conversions that keep all components can only permute their coefficients. As the reference states merge, the degree stays bounded where widely used measures can diverge, and at every amplitude a rotation-symmetric cat state attains its maximum. Our results quantify superposition operationally and reveal conversion constraints created by nonorthogonality.

papers.title: ReproShift: Cross-Version Adaptation of Linux Kernel Fuzzing Crash Reproducers
papers.abstract: Reliable crash reproduction is essential for diagnosing and repairing kernel crashes. Historical crash reproducers preserve concrete bug-triggering knowledge and can be reused for regression testing, bug revalidation, and impact analysis across kernel versions. However, kernel evolution can invalidate these reproducers by changing kernel interfaces, configurations, and execution paths. Migrating them is therefore challenging: the adapted reproducer must identify and modify version-sensitive behavior while preserving the bug-triggering operations and resource dependencies that define the original crash. To address this challenge, we propose ReproShift, an automated framework for cross-version crash reproducer migration by preserving bug-triggering semantics while adapting only version-sensitive behavior. Given source crash artifacts, a source crash reproducer, and a target kernel, ReproShift produces a migrated crash reproducer with same-bug validation evidence. Specifically, ReproShift first constructs a structured source-to-target context to identify migration-relevant kernel changes. It then performs constrained target-aware adaptation to revise version-sensitive reproducer operations while preserving the original trigger logic. Finally, it executes the adapted candidates on the target kernel and uses execution feedback and case-specific crash evidence to iteratively validate candidates and refine subsequent migrations. In a real-world deployment on an evolving upstream kernel, ReproShift further produces 22 upstream crash reports generated from adapted candidates, of which 7 have been fixed and 5 have received explicit maintainer confirmation. To systematically quantify its migration effectiveness, we construct a benchmark of 107 real-world source-target migration cases. ReproShift achieves confirmed same-bug migration in 57 cases, compared with 19 cases using direct replay.

papers.title: Quantum Cyclic XYZ Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: XYZ codes generalize the Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) framework by adding $\sym{Y}$-type stabilizers to the usual $\sym{X}$- and $\sym{Z}$-type ones. We study XYZ codes whose three classical component codes are binary cyclic codes of odd length~$n$. Assigning disjoint sets of irreducible factors of $x^n-1$ to the three Pauli types fixes the number of encoded logical qubits and ensures that the row spaces of the three parity-check matrices intersect pairwise trivially. Then, a coprimality condition between the factors assigned to each type and the reciprocals of those assigned to the others guarantees the required orthogonality. Cyclotomic cosets give a complete and explicit description of the resulting family. We show that, for odd~$n$, a cyclic stabilizer code admits an XYZ representation with cyclic component codes iff its stabilizer generators are invariant, up to a phase, under the qubit permutation $i\mapsto 2i\bmod n$. By fixing the length and the dimension of the code, the proposed cyclic XYZ codes attain the best known minimum distance of stabilizer codes, exceed the minimum distance of the underlying CSS codes, and even exceed the linear-programming upper bounds for general CSS codes.

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization for Inhomogeneous Functions via Locally Adaptive Kernels
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful and general framework for sample-efficient global optimization. Most BO methods rely on stationary Gaussian processes, implicitly assuming that an objective black-box function exhibits homogeneous smoothness across the input space. However, many complex real-world functions have highly inhomogeneous regularity, exhibiting both smooth and rough behavior. This fundamental mismatch between the model and the black-box function severely degrades both sample efficiency and surrogate accuracy of BO. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Inhomogeneous Bayesian optimization framework. We develop a partitioned modeling strategy that dynamically subdivides the search space into subdomains, capturing spatially varying smoothness through locally adaptive kernels. To dynamically adjust the spatial resolution of the surrogate model, this approach utilizes a recursive splitting criterion. Furthermore, we develop a sampling allocation theory, establishing that driving the regional acquisition suprema below a common target level is achieved by polynomially denser sampling in rougher subdomains. Numerical experiments across homogeneous functions, synthetic inhomogeneous functions, and a real-world 8-dimensional LASSO hyperparameter tuning task demonstrate that our approach improves optimization efficiency on synthetic inhomogeneous functions, while performing comparably to Classic BO on homogeneous functions and on the LASSO task. This demonstrates the robustness of the adaptive partitioning mechanism.

papers.title: Principal angles between annihilators of real sedenion zero divisors
papers.abstract: We investigate the relative geometry of annihilators of zero divisors in the real sedenion algebra. Each nonzero zero divisor has a four-dimensional annihilator, whose geometry is associated with an axis in the imaginary octonions. For two prescribed axes separated by an angle $θ$, we establish the exact range of principal angles between their annihilators. The four principal cosines are necessarily $(p,p,q,q)$, where $\cos^2(θ/2)\leq p\leq\cos(θ/2)$ and $0\leq q\leq p$, and every admissible pair is realizable. We further derive an explicit quadratic formula for the principal cosines of any specified pair using two invariants of the associated quaternionic frames. A continuous deformation demonstrates that neither the axis angle nor the underlying quaternion subalgebras together determine the annihilator angles. Finally, we relate these results to the least singular subspaces of sedenion left multiplication through Euclidean projection onto the zero-divisor cone.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity and zero divisors in random graphical groups
papers.abstract: We give a criterion for hyperbolicity of random groups presented by labelled graphs. On $n$ vertices, we prescribe the proportions of the possible sets of outgoing labels. For each generator, we choose a uniform matching between its occurrences and those of its inverse, independently across generators. We condition the graph to have girth at least $\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$ for sufficiently small $c>0$, and take the labels of closed paths as relators. The distribution of outgoing labels determines a matrix of turn weights. Suppose that each letter occurs as often as its inverse and with positive frequency, every vertex has degree at least three, and the entrywise square of the turn matrix has spectral radius less than one. We prove that, with probability tending to one as $n$ grows, the resulting group is torsion-free and non-elementary hyperbolic and admits a finite two-dimensional classifying space. On the same event, every path from a prescribed root to a different vertex has nontrivial label in the group. The proof uses the spectral radius bound to control repeated path labels in diagrams and a local-to-global argument to obtain a linear isoperimetric inequality. Applied to OpenAI's characteristic-two zero-divisor construction, the criterion recovers the hyperbolicity result of Mghirbi and Douglas.

papers.title: A Proposal for Multiplierless RLS Adaptive Filters with Implementation Complexity Constraint
papers.abstract: The so-called sum-of-powers-of-two arithmetic has the advantage of using simple shift and thus avoiding multiplications operations. In this work, we provide a feasible RLS adaptive filter algorithm employing the SOPOT representation. This reduces the computational burden of the RLS algorithm. Therefore, leading to a reduction in the power consumption from a hardware implementation point of view, which is an important feature in the developing of smaller, lighter and more power-efficient portable devices.

papers.title: Coupled Altermagnetic and Valley Physics in Monolayer VBiSe$_3$
papers.abstract: The interplay of compensated magnetism, spin--orbit coupling (SOC), and valley degrees of freedom provides a promising route toward spin--valley control without conventional ferromagnetism. Here, using first-principles calculations combined with Wannier-based analysis, we reveal coupled altermagnetic and valley physics in monolayer VBiSe$_3$. In the absence of SOC, the compensated Néel antiferromagnetic state, whose opposite-spin V sublattices are related only by mirror operations, exhibits momentum-dependent spin splitting with a characteristic $i$-wave altermagnetic texture. Upon inclusion of SOC, the conduction-band states develop anisotropic Rashba-like spin splitting together with a sizable $K/K'$ valley splitting of about $112.2$~meV. Orbital analysis and an effective SOC Hamiltonian identify the hybridization between SOC-active Se-$p_{x,y}$ states and predominantly V-$d_{z^2}$ conduction-band states as an important microscopic origin of the valley splitting. The two valleys carry Berry curvature of the same sign but different magnitude, unlike the opposite-sign pattern of conventional valley Hall systems, so the large valley splitting, rather than a valley Hall effect, offers a possible route to valley-selective carrier occupation by gating. Moreover, a modest $-1\%$ biaxial compressive strain drives the system into a quasi-half-valley-metallic state with valley-polarized electrons and non-valley-polarized holes. These results establish monolayer VBiSe$_3$ as a promising platform for coupled altermagnetic, spin--orbit, and valley phenomena with strain-tunable electronic states.

papers.title: MTL-MHOL: Predicting Online Conversions under Delayed Feedback and Data Sparsity
papers.abstract: This paper proposes the model-agnostic Multi-Task Learning Multi-Head Online Learning (MTL-MHOL) framework for conversion rate (CVR) prediction. Existing approaches typically address key challenges in CVR prediction, such as delayed feedback and data sparsity, in isolation or lack flexibility and practical applicability. MTL-MHOL adopts a time bucketing approach to account for delayed feedback and combines it with multi-task learning of an auxiliary task to mitigate data sparsity. We evaluate the framework on proprietary datasets from a private company and on a public dataset from Criteo. MTL-MHOL matches or outperforms all benchmark models in terms of Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) and Relative Cross Entropy (RCE), and it correctly captures temporal trends in the data using an MLP backbone, while maintaining strong performance with a DeepFM backbone. In particular, MTL-MHOL matches the performance of the advanced delayed-feedback method FSIW, outperforms the entire-space approach ESMM by 21.5% in RCE, and achieves up to 81% lift in RCE compared to the best-performing classical benchmark.

papers.title: Accuracy, Convergence and Consistency of Dark Matter Evolution with the PhotoNs-3 Code
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the accuracy and convergence of PhotoNs-3, a cosmological N-body code employed for the HyperMillennium simulation. In particular, we examine its convergence with respect to parameters that affect the accuracy of the force calculation and the time evolution, such as the softening length and the adaptive time-stepping scheme, and find that it converges very well. Furthermore, using GADGET as the benchmark, we design four sets of simulations to compare the mutual consistency. We compare the power spectrum of the density field, halo density profiles, and the halo and subhalo mass functions. The difference between PhotoNs-3 and the Gadget codes is at the same level as that between Gadget-3 and Gadget-4. Meanwhile, PhotoNs-3 generally achieves a significant computational speedup. This work establishes that the accuracy and reliability of PhotoNs-3 and its simulations are sufficient for Stage IV galaxy surveys.

papers.title: Part-wise Certified State Estimation of Articulated Objects from Passive Stereo
papers.abstract: Robots in manufacturing often handle thin, hinged objects known from CAD models that change shape during the task, like folding cartons. Monitoring such tasks requires estimating the object's articulation state, its pose and the shape of any semi-deformable part. Learning-based estimators generalise across objects but lose precision while handling thin parts. Model-based fitting is precise but often needs accurate depth, a close initial estimate and a clean object mask. We present part-wise certification of an articulated object's state, estimated from passive stereo. Our estimator rivals the precision of the best model-based fitting method without using depth, a close initial estimate or a mask. We detect the corners that the CAD model defines in both stereo images and fit the articulated model to them. Geometric certificates, which we extend from rigid to articulated objects, then tell whether to trust each part, because the fit returns a state even for hidden parts. Certified estimates on unlabelled video become labels that improve sim-to-real transfer. On five of seven simulated objects, we locate the parts we certify three to five times more precisely than the strongest learned baseline on the same readings, given depth and true masks. On a real folding carton, our median corner error on the end panels is 2.1% of the carton's size, at least 40% lower than every learned baseline and also lower than a depth-based fit initialised near the true state.

papers.title: Floquet dark-mode manipulation in a three-mode optomechanical system
papers.abstract: We propose a Floquet sideband method to manipulate the dark-mode effect in a three-mode optomechanical system consisting of a single cavity mode coupled to two mechanical modes. We introduce a periodic frequency modulation for one mechanical mode to generate the Floquet sidebands, one of which is selected to match the resonance frequency of the other mechanical mode, allowing complete destructive interference to produce a mechanical dark mode decoupled from the cavity mode. The semiclassical operating point is determined self-consistently within the framework for linearization of optomechanical interaction, and the linear stability is examined under the rotating-wave approximation. We evaluate the validity of the approximate Hamiltonian by examining the fidelity between the states governed by the approximate and exact Hamiltonians. We further demonstrate dark-mode control by inspecting the bright/dark-mode populations of the system, when a frequency detuning is introduced suddenly. These results may provide a basis for further study of quantum-state storage using the Floquet mechanical dark modes.

papers.title: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman
papers.abstract: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the André-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.

papers.title: Stars on the ascending helium giant branch: II. A metal-rich luminous helium sdO gone astray
papers.abstract: Hot subdwarf stars with masses above $\sim0.7~M_\odot$ expand after core helium exhaustion and ascend the helium giant branch before entering the white dwarf (WD) cooling track. In the first paper of this series, we identified the luminous helium-rich hot subdwarf HE~1518-0948 (HE~1518) as the product of a massive He-WD+He-WD merger in this evolutionary phase. Here we present a detailed analysis of a second luminous helium-rich O-type hot subdwarf (He-sdO), Gaia~DR3~5369742867090186624 (G5369). We derive an effective temperature of $55~000\pm2500$~K, a surface gravity of $\log g = 4.85\pm0.15$, and an upper limit on the hydrogen abundance of $\log (n_\mathrm{He}/n_\mathrm{H})>2.5$. The close similarity of its atmospheric parameters and its helium and carbon abundances to those of HE~1518 indicates that G5369 is also likely the product of a massive He-WD+He-WD merger. In contrast to HE~1518, G5369 is metal-rich, with an iron abundance of about twice solar. The metallicity-adjusted abundance pattern of G5369 for the elements C, N, O, and Ne is broadly consistent with the nucleosynthesis predictions of a composite He-WD merger model and is similar to the observed abundances of R~CrB stars, extreme helium stars, and the O(He) star KPD~0005+5106. The kinematics of G5369 place it near the boundary between the thick disk and halo. Its orbit, with a pericentre of $\sim$3.5 kpc, together with its high metallicity suggests that G5369 most likely originated in the inner Galaxy.

papers.title: Beyond Naming Accuracy: Template Composition and Species-Name Decisions
papers.abstract: Vision-language classifiers identify species by matching images to text prompts containing species names. BioCLIP2 changes its predicted species less often than BioCLIP 2.5 Huge across four photographic templates, but the ranking reverses across a bank of 80 templates. This comparison leaves open whether the reversal depends on the number of templates or their wording. We hold the count at four and compare the classifiers on every four-template subset of the 80-template bank and of a second pool of 24 reviewed photographic templates, keeping images and candidate names fixed. Huge is more consistent across the reviewed pool as a whole, yet 19.09% of its four-template subsets favor Bio-CLIP2 on iWildCam and 5.10% do so on Rare Species. We then test whether both rankings hold on 5,487 frames from previously unused iWildCam sequences. Among 4,356 subsets containing two photo and two photograph templates, simultaneous 95% intervals support lower disagreement for Huge in 1,526 subsets and for BioCLIP2 in 43. Even with the same prompt count and noun mixture, the choice of sentences can determine which classifier appears more consistent.

papers.title: Motion on Demand: Adaptive Optical Excitation for Event Cameras
papers.abstract: Event cameras respond only to brightness changes, so whether an edge is visible depends on image motion perpendicular to it---a motion that constantly shifts with camera and scene dynamics. Rotating a wedge prism in front of the lens introduces controlled image motion to reveal static or slow edges. However, a fixed rotation speed cannot adapt to changing motion conditions: when natural motion is already sufficient, additional optical excitation generates redundant events and introduces unnecessary alignment errors. Inspired by the division of labor between fast haltere feedforward and slower visual feedback in fly gaze control, we present EvGaze, an event camera system that adaptively regulates prism rotation speed. EvGaze employs a learned multimodal controller that integrates luminance, event, and inertial observations, with a fast inertial pathway that refines speed decisions between visual updates. To preserve geometric consistency during speed changes, we compensate for prism-induced image motion at individual event timestamps using measured encoder angles. On EvMotion, EvGaze recovers more edges than full-speed prism rotation with 39% fewer events. On DSEC with simulated optical modulation, it reaches 0.73 feature-tracking success (compared with 0.55 on native events and 0.67 at 180 RPM) while generating 26% fewer events than 360 RPM. Real-device experiments further demonstrate online closed-loop adaptation, reducing average event rates by 17% relative to full-speed rotation.

papers.title: Optimal Window Design for Intercarrier and Intersymbol Interference Power Minimization in w-OFDM
papers.abstract: Block transceivers are essential for modern communication systems, and they are vastly implemented in many day-to-day devices, especially the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) technique. The application of a pulseshaping technique in the OFDM generates the so-called windowed OFDM (w-OFDM). This letter proposes an optimization of the window shape, obtaining minimal intercarrier and intersymbol interference power, ICI, and ISI, respectively. A communication system is simulated by implementing the optimized w-OFDM, and its performance is compared with a non-optimized system using a raised-cosine window.

papers.title: Uncovering the Tells: Efficient Black-Box Audits for LLM Data Contamination
papers.abstract: Existing methods for assessing training data contamination in Large Language Models achieve high accuracy, but fundamentally rely on gray-box access, rendering them inapplicable to fully black-box environments. This limitation forces auditors to rely on full-sequence sampling or rigid heuristics, both of which incur prohibitive inference costs and struggle to isolate the underlying memorization signal. To overcome this, we propose a generation-based black-box framework that infers context-induced information gain from targeted token discrepancies. We introduce a budget-constrained auditing regime, building on the empirical observation that the membership signal is highly sparse and concentrated in a few highly informative tokens. We formalize this sparsity, showing why uniform sampling needs many more samples than a policy that targets informative positions. Empirically, our approach achieves state-of-the-art black-box separation accuracy while needing about 3x fewer queries than uniform position sampling. Finally, we apply this methodology to closed frontier models, exploring its capacity and limits in surfacing potential training data overlaps on commercial APIs.

papers.title: Towards a Global CE$ν$NS Picture
papers.abstract: We present a general framework for extracting and interpreting the Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering (CE$ν$NS) differential cross-section from experimental data. A generalized parametric basis, constructed from common kinematic terms recurring in generalized neutrino interaction models, is employed to numerically constrain the shape and normalization of the observed CE$ν$NS response. The framework was applied to the COHERENT CsI and liquid argon datasets using Bayesian inference, yielding normalization constraints comparable to those reported by the Collaboration while providing additional constraints on the correlated spectral shape. A combined analysis was also performed, exploiting the complementary sensitivities of the two datasets to constrain features of the differential cross-section that are less accessible to either dataset individually. The framework has been implemented in the open-source Julia package Newtrinos.jl, which supports modular forward modeling, parallel computation, and automatic differentiation.

papers.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
papers.abstract: Robot policies must adapt to the speed of moving objects, yet existing benchmarks rarely measure this ability across diverse tasks and speeds. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). Objects are transported through physical contact with a visibly moving belt. Each task has a static counterpart, and each evaluation episode uses the same randomized scene at all 13 speeds. We fine-tune eight vision-language-action and world-action models on demonstrations spanning the full speed range, comparing observations from the current frame alone with those including two past frames. For six models, the success rate peaks at intermediate speeds, and their failures indicate that they tend to produce actions suited to the average demonstration speed rather than to the actual one. Past frames raise the success rate by 10-40 percentage points for three models, and linear probes show that the belt speed is also most linearly decodable from these three. Adding ground-truth speed input to four of the models improves all of them, and a speed estimated from the images keeps most of this gain. These results show that SWEEP-Bench exposes speed-dependent failures and suggest that past frames help only policies from which the speed is most decodable, such as those pretrained on multiple frames. Project page: https://damin3927.github.io/SWEEP-Bench

papers.title: ABI: Actor-Free Behavior-Induced Representations for Zero-Shot Test-Time Guidance
papers.abstract: Behavior-cloning policies show strong ability in sequential control by generating coherent multi-step action chunks, yet their purely imitative objective limits zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks. While offline reinforcement learning offers principled policy improvement, existing methods either require task-specific reward supervision or remain tied to a specific actor during critic training or policy deployment, inflating training cost and restricting cross-policy generalization. We observe that evaluating actions under the data-collecting behavior largely preserves their relative value ordering across target policies, offering a way around actor coupling. Combining this property with reward-free successor prediction, we propose Actor-Free Behavior-Induced Representations (ABI) to learn multi-horizon action-chunk representations from unlabeled trajectories without reward supervision or actor training. At test time, pairing the frozen representation with lightweight task readouts forms a chunk critic that guides target policies without parameter updates and transfers directly across distinct unseen policies. Our analysis establishes when the value ordering is preserved across policies and when selecting among proposed chunks improves closed-loop return. Across 65 locomotion, navigation, and manipulation tasks, ABI's chunk critic guides weak imitation policies to match or surpass zero-shot RL baselines with high sample efficiency, outperforms existing zero-shot critics on identical proposals, and improves externally trained RL actors without retraining. From raw pixels, ABI delivers substantial guidance gains and surpasses prior zero-shot RL baselines on visual manipulation, highlighting its potential for visuomotor control.

papers.title: Robust Mixture Regressions and EM Algorithms via the Log-Truncated Likelihood
papers.abstract: Finite mixture regression is sensitive to gross residual outliers when component errors are modeled by Gaussian likelihoods. We propose a log-truncated likelihood for mixture regression. The likelihood is obtained by integrating a logarithmically growing Catoni-type score and exponentiating the negative integrated score, producing a proper location-scale density with a reusable normalizing constant and EM-compatible responsibilities. Although the induced density itself is lighter than exponential and has all moments, its likelihood score grows only logarithmically; this distinction yields a smooth residual-robust estimator that can be stably fitted when the data are generated from Laplace, Pareto, or even infinite-variance heavy-tailed error mechanisms. We derive deterministic tail envelopes, the location-scale decomposition of the normalizing constant, a rejection sampler, a lower-bounded mixing-weight update, a unique componentwise scale update, and a constrained generalized EM algorithm. The theory gives monotonicity of the observed likelihood and a local population-to-sample perturbation guarantee under standard compactness, contraction, and numerical-accuracy conditions. Simulations and applications to insurance claim severity and crypto return innovations show that the method is a competitive smooth likelihood-based alternative to Gaussian and pseudo-robust EM procedures, especially in residual-outlier regimes, while also clarifying its limitations under high leverage and extremely adversarial contamination.

papers.title: Structure Preservation of $2$-Wasserstein Barycenters on the Real Line with Applications to Log-Concave Distributions
papers.abstract: We study to what extent the $p$-Wasserstein barycenter ($p$-WB) of arbitrary, not only finite, collections of distributions preserves their structure, focusing on shape constraints on the densities, such as monotonicity, unimodality, or log-concavity. This preservation is a generalized convexity property in Wasserstein space, which we call $p$-WB convexity. We investigate $p$-WB convexity of the families of $ϕ$-unimodal distributions: an absolutely continuous distribution $μ$ is $ϕ$-unimodal if composition with $ϕ$ turns a density into a concave function on the interior of the convex support of $μ$. This notion generalizes log-concavity and $s$-concave densities. We find a quantile representation of $ϕ$-unimodality and then use a novel closed-form expression of the quantile density function of the $2$-WB to decide on $2$-WB convexity. In higher dimensions or for $p\neq2$, we give counterexamples ruling out the $p$-WB convexity of $ϕ$-unimodal distributions. On $\mathbb{R}$ and for $p=2$, we characterize which $ϕ$ generate $2$-WB convex families. The family of log-concave distributions is $2$-WB convex, as is the family of distributions with $s$-concave densities if and only if $s\geq-2$. General unimodality, corresponding to $s=-\infty$, is not preserved.

papers.title: GeoMerge-OPD: Balanced Skill Integration in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models excel at individual robotic skills, yet integrating heterogeneous skills into a single policy remains a key challenge for general-purpose robotic control, especially in whole-body tasks with differing manipulation and locomotion requirements. Common multi-skill integration strategies, such as joint fine-tuning and parameter merging, can induce unintended actions during closed-loop execution, severely degrading individual skills. Task-conditioned analysis of expert updates reveals response energy concentrated in a few dominant directions and opposing expert responses along high-energy directions within a shared, task-relevant response subspace. This structure co-occurs with unintended action shifts after merging. We propose GeoMerge-OPD, combining response-space regularization, parameter merging, and on-policy distillation. During independent expert fine-tuning, G-isometry constrains update-response gains within task-activation subspaces; the expert parameters are then statically merged into a student with preliminary multitask capabilities. Fine-tuned task experts serve as teachers, providing velocity-field supervision at the environment observations and intermediate action-flow states visited by the student to calibrate residual behavioral deviations. Experiments with two VLA backbones show strong, balanced humanoid skill integration on SIMPLE and consistent performance on LIBERO and LIBERO-PRO, outperforming joint fine-tuning and multitask reinforcement-learning baselines while maintaining robustness under perturbations.

papers.title: Verifiable Logical-Physical Contracts for Refactored On-Die Power Control Circuitry
papers.abstract: Recent literature allows independent hardware experiments to occupy a single die for scalable and cost-efficient silicon prototyping. Within this framework, specialized hardware functions including low-power control mechanisms can be offered as reusable on-die microservices. However, this requires well-defined contracts connecting digital requests to physical behavior. We present a checkable logical-physical contract formulation including a physical contract model describing service completion between client and provider through formally verified digital guarantees and physically validated completion conditions. We introduce Lightswitch, a proof-of-concept on-die power control microservice. We assess post-layout designs in TSMC 28nm and demonstrate how checkable contracts provide formal guarantees.

papers.title: Logarithmic stability from finite-time boundary measurements in an infinite slab
papers.abstract: We prove logarithmic stability for an inverse convection--diffusion problem in an infinite slab from finite-time partial boundary measurements. The data consist of boundary fluxes generated by a fixed temporal profile and varying spatial Dirichlet inputs. For coefficients with fixed interior support and uniform Sobolev bounds, the data determine the exterior derivative of the drift and a gauge-invariant reaction term with a logarithmic modulus. Prescribing the divergence gives separate stability for the drift and reaction coefficients. The input and observation patches may be arbitrary nonempty open subsets of the same or opposite faces. The proof combines a quantitative passage from finite-time responses to a stationary boundary map with a Runge approximation estimate in the measured $H^{3/2}$ input norm. The first step uses sectorial semigroups on the unbounded slab; the second transfers the partial data to a full boundary map on an interior domain, where magnetic stability estimates apply. We also prove conditional stability for boundary-touching supports and uniqueness from one encoded input with unknown initial state. A tracer-transport application identifies an incompressible velocity and a reaction-loss coefficient.

papers.title: Faster, Smaller, and Better-Looking: Fast-GSVC for 2D Gaussian Video Coding
papers.abstract: 2D Gaussians have emerged as a promising explicit representation for videos. However, fitting Gaussians to a video sequence requires substantial computation, resulting in long encoding times. In this work, we present Fast-GSVC, a 2D Gaussian video codec that accelerates encoding while improving rate-distortion performance. We identify the key bottlenecks in 2DGS training and accelerate optimization through improved initialization, smoother yet more aggressive parameter updates, coarse-to-fine progressive Gaussian optimization, and optical-flow guidance for both Gaussian initialization and temporal propagation. We also discovered that the quantization fine-tuning process of the existing codec does not fully exploit temporal coherence between frames, leading to suboptimal compression. To address this, we preserve spatiotemporal correlations to maintain concentrated residuals and introduce temporal-aware quantization for further improved rate-distortion performance. In our experiments on the UVG dataset, Fast-GSVC reduces encoding time by up to 92.5%, corresponding to a 13.4X speedup over GSVC. At comparable PSNR, it reduces file size by up to 58%; at comparable bit-per-pixel, it improves PSNR by up to 2.5 dB. Project page: https://longanwang-cs.github.io/fastgsvc/.

papers.title: Quantum Variance of Holomorphic Modular Forms and Benjamini-Schramm Convergence
papers.abstract: We study quantum variance for holomorphic modular forms of fixed weight on sequences of compact hyperbolic surfaces converging to the hyperbolic plane in the sense of Benjamini-Schramm. We first show that quantum ergodicity need not hold for an arbitrary choice of orthonormal basis, even for sequences with a uniform lower bound on the injectivity radius and a uniform spectral gap.
