papers.abstract: We compare the class $\mathscr R(Ω)$ of restrictions of full-support planar doubling measures with the class $\mathcal D(Ω)$ of internal doubling measures on a piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domain. These classes coincide in the absence of zero-interior-angle cusps. At any such cusp, $\mathscr R(Ω)\setminus\mathcal D(Ω)$ is nonempty. For power-comparable widths, $\mathcal D(Ω)\subsetneq\mathscr R(Ω)$; for infinitely flat widths the two classes are disjoint. Under smooth endpoint regularity, finite versus infinite contact order gives these two alternatives. Under only $C^1$ regularity, finite logarithmic order does not determine whether the classes intersect, and examples with nonempty intersection and neither class containing the other also occur. For an individual internal measure, membership in $\mathscr R(Ω)$ is characterized by a potential inequality for its axial projection. We prove this criterion by a positive-kernel construction and Whitney mass replacement, and also obtain sufficient conditions for variable-power widths and an independent finite-system criterion.

papers.title: The Science Chapter of the Einstein Telescope Geometry Comparison Report
papers.abstract: This is the Scientific Added Value Chapter of the Einstein Telescope (ET) Geometry Comparison Report, commissioned from the ET Organization by the ET Board of Governmental Representatives. We compare three configurations: a single-site 10-km triangle ($Δ$) and two 15-km L-shaped detectors (2L) at widely separated sites, either nearly aligned or misaligned. We use metrics representative of the ET science case: compact-binary populations, dense matter, cosmography, stochastic backgrounds, multimessenger astronomy, fundamental physics, and continuous and burst sources. All three configurations deliver the ET science case, but they excel in different areas. For most sensitivity-driven science, the 2L configurations outperform the $Δ$. The misaligned 2L is best for localizing and characterizing individual sources, multimessenger astronomy, and bright-siren cosmology. The nearly aligned 2L is best for stochastic backgrounds. The $Δ$ localizes sources better than the aligned 2L and performs comparably to both 2L configurations for continuous and burst sources and at kilohertz frequencies. A 2L orientation of $30^\circ$ is a good compromise between stochastic-background sensitivity and localization. We validate Fisher information matrix (FIM) forecasts against Bayesian inference for $\sim550$ binary black hole and neutron star-black hole signals. Despite substantial differences, the FIM shows no systematic preference for either configuration for intrinsic parameters. For distance and sky localization, the FIM cannot capture multimodality and long-range correlations, leading to larger discrepancies, which however do not affect the ranking. Adding Cosmic Explorer to the network improves the reach of all three ET configurations, especially in volume localization and characterization of high-redshift sources. Differences between geometries shrink, but the ranking is largely unchanged.

papers.title: Finite simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes
papers.abstract: A theorem by Guralnick classifying finite simple groups with subgroups of prime power index implies that $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ is the unique finite non-abelian simple group whose maximal subgroups all have prime power index. Motivated by this result and appealing to Li and Li's classification of primitive permutation groups of degree $p^a q^b$, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes, we classify all finite non-abelian simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes, proving that they are precisely $A_5$, $A_6$, $A_7$, $A_8$, ${\rm PSL}(2,7)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,8)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,11)$, ${\rm PSp}(4,3)$, ${\rm PSU}(3,3)$, and ${\rm PSU}(3,4)$.

papers.title: Reliable Recursive Memory for Causal Multi-scale Video Polyp Segmentation
papers.abstract: Video polyp segmentation (VPS) is essential for computer-aided colonoscopy, as it localizes and tracks polyps frame by frame. However, VPS remains challenging because polyps resemble the mucosa and change quickly in scale, which calls for history beyond a short clip, and because blur, specular highlights, and occlusion often degrade only part of a frame. Existing methods keep history as whole frames, so their cost grows with the history length, and a partly degraded frame carries its degraded content to later predictions. To address these issues, we propose STREAM, a streaming framework for VPS that extends the causal multi-scale aggregation (CMA) of our conference work from a fixed clip to an online stream. STREAM introduces a Recursive Slot Memory (RSM) that summarizes multi-scale features and soft foreground and background cues into a constant number of slots, which the current features read and pass to CMA, supplying long-range history at a constant cost. Furthermore, we design Reliability-Aware Slot Writing (RASW), which estimates a pixel-level quality map from the current frame, supervised by its local error, and uses it to control which locations are written into RSM and how much each slot is updated. Experiments on SUN-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB demonstrate that STREAM achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving the Dice of the conference model from 81.3% to 85.7% on the hardest subset while running at 48 FPS with a constant state of 0.32 MB. Code will be released at https://github.com/wangtong627/STREAM.

papers.title: Dirichlet walls beyond JT gravity and their quantum group interpretation
papers.abstract: We canonically quantize sinh dilaton gravity with finite Dirichlet boundary conditions. The reduced phase space is formulated in terms of the length of a two-sided spacelike geodesic in an effective AdS$_2$ geometry and its conjugate momentum. Canonical quantization leads to a finite-difference Schrödinger equation whose wavefunctions of the universe are given by $q$-hypergeometric functions. These furnish a quantum deformation of the hypergeometric wavefunctions of JT gravity. We further show that the finite cutoff Hamiltonian derived from the bulk analysis admits a natural interpretation as the reduced Casimir of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R}))$ acting on hyperbolic matrix elements. The two scattering wave solutions are hyperbolic matrix elements of the modular double $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R))\otimes U_{\tilde q}(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R))$, and the wavefunction of the universe is their unique combination regular at vanishing length.

papers.title: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$. Assuming the Virasoro conjecture for $D$, we prove that the relative constraints are equivalent to the absolute constraints for $X$. Under the same assumption, we establish compatibility with the degeneration formula for two-component projective semistable degenerations satisfying a completeness condition. Consequently, the Virasoro conjecture for the two components and the gluing divisor implies the conjecture for the general fiber. As an application, we prove the Virasoro conjecture for Enriques surfaces in every integral curve class.

papers.title: Asymmetrical transport distribution function: skewness as a key to enhance thermoelectric performance
papers.abstract: How to achieve high thermoelectric figure of merit is still a scientific challenge. By solving the Boltzmann transport equation, thermoelectric properties can be written as integrals of a single function, the transport distribution function (TDF). In this work, the shape effects of transport distribution function in various typical functional forms on thermoelectric properties of materials are systematically investigated. It is found that the asymmetry of TDF, characterized by skewness, can be used to describe universally the trend of thermoelectric properties. By defining symmetric and asymmetric TDF functions, a novel skewness is then constructed for thermoelectric applications. It is demonstrated, by comparison with ab initio calculations and experiments, that the proposed thermoelectric skewness not only perfectly captures the main feature of conventional skewness, but also is able to predict the thermoelectric power accurately. This comparison confirms the unique feature of our proposed thermoelectric skewness, as well as its special role of connection between the statistics of TDF and thermoelectric properties of materials. It is also found that the thermoelectric performance can be enhanced by increasing the asymmetry of TDF. Finally, it is also interesting to find that the thermoelectric transport properties based on typical quantum statistics (Fermi-Dirac distributions), can be well described by typical shape parameter (skewness) for classical statistics.

papers.title: Seeing Is Locating: Spatial Awareness and Geographic Bias in Decision Language Models
papers.abstract: Decision models, which output probability distributions over candidate labels instead of generating text, are increasingly used as classifiers and evaluators for inputs associated with real-world locations. However, it remains unclear whether they can leverage spatial context and whether their predictions are geographically biased. We introduce GeoDecisions, a multimodal benchmark for evaluating the spatial awareness and geographic bias of decision models. GeoDecisions comprises two tasks: (1) geo-aware image classification, and (2) location rating on objective and subjective topics. Evaluating six decision models against supervised task-specific models, we find that spatial awareness requires vision: textual coordinates alone provide insufficient context for classifying everyday photos and satellite images. We also find substantial geographic bias. On everyday photos, despite achieving higher accuracy, open-weight decision models exhibit more spatially clustered errors than supervised models. Moreover, across all five subjective topics, every decision model gives lower ratings to locations with lower socioeconomic conditions. Finally, we propose a training-free method that combines decision models with a location prior to improve their spatial awareness without substantially increasing performance bias. Our code is available at https://github.com/cruiseresearchgroup/GeoDecisions.

papers.title: Proper and Optimal Scoring Rules for Risk-Averse Agents
papers.abstract: Scoring rules are used to elicit probabilistic beliefs through payments that depend on reports and realised outcomes. We ask how these rules should be designed to induce truthful reporting and incentivise costly information acquisition when the agent is risk averse. For agents with entropic risk preferences in finite state spaces, we characterise proper scoring rules through an exponential transformation, derive optimal structures for information acquisition under bounded payments, and obtain explicit optimal coefficients in the binary case. The risk-neutral limit preserves properness and, in the binary case, optimality, while recovering the optimal betting structure for nonbinary states. For optimal design in the binary model, it suffices to focus on rules whose associated concave function is affine on each side of the prior. The optimal coefficients depend only on the prior and the risk-aversion parameter. The binary optimal rules we construct also admit an exact transformation from a particular risk-neutral optimal rule. In the nonbinary model, optimal design reduces to choosing the best prior bound in a transformed betting mechanism.

papers.title: Connected descent and Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles
papers.abstract: We answer a question by Hui Zhang and show that, for any smooth, quasi-projective, geometrically integral variety X over a number field k, the connected descent set for 0-cycles is equal to the Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. In particular, the connected descent and the abelianised connected descent sets for 0-cycles coincide. In the same spirit, we also show that the descent set under all tori for 0-cycles is equal to the algebraic Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. Finally, we give a new formulation of Conjecture (E) using the connected descent sets.

papers.title: A sharp threshold in the Li--Lin open problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study positive solutions to the problem \begin{equation*} -Δu = |x|^{-s_2}u^{2^*(s_2)-1} - \la |x|^{-s_1}u^{p-1} \quad \text{in }\Om, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partial\Om, \end{equation*} where $\Om\subset\R^N$ ($N\ge 3$) is a bounded domain with $0\in\partial\Om$, $0\le s_1<s_2<2$, $2^*(s)=\frac{2(N-s)}{N-2}$, $2^*(s_2)<p<2^*(s_1)$, and $\la>0$. This is the Li--Lin open problem \cite{LL} in the form studied by Cerami, Zhong, and Zou \cite{CZZ} and by Tang and Tang \cite{TT1}. Assume that $\partial\Om$ is $C^{1,α}$ near $0$ with a leading term of homogeneity $1+α$, and set $θ=\frac{(N-2)(2^*(s_1)-p)}{2}$. We prove that a solution exists for every $\la>0$ if $θ>α$ and the $α$-mean curvature of $\partial\Om$ at $0$ is negative, whereas $\la^*=\sup\{\la>0:\text{a solution exists}\}$ is finite if $θ\leα$, without any curvature assumption. For $α=1$, this removes the restriction to almost every $\la$ in \cite[Theorem 1.6]{CZZ}, answers a question of Zou \cite{Z}, and disproves the conjecture in \cite[Remark 1.7]{TT1}. The proofs rely on a scale-invariant estimate uniform in $\la$, a Hadamard-type identity for the half-space extremal and a localized Pohozaev identity combined with sharp decay estimates. Notably, no regularity of $\partial\Om$ is required away from $0$.

papers.title: Geometric distinguishability of two-source gravitational-wave signals from the extrinsic geometry of the single-source waveform manifold
papers.abstract: Overlapping gravitational-wave signals can produce strong degeneracies in which a multi-source waveform is accurately represented by a single effective source. We formulate this source-confusion problem geometrically by treating the family of single-source waveforms as an embedded manifold in the noise-weighted detector Hilbert space. We introduce the distance-to-manifold statistic, defined as the minimum residual obtained by fitting a waveform with the single-source model, and show that its squared value is directly related to the maximized likelihood difference between two-source and single-source hypotheses in the noiseless limit. For two sources with nearby parameters, perturbative minimization demonstrates that the effective single-source fit absorbs all leading tangent-space deformations. The first irreducible residual lies in the normal space of the waveform manifold and is governed by its second fundamental form. We validate our approach using a six-parameter frequency-domain inspiral model with a LISA-like time-delay-interferometry response. Direct optimization reproduces the predicted quartic scaling over the numerically resolved regime, while two-dimensional confusion-zone maps reveal strongly anisotropic distinguishability boundaries. These results establish extrinsic waveform-manifold curvature as a coordinate-independent diagnostic of local multi-source confusion and provide a practical framework for identifying parameter-space directions in which overlapping gravitational-wave sources are most difficult to resolve.

papers.title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents
papers.abstract: Persistent tutoring agents do more than answer questions: they manage course files, practice records, and learner profiles that govern future lessons. In such stateful settings, knowing what to teach does not guarantee knowing what to change. We identify a pervasive failure mode, content-state decoupling, where agents deliver pedagogically sound responses while silently corrupting workspace state through unwarranted updates, missed prerequisites, or unintended side effects. Text-level judges overlook these state errors, whereas isolated tool-call checks break down because whether a write action is valid depends jointly on the learner request, prior state, and execution order. We propose State-Verified Reinforcement Learning, which supervises online policy optimization directly through verifiable workspace transitions. Within isolated sandboxes that snapshot state around every tool call, a deterministic verifier audits tool effects, workflow ordering, and native auto-sync side effects, pairing graded partial credit with a hard gate that zeroes episode reward upon any critical violation. Whenever no critical violation occurs, an evidence-grounded judge scores actual saved artifacts rather than agent claims. We pair 1,000 verifiable training instances with an independently authored, human-reviewed evaluation benchmark of 60 tasks spanning 11 educational categories and 16 native tools. After online GRPO training, Qwen3.8-27B raises category-weighted strict success on our benchmark from 51.47% to 80.74% (+29.27 points), cutting content-pass-only execution failures from 45.6% to 13.7% and required state-check failures from 63 to 1 across 180 trials. The resulting policy outperforms seven reference baselines by over 20 points while reducing output tokens by 17-39% across seven of eight external benchmarks without regressing on general reasoning or tool use.

papers.title: JONES-19: A Cultural Image Dataset Based on The Grammar of Ornament
papers.abstract: We introduce JONES-19, a high-quality image dataset documenting 1,901 ornament designs belonging to nineteen human cultures. The images and their annotations are based on an open access archive of The Grammar of Ornament (London, 1856), by Owen Jones. The dataset poses numerous challenges as a benchmark for computer vision classification tasks and for research at the intersection of machine learning and art and design: a small sample size, image samples of human-designed artifacts rather than common objects in-context or natural scenes, imbalanced class distribution, and image distinctions based on fine details involving line patterns, reliefs, and colors. As a design-inspired dataset, JONES-19 can serve as a benchmark for various research fields, such as visual recognition, data-efficient learning, art-historical research, architectural style analysis, and cultural heritage. This paper describes the curation of the JONES-19 dataset and reports a baseline classification benchmark that evaluates the suitability of the dataset for training classifiers and exposes insights into inter-class relationships--particularly cultural similarities--by examining patterns in misclassification errors. The dataset and its accompanying documentation are available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/harvardseas-cultural-ornaments/JONES-19.

papers.title: RAPID: Codec-Aware Video Decoding for Efficient Long-Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Recent vision-language models (VLMs) can process hour-long videos, but the large number of input frames incurs substantial inference overhead. Existing approaches to efficient long-video understanding largely overlook video decoding, which can take longer than LLM prefill. We propose RAPID (Reference- and Access-Point-Informed Decoding), a codec-aware framework that exploits information embedded in compressed bitstreams to reduce both frame decoding and selection costs. RAPID consists of two components. RAPID-Dec exploits reference-frame information and random access points to skip unnecessary frames and decode the retained frames in parallel while preserving exact reconstruction of the target frames. It achieves up to a 3.7x decoding speedup over the fastest baseline on H.264/AVC videos. RAPID-Sel uses keyframes as coarse representatives of video segments, avoiding the dense candidate decoding and scoring required by existing frame selection methods. It achieves comparable accuracy with up to a 3.0x preprocessing speedup. Together, RAPID achieves a 4.9x time to first token (TTFT) speedup on hour-long videos over a state-of-the-art frame selection method using the fastest baseline decoder.

papers.title: Splitting Belief Bases Conditionally based on Constraints for c-Representations and their Solutions
papers.abstract: Splitting notions for conditional belief bases aim at localizing reasoning and computation tasks to subbases containing only the relevant parts of the belief base. Among the different reasoning mechanisms, c-representations, a special kind of Spohn's ranking models, have been shown to provide high-quality inferences. c-Representations can be conveniently specified via a constraint satisfaction problem. In this article, we introduce the notion of conditional constraint splittings, extending constraint splittings by also allowing the subbases to share conditionals. Taking inspiration from conditional syntax splittings, we identify the subclasses of safe and fully localized conditional constraint splittings, allowing us to locally and independently solve the constraint system on the subbases. We also generalize solution splittings for c-representations to safe conditional c-solution splittings and provide an in-depth analysis of their relationship to conditional constraint splittings. Additionally, we elaborate on the relationship of these new splitting notions to safe and generalized safe conditional syntax splittings and also to safe covers, which have been proposed for localized computation of c-representations.

papers.title: Near-Far Attention: Region-Aware Sparse Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Decoding
papers.abstract: Sparse attention reduces the cost of long-context decoding, but token selection introduces additional scoring and ranking overhead. Moreover, uniform page scoring overlooks differences in relevance between near and far context. We propose Near-Far Attention (NFA), which adapts retrieval to regional attention patterns while keeping candidate scoring lightweight. During prefill, the Lightweight Gate Estimator identifies regions that can be skipped during decoding, adding less than 1% to dense-prefill time. For the remaining regions, the Calibration-Free Subspace Extractor supplies compact features shared by page-level and token-level scoring without offline calibration. The Distance-Aware Two-Level Selector then scores near and far pages differently and jointly ranks candidate tokens under a shared budget. Evaluations across model families, parameter scales, and GQA/MLA architectures show aggregate task quality comparable to full attention. On Qwen3-8B at 512K context length, NFA achieves up to $5.49\times$ operator speedup and $2.97\times$ whole-model decoding speedup over FlashInfer, including selection overhead.

papers.title: Irreducible shallow tanh neural networks are a manifold
papers.abstract: Neural networks (NNs) have been increasingly used as function approximators, motivating the study of the geometry of their function spaces. We study the set of functions represented by shallow neural networks with hyperbolic tangent activation, fixed input and output dimensions, and $n$ hidden neurons. In particular, we prove that the subset represented by irreducible networks in the sense of Sussmann (Neural Networks, 1992), i.e., networks with no redundant neurons, is a smooth embedded submanifold of the Sobolev spaces $\mathrm{W}^{\ell,p}$ on bounded sets for any $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\in[1,+\infty]$. The key step is to show that if a sequence of networks converges in $\mathrm{W}^{\ell,p}$ to an irreducible network with the same number of hidden neurons, then the parameters of the approximating networks remain bounded. Finally, we show that this manifold has exactly $n+1$ connected components when both the input and output are scalar, and is connected otherwise.

papers.title: An Experimental Apparatus for Embodied Conversational AI: A Simple Implementation Coupling a Commercial Voice AI with an Avatar
papers.abstract: As generative AI becomes integrated into everyday life, understanding how avatars shape human-AI interaction and the perception of AI as a social partner is becoming increasingly important. This paper builds a research instrument on audio-output coupling, which connects the audio output of a generative AI to an external avatar. There are two implementations: the browser implementation captures the audio of a tab selected through screen sharing without installing additional software, and the desktop implementation captures the audio of the service embedded in the application. Both work with the voice AI as people ordinarily use it, and as a method neither depends on a particular service. The implementation reported here, Deskmate, generates speech state, mouth shape, and expression from low-level features such as voice-band mean amplitude, RMS, peak, and transients. Because it uses no microphone, speech recognition, or transcription, Deskmate acquires neither the user's voice nor the content of the conversation. Records of the conversation remain with the voice AI provider, but none are kept automatically on the side of Deskmate. Three interchangeable backends are provided for rendering the avatar: 3D (VRM), 2D (Live2D), and CSS. Deskmate allows researchers to manipulate avatar presentation as an experimental condition, without changing the commercial service's interface, voice, or response generation. Because conversation content is not held fixed, the estimand is the total effect, including the changes in the participant's speech and the AI's responses that the presentation brings about. A server edition, served from the researcher's server for online experiments, is also provided. The effectiveness of avatar presentation has not yet been evaluated; this paper reports the design and implementation.

papers.title: On \(q\)-ary Minimal Linear Codes from Hierarchical Posets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study several families of \(q\)-ary linear codes constructed from two-level hierarchical posets over finite fields \(\mathbb{F}_q\), where \(q>2\). By using generating functions and additive characters, we determine their complete weight distributions, dimensions, and minimum distances. This paper focuses on constructing minimal codes that violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition. By analyzing the weight distributions and support sets of the codewords, we show that a large class of the constructed codes are minimal and strictly violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.

papers.title: Body and Soul: Decoupling Robotic Brain and Policy with RoboHarness-Zero
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can execute individual skills but fail to complete tasks that require combining several of them. In our audit of Xiaomi-Robotics-1, an estimated 43\% of failures involve choosing the wrong target or losing track of task progress. Wrapping a frozen VLA in a vision-language model (VLM) harness is a natural remedy. Existing harnesses can gain substantially from task- and policy-specific preparation, raising the question of how much of that gain transfers to a new task or policy. An ideal harness should (i) need minimal preparation for a new task, (ii) need no redesign for a new policy, and (iii) preserve standalone capabilities the policy already has. To the best of our knowledge, our \ours{} is the first harness built this way. Its premise is that choosing targets and tracking progress are easy for a VLM such as GPT-6 without task preparation, while the frozen VLA already handles continuous, contact-rich motion. The frozen VLA therefore executes continuous control while the VLM plans zero-shot and monitors execution; when progress stalls or targets drift, the VLM first rephrases the instruction and, only as a fallback, executes short generated code over generic motion primitives before returning fine control to the VLA. The supervision rules stay fixed across policies, requiring only a thin interface adapter and an automatically profiled skill configuration per policy. On 200 RoboCasa365 scenes, \ours{} with GPT-6 Astra raises the success rate of frozen Xiaomi-Robotics-1 from \textbf{\color{blue}57.5\%} to \textbf{\color{blue}70.5\%} and preserves \textbf{\color{blue}90.4\%} of its standalone successes (104/115) while rescuing 37 of 85 failures. On a shared 50-scene subset, the same rules add 8 to 10 percentage points to each of four other frozen policies, while existing preparation-based harness systems often fail to transfer to a new policy.

papers.title: Femtosecond laser-controlled production of functional titanium niobate layers from TiO$_{2}$/Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders
papers.abstract: Conventional synthesis methods of titanium niobates (TNO) require prolongated high-temperature treatments. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we have developed a confined powder-bed femtosecond (fs) laser-based technique to sinter TNO films starting from a mixture of TiO$_{2}$ and Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders, avoiding furnace-based approaches. The influence of laser-processing conditions on film formation, phase composition, and microstructure is systematically investigated, demonstrating that different TNO phases and morphologies can be obtained by controlling the laser pulse energy. A comprehensive characterization of the processed films has been performed, providing insights into the mechanisms governing their formation, which appear to share key features with laser-induced backward transfer (LIBT) processes. Our findings establish the relationship between laser-processing conditions and TNO film formation, highlighting the potential of confined powder-bed fs-laser processing as an alternative route for manufacturing functional oxide layers. Tentative applications of these layers are finally discussed.

papers.title: Boundary Stabilization of Mixed Traffic Flow With Connected Automated Vehicles
papers.abstract: This paper addresses boundary stabilization of stop-and-go oscillations in mixed traffic containing human-driven vehicles (HVs) and connected automated vehicles (CAVs). A penetration-dependent fundamental diagram is constructed from vehicle-class headways and effective spacing and embedded in an Aw--Rascle--Zhang (ARZ) model. Backstepping yields full-state and output-feedback controllers for the nominal linearized system. Exponential stability and finite-time convergence are established for the linearized system. Closed-loop simulations over CAV penetration rates from 0 to 1 show that increasing penetration raises the equilibrium speed and flow and reduces the convergence time for both the state-feedback and output-feedback controllers. A proportional-integral (PI) controller benchmark, input magnitude and rate constraints, physical sensor noise, and a sensitivity analysis are also considered to assess the performance of the controllers. We further illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed control methods and the simulation framework through a fundamental diagram calibration using the TGSIM dataset. These results quantify the traffic performance changes and identify the limits of the proposed method.

papers.title: Bilinear sum involving $GL(3)$ Fourier coefficients
papers.abstract: In this article, we use the circle method to establish non-trivial bounds for certain summatory functions and a bilinear sum involving the Fourier coefficients of a general Hecke-Maass cusp form on $SL(3,\mathbb{Z})$.

papers.title: Fetch, Read, Reuse: How AI Search Agents Bend the Web's Rules
papers.abstract: AI search agents form a new and fast-growing class of web traffic. Like a browser, they fetch pages on demand for one user; like a transcoding proxy, they rewrite what they fetch; and like a shared cache, they answer other users' questions from the stored copy. The rules publishers rely on, such as robots.txt, Retry-After, and Cache-Control, were written for more familiar clients, so the agent's vendor decides which of them to follow. We present a black-box measurement study of how these agents fetch, read, and reuse pages, covering the search APIs of OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Google and the consumer apps of ten services. We find that OpenAI and xAI do not honor robots.txt, and no service acts on Retry-After. Services silently read less than the origin served: OpenAI drops some formats, no service reads JavaScript-only content, and xAI reads only the first 0.5 MB of a page. OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI share fetched pages across users and largely ignore Cache-Control, so answers can reflect outdated pages for 30 minutes to a day or more. Publishers therefore lack effective control: directives are advisory and followed selectively, describe the served page rather than the rewritten copy, and bound how long a copy is reused but not how many answers it serves. We release our code and data.

papers.title: Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models
papers.abstract: In text to image AI models, fixing the prompt and the random seed is widely assumed to fix the image. We show that it does not on GPUs. We evaluate six text-to-image models (diffusion and autoregressive) under four numerical precisions and quantizations on three GPU types (RTX A6000, RTX 6000 Ada, and H100 NVL), across up to 100 prompts per set for all six models. For each configuration we compare, with the prompt and seed fixed, the image generated alone with the image generated inside a batch, and we also compare across GPUs. Every replay control reported here is bit-exact, so the variation is not random noise: the execution setting, mainly the batch composition and the GPU, decides the output. The effect is large and model dependent. Structural similarity between the single-image and the batched output falls to 0.580 for an autoregressive model in bf16 and to 0.551 with int8. For a second autoregressive model in bf16 it falls to 0.261 with sampled decoding and to 0.229 with greedy decoding, and for an fp8 diffusion model to 0.68. A diffusion model in bf16 stays close to the batch-1 output (0.96-0.98) but changes every image. In most cases the batched image is a different but equally valid image; in some, such as prompts with digits and counters, it is visibly worse. Cross-GPU differences are of the same order as the batch effect: for one autoregressive model in bf16 compared across two GPU architectures (RTX 6000 Ada versus RTX A6000), no image is bit-identical and the cross-GPU LPIPS (0.355 to 0.383) matches the batch effect within one GPU (0.347 to 0.381). The consequences are direct: seeds do not make results reproducible, benchmarks and image-quality comparisons that mix batch sizes or hardware can be biased, and safety audits and A/B tests on generated images need the serving setup reported.

papers.title: A corank one Lipschitz normally embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with non-trivial link
papers.abstract: We show that the knot-triviality theorem for Lipschitz normally embedded (LNE) corank one surface singularities in $\mathbb{R}^4$ proved by Birbrair, Mendes and Nuño-Ballesteros (2018) does not generalize unrestrictedly. More precisely, we exhibit a polynomial map germ $F:(\mathbb{R}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{R}^4,0)$ of corank one at the origin, with isolated singularity and $2$-jet $(x,0,0,0)$, whose image $X=F(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is LNE at the origin, yet its link is the granny knot $T\#T$, and hence non-trivial. The example is obtained via a general uniform-degree homogenization procedure applied to a known polynomial parametrization of the trefoil knot. We also give a finitely $\mathcal A$-determined polynomial realization with the same LNE and knot properties.

papers.title: Beyond the Blueprint: The Continuing Evolution of Turing's Theory of Morphogenesis
papers.abstract: Turing's article ``The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis'' has profoundly influenced conceptual views on the emergence of biological form across scales and species. It has also served as a foundational framework to guide experimental investigations into the mechanisms that underlie pattern formation. In this article, we trace the historical development of Turing's ideas and examine their integration into contemporary research programs. We critically assess the broad and often overlapping concepts that have derived from Turing's work, both highlighting value in productive applications of the theory and suggesting that skepticism should remain in overly simplistic validations. By clarifying these concepts and their intrinsic limitations, we rethink contemporary approaches aimed at understanding the essential principles that govern biological pattern formation. We pose some important challenges that will require interdisciplinary expertise to overcome, and which will necessitate fundamentally new paradigms to understand the physical origin of Darwin's ``endless forms most beautiful''.

papers.title: GC-MoE K3: A Green-Context Role Graph for Latent Mixture-of-Experts Decode
papers.abstract: Kimi K3 combines a latent routed mixture of experts with full-width shared experts. A complete feed-forward evaluation must score and select experts, project tokens into the latent space, exchange tokens across expert-parallel ranks, compute the routed and shared branches, and normalize and project the routed sum before joining the branches. We present GC-MoE K3, a datacenter Blackwell implementation that schedules this entire evaluation as a CUDA Graph across two Green Contexts. Five base roles split input projection, routing, dispatch, expert computation, and finalization. Dispatch can fill the routed input ring while the compute partition evaluates shared experts. Finalize waits for the expert owners needed by each token and overlaps routed reduction and RMSNorm with loading the output projection weights. Conditional roles reuse the communication partition for routed computation and reduce split-$K$ projection partials. On GB200 at EP8, EP16, and EP32, the operator is faster at all 24 measured configurations than the paired SGLang-style reference (mean speedup $1.1324\times$). A comparison with historical vLLM-style measurements gives $1.3651\times$ across the same 24 shapes. Both latency comparisons time single-layer graph replay on synthetic K3-shaped inputs with a residual prefix. The separate paired numerical suite passes all 142 cases and 2,936 rank checks.

papers.title: Dirichlet does not imply Regularity for general elliptic operators in smooth domains
papers.abstract:
In the upper half-space $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$, $n\geq2$, we show that there exists a real, diagonal, strongly elliptic matrix $A$ of bounded measurable coefficients, smooth in the interior of $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ and continuous on its closure, such that for the elliptic operator $L=-\operatorname{div}A
abla$, the Dirichlet problem with data in $L^p$ is solvable, for every $p\in(1,\infty)$, but the Dirichlet-Regularity problem is not solvable for any $p\in(1,\infty)$. The counterexample has the following properties, in particular: 1. $A$ equals the identity matrix at the boundary and their $L^\infty$ distance in $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ can be made arbitrarily small. 2. $A$ satisfies that $t|\partial_t A|^2$ is a Carleson measure. 3. $A$ fails to satisfy the Dahlberg-Kenig-Pipher condition only slightly, in the sense that for every $q>2$, $t^q|
abla A|^q rac{dxdt}{t}$ is a vanishing Carleson measure, but $t|
abla A|^2$ is not a Carleson measure. The counterexample resolves a long-standing question of C. Kenig.

papers.title: Towards a unified treatment of structured deformations theories
papers.abstract: Relying on the theory of $\mathcal B$ gradients, with $\mathcal B$ a $\mathbb C$-elliptic homogeneous linear partial differential operator of order $k$, with constant coefficients, we propose a method which allows to treat in a unified way the theories of structured deformations. Introducing the space of structured $\mathcal B$-deformations, $SD_{\mathcal B}$, we establish an integral-representation result for the associated energies, involving both bulk and surface contributions. Our approach relies on a direct application of the global method for relaxation, suitably adapted to the space of functions of $\mathcal B$-bounded variation.

papers.title: Where Compositionality Hides: Shared-Content Interference in Vision-Language Retrieval
papers.abstract: Paired compositional benchmarks such as Winoground ask each image to prefer its matching caption and each caption to prefer its matching image. A failed Group decision can come from a wrong caption preference or from the cross-image comparison alone, and Group Score merges the two. Choosing between retraining the encoder and changing the scoring rule therefore requires separating them. We study mean-erasure, which projects each frozen image embedding away from the mean of the two normalized candidate captions. We prove that the projection preserves every within-image caption ranking and makes Group Score equal baseline Text Score. On Winoground, mean-erasure raises CLIP ViT-B/32 Group Score from 9% to 31%, and five CLIP and SigLIP checkpoints gain 21 to 27 percentage points. ColorSwap shows a similar gain for color-object binding. A score decomposition shows that about 60% of Image failures already score the correct joint assignment above the swapped one and fail only on an offset between the two images. Fixed corrections and a learned bilinear scorer gain under one point. A direction estimated from retrieved captions gains about five points with two captions and falls below baseline with sixteen. Before retraining an encoder for paired retrieval, measure the Group loss that mean-erasure recovers: gains beyond baseline Text Score require changing the caption decisions themselves.

papers.title: Correlated chemical and displacive disorder in a lithium-rich disordered rocksalt revealed by electron diffuse scattering
papers.abstract: Lithium transport in disordered rocksalt cathodes depends on local cation arrangements and atomic distortions that are hidden from average-structure analysis. Resolving both contributions experimentally remains challenging, particularly in powders where directional information is lost. Here, we use electron diffuse scattering and three-dimensional difference pair distribution function analysis (3D-ΔPDF) to resolve occupational and displacive correlations in the model lithium-rich rocksalt Li{_2.5}TiO{_3}F{_0.5}. We identify an unusual combination of like-cation first-neighbour and unlike-cation second-neighbour preferences with correlated anion displacements towards Ti and accompanying cation displacements. A minimal pair-interaction model incorporating these displacements reproduces the principal diffuse-scattering and 3D-ΔPDF features and improves agreement with powder-PDF measurements. The experimentally constrained cation configurations exhibit an above-random population of 0-TM lithium-migration environments. These results establish electron 3D-ΔPDF as a route to constrain atomistic models incorporating chemical order and local relaxation, providing a foundation for assessing their combined influence on lithium migration in disordered rocksalt materials.

papers.title: Metal-Dielectric Bilayer Supported Nanoporous Silver Substrates for Ultrasensitive Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
papers.abstract: Resolving the chemical footprint of molecules in analytes is of fundamental interest in biosensing and biomedical applications. Surface-enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) spectroscopy is a powerful tool for non-invasive molecule investigation, and there is a continuous effort to develop highly efficient SERS substrates that can be fabricated at low cost and tuned to the desired spectral range of investigation. Here, we show that the Raman signal of porous silver films can be significantly enhanced by integrating a thin dielectric layer and a metallic backreflector underneath the porous metal film. We call this architecture nanoporous metal on dielectric metal (NPMoDM) and show that it leads to much stronger near-field enhancement in the bulk of the film. Additionally, the spectral band of enhanced sensitivity can be tuned by the thickness of the dielectric layer within the visible spectral range. With rhodamine 6G and para-aminothiophenol as target analytes, we demonstrate SERS detection of substrates incubated with zeptomolar concentrations of the analyte, which corresponds to only few molecules present on a mm2 surface area. Our approach introduces a tunable and scalable (lithography-free) platform for ultrasensitive SERS applications, with a readily accessible surface for analyte functionalization.

papers.title: Chiral crossover responses in a magnetic field: Finite-$μ_5$ matching in the NJL model
papers.abstract: We investigate how independent information at finite chiral chemical potential $μ_5$ constrains pseudocritical-temperature responses in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model under a magnetic field. Vacuum calibration alone leaves the coefficient $c_r$ of the additional interaction $δΩ_r=c_rμ_5^2(M-m_0)^2$ undetermined. We compare soft-cutoff (SC) and Pauli-Villars (PV) vacuum regularizations, each combined with the direct treatment (D) or the magnetic finite-difference scheme (MFDS). The reference SC and PV treatments exhibit opposite finite-$μ_5$ responses already at $eB=0$. Matching the $eB=0$ scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio predicted by unitarized chiral perturbation theory gives $c_{\mathrm{SC}}=-0.07112$ and $c_{\mathrm{PV}}=0.22479$. Holding these coefficients fixed at $eB=0.1,0.2,0.4$ GeV$^2$ reduces the four-treatment spread of the normalized finite-$μ_5$-induced mass-inflection temperature change by factors of approximately $7.5$-$15.3$ at $μ_5=0.15$ GeV and $18.1$-$32.6$ at $μ_5=0.30$ GeV. For the distinct scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio at $μ_5=0.15$ GeV, the spread decreases by factors of approximately $74$, $27$, and $14$ at the same magnetic fields, respectively. The reduction in regularization-dependent finite-$μ_5$ responses thus persists at the sampled nonzero magnetic fields without further matching.

papers.title: DelayOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation from a Synchronous Teacher for Real-time Asynchronous Policies
papers.abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies incur substantial inference latency due to their large vision-language backbones and iterative denoising. Asynchronous execution reduces this latency by generating the next action chunk while executing the current one, but the new chunk is conditioned on a stale observation, degrading performance as the delay increases. We investigate this mismatch by comparing actions predicted from observations at planning and execution times. We find that these predictions differ little on expert demonstrations but diverge substantially on the policy's own delayed rollouts, particularly in failed episodes. Motivated by this observation, we propose DelayOPSD, which trains an asynchronous policy to imitate its synchronous counterpart on the policy's own rollouts. Specifically, a synchronous teacher, obtained from the same policy using the observation at execution time, supervises a delayed student that observes only the earlier frame and the actions still being executed. The student learns to match the teacher throughout its own denoising process. Under a 10-step delay, training SmolVLA on demonstrations achieves only 70.2% success, comparable to naive asynchronous execution (70.4%), whereas training on its own rollouts improves success to 78.7%. Across LIBERO and Kinetix, DelayOPSD achieves the highest average success among the compared methods, without introducing additional modules at deployment. On a real robot, it further improves success from 46% to 62%.

papers.title: CyberDualEval: Measuring Dual-Use Cyber Risks in Frontier Language Models
papers.abstract: While frontier language models are becoming capable cybersecurity assistants, they also create a dual-use cyber risk: the same capabilities that help defenders identify and analyze vulnerabilities can similarly help attackers weaponize them. Existing cyber benchmarks measure either raw offensive capability or generic refusal behavior, overlooking the dual-use cyber assessment of preserving benign security utility while refusing assistance that materially advances misuse. We introduce CyberDualEval, a benchmark with 430 vulnerable tasks for measuring dual-use cyber risk in frontier language models. Each task is decomposed into three phases of increasing operationalization: security analysis, proof-of-concept generation, and exploit generation. To quantify the residual cyber risk, we annotate each task with a Task Weaponization Score that measures how much work remains to turn the resulting artifact into unauthorized cyber misuse. CyberDualEval assesses ten closed- and open-weight language models both on correct compliance and on task performance, developing four deterministic mechanisms for determining per-phase success on a large subset of the dataset. Our evaluation reveals that none of the existing frontier models effectively navigate helping with safe requests and refusing risky ones, characterized by being overly-cautious. On the other hand, recent open-weight models rarely refuse and demonstrate strong validated accuracy on risky requests.

papers.title: BEND: Spectral Bregman Losses for Multi-Image Unlearning in Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion models memorize training images and reproduce them almost verbatim when prompted, creating copyright and privacy liabilities. Data unlearning erases the influence of specific training samples from a trained model without retraining, and is two-sided: it must forget the targets while preserving generation quality on everything else. Prior methods use the squared-L2 diffusion loss, at most with a hand-set frequency mask; however, it is known that every Bregman divergence is a mathematically valid choice and the squared-L2 is only the simplest example. BEND is the first to search this family: it fits a spectral Bregman divergence to the unlearning task through a bilevel loop, so the loss itself is shaped to forget thoroughly while protecting quality. It also redirects a memorized image to the mean of its retain images, where ReTrack, the state of the art, redirects it to a single near-copy. On Stable Diffusion, a single BEND model erases all 48 verifiably memorized benchmark images at once. It forgets at least as much as per-target, sequential, and jointly trained ReTrack (SSCD 0.084 versus 0.094-0.120), at the quality of the model before unlearning (CLIP-IQA 0.81 versus 0.64-0.69). BEND also outperforms the state of the art on CelebA-HQ in all three measures of the benchmark, and matches or exceeds it on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

papers.title: ReDiffDet: Rotation-equivariant Diffusion Model for Oriented Object Detection
papers.abstract: The diffusion model has been successfully applied to various detection tasks. However, it still faces several challenges when used for oriented object detection: objects that are arbitrarily rotated require the diffusion model to encode their orientation information; uncontrollable random boxes inaccurately locate objects with dense arrangements and extreme aspect ratios; oriented boxes result in the misalignment between them and image features. To overcome these limitations, we propose ReDiffDet, a framework that formulates oriented object detection as a rotation-equivariant denoising diffusion process. First, we represent an oriented box as a 2D Gaussian distribution, forming the basis of the denoising paradigm. The reverse process can be proven to be rotation-equivariant within this representation and model framework. Second, we design a conditional encoder with conditional boxes to prevent boxes from being randomly placed across the entire image. Third, we propose an aligned decoder for alignment between oriented boxes and image features. The extensive experiments demonstrate ReDiffDet achieves promising performance and significantly outperforms the diffusion model baseline.

papers.title: Assembly-JEPA: Using World Models for Fine-Grained Industrial Image Verification
papers.abstract: Automated verification of industrial assembly processes remains a challenging problem due to substantial visual variability, limited availability of labeled defect data, and the fine-grained nature of many assembly errors. Existing approaches often rely on object detection, CAD models, or supervised classification pipelines, which can struggle to generalize across changing products and assembly configurations. In this work, we propose a novel self-supervised assembly verification framework based on Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs). Starting from the JEPA-based world model LeWorldModel, we investigate how the architecture must be adapted to verify the correctness of fine-grained assembly operations. To this end, we formulate assembly verification as a predictive world modeling task operating on before-and-after observations of assembly processes. Experimental results on industrial assembly tasks demonstrate that the proposed approach reliably detects both fine-grained incorrect assembly states and action-state mismatches, achieving an AUROC of 86.9% on a newly introduced assembly verification dataset. These results indicate that JEPA-based predictive representations constitute a promising foundation for robust and data-efficient industrial assembly verification.

papers.title: Density of states for random Schrödinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder
papers.abstract: We study the density of states of random Schrödinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder. Using an integration-by-parts supersymmetric representation, we prove smoothness of the density of states and Wegner estimates in the strong-disorder regime. We are particularly interested in mixed-sign correlation kernels, which serve as a toy model for the hyperbolic structures arising in the analysis of averaged squared Green's functions. Our approach applies to a broad class of correlation kernels and disorder distributions, including $α$-stable laws.

papers.title: Asynchronous Uplink Multi-UE Networked Sensing via Multipath Correlation
papers.abstract: Multiuser uplink sensing offers a promising paradigm for networked sensing by leveraging signals from multiple user equipment (UEs) to enhance sensing coverage and performance. This paper investigates asynchronous multiuser uplink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access sensing by exploiting correlated multipath structures across UEs. A common frontend first mitigates the dominant timing offsets (TOs), carrier-frequency offsets (CFOs), and phase offsets (POs) through LoS-referencing and constructs a reduced delay-angle-of-arrival (AoA) search space. Two alternative multiuser sensing estimators are then proposed, with different mechanisms of explicitly and implicitly exploiting UE correlation, respectively. The first explicitly adopts a latent-group shared-private sparse Bayesian learning (Group-SBL) model to exploit group-shared propagation structures while accommodating UE-specific components. The second combines calibrated multiuser observations for joint multiple signal classification (MUSIC) processing, recovering a global delay-AoA pool that can be further associated with individual UEs. Residual-TO refinement is conducted with both estimator updates, followed by local-grid delay-AoA refinement and residual common-phase compensation before Doppler estimation. Simulations under a 5G New Radio-compatible uplink configuration show that both multiuser schemes outperform their corresponding per-UE baselines, with larger gains as cross-UE propagation correlation increases.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Dynamics of R-loop Formation in the CRISPR-Cas9 System
papers.abstract: The binding specificity of CRISPR-Cas9 is governed by the stepwise formation of an R-loop, in which the sgRNA displaces the nontarget DNA strand and hybridizes with the target strand in discrete base pair steps. Here we develop a nonequilibrium dynamics framework that models R-loop formation as a continuous-time Markov birth-death process over twenty base pairs. Each transition rate is derived from Eyring transition-state theory and the Bell model, and combines three physical contributions, i.e., the torsional strain generated by the B-form to A-form helical conversion at the unwinding front, a base stacking correction that couples neighboring base pairs, and the allosteric work supplied by Cas9 conformational changes. We further derive the entropy production of the process, which is decomposed into activation, stacking, torsional, and allosteric terms. The resulting prediction model uses no external thermodynamic database and reaches Spearman correlations of 0.84 and 0.82 in two independent libraries of dCas9-sgRNA mismatch variants measured in vivo. The mismatch-type dependence is carried by one twist deviation and one pairing weight per type. Our model recovers the seed region sensitivity, the PAM-proximal activity gradient, and the moderate cost of dDrG mismatches, while isolating the high-activity double mismatch tail as the regime in which the present free-energy mapping is inadequate. The framework gives quantitative predictions on how DNA supercoiling and sequence context modulate binding affinity, and provides a mechanistic basis for sgRNA design.

papers.title: Quasilinear elliptic equations involving asymptotically linear operators
papers.abstract:
In this paper we aim to study in a unified fashion existence and regularity properties of solutions to a very general class of Dirichlet boundary value problems such as  egin{equation}\label{P1abs}	ag{1}  egin{cases} - \mbox{div}\left(\displaystyle ϕ(|

Among others, most of the far-famed operators derived from functionals with linear growth, as for instance the $1$-Laplacian and the minimal surface operator are included in our model. Under suitable assumptions on the data we prove existence and regularity results for problem \eqref{P1abs} which recover the sharp thresholds known in the model cases.

papers.title: Solvability of one-dimensional sub-quadratic BSDEs with unbounded stochastic coefficients
papers.abstract: This study is devoted to solvability of the unbounded solutions of a class of one-dimensional sub-quadratic backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with unbounded stochastic coefficients and general time horizons. In a general sub-exponential moment integrability space linked with the stochastic coefficients, we first establish existence of an unbounded solution of the preceding BSDE when the generator $g$ has a one-sided linear growth in the state variable $y$ and a sub-quadratic growth in the state variable $z$, and then prove a comparison theorem of the unbounded solutions of such two BSDEs when either of generators satisfies an extended convexity/concavity condition in $(y,z)$ with unbounded stochastic coefficients, yielding naturally the uniqueness of the solution. Particularly, the unbounded stochastic coefficient before the state variable $y$ is supposed to take values in $\R$ such that the required integrability condition of the terminal value may be weaker than that under the usual situations. These findings incorporate and generalize some corresponding known results.

papers.title: Non-intrusive Differentiation of High-Performance Seismic Solvers
papers.abstract: Differentiable frameworks for seismic tomography compute model gradients without hand-derived adjoint sources. Some differentiate through wave propagation, which can be costly in time and memory at scale. Others use native adjoints with automatically constructed sources, and the efficiency is largely determined by forward and adjoint solves. Mature seismic solvers offer efficient, well-tested propagation, but a reusable workflow is still needed to connect them to user-defined misfit functions. Here we present a non-intrusive workflow and an Agent Skill for adapting existing seismic solvers to differentiable inversion. We apply automatic differentiation (AD) to the preprocessing and misfit, stopping backpropagation at the synthetic data. The solver injects this data derivative at the receivers to form the adjoint source, then computes the model gradient from the native forward and adjoint simulations. To assess accuracy and computational cost, we compared our hybrid implementation (HybridADFWI) with full AD in ADFWI using the same forward solver. Across six settings, the gradients agreed to within $1.4\times10^{-6}$ in relative $L_2$ norm. For one iteration, HybridADFWI was 2.4-4.6 times as fast as ADFWI and used 5-22% less peak reserved GPU memory. Guided by the Skill, a coding agent adds missing adjoint routines, verifies gradients, and runs recovery tests for user-selected model parameters. We applied the Skill to two independent solvers, building DiffSPECFEM2D and DiffAxiSEM3D. In the P-wave velocity tests, DiffSPECFEM2D recovered the main dipping layers of Marmousi-II, and DiffAxiSEM3D recovered the overall shape of the SEG/EAGE salt body. Both frameworks support user-defined misfits while preserving native kernels and parallel execution.

papers.title: VeriOrigin: A Proactive Image Protection Framework for Provenance, Tamper Localization, and Lossless Recovery
papers.abstract: Versatile watermarking, which seamlessly integrates provenance and tamper detection, has recently attracted widespread attention. In this paper, we propose \textbf{VeriOrigin}, a comprehensive and unified image protection framework that not only robustly achieves provenance and highly precise tamper localization under various complex distortions, but also guarantees perfect recovery of the original cover in lossless channels. To realize this framework, we depart from conventional flow based architectures. Instead, we design \textbf{XOnet}, a CNN based invertible encoder. XOnet comprises two standard CNN based watermarking sub networks, Xnet and Onet, which achieve reversibility through cross residual prediction. Based on XOnet, we train the proactive protection scheme via a two stage strategy: first optimizing the watermarking branch, followed by the tamper localization branch. During inference, the cover image undergoes sequential watermarking and tamper residual embedding. Extensive experimental results on four datasets demonstrate that VeriOrigin achieves precise tamper localization and strong robustness, while guaranteeing lossless cover recovery for integrity authentication. Project page is available at https://veriorigin.github.io/

papers.title: Can LLMs Understand Human Rules?
papers.abstract: Rules help people coordinate and cooperate for mutual benefit. For AI models to coexist with humans and other AI systems, they will need to interact with and navigate such rules successfully. But such interactions require AI systems to recognize not only when a rule permits or prohibits a particular action, but also cases where people may reasonably disagree about whether a certain action is appropriate. This paper introduces the RULES benchmark---building on a set of 300 images depicting signs posted around New York City, and accompanied by 937 scenarios---to test frontier models' ability to discern whether a proposed action is socially acceptable, unacceptable, or would generate disagreement. At first pass, we find that frontier models exhibit robust performance on the benchmark, successfully engaging with human-written directives in naturalistic visual environments, and correctly determining the social acceptability of a wide range of everyday activities. However, we further find that models systematically fail to recognize certain widely accepted permissible exceptions to a rule, indicating a critical shortcoming in model understanding. Moreover, models struggle to identify instances where humans disagree regarding the application of a given rule; in these instances, models tend to identify proposed actions as unacceptable, rather than as appropriate targets of disagreement. We do find that ensembling a series of diverse models together begins to recover the disagreement signal. Overall, our findings identify significant limitations in AI performance on human rules.

papers.title: Collective order from language models without communication, memory or shared context
papers.abstract: Physical matter orders without a centre: units interact only with neighbours, and fluctuations carry them over energy barriers from a locally stable arrangement to the ordered state. We ask whether language-model agents can do the same, treating each memoryless query as a particle that sees its neighbours but cannot communicate, has no identifier or shared context and receives the same question as all others. Such a particle behaves as if at zero temperature: told a rule or a temperature, it returns the most probable state, and a collective can freeze in a local minimum. We therefore give each particle only a goal and a die whose weights it sets itself, and test several models. Some of them use the die as a noise source even at a local optimum, with weights that fall with the energy cost of the move; on a lattice the energy of one of them climbs over barriers and reaches the ground state, where the noise stops by itself. Particles in three-lane counterflow also order, from mixed traffic into one-way lanes: a spontaneous symmetry breaking. Decentralized collective order can thus arise from disorder without communication, memory or shared context, with noise that the particles choose themselves.

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Local Smoothing in Noncommutative Spaces and Its Applications
papers.abstract: We prove local smoothing for planar half-waves with coefficients in a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $M$. For $N\ge2$ and $P_N=ψ(|D|/N)$ with $ψ\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$, we obtain $\|e^{it|D|}P_N f\|_{L^4([1,2]\times\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}\le C_ψ\sqrt{\log(2+N)}\|f\|_{L^4(\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}$ uniformly in $M$ and its trace. Pairing the Dirichlet energies for $M$ and its opposite algebra cancels a determinant contribution that can have either sign. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>σ(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. The finite-$p$ bounds transfer to quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes, answering the question of Hong, Lai and Wang about the range $s>σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$ on generalized Moyal planes. For $1<p<\infty$ and complex $α$ with $\operatorname{Re}α>\max\{2/p-1,1/p-1/2,-1/p\}$, we prove maximal inequalities over all radii for generalized circular means on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes. For an action $β$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ on $M$ by normal trace-preserving $*$-automorphisms with norm-continuous $L^p$ orbits, the orbit mean $A_{t,β}^αx$ converges bilaterally almost uniformly to $πx/Γ(1+α)$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $x\in L^p(M)$. We also obtain estimates for truncated cone multipliers on three-dimensional Euclidean and quantum Euclidean spaces, and full-radius row and column bounds for Stein's square function on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes.

papers.title: GeoRead3D: Grounding Part Descriptions for 3D Pointing and Reorientation
papers.abstract: Language often refers to an object by its parts, as in asking to point to a part or to turn an arbitrarily posed object so that two named parts lie in given directions. Both tasks need the direction from the object's center to the part's center, not the part's own orientation. A natural approach segments the part and takes the centroid of its mask. However, high mask overlap predicts the pointing direction poorly when a part is spread out relative to its distance from the object center. Language-guided part segmentation is trained and evaluated by mask overlap, which leaves a gap between the masks it produces and the part geometry that these tasks use. We close this gap by learning point evidence, weights over the observed points whose weighted centroid gives the part's location. Geometric Readout Supervision (GRS) trains these weights through the centroid's position and adds direction supervision on the parts used in reorientation commands. GRS improves both tasks even with a single frozen encoder and a single input pose. We implement this supervision in GeoRead3D, a system for pointing and reorientation from part descriptions. A language model maps each description to a known part name. Dual-Route Part Evidence combines refined segmentation evidence with directly predicted point evidence to locate each part. On PartNeXt and Artiverse, GeoRead3D points within $22.5^\circ$ for 74.1% and 60.0% of queries, 5.8 and 7.3 percentage points above the strongest baselines. Its reorientation success exceeds the strongest baselines by 10.4 and 7.8 points.

papers.title: Identax: A Toolbox for Efficient Learning of Linear, Parameter-Varying, and Nonlinear Systems in JAX
papers.abstract: Accurate data-driven modelling of dynamical systems is increasingly important across engineering disciplines, yet state-of-the-art identification methods are often computationally demanding, opaque, or poorly scalable. We present Identax, a JAX toolbox for identifying linear, Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) and nonlinear systems, designed as an extensible foundation for system identification research. Its modular design allows model structures, identification criteria and optimization methods to be extended independently. The first release provides state-space and Linear Fractional Representation (LFR) models, multiple-shooting criteria for parallel training, and a transparent optimization pipeline. On the Silverbox benchmark, an LPV-LFR model outperforms all previous black-box results while training in under three minutes on a CPU. On a control moment gyroscope, Identax matches state-of-the-art accuracy.

papers.title: sudo L7: Can Coding Agents Act Like Staff Engineers?
papers.abstract: Coding agents can now turn a well-specified ticket into a patch that passes its tests. Experienced engineers also notice risks the request never mentioned, question flawed premises, reuse what already exists and say plainly what they did and did not check. We present sudo L7, a benchmark of 60 software-engineering tasks written by staff-level engineers, mostly in private production codebases and each built around a place where a frontier model failed. A task pairs a realistic, underspecified request with a hidden, expert-authored rubric of atomic criteria (1,287 in all), tagged with eight behavioral dimensions from functional correctness to truthful reporting. An agentic grader reads the agent's transcript, inspects and runs its code, and treats test output as evidence. An attempt passes only if it meets every criterion of the two highest severities, and more than half of these gating criteria test something other than functional correctness. On the public leaderboard as of November 2026 (19 models, each in its developer's harness or in OpenCode, three attempts per task), Claude Fable 5.2 passes 52.2% of attempts, Claude Sonnet 5.5 50.6% and Claude Opus 5.5 46.1%. GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra pass 31-34%, and the other 13 models at most 18.9%. In a human-label study, three candidate model graders each agreed with a software engineer on 85-86% of criterion verdicts, about as often as two engineers agreed with each other. Cases from the benchmark show how one unsupported claim can fail an otherwise strong attempt and illustrate two sides of engineering judgment: flagging hidden hazards and avoiding needless work.

papers.title: JEPA-ICL: Progress-Aligned Latent Plans for In-Context Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Demonstrations show how a task can be completed, but differences in embodiment, appearance, and execution speed make it difficult to identify the guidance relevant to the robot's current progress. We introduce JEPA-ICL, a vision-language-action framework that couples predictive planning with demonstration learning. The policy learns to plan by predicting ordered future states in JEPA feature space up to subtask completion, capturing what remains to be accomplished. These plans guide action generation and locate relevant stages in demonstrations, whose JEPA-supervised content features provide progress-aligned context. Learning from this context, in turn, updates the shared policy that produces the plans and actions. This coupling connects anticipating the robot's own execution with reusing demonstrated experience. On the Imitator Game, JEPA-ICL achieves 80.0% seen-task success under C15 pretraining, outperforming Zero-WAM by 12.0 percentage points. Without contextual demonstrations, JEPA-ICL outperforms the VLA-JEPA variant without human-video pretraining, improving success rates from 96.1% to 97.6% on LIBERO and from 62.9% to 73.2% on LIBERO-Plus. With demonstration-based training and contextual guidance at inference, LIBERO-Plus success further increases from 73.2% to 75.2%.

papers.title: Field-Level Crop Classification via Similarity-Induced Supervision from Imperfect Labels
papers.abstract: Regional-scale crop mapping is critical for food production monitoring, yet remains challenging in tropical regions, where persistent cloud cover limits optical imagery. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) enables continuous observation throughout the agricultural cycle, but a second obstacle is label quality: national-scale land cover products exhibit systematic biases that underestimate less prevalent crops, and training directly on them inherits and amplifies their errors. This work proposes a methodology to build large-scale crop classification models from imperfect public land cover products, requiring no new field campaign, ground survey, or manual label correction. The approach combines two mechanisms. The first reduces the semantic inconsistency of the labels by shifting supervision from the sample level to the group level: a similarity-based clustering model organizes SAR time series into coherent groups, and noisy labels are used only to assign each group its most representative class. The resulting clusters are highly pure with respect to the reference classes (89.0% and 91.2% in the two study regions). The second reduces the spatial inconsistency of the predictions: a segmentation model delineates crop field boundaries from optical imagery, and patch-level predictions are consolidated by majority voting within each field, yielding spatially coherent maps. Evaluated in two Brazilian municipalities, Campo Verde (Mato Grosso) and Luís Eduardo Magalhães (Bahia), the approach consistently outperforms the noisy baseline in mean class accuracy, with gains of up to 10.14 percentage points, especially for minority crops. A state-scale analysis across Mato Grosso and Bahia shows stable behavior without further model adjustment, and the derived municipal crop areas are consistent with official IBGE/PAM statistics, an independent estimate the model never observes.

papers.title: When Do Spatial Plans Help Text-to-Image Generation? Causal Control, System Utility, and Text Responsiveness
papers.abstract: A generator can follow a spatial plan, but the benefit of supplying that plan depends on what the model can already do from text. In a controlled study with 18 paired training seeds, correcting predicted positions and sizes improves spatial intersection-over-union by 0.030, yet direct text is non-inferior at matched training compute. In a pretrained generator, a fixed rule layout improves two-object task success over the same text-only adapter by 12.50 percentage points, mostly by separating objects that already appear in the correct order. We then ask whether a more precise instruction can achieve the same separation across conditioning paths. On 288 new task families, adding a minimum-gap instruction improves success by 37.15 points with the text-only adapter, by at most 0.69 points with widely spaced regions, and by 6.94 points with tightly spaced regions. Under tight regions, 230 of 288 baseline images have the correct objects and direction yet miss the required gap, ruling out a high baseline success rate as the sole explanation for the weak text response.

papers.title: Queuing for Secrets: Model-Based Remote Timing Attacks
papers.abstract: Remote timing attacks exploit variations in response times to infer sensitive information about remote systems. Their effectiveness, however, is often limited by the difficulty of accurately modeling the stochastic nature of server-side response times, taking into account the intrinsic variability of the service time of a request and the impact of varying workloads on the observed response times. In this article, we propose a new stochastic framework for remote timing attacks based on queuing models and Bayesian statistics. We assume that the attacker knows the service time distributions of two classes of requests and that the information leakage occurs when a malicious observer can distinguish with high probability the class based on the observed response times in the presence of noise induced by exogenous workload. Our experimental evaluation on popular websites demonstrates the practical viability of the approach: our attack outperforms formal techniques based on deterministic service times and existing empirical techniques, while requiring less tuning and fewer hyper-parameters compared to previous formal approaches. Overall, our results show that principled stochastic modeling can provide a solid foundation for building more effective remote timing attacks under realistic network and workload conditions.

papers.title: A one-third bound for domination in cubic graphs of girth at least six
papers.abstract: A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $S$ has a neighbor in $S$. The domination number $γ(G)$ is the minimum size of a dominating set of $G$. In 2010, Verstraëte conjectured that every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$ and girth at least six satisfies $γ(G)\le n/3$. More recently, Dorbec and Henning established this bound under the additional assumption that $G$ contains neither a $7$-cycle nor an $8$-cycle. We prove Verstraëte's conjecture in full. As a corollary, we settle the $C_4$-free case of Kostochka's conjecture, which asserts that the same bound holds for all cubic bipartite graphs.

papers.title: AXE: AlpaSim E2E Closed Loop Challenge Technical Report
papers.abstract: This report presents a comprehensive pipeline for developing an end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving model for the Physical AI AV Track. The framework consists of data curation, HD map auto-labelling, data-driven imitation learning, and simulator-based reinforcement learning. To ensure safety in the closed-loop setting, we introduce a selection-based E2E planning approach that leverages object detection and BEV segmentation to filter out trajectory candidates likely to cause collisions or off-road driving. Trained on NVIDIA NuRec and the NVIDIA PAI-AV dataset, our method scores a fixed vocabulary of trajectory candidates for collision, drivable-area compliance, and progress learned from simulated rollouts, and selects the best candidate that passes the filter.
