Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. PCM transforms compressed motion history from Mamba recurrent states, together with state changes and text-conditioned features, into dynamically updated content slots accessible to local attention. To enable efficient inference, we further develop an execution scheme tailored to this architecture, combining CUDA Graph replay, fused kernels, and execution-flow simplification while preserving the canonical history update. Evaluations on retargeted HiPHI demonstrate accurate terminal control over rollouts of up to 39.52 s, while short-horizon comparisons on BONES Seed and retargeted HumanML3D show that the model also retains strong spatial control and text-motion matching. On an RTX 4090, the optimized execution reduces median complete-window latency from 1685.35 to 276.14 ms, achieving a median paired speedup of 6.138$\times$ while preserving identical outputs and committed states in the tested rollouts. Moreover, we conduct extensive real-world evaluation on the Unitree G1, demonstrating sequential text-guided action composition, expressive motion, and interactive locomotion through keyboard and mouse control.

papers.title: Segment Anything In-Context via Visual Demonstrations
papers.abstract: We present the Segment Anything Model via Visual Demonstrations (SAYD), a foundation model for in-context segmentation. Given visual demos comprising prompt images and their segmentation masks, SAYD segments coherent regions (e.g., objects or their parts) in a query image by establishing visual correspondences between the prompts and the query. SAYD generalizes to previously-unseen segmentation tasks, including those requiring tacit visual knowledge or involving concepts that are difficult to articulate unambiguously in language. We train SAYD on 12 public datasets originally curated for panoptic segmentation using our proposed techniques, including a lightweight mask decoder for prompt-agnostic mask generation and a learning mechanism for recognizing novel query classes absent in the prompts. These innovations enhance both computational efficiency and out-of-domain generalization. Consequently, SAYD significantly outperforms existing methods of in-context segmentation and open-vocabulary segmentation across 24 out-of-domain benchmarks, spanning natural, biological, ecological, cosmological, medical, pathological, and satellite imagery.

papers.title: The Optimal D.C. Bound Is Dominated by the Reciprocal of the Lovász Theta Number
papers.abstract: We resolve a question left open by Anstreicher and Burer (J. Global Optim. 33, 299--312, 2005). For the standard quadratic formulation of the stability number, we prove that the optimal difference-of-convex (D.C.) bound is at most the reciprocal of the Lovász theta number. The dominance is strict whenever the Lovász theta number is not exact.

papers.title: Binning is Sinning: Absolution for the Unbinned Supernova Hubble Diagram
papers.abstract: Cosmological analyses of Type Ia supernovae use a covariance matrix to describe statistical noise and systematic uncertainties. To fit a Hubble diagram with an unbinned covariance matrix, the CPU cost scales as O(N^3) for N supernovae, which has motivated compression into bins that loses information and reduces self-calibration power. To remove the need for lossy compression, we present a method that greatly reduces CPU time for matrix inversion and cosmology fitting, as well as matrix storage. For systematic covariances constructed from K per-supernova distance-shift vectors, we retain the exact representation C = D + U U^T, with diagonal statistical covariance D, and use the Woodbury factorization identity to efficiently invert C, significantly reducing computing time and disk storage without losing information. We implement this method in SNANA and validate it on simulated samples for LSST (N ~ 5,300, K = 18), Roman+LSST (N ~ 15,000, K = 30), and 10-yr LSST (N ~ 134,400, K = 18). For 10-yr LSST, matrix inversion and cosmology fit time is ~10 weeks using a dense (unbinned) matrix with 18 billion elements, and is reduced to ~1.5 hr using the factorization method. It also reduces covariance matrix disk storage by a factor of 1,800 (36 GB to 20 MB). In all validation tests, the best-fit cosmological parameters are nearly identical to the unbinned fit, and the dark energy figure of merit (FoM) agrees to better than 0.1% accuracy; the small differences are likely due to numerical artifacts in the pipeline. For the LSST and Roman era, this factorization method enables large unbinned supernova analyses with significantly reduced computing resources compared to previous analyses using a dense matrix, while preserving all information in the covariance model.

papers.title: Global strong solvability of the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations for large initial data
papers.abstract: In 1995, Kazhikhov and Vaigant introduced a two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes model with constant shear viscosity and bulk viscosity $λ(ρ)=ρ^β$. For $β>3$, they proved global existence of smooth solutions for arbitrarily large initial data with strictly positive density. More recently, Fan-Jiang-Li-Lü (arXiv:2611.20264, 2026) proved global strong solvability for every $β>1$ in bounded simply connected domains with Navier-slip boundary conditions. In this article, we prove global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the Kazhikhov-Vaigant model on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ at the critical point $β=1$, for every $γ>1$ and arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum.

papers.title: On the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on a product with a torus
papers.abstract: We prove that if $N$ is a closed smooth manifold admitting a Riemannian metric of negative sectional curvature and $T^k$ is the $k$-dimensional torus, then there is a retraction from the moduli space of nonpositively curved Riemannian metrics on $T^k\times N$ onto the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$. As an application, we combine our retraction with Tuschmann and Wiemeler's work on the rational topology of the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$ to deduce that the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on $T^k\times N$ has nontrivial higher rational homotopy and cohomology groups when $k\geq5$.

papers.title: QuakeConsensus: Reducing false detections in automatic earthquake catalogs through consensus phase association
papers.abstract: Automatic earthquake catalogs rely on phase associators to group the picks of a phase picker into events. Associators also produce false events that inflate the catalog. We measure the false events of five associators, PyOcto, GaMMA, REAL, GENIE, and backprojection, on two benchmarks built from observed phase picks in Taiwan. The first benchmark isolates 28,129 cataloged earthquakes in 20-minute windows, adding noise by shifting unassociated picks independently. The second evaluates 11,917 earthquakes from the 2024 $M_w$ 7.4 Hualien aftershock sequence, shifting unassociated P and S pairs together. We also propose a consensus association strategy that keeps an event found by at least two associators. With noise picks, single associators produce 5.3% to 10.2% false positives on the regional benchmark and 11.8% to 46.8% on the Hualien benchmark, whereas the consensus catalog reduces these false positive percentages to 4.2% and 11.5%, respectively. The consensus has the highest F1 score and the smallest percentage of false positives on both benchmarks.

papers.title: Parking Functions inspired by board games
papers.abstract: We introduce two new parking schemes inspired by the classic board games Monopoly and backgammon. We consider a one-way street with $n$ parking spots and a queue of $n$ cars waiting to park. Each car has a preferred parking spot and enters in sequence to park. Under the Monopoly parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. Under the backgammon parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it bumps the already parked car out of that spot and takes its place. The bumped car then returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. A preference list is a parking function for a given parking scheme if all cars successfully park under that scheme. We prove that all preference lists are parking functions under both the Monopoly and backgammon parking schemes. However, the final parking order differs significantly between the two schemes. For a fixed permutation $π$, we provide a product formula for the number of Monopoly parking functions resulting in the outcome $π$. Analogously, we show that the number of backgammon parking functions with outcome $π$ is bounded below by $2^{n-1}$ and bounded above by the $n$-th Catalan number. We also obtain exact formulas involving Motzkin numbers for several families of outcomes. We define the displacement of a car as the absolute difference between the spot where a car ultimately parks and its preferred spot. Displacement multisets encode the displacements for cars with nonzero displacement. We provide formulas for the number of backgammon parking functions with a fixed displacement multiset of cardinality at most $2$, as well as for the number of Monopoly parking functions whose displacement multiset is a given singleton set. We conclude with some directions for further research.

papers.title: Unveiling the Complex high-pressure phases of Sodium at the Melting Curve Minimum via Data-Drive Crystal Structure Prediction
papers.abstract: Sodium exhibits a remarkable concentration of complex crystalline phases near its melting-curve minimum, yet the atomic arrangements of several experimentally observed phases remain unresolved. Here, we combine CALYPSO crystal structure prediction with Deep Potential models developed through concurrent learning to explore this structural landscape. Searches over more than 1.6 million configurations recover the previously reported $I4/m$ structure of $tI50$ and identify candidate atomic arrangements for $oC120$ and $aP90$, together with three additional low-enthalpy structures, $tI52$, $oP72$, and $oP92$. The proposed candidates reproduce key features of the experimentally indexed cell geometries. First-principles enthalpy calculations, Gibbs free-energy comparisons, and solid--liquid coexistence simulations reveal close competition among these structures and established sodium phases. Near the calculated reference melting minimum, $tI50$ is favored over $cI16$ and $oP8$, whereas $oC120$ and $aP90$ remain closely competitive, with their relative stability sensitive to model accuracy. These results provide testable structural models for unresolved experimental phases and reveal multiple closely competing low-enthalpy configurations near sodium's melting minimum

papers.title: Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay
papers.abstract: Biological neural networks (like the hippocampus) can internally generate "replay" resembling stimulus-driven activity. Recent computational models of replay use noisy recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained to path-integrate. Replay in these networks is described as Langevin sampling, but this theory alone fails to capture the environmental exploration and temporal compression observed in real biological replay. To close this gap, we re-examine spontaneous noisy RNN activity ("replay") as Langevin sampling, one timestep at a time, from a time-series distribution resembling lived experiences (unlike previous works which defined sampling as Monte Carlo inference over a static distribution). We provide a normative second-order Langevin sampling framework wherein spike-frequency adaptation drives spatial exploration at the cost of speed, and momentum via dendritic input differentiation drives temporal compression. We numerically verify our framework via simulations of noisy RNNs trained on 2D triangular and T-maze navigation activity, and others trained on place cell activity of synthetic rats. Crucially, we observe that simultaneous adaptation and momentum increases both replay exploration and speed, and provide one of the first accounts for biologically plausible temporal compression in rate-based RNN replay. Our findings encourage experiments into whether dendritic input differentiation, or other mechanisms, may support temporal compression in memory circuits like the hippocampus.

papers.title: Logarithmic Potential and its Applications in Conformal Geometry
papers.abstract: We establish an intrinsic characterization of the end invariants $ν_i$ in the Chern--Gauss--Bonnet formula for complete, simply connected, locally conformally flat 4-manifolds with non-negative scalar curvature and $Q$-curvature non-negative outside a compact set. For each end $M_i$, we show that $ν_i$ is the cube root of its normalized asymptotic geodesic-ball volume growth: \[ ν_i=\left(\lim_{r\to\infty} \frac{V_g(B_r(p)\cap M_i)}{(π^2/2)r^4}\right)^{1/3}. \] This characterization uses only the Riemannian distance and volume of $g$; it is independent of the base point $p$, the choice of compact truncation of the end, and any conformal coordinates. The proof is based on asymptotic radial symmetry of the logarithmic potential outside a sparse $\mathscr{E}$-set, inspired by Hayman's work \cite{hayman1960slowly}, together with comparisons of radial lengths and geodesic distances.

papers.title: Active sensing as control over sensory acquisition
papers.abstract: The term "active sensing" is used across neuroscience and engineering to describe a wide range of sensing behaviors, but there is no consensus on what makes sensing "active." We propose that the behaviors grouped under this label are better understood as forms of control over sensory acquisition and develop a framework that distinguishes three interacting forms of control. Mechanistic control physically structures sensory input, strategic control modulates sensing in closed loop through adaptive and attentional processes, and agentic control concerns the sensing policies available to an agent and its authority to choose among them. These forms of control can occur separately or in combination, and have distinct consequences for sensory input, perception, behavior, and performance. The framework clarifies active-passive comparisons and provides a common basis for analyzing biological, engineered, and hybrid sensing systems by asking what is controlled, how, and by whom.

papers.title: G-Wave: Bit-to-Waveform Generation for Adaptive Wireless Communications
papers.abstract: Wireless waveforms are traditionally hand-designed for general propagation conditions, rather than adapted to each specific environment. Existing neural transceivers seek such adaptation, but often rely on relatively simple architectures with limited long-range modeling capability. More expressive Transformer-based generative architectures are difficult to apply directly because wireless communication demands extremely accurate bit recovery, often with BER below 0.1%, while providing no ground-truth waveform supervision. To address these limitations, we introduce G-Wave, a channel-conditioned generative transceiver that directly synthesizes environment-adaptive physical time-domain waveforms from bits. G-Wave consists of Transformer-based transmitter and receiver models equipped with a multiscale architecture that combines long-range sequence modeling with fine-grained signal synthesis to meet the stringent precision required for communication. The two models are jointly optimized end-to-end using only bit-reconstruction error, allowing the waveform itself to be discovered without waveform labels. Across diverse 3GPP wireless environments, G-Wave achieves lower BER than the SOTA neural transceiver (DeepOFDM) and a strong conventional baseline (OFDM) under estimated channel information, reducing mean BER by 42.4% and 72.6%, respectively.

papers.title: Particle Belief Representations for Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
papers.abstract: Particle filters flexibly represent complex, multimodal beliefs but expose them as weighted, unordered sets incompatible with conventional fixed-dimensional policies. We study particle-belief encodings as inputs to reinforcement-learning policies while holding belief estimation and policy optimization fixed. We compare statistical summaries, cumulant-generating-function (CGF) features, and permutation-invariant set encoders. Trainable encoders are learned end-to-end or pretrained through belief reconstruction or task-specific prediction. Across eight tasks, pooling-based set encoders and gradient CGF features are reliable end-to-end, while the Set Transformer achieves the highest performance with appropriate pretraining. Task-specific pretraining helps when its target captures decision-relevant belief structure, whereas reconstruction pretraining and latent alignment provide more selective benefits. For selecting and training particle-belief encoders in partially observable Markov decision processes, our results show that an encoding that reconstructs the belief well is not necessarily a good input for control.

papers.title: Trusted Advice for Scheduling on Unrelated Machines
papers.abstract: Scheduling on unrelated parallel machines under standard objectives, such as makespan minimization or max-min fairness, has posed fundamental theoretical challenges for decades. A prominent example is the longstanding factor 2 approximation barrier for the Min Makespan problem established by Lenstra, Shmoys, and Tardos (1990). We investigate these fundamental challenges within the framework of algorithms with trusted advice. We consider a setting in which a trusted oracle is accessed once and reveals partial but entirely accurate structural information about an optimal solution. This framework allows us to quantify the improvements in approximation guarantees enabled by various trusted advice. We formalize a hierarchy of trusted advice oracles, ranging from a strong oracle that reveals the exact assignments of long jobs to a weaker oracle that indicates only which machines process such jobs. By exploiting this information, we obtain approximation guarantees beyond the classical worst-case barriers. In particular, we show that even the weakest oracle improves the approximation ratio for Min Makespan to $\sqrt{3}\approx 1.732$. We also obtain improved ratios of $(\sqrt{33}+1)/4\approx 1.686$ and $(5\sqrt{7})/8 \approx 1.654$ for Restricted Assignment and Graph Balancing, respectively. For the max-min fairness objective, known as the Santa Claus problem, we obtain a 2-approximation using our weak oracle. Finally, we show that these problems remain NP-hard to approximate within certain constant factors even with the trusted advice oracles considered. Interestingly, for the Santa Claus problem, we show a lower bound of 2 which is tight and matches the classical oracle-free bound.

papers.title: Reparameterizing Your Object Detectors for Weight Space Programming
papers.abstract: Weight-Space Programming (WSP) edits network weights without backpropagation, yet directly editing converged object detectors stalls or collapses because set prediction penalizes duplicate boxes as false positives while compact parameterizations trap weights in an isotropic Euclidean minimum. We propose Inverse-Reparameterized Object-Detection WSP (IR-ODWSP), lifting detector layers via exact function-preserving operators (E, C) into decoupled moment, 2D-DCT, PCA, and Stiefel-Procrustes subspaces. Solving winner-exclusive updates and folding back (Delta Params=0%, Delta FLOPs=0%) induces an anisotropic Riemannian metric, improving all 26/26 MS COCO settings across 17 YOLO26, EdgeCrafter, and RF-DETR detectors (up to +0.31 APs), +1.42 mAP cross-basin COCO-O, zeroimage repair (+2.95 mAP), and label-free weather adaptation (+2.79 AP). Without retraining, IR-ODWSP supports -100% to +100% latency budgets across bridged contraction, 1.00x folding, dynamic (IR-ODWSP-DYN), and static (IR-ODWSP-SG) graphs: -10% retains 51.62 AP / 33.48 mAP, while positive budgets scale monotonically (+0.30 AP at +10%, +1.12 on RF-DETR-N; 54.83 AP at +100%; 55.91 AP / 35.44 mAP in IR-ODWSP+). Source code is released at https://github.com/WongKinYiu/ODWSP.

papers.title: An eight-channel RFSoC waveform digitizer with AC- and DC-coupled front ends and transparent dual-DDR event memory
papers.abstract: We present Transparent Dual-DDR Event Memory (TDEM) for the triggered readout of an eight-channel radio-frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) digitizer. With either an AC- or a DC-coupled front end, each accepted trigger records 4096 samples per channel at 5 GSa/s. Two pulses 100 ns apart produced separate, overlapping records. On one DC-coupled input, interleaving calibration reduced an eight-sample periodic residual by a factor of 29 at +100 mV, but not at zero input. After a power cycle, the digitizer restored the coefficients for all eight DC-coupled inputs without a training tone. TDEM assigns complete events to 64- and 32-bit DDR4 memory interfaces in a 2:1 ratio. With this allocation alone, host page requests still determined which memory served each read. In two runs of approximately 6 s at 160 kHz, the peak receiver backlog fell from 20 140 events with the earlier readout to 1457 with event-level prefetch. Prefetch raised the sustained rate of the DC-coupled system from 150 to 170 kHz under repeated host readout pauses. With the same receiver design and a revised host buffer allocation, the AC-coupled system passed three 30 min tests at 175 kHz, each with 48 readout pauses and no rejected triggers. Without imposed pauses or background load, the host verified all 323 452 631 events in 30 min at 179.7 kHz. At 180 kHz, triggers were first rejected at the digitizer, consistent with a modelled transmitter capacity of 179.730 kHz for this event format.

papers.title: Infrared Relaxation Modes and the Emergence of Collective Order in Neural Dynamics
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic field theory of collective order formation in interacting nonlinear neural systems. Integrating out microscopic neural degrees of freedom yields an effective action whose quadratic kernel determines the ordering threshold, while higher-order connected responses govern nonlinear stabilization. Spectral decomposition reveals that relaxation rates and collective-mode overlaps control collective instability and memory dynamics. Enhanced infrared spectral weight lowers the critical coupling and generates long-time memory, revealing a common spectral origin of collective ordering and persistent dynamics. Controlled numerical constructions verify the spectral dependence of collective instability and response, while nonlinear mean-field scaling follows from the microscopic Landau expansion. Transformer Jacobian spectra further reveal learning-induced infrared organization and transient memory enhancement consistent with critical-like response. Our results establish a microscopic framework linking neural interactions, collective order, and long-time memory.

papers.title: Topological Pharmacokinetics: A Model-Free Framework for Quantifying the Shape of Concentration-Time Curves
papers.abstract: Pharmacokinetic analysis compresses concentration-time curves into scalar summaries (non-compartmental analysis, NCA) or pre-specified compartmental models, approaches that are either model-free but shape-blind or shape-sensitive but structure-dependent. We introduce Topological Pharmacokinetics (TPK), a framework that reads curve shape directly from data without committing to any model. TPK delay-embeds each curve into a state-space trajectory and applies persistent homology to extract a nine-component topological invariant: multi-scale shape descriptors (peak hierarchy, secondary-peak isolation, loop structure) with established perturbation-stability properties. We evaluate the framework on four layers of increasing realism. Monophasic linear systems generate no spurious cyclic signals, whereas double-site absorption and enterohepatic recirculation produce distinct loop signatures; 12 nonlinear scenarios resolve as curvature-without-cycles; a weak endogenous rhythm survives superposition with a large exogenous drug signal (inter-peak interval recovered at exactly 24 h); and loop detection stays stable to 10 percent of Cmax additive noise and to sampling thinned to 7 points. As clinical proof of concept, we apply the same pipeline to 15 mycophenolic acid profiles digitized from a published kidney-transplant study. The secondary-persistence ratio associates with ex vivo gut-microbiome reactivation at Spearman rho = 0.815 (p = 0.0002, q = 0.002), whereas the tested exposure metrics show weak, nonsignificant associations (rho <= 0.38). Analyses are fully automated and reproducible; code and data are public. TPK is proposed as a complementary, model-free, shape-sensitive layer alongside NCA and model-based methods.

papers.title: Explicit Response Formulae and Request Problem for Smooth Expanding Endomorphisms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the higher order differentiability of physical measures, in the category of smooth expanding endomorphisms of compact manifolds, and we establish the explicit response formulae of any order. The proof is based on the elegant Keller-Liverani-Gouëzel perturbation theory of transfer operators. Furthermore, we provide the solutions to the high order request problem, which is regarded as the inverse problem to response formulae, that is, we make perturbations to realize prescribed responses up to any finite order, and we establish the existence of minimizers for a relaxed optimization problem associated with suitable cost functionals.

papers.title: Towards Agentic Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
papers.abstract: Video corpus moment retrieval (VCMR) requires finding the video and time interval that match a text query in a corpus of videos. We present RELAY, a training-free framework for VCMR that shares memory across queries. RELAY processes a batch of queries in three stages: search with a query bank, ranking with video notes, and localization with video prompt caching. In the search stage, an embedding model scores each video by its best-matching frame. The query bank penalizes videos that score highly for many other queries in the batch. In the ranking stage, a vision-language model (VLM) writes notes on each candidate video's scenes, people, objects, and actions once. Then, a large language model (LLM) reranks the candidates from these notes. In the localization stage, a VLM predicts the time interval of the moment in the top-ranked video. When multiple queries select the same video, prompt caching lets the VLM reuse its frames. On the three VERIFIED benchmarks, RELAY outperforms the trained baselines in video retrieval R@1 without training. Without any labeled moment, its predicted intervals are shorter than the annotated ones. In VCMR, it achieves similar performance to VideoSearch-R1 on one benchmark and trails it at IoU 0.5 on the other two. Human annotators also mark shorter moments than the original annotations of the benchmarks. A single margin, calibrated on a few labeled queries, widens the predicted interval to the annotation convention of the benchmarks. With it, RELAY outperforms the trained baselines in VCMR at IoU 0.5.

papers.title: Weight Averaging at Small Budgets Confounds Formula-Labeled Pretraining in Microstructure-Property Regression: A Pre-Specified Study with Post Hoc Rechecks
papers.abstract: Closed-form physics formulas can label synthetic microstructures at no cost, so supervised pretraining on those labels is an alternative to self-supervised pretraining when labels are scarce. One pre-specified protocol tests this on two public simulated benchmarks, two-phase conductivity and short-fiber stiffness: a ConvNeXt-Small is pretrained on 150,000 synthetic images by formula regression or masked reconstruction and fine-tuned on 100, 400, or 1,600 labels. Five fine-tuning seeds from one formula checkpoint have mean residual correlations of 0.994 (conductivity) and 0.999 (stiffness). On conductivity the formula network compresses its predictions (slope 0.64) and has four times the 400-label error of ImageNet initialization. Two confounds interact: the generator renders the low-conductivity phase with the opposite contrast polarity, and the exponential moving average (EMA; decay 0.995, no bias correction) still holds 16% of the initial weights after the 400-label schedule. Without the EMA the slope is 0.97, and over three subsets and five seeds the mismatched checkpoint has 1.4 times the ImageNet error (0.0119 versus 0.0084). Three pretraining runs per polarity leave the comparison inconclusive: matched means (0.0086, 0.0111, 0.0118) fall below mismatched means (0.0119, 0.0120, 0.0123) in aggregate (0.0105 versus 0.0121) but overlap on two of three subsets, and the matched spread (0.0032) exceeds the mismatched spread (0.0004). On stiffness without the EMA, formula pretraining lowers the 100-label error by 18% versus ImageNet over five seeds, including a re-initialized head, while ImageNet seeds also correlate at 0.992. Weight averages that start at the pretrained weights can dominate small-budget comparisons and should be rechecked at the last weights.

papers.title: Sondheimer oscillations in Weyl semimetal films
papers.abstract: In conducting films subject to an out-of-plane magnetic field, electron motion between the surfaces gives rise to conductance oscillations periodic in magnetic field, known as Sondheimer oscillations. While this size effect has been investigated in conventional metals, its dependence on the Berry curvature of topological materials remains less explored. In this work, we extend the semiclassical Boltzmann description of Sondheimer oscillations to type-I Weyl semimetal films. We account for the Berry curvature, the orbital magnetic moment and the effect of the Zeeman coupling on the Fermi wavevector and the electronic group velocity. The Berry curvature and the orbital magnetic moment generate a beating pattern and chirping in the Sondheimer oscillations. In the thick-film and thin-film regimes, we provide analytical expressions for the longitudinal conductivity, which highlight the interplay between electronic band topology and boundary-scattering in magnetotransport.

papers.title: Escriba-OCR: A 1B Vision-Language Model for Error-Preserving Transcription of Handwritten Portuguese Essays
papers.abstract: Feedback tools and research on learner writing need transcriptions of handwritten essays that keep exactly what the student wrote: misspellings, line breaks, struck-through words and insertions. Vision-language models (VLMs) read handwriting well, but they also tend to rewrite it into correct language. We measure this on BRESSAY, 1,000 handwritten Brazilian Portuguese essays, with a benchmark that adds error preservation, invented errors, edit-markup precision and recall and line structure to the character error rate (CER) and uses paired bootstrap confidence intervals. We restrict the study to open-weight models that schools can run on their own hardware. Of 22 open baselines, the best, Qwen3-VL 235B-A22B, reaches 5.6% CER on the 199 test pages; none reproduces the edit markup reliably, and every VLM replaces 39-78% of the words absent from a Portuguese dictionary with dictionary words. We fine-tune LightOnOCR-3-1B on the 647 training pages in 85 minutes on one GPU. The resulting Escriba-OCR-1B reaches 2.06% CER, 3.5 points below the best baseline (95% CI [-4.2, -2.9]); under the ICDAR 2024 competition metric it reaches 2.1% CER, below the best published page-level results (2.2-2.4%). It recovers 67% of insertions and 77% of illegible deletions, and reproduces the line structure of 97% of the pages, but still normalises 60% of likely misspellings. Three seeds agree within 0.04 CER points, and quantised to 4 bits the model runs on an ordinary CPU at about one minute per page. On 40 letters of another corpus it matches its base model (without that model's appended comments) but misreads unseen words more often; weight interpolation recovers half the gap. A teacher's review finds that 45% of the judgeable apparent corrections are errors in the BRESSAY ground truth, so dictionary-based scores likely understate preservation. We release the model, the benchmark code and the review data.

papers.title: ProMix: Efficient Data Mixture Optimization for Robotic Imitation via Proxy-Reference DRO
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel in open-world manipulation, yet their performance often saturates when training data are naively pooled across heterogeneous robots, tasks, and environments. Distributionally robust data mixture optimization, exemplified by Re-Mix, can recover much of this performance, but its weight search requires training full-scale policies twice on the entire corpus, placing it out of reach for most laboratories. We present ProMix, a compute-efficient instantiation of the proxy-reference DRO recipe for robotic imitation learning: a 15M-parameter proxy learns per-domain sampling weights by minimizing worst-case excess loss against a frozen reference model, and the learned weights transfer, without re-tuning, to VLA backbones up to 7B parameters. We further provide, to our knowledge, the first controlled analysis of the reference model's role in robotic DRO, showing that removing it induces over-pessimism toward noisy, low-quality domains (-3.8% average and -14.3% worst-domain success rate), and that entropy regularization is needed to prevent weight collapse. Evaluated on 9500 real-world episodes from the Open-X Embodiment dataset, ProMix improves the average success rate over uniform mixing from 68.4% to 76.2%, matching Re-Mix within evaluation noise while reducing mixture-optimization cost to a backbone-independent 11 GPU-hours - versus 16 GPU-hours at the 50M comparison scale and 192 GPU-hours at 7B for full-scale searches - with a +17.1% absolute gain on the worst-case domain.

papers.title: Trajectory Visibility at First Sight
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a simple polygon with $n$ vertices, and let two moving entities $q(t)$ and $r(t)$ travel at constant (possibly distinct) speeds $v_q$ and $v_r$ along line-segment trajectories $τ_q$ and $τ_r$ inside $P$. We study the first-visibility time $ t^* = \min\bigl\{\,t \ge 0 \mid \overline{q(t)\,r(t)} \subseteq P\,\bigr\}, $ the earliest moment at which the segment joining $q(t)$ and $r(t)$ lies entirely within $P$. Prior work by Eades et al.~\cite{swat2020,eeades-phd} focused on the decision version of this question in a simple polygon. They gave a one-shot decision algorithm running in ${O}(n)$ time. For a stationary entity and a moving one, they gave a data structure with ${O}(n \log n)$ preprocessing time and ${O}(n)$ space that answers decision queries in ${O}(\log n)$ time. For two moving entities, after ${O}(n \log^5 n)$ preprocessing time, they built a data structure of size ${O}(n \log^5 n)$ with ${O}(n^{3/4}\log^3 n)$ query time. Variants for polygonal domains with holes or when entities cross the boundary of $P$ lie beyond our scope. In this work, we go beyond decision to compute $t^*$ exactly under three models for a simple polygon $P$. When both trajectories are fixed in advance, we preprocess $P$ in ${O}(n)$ time and space and answer each query $(v_q, v_r)$ in ${O}(\log n)$ time. If one trajectory $τ_r$ is fixed while $τ_q$ is given as a query, we build a structure in ${O}(n \log n)$ time and space that computes $t^*$ in ${O}(\log^2 n)$ time per query. When neither trajectory is known in advance, we develop a data structure with ${O}(n^{1+\varepsilon})$ expected preprocessing time and ${O}(n)$ space that achieves ${O}(n^{1/2}\,\text{polylog}(n))$ expected query time for any fixed $\varepsilon > 0$.

papers.title: Which Layer to Trust? Layer Selection in Frozen Speech Encoders for Singing-Voice Deepfake Detection under Signal Corruption
papers.abstract: Frozen self-supervised speech encoders have been frequently used for audio deepfake detection. However, the layers are usually chosen from a development set. We examine this choice for singing-voice deepfake detection on CtrSVDD. We train one detection head per layer, plus a learned layer mix, on frozen XEUS (3-4 seeds) and XLS-R (2 seeds). We test on clean audio and under noise, reverberation and lossy coding. On clean audio, the middle layers beat the last layer in both encoders and the learned mix does not beat the best single layer. The layer chosen on the development set is 2.3 (XEUS) and 4.1 (XLS-R) percentage points of EER worse than the best test layer. Under noise and coding, XEUS's best layers stay in the middle, while under reverberation its upper layers catch up, whereas XLS-R's best layer moves shallower. In an exploratory analysis, XEUS detects a commercial synthesis attack best with an earlier layer, especially under noise. The layer therefore cannot be chosen reliably on an in-domain development set and clean audio alone.

papers.title: Deep Discriminative Feature Fusion of Convolutional and Attention-Based Recurrent Representations for Subject-Independent ECG Stress Recognition
papers.abstract: Stress has become a significant concern because of its negative impact on both physical and mental health and therefore drives the need for reliable automated systems to assess stress levels. Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals provide a non-invasive and objective measure of physiological stress responses and have emerged as a promising modality for continuous stress monitoring. While deep learning techniques have achieved encouraging results in ECG-based stress detection, many studies focus only on one type of feature representation, and therefore limit their ability to capture both the morphological patterns and temporal dynamics embedded in ECG signals. To address this limitation, in this paper, we propose three deep learning-based feature fusion frameworks for ECG-based stress classification. These are Residual Feature Fusion (RFF), Bidirectional Feature-Wise Cross-Attention Fusion (BFCAF), and a novel Cross-Attention Residual Fusion (CARF) framework that combines the strengths of residual learning and bidirectional cross-attention within a unified architecture. A 1D Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) and a BiLSTM-Attention network are used to extract complementary morphological and temporal representations from ECG signals, respectively. The proposed fusion frameworks leverage these heterogeneous representations to improve feature interaction, information preservation, and stress discrimination. The proposed frameworks are evaluated using subject-independent Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross-Validation (LOSOCV) on the RML and WESAD datasets for three-class stress classification. Experimental results show that the proposed feature fusion methods consistently improve performance over individual CNN and BiLSTM models, with CARF achieving the highest accuracies of 83.1% and 77.91% on the RML and WESAD datasets, respectively.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Classifiers for Lightweight IoT Intrusion Detection Using Feature Reduction
papers.abstract: Machine learning-based intrusion detection systems can improve IoT security, but high-dimensional traffic features and imbalanced datasets may reduce model reliability and deployment feasibility in resource-constrained environments. This study presents a lightweight binary IoT intrusion detection framework using an approximately balanced CICIoT2023 derived dataset, feature reduction, and comparative machine learning evaluation. The original multi-class attack labels were converted into two classes: Benign and Malicious. To reduce class bias, malicious traffic was randomly undersampled to obtain an approximately balanced binary dataset. Information Gain Ratio and Gini Decrease were then used to rank traffic features and generate reduced feature subsets of 38, 30, 20, 10, 5, and 3 features. Five machine learning classifiers, including Random Forest(RF), Decision Tree(DT), Naive Bayes(NB), Logistic Regression(LR), and Support Vector Machine(SVM), were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. The results show that Random Forest achieved the strongest overall performance. In particular,the 20-feature subset achieved accuracy of 99.1% and MCC of 0.982, matching the full-feature model while reducing feature dimensionality by approximately 47.4%. The 10-feature subset also maintained strong performance with accuracy of 98.9% and MCC of 0.979, reducing the feature space by approximately 73.7%. These findings demonstrate that balanced binary classification and progressive feature reduction can preserve detection effectiveness while improving lightweight IDS feasibility.

papers.title: Arcadian: Open-Source Humanoid Ecosystem for Accessible and Customizable Research and Education
papers.abstract: Reproducing and modifying a meter-scale humanoid remains challenging for research and teaching groups with limited fabrication resources and engineering support. This paper presents Arcadian, an open-source humanoid ecosystem that offers accessible and customizable humanoid hardware and software with community support. Arcadian aims to strike a balance among cost-effectiveness, structural durability, and full customizability, lowering the barrier to entry for research and education. Specifically, this meter-scale humanoid adopts metal-embedded 3D printing to achieve a high strength-to-cost ratio, eliminating the need for computer numerical control (CNC) machining while retaining design flexibility. Extensive simulation and hardware tests validate the design: a reinforcement-learning (RL) locomotion policy trained in simulation transfers to the hardware, and a virtual reality (VR) teleoperation interface drives both arms for simple manipulation tasks. The robot is around one meter tall and costs approximately $6,800 to build. All computer-aided design (CAD) models, the bill of materials, assembly documentation, and training and deployment code are publicly released, distributed through Tnkr.ai and MakerWorld and supported by a Discord server and a project forum through which community feedback informs design updates. The ecosystem resources are available at https://anonymous-humanoid.gitbook.io/docs.

papers.title: FL-CsLoc-DH: A Federated Learning-Based Crowdsensing Localization under Dual Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Mobile Crowdsensing (MCS) provides a scalable way to collect indoor fingerprints and reduce professional calibration effort. To protect the location privacy of participating clients, Federated Learning (FL) is used so that raw fingerprints and measurement trajectories remain local. However, owing to the open and uncontrollable nature of MCS, participating clients collect fingerprints in different propagation environments and possess unequal labeling availability. These conditions jointly cause data and annotation heterogeneity, which degrades FL-based crowdsensing localization. In this work, we propose FL-CsLoc-DH, a federated semi-supervised learning framework for crowdsensing localization under dual heterogeneity. FL-CsLoc-DH coordinates Two-Stage Noisy Gradient Rejection (TS-NGR), Soft Fisher Confidence Alignment (S-FCA), and Trajectory-Smoothed Model Averaging (T-SMA) throughout localization model learning. TS-NGR suppresses unreliable client updates caused jointly by environment dependent data shifts and noisy pseudo labels. S-FCA limits parameter increments dominated by unlabeled data, thereby alleviating annotation heterogeneity during local training. T-SMA smooths the aggregated global localization model trajectory to reduce drift induced by data heterogeneity. Experiment results show that the three mechanisms provide complementary improvements in localization accuracy under the MCS environment while retaining raw client data locally.

papers.title: Sharp integral Ricci pinching on manifolds with positive total scalar curvature
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a closed connected Riemannian three-manifold with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$, and assume that $M$ is not diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We prove the sharp integral Ricci pinching inequality $$\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{6}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2.$$ Moreover, equality holds if and only if $(M,g)$ is locally isometric to $\mathbb{S}^2(a)\times\mathbb{R}$ for some $a>0$. By the same method, we prove $\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{12}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2$ on closed four-manifolds with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$ that have a finite cover with positive first Betti number, and we provide a new proof of Gursky's inequality. We also show that the corresponding inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq 5$, and we give a metric on $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1$ that disproves a conjecture of Ge, Li and Lian.

papers.title: Characterizing Frozen SSL Encoders and Backends for Cross-Domain Speech Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) encoders are the dominant front end for speech deepfake detection, and the prevailing recipe fine-tunes the full encoder on a small spoofing corpus, maximizing in-domain accuracy at the cost of known degradation under domain shift. Taking a recent cross-attention fusion of SSL and constant-Q cepstral features as a fixed reference recipe, we freeze its encoder and ask which encoder and which backend behave best across domains. We cross two frozen encoders, the massively multilingual XEUS and Wav2Vec2 XLSR-53, with two backends, multi-head factorized attentive (MHFA) pooling and AASIST, and evaluate on ASVspoof 2019 LA, ASVspoof 2021 LA and DF, In-the-Wild (ITW), and ASVspoof 5, training every system in one pipeline over three seeds. We report three findings. First, encoder and backend interact: MHFA suits the stronger encoder, while AASIST recovers more from and stabilizes the weaker one. Second, within this recipe, the frozen encoder produces large, repeatable differences. With MHFA, frozen XEUS lowers error relative to frozen XLSR-53 by 58-77% on LA21, DF21, and ASV5, and more modestly on ITW. This ordering persists in a matched-aggregation ablation, and a capacity-matched WavLM Large diagnostic shows that parameter count alone does not explain XLSR-53's weaker performance. Third, against a three-seed fine-tuned baseline, frozen XEUS updates under 0.4M parameters versus 316M, wins on ASVspoof 5 (in EER and min-DCF) and modestly on LA21, trails on DF21 and ITW, and shows lower seed variation on three of the four out-of-domain sets.

papers.title: Grothendieck--Serre for quasi-split groups over two-dimensional regular local rings
papers.abstract: We prove the Grothendieck--Serre conjecture for quasi-split reductive group schemes over two-dimensional regular local rings, that is, every generically trivial torsor under a quasi-split group scheme $G$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension two is trivial. Our main result is new when $R$ is ramified and generalizes Nisnevich's result by removing the assumption that the residue field is infinite. By formal patching of torsors and valuative criteria, we are reduced to showing a product formula when $G$ is semisimple and simply connected. Then, we take advantage of relative simple reflections and relative Bruhat decomposition to prove a generation by rank-one subgroups. The analysis on Dynkin diagrams with Galois actions reduces us to $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and three-dimensional $\operatorname{SU}$ factors. For the special unitary case, we treat Hermitian forms by using stabilizations and cancellation to finish the proof.

papers.title: Sharp constant off-diagonal extrapolation for Muckenhoupt bases
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a sharp constant version of off-diagonal extrapolation for matrix weights, improving the result we proved in an earlier paper. In an appendix, we give a new and simpler proof of this result in the scalar case.

papers.title: Exceptional Rays of Invariant Processes on Trees
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an ergodic, non-constant random process on the $d$-regular tree $T_d$, with marginal distribution $X$. We prove that there always exist "exceptional" rays, whose asymptotic means are at least $\mathbb{E}(X)+δ$; furthermore, for edge processes, $δ> 0$ can be taken to depend only on the law of $X$. We compare different definitions of "maximal asymptotic means", relating them to different notions of speed of tree-indexed random walks.

papers.title: Where does pancreatic lesion segmentation fail on public CT? An attenuation-stratified analysis of a duct-guided pipeline on PanTS
papers.abstract: Lesion segmentation is a building block of most CT pipelines for pancreatic cancer detection, yet lesion overlap scores stay low. Instead of proposing a new architecture, we report where an end-to-end pipeline fails on a large public dataset. On PanTS we built a three-stage pipeline: pancreas segmentation, maps of the main pancreatic duct (MPD) and common bile duct (CBD), and a lesion model that receives the CT with or without the predicted duct maps. Both lesion models were trained identically on 4007 scans and evaluated once on 737 held-out test scans (127 with a lesion) under a comparison rule fixed before the test run. Lesion Dice was 0.213 with duct maps and 0.209 with CT only (paired difference +0.004, 95% CI -0.011 to +0.019). The duct maps raised the share of lesions touched by a prediction (+0.079, 95% CI +0.024 to +0.134) but also enlarged predictions in lesion-free scans, and lesion-like regions were predicted in all lesion-free test scans. Out of fold, keeping only the predicted components that touched the lesion raised Dice only from 0.285 to 0.309; the loss came mainly from the extent of correctly located predictions. Clearly hypoattenuating lesions, which intensity alone separates from normal pancreas, had the lowest coverage (median 16.6%). From the predicted maps alone, the MPD diameter separated lesion from lesion-free test scans with AUC 0.794 (95% CI 0.747 to 0.839), while the CBD diameter was weak (AUC 0.603) and added nothing. Code for training, inference and evaluation is publicly available.

papers.title: Cylindrical dimers and monomial immanants
papers.abstract: For a bipartite graph on a cylinder, group its perfect matchings by homological height and sum their weights in each group. We prove that every minor of the resulting Toeplitz matrix has nonnegative coefficients in the edge weights, settling a question recorded by Lai. We first prove conjectures of Galashin and the author concerning directed cycles in cylindrical networks, and then deduce the dimer theorem from them. A related, stronger positivity property for superpositions of cylindrical matchings turns out to be equivalent to Stembridge's interval-product conjecture on monomial immanants. Using annular webs, we prove this conjecture for partitions with at most four columns. A stretching argument extends this to all partitions with parts in $\{n,2n,3n,4n\}$.

papers.title: Semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash on H5N1 One Health questions
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) has re-emerged as a One Health concern since 2024, and the public is increasingly consulting large-language-model (LLM) chatbots for health information during outbreaks. Before a chatbot's accuracy can be meaningfully assessed, its consistency must first be understood, so that any single response can be trusted as a fair representative of the model's behavior. We characterized the semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 (OpenAI) and Gemini 3 Flash (Google) on 15 H5N1 One Health questions sourced from social media discourse by adopting and extending a centroid-based evaluation framework. Each question was submitted 30 times and reformulated using five Chain-of-Thought (CoT) variants with 30 runs each, yielding 5,400 responses. Pairwise cosine similarity was computed on MPNet embeddings, with sensitivity analyses across three additional transformers. Statistical inference combined standard nonparametric tests (paired Wilcoxon and Friedman with Holm--Bonferroni correction) with inter-embedding agreement statistics (ICC(2,k) and Cronbach's $α$) introduced here as a methodological addition. Both models produced high mean consistency (0.93--0.97, rescaled to {[}0, 1{]}). GPT-5 showed reproducibility significantly higher than repeatability (W = 3.0, p = 0.0003), whereas for Gemini 3 Flash the two metrics were statistically indistinguishable (W = 42.0, p = 0.33). Differential Diagnosis ranked among the top two CoT framings for consistency in both models. The tested chatbots behave as semantically stable sources on H5N1 One Health questions, and the developed consistency evaluation framework is portable to other domains.

papers.title: Electric polarizabilities with phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: While projector quantum Monte Carlo methods are known for producing accurate ground-state energies, the prediction of other properties that encode the electronic response to applied electric and magnetic fields has historically been challenging. In this work we demonstrate that the electric (static) polarizability tensor, which is formally a second-derivative of the energy with respect to electric fields, can be efficiently computed with phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo using a correlated sampling finite-difference strategy. With simple Hartree-Fock trial wave functions, we investigate a series of small molecules (some of which are difficult for approximate density functionals), polyacenes of increasing size, and ferrocene as a representative organometallic complex. The methodology is scalable to relatively large molecules involving thousands of basis functions, and with appropriate trial wave functions remains robust for strongly correlated electronic states, as we show for the stretched dinitrogen molecule. This work opens the door to the computation of a host of other second-order molecular properties with auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo, which will inform the ongoing search for optimal trial wave functions and extend benchmark-quality training data sets for the refinement of semi-empirical and machine learning models for quantum chemistry and molecular simulation.

papers.title: Context-Aware Proactive Self-Adaptation: A Two-Layer Model Predictive Control Approach
papers.abstract: In self-adaptive software systems, the role of context is paramount, especially for proactive self-adaptation. Current research, however, does not fully explore context's impact, for example on priorities of the requirements. To address this gap, we introduce a novel contextual goal model to capture these factors and their influence on the system. Using this, we propose a two-layer control mechanism with a context-aware model predictive control to achieve proactive adaptation for the software system and adaptation for the controller itself. By contextual prediction and a more accurate system model, our approach utilizes model predictive control to facilitate timely and efficient system adaptations, improving both performance and adaptability. Meanwhile, we perform requirement adaptation to update the contextual goal model, which in turn updates the objective function and constraints of the controller. Our experimental evaluations across two scenarios demonstrate the significant benefits of our approach in enhancing system performance.

papers.title: World Models Are the Right Foundation for Simulating Mars Terraforming
papers.abstract: Terraforming Mars is a long-horizon, action-conditioned control problem that requires predicting atmospheric responses to interventions over centuries to identify effective policies. This position paper argues that physics-regularized recurrent state-space world models are the most promising foundation for this setting. Data-driven climate emulators lack action-conditioning, and physics-based general circulation models (GCMs) are too expensive for policy search. Among learned world models, recurrent state-space architectures with physics constraints are better suited than transformer-based alternatives: they provide native uncertainty quantification through their stochastic-deterministic decomposition, remain stable under sparse non-terrestrial training data, and enforce physical consistency at each rollout step. To make this position concrete, we describe a potential architecture combining JEPA-inspired latent encoding, universal differential equation constraints, and a Dreamer-lineage planning head. We also introduce MarsWorld, an open benchmark proposal for intervention-conditioned planetary world models, and discuss broader implications and objections.

papers.title: Global classification and local asymptotics for a Monge-Ampère obstacle problem
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq2$ and $0<q<n$. We prove that every nontrivial convex entire solution of $$\det D^2v = v^q, \quad v \geq 0, \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n$$ with bounded (possibly empty) coincidence set $\{v=0\}$ is affine equivalent to a radial solution. Together with the classification for unbounded coincidence sets by Jin-Tu-Xiong \cite{JTX2025}, this completes the classification of nontrivial nonnegative convex entire solutions. The proof uses an affine-invariant monotonicity formula extending the two-dimensional formula in Mooney-Sen \cite{MooneySen2026}. Combining this global classification with level-set parametrization and spectral analysis, we also obtain precise asymptotics of local solutions at isolated zeros, settling the remaining case, namely, a singleton free boundary, in the regularity theory for the Monge-Ampère obstacle problem studied in \cite{JTX2025}.

papers.title: Tight Query Depth of Recursive Randomized Greedy MIS
papers.abstract: The randomized greedy maximal independent set (RGMIS) algorithm processes vertices in a uniformly random order and greedily constructs an MIS. Its recursive formulation decides whether a vertex belongs to this MIS by querying lower-ranked neighbors in increasing rank order, stopping when a neighbor in the MIS is found. We prove that, on every $n$-vertex graph, this recursive algorithm has $O(\log n)$ query depth with high probability, even without memoization. The bound holds simultaneously for all starting vertices and is asymptotically tight even on bipartite graphs. The proof combines a bound on the total expected number of query paths with an exposure argument: paths with many two-edge shortcuts are unlikely, while the remaining paths admit sufficiently many applications of a two-hop probability bound.

papers.title: Landscape and Taxonomy of Prompt Engineering Patterns in Software Engineering
papers.abstract: Advancements in large language models (LLMs) have enhanced their ability to handle ambiguous user instructions. However, effective prompt patterns remain crucial for usability and comprehension. This article presents a taxonomy of prompt engineering patterns for software engineering. It is based on a systematic literature review that was conducted in early 2023, when LLMs still faced significant limitations in context length and inference capabilities. Our study explores techniques that enhance the usability and reliability of LLMs, emphasizing the ongoing importance of well-designed prompts in optimizing task performance. Our findings highlight the critical role of prompt patterns in maximizing LLM's potential, even as their capabilities continue to evolve.

papers.title: GlobalHRBench: Does Changing the Question Language Change the Legal Answer?
papers.abstract: Language matters when deploying LLM agents across borders, especially in law, where the governing rules must hold across working languages. Does changing the language of a legal question change answer accuracy? We introduce GlobalHRBench, pairing 240 employment-law problems across eight jurisdictions and eight languages while fixing facts, applicable law and required conclusions. We evaluate nine models on all 1,920 prompts in independent, closed-book, single-answer trials, scoring legal correctness, completeness and answer-language compliance. GPT-6.1 Sol leads at 76.2% strict passes, with a 5.8% relative best-to-worst language decline, compared with 42.2% for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Kimi K3.1 Pro and Claude Sonnet 5.5 reverse order between English and Chinese. A four-model study on 16 paired families compares closed-book answers with governing evidence, added cross-jurisdiction distractors and removal of a governing passage. Governing evidence corrects legal errors and shortens reasoning on recovered answers, yet recognizing an evidence gap does not ensure correct application of the rules that remain. These findings motivate multilingual training for accurate, efficient and evidence-supported answers, and deployment evaluation in the user's working language.

papers.title: LexiDet-OVD: Benchmarking Lexical Sensitivity in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary object detectors localize objects from free-form text prompts, but their reliability depends on how users describe the target. Standard evaluations usually test a fixed class name, leaving prompt-induced failure modes underexplored. We introduce LexiDet-OVD, a benchmark and metric suite for studying lexical sensitivity in open-vocabulary object detection. We organize prompt sets into equivalent, conditional, and broad semantic scopes, and evaluate four detector families on fixed COCO and LVIS samples, each covering 30 classes (800 held-out COCO images and 1,000 LVIS images). Beyond mean and worst-prompt AP50, we report P10, CVaR at 20%, leave-one-prompt-out influence, detection agreement, box consistency, and confidence variance using one-to-one multi-instance matching. Equivalent-prompt best-to-worst gaps range from 5.3 to 23.4 points on COCO1000 and from 5.1 to 29.9 points on LVIS1000-30c, showing that strong average accuracy and lexical stability are distinct properties. We compare maximum-score selection, weighted-box fusion, Prompt Consensus, and an exploratory fusion rule. Aggregation recovers performance in several settings, but no method dominates all model-dataset pairs. A controlled Detic/SHiNe comparison further shows that semantic hierarchy enrichment does not by itself eliminate lexical sensitivity. These results support reporting prompt-distribution robustness alongside conventional open-vocabulary detection accuracy.

papers.title: Ego2Wrist: Bootstrapping Wrist-View Synthesis from Egocentric Video
papers.abstract: Wrist cameras provide an action-centric view that is directly relevant to robot manipulation. However, collecting human wrist-camera videos at scale is challenging due to cumbersome setups that can interfere with natural hand movements. In contrast, head-mounted human egocentric videos are much easier to scale. We introduce Ego2Wrist, which synthesizes synchronized wrist-camera views from human egocentric videos and task descriptions. Trained on approximately 940 hours of paired head- and wrist-camera recordings, Ego2Wrist jointly generates three views. To evaluate generated wrist views without ground truth, we propose hand-centric cross-view consistency (HCC), which measures consistency between generated wrist views and corresponding hand regions in the input head view. HCC ranks model checkpoints comparably to ground-truth-based LPIPS, and human evaluators prefer HCC-selected generations in 77% of responses. Evaluated on four datasets, Ego2Wrist outperforms fine-tuned WorldWander, reducing LPIPS by 28% and receiving human preference in 76% of responses. More importantly, HCC facilitates recursive self-improvement on in-the-wild egocentric videos by selecting generated wrist views for further training. Generation quality progressively improves over three rounds. These results demonstrate a scalable approach to generating real-world wrist-view human manipulation videos for robot policy training.

papers.title: A Positron Spectral Dip near 20 GV in Selected Orbital Projections of AMS-02 Data
papers.abstract: We analyze more than a decade of public Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS-02) data (2011-2021), matching daily electron and positron spectra to the orbital record on 3268 common dates. For each sky window we weight the spectra by the time the orbital zenith spends there and divide each rigidity bin by its all-date mean. At 16.6-22.8 GV, the normalized positron flux dips below its neighboring bins in several projections. At the Galactic center and the Crab, the positron dip exceeds the electron dip by $3.04\pm1.19$ and $3.57\pm1.22$ percentage points, respectively (statistical errors). A scan centered on 1177 Fermi-LAT catalog sources also finds dips at PKS~0301$-$243 and PKS~1424+240. At fixed rigidity, 13.8\% of trials that shift the spectra relative to the orbit produce a dip somewhere in the catalog at least as deep as the observed maximum. An isotropic intensity with the measured daily spectra reproduces every projection exactly. In a zenith pencil-beam model, direct positron annihilation on a common cold-electron column at the Galactic center and the Crab produces less than 0.10 percentage points of dip depth in either projection.

papers.title: Circle-Pattern Linear Systems for the Twenty Trivalent Delaunay Types of a Genus-Two Surface: Rank, Feasibility and Polytope Dimension
papers.abstract: The hyperelliptic quotient of a closed genus-two Riemann surface is a hyperbolic sphere with six cone points of angle pi. Its Delaunay triangulation T is dual to a trivalent Voronoi graph G of one of twenty combinatorial types. For each type we study the angle system Ax = 1, x >= 0, where A is the vertex-edge incidence matrix of T and pi x_e is the angle subtended at a cone point by the Voronoi edge dual to e, equivalently the intersection angle of the two circumcircles adjacent across e. We prove that rank A = 6 for all twenty types, including the six whose triangulation has a loop, so the affine solution space always has the dimension of Teichmuller space. The polytope P = {Ax = 1, x >= 0} behaves differently. It is six-dimensional for exactly ten types, the ten Delaunay-realizable ones. For nine types it has dimension one, two or three, because non-negativity forces some wedge angles to vanish, and for the type of signature (2,2,2,2,8,8) it is empty. We show that five of the nine and the empty type never occur as Delaunay triangulations, and that the other four occur only as triangulations of non-trivalent Delaunay decompositions. Every vertex of every P is half-integral, as for fractional perfect matching polytopes. For the ten full-dimensional types every facet x_e = 0 lies at an edge where the Whitehead move is admissible, though not conversely, and the move identifies the facets of the two polytopes; these identifications pair the facet orbits of the ten cells under their automorphism groups. The free unfolding of the gluing grows at rate about 7.093. All finite statements are checked by an independent program, and the rank, infeasibility, forced coordinates, dimensions, vertices and facets are verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety
papers.abstract: Runtime guardrails protect mobile GUI agents by assessing each proposed action before execution, but existing guardrails rely on cloud hosted large multimodal models, exposing every screen to a remote server, including private information such as payments, messages, and medical records. We propose MobileGrail, an on-device deployable model that addresses both. It maintains a recurrent task state that retains only the evidence subsequent safety decisions depend on, so that authorization and execution progress persist beyond the short context. To intervene early while keeping the safety boundary precise, it learns two labels, unsafe and block: unsafe marks the action that commits a violation, whereas block may be issued at any step of an intervention window, which spans from the first action that the user's authorization no longer explains to the committing action itself. To support training, we build an environment of 32 applications whose backends verify the effect of every action, supplying verified labels for supervision and rewards for reinforcement learning to calibrate intervention timing. We also build MobileVeto, an offline benchmark of unsafe trajectories largely on held-out applications, each paired with a benign counterpart. On MobileVeto, MobileGrail built on Qwen3.5-2B intercepts 76.2% of violations, up from 64.5% for its prompted backbone, while reducing premature intervention from 58.6% to 5.2%, outperforming the cloud-based OS-Sentinel on both. We further conduct online evaluation on GhostEIBench, where MobileGrail guarding a Qwen3.8-27B agent reduces fully successful attacks from 13 to 3 of 110 tasks while raising task completion from 48 to 58. Quantized to 4 bits, MobileGrail runs on a Snapdragon 8 Elite at a median latency of 4.7 s, comparable to the 5.1s of cloud-hosted Gemini 3.8 Flash.

papers.title: When Source-Domain Validation Fails to Transfer: A Staged Study of Hyperparameter Selection
papers.abstract: Hyperparameters for an unseen domain are often selected using held-out examples from the available source domains. Withholding entire source domains during validation seems to better reflect deployment shift, but does this produce better selections on independent targets? We investigate this question through two complementary studies. A preliminary factorial experiment crosses particle swarm optimization and random search with pooled source validation and a leave-one-source-domain-out mean-minimum fitness on PACS and Multi-Domain Sentiment. The domain-aware fitness does not provide a consistent target advantage. We then separate selector development from confirmation using a shared pool of 64 configurations per task across four image benchmarks. Complete target-performance landscapes on VLCS and Office-Home inform one rule: retain the top 16 configurations by pooled source validation, then select the largest leave-one-source-domain-out mean-minus-standard-deviation score. The rule is frozen before evaluation on TerraIncognita and SVIRO. Across their 14 target domains, its equal-dataset-weighted balanced-accuracy difference from pooled validation is +0.097 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval [-0.685, +0.960]), with five wins and nine losses. Exploratory analyses reveal substantial variation across datasets, target domains, and training seeds. These results do not establish equivalence or a general failure of domain-aware validation. They show that the evaluated source-domain criteria did not establish reliable target gains under the tested protocols, and motivate assessing selection rules on datasets independent of those used to develop them.

papers.title: Quantum-Memory Forensics for Tampered Quantum Seals: Resource-Dependent Sample Gains
papers.abstract: Quantum seals reveal that an object was disturbed, but not where, with which tool, or when the tool changed. We study quantum-memory forensics for sealed items returning through an untrusted network where one tool opens many. Each seal cell is half of a Bell pair whose partner the verifier keeps in a protected quantum memory, a secret Pauli frame turns any attack into a Pauli channel, and a three-tier report localizes the tampering, learns a hidden-parity fingerprint of the tool and detects a tool switch in arrival order, not necessarily in attack order. Attribution concerns attackers who do not erase that fingerprint, which a random Pauli layer would do cheaply. Each result is stated within one of four verifier classes. For per-unit verifiers, which never couple two seal units and hold no untouched reference, the sample separation is asymptotically exponential, by reduction from a known lower bound for one parity of strength up to 1/3. On ten tampered cells it is proved to be at least \qnProvedUniformMin-fold against non-adaptive stabilizer probes and observed in simulation at \qnEoneRatioFine-fold. Against an implemented self-referencing strategy the simulated gain is about twice the inverse squared strength. The value also depends on the attack: destroying the untouched cells makes the reference necessary, whereas copying errors exposes the fingerprint to reference-free probes. We derive the vault's qubit inventory and simulate a seal requirement curve: ten times more seal noise lengthens the seal's lifetime \qnSealLifeGainFive-fold at \qnSealRhoFive{} times the attribution cost at $r=10$.

papers.title: Second Moment Penny Packings via Rolling Spaces
papers.abstract: We solve the unrestricted minimum second moment problem for six unit disks in the plane by proving that the minimum is \(29/3\) attained uniquely up to isometry and relabelling by one disk together with five of its six neighbours in the triangular lattice. The realised contacts themselves define the space of admissible motions, while the directions preserving those contacts to first order define the rolling space consisting of motions whose relative velocities have zero normal component at every realised contact. Together, these spaces lead to an exact tangent cone formula and to a criterion by which a strictly positive centroidal contact balance, combined with rolling rigidity, implies strict local minimality modulo Euclidean motions. Our method recovers the classical five disk minimum \(34/5\) of Graham and Sloane, previously the largest unrestricted case known exactly. Geometric reductions and a graph census reduce the global search to finitely many contact graph classes. Exact analysis and validated interval arithmetic then exclude competing configurations, establishing the global bounds and uniqueness. Our method allows us to pass from putative lattice extremisers to unrestricted optimality.

papers.title: The Temporal Residual: Fast and Effective Retrofitting of Latent Feedback into Pretrained Language Models
papers.abstract: A transformer language model computes a deep hidden state for every token but uses it only to sample that token. Existing latent-feedback designs, which feed hidden states back across tokens, are mostly built in during pretraining and gain little when added to a pretrained model. We introduce the temporal residual, a second residual stream that every sublayer reads and writes and that is carried from each token to the next. It adds 2,752 parameters to a 4.2B-parameter model and starts exactly at the pretrained network. Retrofitted onto Qwen3.5-4B-Base with 5B tokens of training, it beats a standard model trained on the same data by 7, 13 and 5 points on AIME 2024, AIME 2025 and AMC 2023, writes shorter solutions, and stays ahead at matched training compute. The separate stream matters: prior designs that feed state into the existing stream recover at most 40% of the gain when retrofitted. Validation loss can mislead: the recipe with the lowest loss gains nothing at decoding. Trained with filler tokens in place of reasoning, the model reasons in its hidden state: its GSM8K accuracy with no visible reasoning rises from 21% to 40%, and falls back when the carried state is zeroed.

papers.title: Construction of a Deployable Closure Model for the Transport of Turbulence Dissipation Rate with Hard-Constrained Physics-Informed Machine Learning
papers.abstract: We present a hard-constrained physics-informed machine learning (PIML) method for constructing a deployable closure model for the transport of turbulence dissipation rate. The framework is built from modules, each performing a single task. The closure module represents the closure with a small network, while the state module represents the flow state during training. The closure network is coupled to the state network through the governing equation residuals. This coupling allows us to learn the closure without using reference closure values as training targets. The coordinate module learns monotone input coordinates that help both networks resolve sharp changes. Within the network architecture, the boundary condition (BC) module imposes boundary values exactly using the Theory of Functional Connections, and the realizability module keeps the closure realizable. We study decaying homogeneous isotropic turbulence (HIT) and learn $ψ$, the closure function governing dissipation rate decay, from trajectories obtained in experiments and direct numerical simulations. Here, the state module is a Deep Operator Network (DeepONet), the BC module imposes the initial state and the closure's low and high Reynolds number limits, and the realizability module ensures growth of the Taylor microscale. The framework reduces the root mean square of the closure variation across ten random seeds by about 95\% relative to the unconstrained model over the training and held-out range. The deployed 18-parameter closure network requires only the Taylor scale Reynolds number $Re_{λ_g}$ and can be exported as a standalone C function.

papers.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincaré algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.

papers.title: PACT: Plan-Action Consistency Training by Preserving Correct Plans and Repairing Actions in GUI Agents
papers.abstract: GUI agents can formulate a correct immediate plan in their reasoning yet emit an action that fails to execute it, creating an execution gap. This recurring mismatch undermines reliable task completion, as a single execution error can derail a multi-step workflow. In outcome-supervised reinforcement learning, broadcasting a negative response-level advantage across all generated tokens risks penalizing valid planning together with erroneous execution. To address this credit-assignment conflict, we introduce PACT (Plan-Action Consistency Training), a training framework that combines reference-aligned plan protection and plan-aligned action repair without altering the original scalar action reward. Using annotated reference actions to identify execution gaps, PACT protects the verified plan by masking negative policy-gradient contributions across its token span. Keeping the generated reasoning unchanged as context, it then favors the reference action over the emitted erroneous action through a preference surrogate with stop-gradient pair weights.
