Here, we prove that this universal drift is exact at all times, requiring only translation invariance and U(1) symmetry. Furthermore, we prove that it is sufficient for the circuit to be translation-invariant on average by deriving the same result in the random case. Finally, we demonstrate that breaking translation invariance immediately results in deviations from this universal prediction.

papers.title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control
papers.abstract: Improvements in multi-modal capabilities have enabled agents to act directly as robot policies, a setting we refer to as agentic robot control (ARC). We introduce RoboARCade, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control. The tasks build on existing open-source benchmarks, which we make harder by widening the range of initial conditions. RoboARCade is easy to use and extend: all tasks run on a single simulation backend, MuJoCo, each task is a self-contained data pack, and agents connect through interchangeable interfaces, so new tasks, agents, and interfaces can be added independently. The benchmark separates leading agents: GPT-6 Astra achieves 49.8% compared with 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, leaving substantial room for improvement. Comparing two interfaces, we find that a richer visual interface adds only 1.5 to 6.8 points at 1.7 to 2.3 times the cost. Failures stem mostly from choosing a poor manipulation strategy or executing a good one imprecisely, rarely from misunderstanding the scene, and agents incorrectly claim success on 24% to 39% of attempted subtasks. Agents can also improve without human input: one successful demonstration in context raises Astra's score from 53.5% to 73.0% on a five-task subset, and a prompt the agent writes and revises itself reaches 72.0%. Code, videos and full traces are available at roboarcade.org.

papers.title: Dynamic response of tunnels and buried conduits under moving loads by coupling nonmatching isogeometric and scaled-boundary discretizations
papers.abstract: Moving-load analysis of tunnels and buried conduits requires resolving local structural response together with wave propagation and radiation in the surrounding soil. We develop a nonmatching coupling formulation within a Fourier-based dimensional reduction framework (2.5D), allowing independent discretization of the near-field and propagation domains. An $L^2$ projection on a common partition of the physical interface transfers displacements between the traces, and its Hermitian adjoint transfers interface forces so the reduced system preserves virtual work. The near field uses a geometry-independent field approximation with truncated hierarchical B-splines, permitting local refinement on fixed CAD geometry. The surrounding soil uses quadtree scaled-boundary isogeometric analysis with unified Bézier trace extraction and connects to the homogeneous unbounded exterior through a scaled-boundary impedance. Homogeneous half-space comparisons and an analytical cylindrical-cavity solution verify the components and the coupled system. In the cavity benchmark, hierarchical refinement improves near-field accuracy with the interface trace and surrounding discretization held fixed. A layered pavement with a buried conduit and twin modified-D tunnels demonstrate coupling across open and closed interfaces, including disconnected components. Conduit cover mainly changes peak radial and hoop stress magnitudes. Transverse load offset also shifts their governing sectors. For the twin tunnels, increasing the centre spacing from $1.75$ to $3.00$ times the excavation width reduces the unloaded tunnel's peak mean cross-sectional displacement by $25.5\%$ and its peak tangential lining stress by $66.6\%$.

papers.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
papers.abstract: We study the Jacobians of a genus-two family with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We realize these abelian surfaces as factors of cyclic-cover Jacobians and determine their integral rank-two monodromy. For the real embedding with $\sqrt5>0$, the projective image is the Hecke group $Δ(2,5,\infty)$; the conjugate real image is nondiscrete. After a finite base change, we give an explicit degree-four map from Cohen--Wolfart's Hecke cyclic curve to the genus-two curve. Four deck translates of the induced Jacobian pullback give an integral isomorphism from the fourth power of the surface to the eight-dimensional primitive order-$20$ factor, with an explicit nonproduct polarization. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ torsion-line covers are normalizations of quadratic fibre products of genus-one triangular modular curves. We also describe the associated split and nonsplit Cartan-normalizer covers. Finite-field hypergeometric traces give the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation with a twist by the quadratic character of $2$.

papers.title: Thurston algorithm for real entire maps: existence and uniqueness
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the real Thurston pullback algorithm for entire maps with finitely many finite singular values, all real. Given a finite forward-invariant marking containing the singular values and satisfying an interval no-Levy-cycle condition, the pullback is shown to have a unique fixed point and it is shown that every orbit converges to it. The resulting entire map uniquely realises the marked dynamics up to positive affine conjugacy. Thus this paper established Thurston realisation and uniqueness in the setting of real entire maps with a finite postsingular set. As usual, the realisation problem reduces to the existence of a fixed point of the Thurston map $T$ which in the real setting acts on a simplex $W$ of dimension $s-2$ if the required postsingular set consists of $s$ points. The key estimate concerns a finite real preimage interval: when its critical multiplicity is bounded and its endpoint values stay separated from the singular values unless they equal to one, its hyperbolic diameter grows at most double-logarithmically as the separation tends to zero. An expansive marking (absence of Levy cycles) then rules out configurations near the boundary of the simplex whose displacement under the Thurston map is at most a fixed multiple of their distance to the boundary. Using a version of the Brouwer fixed point theorem, this immediately implies that the Thurston map $T$ has a fixed point. The argument permits infinitely many real and non-real critical points and different behaviours as the real variable tends to $+\infty$ and $-\infty$. Additional estimates for fixed labelled inverse branches, which are not strictly necessary for the proof of the Main Theorem, are given in the appendices.

papers.title: A true $Π^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
papers.abstract: We give a true $Π^0_1$ sentence $φ$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehatϕ$ denotes its interpretation on $ω$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehatϕ$ is a $Π^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.

papers.title: Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines with Automatic Model Complexity Inference
papers.abstract: Tensor network (TN) kernel machines speed up supervised learning by using low-rank TNs to reduce computation and memory. Most of these methods, however, are deterministic: they ignore parameter uncertainty, and their model complexity has to be tuned manually. Bayesian TN kernel machines remove both limitations, but only for the CANDECOMP/PARAFAC decomposition (CPD), which has a single rank. For the more general tensor train (TT), manual tuning is even more costly, since every one of its ranks must be chosen. In this paper we propose Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines (BTT-KM), which place hierarchical ARD-type priors on the TT cores and infer all TT ranks and feature dimensions from data. Mean-field variational inference leads to a Bayesian alternating least squares algorithm with the same computational complexity as its deterministic counterpart, and gives a closed-form predictive distribution. On synthetic data, BTT-KM shrinks an over-parameterized initialization to a low-rank model close to the ground truth, and on UCI benchmarks it is competitive with state-of-the-art methods, with predictive coverage closest to the nominal value.

papers.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
papers.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.

papers.title: The Cost of Minimal Completeness: Gamma-to-Delta Aliasing in Discrete Markets
papers.abstract: In one dimension, the symmetric binomial tree replicates quadratic payoffs using the Delta of its own price function. For every $d\geq 2$ and every centered, isotropic, minimally complete $(d+1)$-state model with $d$ risky assets, by contrast, some quadratic payoff requires a replicating hedge different from that Delta. In this nonredundant finite-state setting, centered one-step payoffs are spanned by the $d$ asset innovations; centered second-order (Gamma) contributions are therefore represented as first-order trading gains, potentially inducing additional asset holdings. We call this effect Gamma-to-Delta aliasing and measure it by the linear operator $\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)=\mathbb{E}[(ξ^\top Hξ-\operatorname{tr}H)ξ]$, where $ξ$ is the normalized one-step innovation and $H$ the Gamma matrix. For quadratic claims the replicating holding exceeds the price Delta by exactly $\sqrt{h}\,\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)/2$, where $h$ is the time step. Trading this holding in a Brownian market adds the tracking-error variance $hT|\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)|^2/4$, a fixed multiple of the ordinary discrete-Delta error that does not vanish in relative terms as $h\downarrow0$. We prove that the smallest worst-case aliasing over all minimally complete models is $\sqrt{d-1}$, so the worst-case relative excess variance is $(d-1)/2$; both are attained uniquely by the equal-probability regular simplex. For unit-Frobenius positive-semidefinite Gammas and for unit rank-one Gammas, the sharp minimax value is $(d-1)/\sqrt{d}$, with the same unique optimizer. We also show how aliasing trades off against unhedgeable quadratic risk when more states are allowed, and derive the leading implementation cost for smooth claims.

papers.title: On the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties of the differential system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$
papers.abstract: A prolongation variety of a polynomial differential system $S$ is an algebraic variety defined by the equations of $S$ and their derivatives up to a given order. We compute the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties associated with the system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$ in terms of the prolongation order, thereby proving a conjecture stated by Gleb Pogudin in Section 2, Question 6 of "Some Open Problems in Differential Algebra". Our approach is motivated from the beginning by doing computational experiments in OSCAR in order to find the number of solutions of a zero-dimensional system using algebraic Thomas decomposition. The result will follow from a coprimality condition on a family of polynomials with integer coefficients, which is verified by showing that their roots satisfy a strong interlacing property. Finally, we propose an extension of the conjecture for the systems $x_1'=x_2^n$, $x_2'=x_1^n$ with $n>2$.

papers.title: Fluctuating resource availability stabilizes coexistence beyond the oscillatory tragedy of the commons
papers.abstract: Fluctuations in ambient conditions such as temperature and humidity can alter the effective availability of a shared resource at a given abundance. Standard evolutionary games with environmental feedback treat the payoff matrix as a deterministic function of resource abundance, leaving open how fluctuations in availability affect the oscillatory tragedy of the commons. Using noise-corrected replicator dynamics and individual-based birth-death simulations, we show that zero-mean fluctuations in resource availability can stabilize an interior equilibrium and suppress coupled strategy-resource oscillations. We derive an analytical criterion, in terms of the payoff structure and feedback dynamics, for when increasing noise favors local stability. These findings identify environmental variability as a mechanism that can promote strategy coexistence and help maintain shared resources in systems prone to recurrent depletion.

papers.title: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
papers.abstract: Omni models answer questions about videos by jointly processing sampled frames and audio in one turn, while VLMs have become strong agents that can search a video over many turns. We ask how far a model can go without hearing the audio, and present \method, a simple multi-turn harness built on such a VLM that never hears the audio directly: speech is transcribed into text, and the VLM sleuths the video without a predefined workflow. On four omni benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, \method achieves the best average accuracy: \textbf{75.0\%}, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and it tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with \textbf{77.8\%}; with Qwen3.8-27B, it is comparable to open-source omni models on short videos and better on long ones. We draw three insights: searching outperforms passive observation; agentic ability matters as much as direct audio access; and small agentic models are highly competitive. So we provide a simple but effective starting point for omni video understanding.

papers.title: Matching the Training-Time Weight Rule in Inference-Time Expert Deactivation
papers.abstract: The performance impact of expert deactivation depends on both the disabled set and the routing and weighting of the remaining experts. We compare removal, freezing, remaining-expert renormalization, and unnormalized re-routing on identical disabled sets across five instruction-tuned checkpoints from four model families, with a base OLMoE checkpoint as an additional comparison. A weight-sum model separates the loss of disabled contributions from changes in expert-branch scale and predicts the highest-loss implementation from the training-time weight rule, with remaining-expert renormalization for raw-probability models and unnormalized re-routing for normalized-weight models. All five checkpoints match this prediction. Matched survivor sets isolate weight handling. On one DeepSeek-V2-Lite disabled set, freezing yields a perplexity of 17.21 while renormalization yields 258,621.64. At 50 per cent deactivation using activation-based selection, perplexity reaches 1.4 to 73 times the intact baseline under the training rule and 14 to 28,740 times the baseline under a rule mismatch. The same model extends to inference-time width, where the penalty from additional renormalization grows as the number of active experts decreases, and OLMoE exhibits this trend. Multiple-choice and free-form evaluations separate likelihood collapse from answer accuracy and reveal differences in generation behavior. Training-time weight rules are therefore a practical reference for expert pruning, offloading, and width adjustment.

papers.title: Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments
papers.abstract: As agents become more capable, they are moving beyond one-off tasks toward sustained assistance across successive user goals. Such assistance requires agents to discover how unfamiliar environments work, reuse what they learn across tasks, and keep that experience current as environments evolve. Existing benchmarks increasingly study experience reuse and adaptation, but provide limited insight into which parts of accumulated experience agents revise, retain, or lose. To address this gap, we introduce ReScopeBench, a benchmark for the experience lifecycle across 18 interactive environments. It distinguishes structural experience about how an environment is organized and accessed from rule experience about reusable principles and constraints that guide decisions across tasks. To study how experience is acquired, reused, and revised, we propose an experience-first construction approach. It builds task streams around shared experience and introduces silent environmental changes. We evaluate task performance and track changes in saved experience throughout each stream. Across 20 models, we find that retained experience improves task performance, but agents struggle to keep it current as environments change. Even when the required experience is correctly recorded, agents do not always complete tasks successfully. These findings identify selective maintenance and effective use as complementary challenges for long-lived agents.

papers.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree $Δ\ge750$ satisfies the Borodin--Kostochka inequality $χ(G)\le\max\{ω(G),Δ-1\}$, conjectured for all $Δ\ge9$. Reed (1999) established the inequality for $Δ\ge10^{14}$, and Liu, Sun, Wang and Zeng (2026) lowered the threshold to $5.3\times10^6$. To extend a random partial colouring over large cliques, we find repeated colours using adaptively chosen vertex-disjoint stars and apply Hall's theorem to the available colour lists. We verify the required probability bounds by rational and interval arithmetic with directed rounding.

papers.title: Ground-Wing: A Parametric 3D Wing-in-Ground-Effect Dataset for Benchmarking Neural Surrogate Models
papers.abstract: This paper presents a CFD dataset of a highly parametrized 3D wing operating in ground effect, designed for benchmarking neural surrogate models for aerodynamic prediction, using a wing shape and flow conditions typically encountered in motorsport applications. The dataset comprises 770 RANS simulations of 194 unique wing configurations, sampled across 27 airfoil profile variants and 4 distances from the ground, spanning variations in wing sweep, chord, taper, angle of attack, and tip twist. Six neural network architectures representing distinct paradigms --- convolutional (DoMINO), graph-based (X-MeshGraphNet), transformer-based (AB-UPT, GeoTransolver, GAOT), and JEPA-based (AeroJEPA) --- are evaluated on their ability to predict surface pressure coefficient and wall shear stress distributions, from which integral drag and lift coefficients are recovered. The dataset is intended to be used as a challenging benchmark for surrogate CFD models, due to the uniqueness of the ground effect being absent from other wing and airfoil datasets. The dataset is available for download at https://huggingface.co/datasets/andreacenzato/Ground-Wing

papers.title: When Model Rankings Move Without Model Change: A Registered Audit of Evaluation Contracts in Neural Prediction Pipelines
papers.abstract: Evaluation reports cite sliced differences, most prominently the intra-inter gap in document-level relation extraction (DocRE), as capability evidence. Such gap readings are joint properties of models and evaluation contracts: scoring function, gold version, threshold, output format, and prompt language. With predictions frozen, switching only the gold reverses a method ordering (+0.0363, CI excluding zero; retrained stand-ins), leaving it tie-level. The flip survives Holm correction (exploratory tier); ten of thirteen flips share one contrast (fixed vs decoded threshold). Rename-only revisions cannot move a reading (Delta = 0); re-annotation moves it +0.862 UD points. We formalize this as an evaluation leverage account centered on a rank-flip condition. Constructively, the audited evaluation reading (AER; post-freeze) aggregates a comparison over declared contracts, declares ties when they disagree, prescribes seeds, and filters unverifiable settings. On WMT19 it is indistinguishable from the best single contract at the exploratory, convention-stable margin epsilon = 0.10 (chosen post-freeze); its tie declarations cover every contract-induced flip (14/14), at a priced false-tie cost (66.1%/88.0% of declared ties; single contracts: 58.7-71% de-en, 86-91% zh-en). Coverage drops to 73% held out and 3/13 on the denser DocRE registry (declare-tie-if-any-flip: 89%): the guarantee is grid-specific. Evidence spans DocRE, HacRED, a UD probe, released gold revisions, and a replication. Failed preregistered predictions are retained as boundaries. A 5% violation gate bounds survivor-selection bias. We release EvalLever, a registered audit workflow (147 amendments, tiered status). On a three-judge WMT19 grid its ensemble suppresses part of the sign instability (13-15 to 9; one preregistered criterion fails).

papers.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
papers.abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.

papers.title: On the Conditional Consistency of the Bootstrap
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the conditional consistency of the bootstrap. The target is the conditional law of a statistic given a common shock, and the bootstrap approximates it by the law of a resampled statistic conditional on the shock and the data. We call the bootstrap consistent if these laws are close in the Kolmogorov distance for almost every realization of the shock. The conditioning $σ$-algebras are allowed to be unrelated across sample sizes, and both the comparison law and the dimension of the data may vary with the sample size. We give sufficient conditions for consistency in this sense, show that they yield asymptotically correct conditional coverage for bootstrap quantiles, and provide a finite-sample bound on the coverage error. We also relate the Kolmogorov formulation to the merging of probability measures. The results are specialized to statistics depending smoothly on an estimator or on an estimated nuisance parameter.

papers.title: Knowledge-Guided Floodwater Level Reasoning for Cloud-Edge Collaborative Monitoring
papers.abstract: Frequent urban floodwater poses a serious threat to the safety and efficiency of intelligent transportation systems. Existing vision-based methods for floodwater level detection face two main limitations. First, the lack of explicit reasoning leads to poor detection performance and little interpretability. Second, these methods struggle to generalize to the complex and varied real-world road scenes seen from different viewpoints. To address this, we reformulate the task as an explicit visual reasoning problem and propose HydroReasoner, a floodwater level reasoning framework designed for cloud-edge collaboration. HydroReasoner builds on Qwen2.5-VL and is trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization. To address the scarcity of reasoning process annotations, we build a floodwater domain knowledge graph HydroKG and design a novel KG path reward. Through deterministic graph traversal over HydroKG, this reward supervises the model's reasoning process at a fine granularity, which improves both reasoning and generalization. For edge deployment, we apply 4-bit quantization to the model, cutting GPU memory usage by 57% and inference latency by 43% while out-of-domain accuracy drops by only 0.2 percentage points. We also propose a confidence-based cloud-edge routing mechanism, which improves system safety and eases the computational load on the cloud. In addition, we build HydroLevel, a floodwater benchmark dataset of 3,000 images, for training and evaluating the model. Experimental results show that HydroReasoner achieves detection accuracy 4.0 and 13.6 percentage points higher than conventional vision baselines in the in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations respectively, with performance dropping by only 4.4 percentage points out of domain.

papers.title: Randomized, Quantum and Postselected Multitape Time in Deterministic Space t/sqrt(log t)
papers.abstract: We show that a bounded-error multitape Turing machine running in time $t$ can be simulated deterministically in space $O(t/\sqrt{\log t})$, with no constructibility assumption on $t$. The simulation computes any bit of the exact number of accepting coin strings, so it also covers majority, postselected, nondeterministic and modular acceptance. It uses the tensor-network contraction behind the recent refutations of the Exponential Time Hypothesis, which Cruz used to put nondeterministic time $T$ in space $T(\log\log T)^2/\sqrt{\log T}$. Our space accounting removes the $(\log\log T)^2$ factor. Writing a pair of quantum paths as one weighted classical run, we obtain the same bound for bounded-error quantum time with polynomial-time computable amplitudes, for postselected quantum time with algebraic amplitudes, and for quantum Merlin-Arthur time with witnesses of $O(t/(\log t)^{3/2})$ qubits. For explicit circuits, acceptance probabilities of $S$-gate quantum circuits and #CircuitSAT for $S$-gate Boolean circuits are computed exactly in space $O(S/\sqrt{\log S})$ plus the logarithm of the description length. As consequences, for every constant $K$ some language in deterministic linear space differs, at every large input length, from every bounded-error or postselected quantum machine running in time $o(n\sqrt{\log n})$ with $Kn$ bits of advice; another has correlation $O((\log n)/\sqrt{n})$ with every randomized or algebraic-amplitude quantum machine of that time with $\log^2 n$ bits of advice; and DSPACE$(n)$ is not contained in BPTIME$[o(n\sqrt{\log n})]$ with constant-length advice that may depend on the coins. Finally, exact counting or postselected simulation in space $T^{1-\varepsilon}$ would refute the Weak Exponential Time Hypothesis.

papers.title: What Helps Denoising Can Hurt Memory: Rethinking History in Long Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video generators produce videos block by block from historical context. They are trained within a bounded horizon, whereas inference can extend far beyond it, causing temporal consistency to gradually decrease. Existing methods focus on eliminating this mismatch, but we instead ask whether the historical context used in training remains suitable for inference. Each block reads historical context in two stages, when denoising generates it and when committing writes it into the KV cache for later blocks. We find that older historical context such as the sink helps denoising but can hurt later blocks when read during committing, even in generators trained to read it there. We also show that as committing reads more preceding blocks, clip-to-clip Subject Consistency rises, plateaus, and then declines. We therefore propose Commit Forcing, a training-free rule that organizes committing into a chain. Each committing pass reads only the preceding block's stored KV, while denoising keeps the base historical context. Commit Forcing improves 60-second VBench Quality and Total on all 6 generators, by up to 1.27 and 1.10 points. Its consistency gains extend to 240-second videos, and it achieves an 82.9% win rate in overall human preference on 120-second LongLive videos.

papers.title: AI Data Analysis: A New Approach - Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis
papers.abstract: AI data analysis today is three fragmented worlds: LLMs understand semantics but cannot compute; BI aggregates precisely but is stateless; ML processes large-scale data on a stateful kernel but lacks semantics. This paper proposes a combination mechanism, named Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis, that fills a still-open gap - the multi-engine joint context: the data context is embedded into LLM conversational analysis, where the LLM serves only as the semantic, reasoning, and orchestration layer (not computation) and connects four engines through the 1M context window - Python and R ML kernels, SQL over relational databases, Cypher over graph databases - yielding two multiplications, "semantics and precise computation" and "relational and graph", under enterprise-grade governance. The novelty is a four-dimensional coordinate system: horizontal (engine kinds), vertical (state flow - the watershed), spatial (business generalization), temporal (iterative convergence); a deterministic grounding method (one-shot injection of schema.json + notes.md, M+S) carries the spatial and temporal dimensions. Empirically, all four dimensions are substantiated: horizontally, four engines are quantified - SQL, Cypher (96.5% on CypherBench movie), ML in Python and R (TabReD weather); vertically, state flows across engines and grounding is reused across kernels; spatially, SQL generalizes across three business databases - AdventureWorks 91.3%, financial 95.3%, formula_1 94.6% (average), about 20-23 points above single-shot SOTA 74.45%; temporally, accuracy converges monotonically as notes accumulate. The core invariant - the separation of semantics from computation plus a cross-data-domain persistent context - does not expire as LLMs and agents evolve or engine forms change.

papers.title: von Neumann-Morgenstern stable sets in job matching problems
papers.abstract: We show that a von Neumann-Morgenstern (vNM) stable set generically exists in the many-to-one job-matching model. Unlike the core, which can be empty in this model, a vNM stable set exists whenever there is a unique efficient matching: the set of all individually rational (IR) and efficient outcomes form a vNM stable set. If an economy has multiple efficient matchings, a vNM stable set may not exist. If the vNM stable sets are required to be rich in a certain sense, then such a rich vNM stable set exists if and only if the set of efficient matchings is essentially unique, and the set of all efficient and IR outcomes forms the unique rich vNM stable set.

papers.title: Weak-coupling selection and finite-torus entropy in the triangular Ising antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: An antiferromagnetic second-neighbor interaction favors stripe order in the triangular-lattice Ising antiferromagnet, but uniform stripes cannot close when both primitive periods are odd. At each fixed odd size $L\geq5$, we minimize this interaction over the ground states of the zero-field nearest-neighbor model on an $L\times L$ torus. We prove a minimum total interface length of $4L$ and classify all $L^2(L^2-1)/2$ selected states. Under the uniform measure on these states, the area fractions of the three stripe orientations approach a uniform distribution over all nonnegative triples summing to one. Thus selection reduces an exponential degeneracy to polynomial growth, while the whole-sample orientation fractions remain broadly distributed. We also derive explicit two-sided entropy-density bounds for periodic spin ground states and honeycomb dimer coverings on $M\times N$ tori, where $M$ and $N$ are the periods along the two primitive lattice directions. For all $M,N\geq3$, the errors relative to the bulk residual entropy are bounded by explicit constants times $\min(M,N)^{-2}$, without an aspect-ratio restriction. These bounds give finite-size accuracy guarantees and control the exponentially small fraction of unperturbed ground states that survive the selection.

papers.title: High-fidelity simulation and reduced-order modeling of optical pumping in quantum devices
papers.abstract: Predicting spin polarization and light attenuation in optically pumped atomic devices requires solving the coupled diffusive quantum master equation (DQME)--light system. Its nonlinearity, spatially nonlocal coupling, and physical admissibility constraints make high-fidelity numerical simulation challenging. We develop a structure-preserving high-fidelity solver that combines second-order finite differences for three-dimensional atomic diffusion, explicit pseudo-time marching for atomic populations, and an exponential integrator for light propagation. Under a derived time-step restriction, the solver preserves population normalization and nonnegativity, as well as the positivity and monotonic attenuation of the light intensity. Three complementary test cases based on an analytical reduction, asymptotic limits, and an analytical invariant are constructed to verify the solver. To accelerate repeated parameter queries, we eliminate the light field and construct a reduced-order model (ROM) using proper orthogonal decomposition and Galerkin projection of the resulting integro-differential formulation involving only atomic populations. An exact quadratic expansion of the spin-exchange term and discrete empirical interpolation of the optical-pumping term make the cost of evaluating the reduced operators independent of the full-order dimension. Numerical tests verify the solver and demonstrate ROM accuracy outside the training set. The GPU implementation completes simulations with millions of unknowns in minutes, while single-core ROM evaluations take seconds, achieving respective speedup factors exceeding 150 and 7000 relative to the single-core high-fidelity solver.

papers.title: Coarse3D: Controllable and Faithful Sparse Structure Generation for Image-to-3D
papers.abstract: Coarse-to-fine 3D-native generation relies heavily on the first-stage sparse structure, which determines the global orientation and overall geometry for subsequent refinement. However, existing coarse generators suffer from two key limitations: their orientation is difficult to control due to ambiguous semantic canonicalization, and their structures are often inconsistent with input images due to weak 2D-3D grounding. We propose Coarse3D, a sparse-structure generation model that produces orientation-controllable and structurally faithful voxel geometry from arbitrary unposed images. Coarse3D introduces three designs: a first-frame anchored canonical space that aligns generation with the first input view while preserving object-centric normalization; a dual-tower DiT that couples generation with auxiliary feed-forward reconstruction to learn spatially grounded features; and spatial-prior guided attention that regularizes cross-attention with pixel-to-voxel correspondence. Coarse3D can directly replace the coarse stage of existing pipelines. Experiments show that it substantially improves sparse structure quality and consistently enhances final 3D generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

papers.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
papers.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched problems, cross-scale problems score 8.7 points below single-scale ones. Half of the problems are solved by at most one model, and models fail chiefly by endorsing what is plausible rather than what was observed. A domain-adaptation study with meta-weighted continued pretraining and scale-modular self-distillation raises an open-weight model from 36.7% to 55.4%, matching the strongest proprietary model, with improvements on public materials benchmarks and no decline in aggregate performance on general benchmarks. FrontierMat provides a testbed for measuring progress toward language models that support frontier materials R&D.

papers.title: Let LiDAR Decide Where to Look: Geometry-Measured Token Selection for Efficient Sparse Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Vision-centric autonomous driving models encode thousands of image tokens per frame, yet most depict sky, buildings, or empty road---content irrelevant to planning. Worse, these tokens dilute the planner's attention: we show that randomly discarding 75% of tokens already outperforms the dense model, because the planner can concentrate on the remaining driving-critical content. Building on this finding, we present Geometry-Aware Token Selection (GATS), which uses LiDAR and radar point projections to select a small fraction of image tokens before the vision backbone runs. Because the selector operates on measured 3D geometry rather than visual features, the backbone encodes only the selected patches, cutting end-to-end FLOPs by up to $18\times$. Each kept token receives a 3D anchor from its LiDAR point and is fed to a self-supervised latent world model that predicts future features and 3D displacements without box annotations. At 25% budget, GATS achieves a 3-sec L2 displacement error of 0.520 m on nuScenes and an EPDMS of 88.9 on NAVSIM---surpassing the dense baseline (0.573 m / 85.9) at $6.6\times$ fewer total FLOPs. At an extreme 10% budget (24 GFLOPs, $18\times$ reduction), it still beats the dense baseline on both nuScenes (0.537 m vs. 0.573 m L2) and NAVSIM (87.9 vs. 85.9 EPDMS). On 739 intent-critical scenarios, GATS covers 95.8% of hazardous vehicles and achieves a 0.09% collision rate---73.5% lower than the dense model (0.34%).

papers.title: Strong-deflection scaling in nearly symmetric thin-shell wormholes
papers.abstract: The angular winding of a returning light ray can grow while the family of admissible impacts disappears. We characterize this competition near reflection symmetry in a static thin-shell wormhole joining Schwarzschild exteriors of slightly different masses. Exact shell-frame matching fixes the reflected interval, and a normal coordinate at each nondegenerate photon-sphere maximum gives a composite angular expansion with controlled error on compact interior channel intervals. The result remains valid when the throat distance divided by the mass contrast tends to zero, stays finite or diverges. For a throat distance proportional to a positive power of the fractional mass difference, the width exponent increases from one toward two and then saturates, while the logarithmic winding coefficient decreases from three toward two. Fixed-throat configurations retain their finite-distance amplitude and coefficient three. Reference-subtracted profiles connect the intermediate sector to finite and vanishing scaled throat positions. Independent quadratures test the scaling laws and resolve the slower convergence associated with changing scale ratios. The shrinking solid-angle aperture follows directly from the critical-impact gap. For an axial observer and a transparent test disk confined to the same exterior, the return-phase condition selects the admitted intersections; sampled near-symmetric configurations shift the first available global crossing to a later label. The closing aperture and increasing winding are therefore linked by the accessible radial extent, with disk access determined by the phase accumulated on the emitting segment.

papers.title: Thin-shell wormholes from magnetic black holes in exponential electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Transparent magnetic wormholes can share a black hole exterior while their supporting matter controls the response of the throat. We construct symmetric thin shells from the magnetic black hole of exponential nonlinear electrodynamics and derive their equilibrium stresses and linear radial stability criterion. Restricting the seed to its zero-bare-mass magnetic branch ties the charge and coupling along the fixed-mass family. In the sampled configurations, calibrated linear barotropic shells are unstable, whereas variable phantom and variable Chaplygin laws admit locally stable radial sectors. Explicit radius dependence strengthens the phantom restoring term; the Chaplygin response cancels the divergent inverse lapse contribution and permits stable sectors close to a non-extremal seed horizon. The surface density remains negative, although an inner interval satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. At the seed photon sphere, the two variable laws share an exact stabilization threshold. The complete radial averaged null energy remains negative even when the proper shell energy tends to zero. Numerical null geodesic imaging uses independent, minimally coupled light and transparent junctions, with celestial sources and rotating thin disks truncated at the ISCO. For observer-side disk emission with the prescribed ISCO truncation and a throat below the seed photon sphere, inclined images coincide with the seed black hole image. A throat above that sphere removes selected returning contributions while preserving much of the bright primary structure. Illuminating the opposite exterior adds inner disk arcs, but a central dark region can survive because the disk does not illuminate every transmitted direction. The resulting image degeneracy depends jointly on the retained null trajectories and the emitting support, rather than on the presence of a horizon alone.

papers.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate right and left matrix Riemann--Hilbert problems and derive parametric formulas for reconstructing both components. These formulas also use a transported profile determined by the initial ratio of the two momenta. Under suitable regularity and positivity assumptions, we show that a solution of the right Riemann--Hilbert problem, together with this profile, yields a local solution of the 2-mCH system. For a common constant background, we construct a family of smooth reflectionless solutions associated with a single pair of discrete eigenvalues. The scalar soliton, obtained when the profile vanishes, is the only travelling wave in this family.

papers.title: Generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and unirationality of del Pezzo surfaces of degree $2$
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and study their relation to quasi-étale double covers. As an application, we prove that a del Pezzo surface of degree $2$ over an infinite field of characteristic different from $2$ is unirational if it has a rational generalized Eckardt point. This settles a case left open by Manin's construction. We also obtain unirationality results for Du Val del Pezzo surfaces of degrees $1$ and $2$, and discuss applications to the Hilbert property, equivariant unirationality, and the real plane Cremona group.

papers.title: Inelastic Kinetic Decoupling in WIMP Leptogenesis: A Minimal $Z_4$ Model
papers.abstract: We study a minimal $Z_4$-symmetric extension of the Standard Model in which a singlet Dirac fermion $χ$ constitutes dark matter, whose annihilations generate a lepton asymmetry through WIMP leptogenesis. Kinetic equilibrium is maintained mainly by the inelastic conversion $χL\leftrightarrow\barχΨ$. Compared with the near elastic regime, a sizable mass gap suppresses the conversion rate more rapidly as the Universe cools. This naturally drives kinetic decoupling to earlier times, even away from resonance. Starting from the full inelastic collision operator, we derive an effective momentum transfer rate for kinetic decoupling. We then solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for the dark matter abundance, its temperature $T_χ$, and the $B-L$ asymmetry. Early kinetic decoupling can significantly modify the relic abundance, although near resonance this modification can be reduced by annihilation-induced heating. The $B-L$ asymmetry can be affected when asymmetry production overlaps with a substantial departure from kinetic equilibrium. In our scan, the largest deviations occur mainly for $x_{\rm lep}\gtrsim x_{\rm cd}$. After imposing our constraints, asymmetry production typically ends before chemical decoupling, leaving the final asymmetry essentially unchanged. For indirect detection, we generate the photon spectrum with Pythia and evaluate the Fermi-LAT dwarf spheroidal likelihood.

papers.title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right
papers.abstract: Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) is now a common ingredient in language-model pre-training, as it improves downstream performance and enables faster inference through speculative decoding. We identify a flaw in standard MTP training, in which a residual component of the MTP gradient interferes with both next-token and multi-token learning, increasingly so with scale. Specifically, the MTP cross-entropy gradient can be decomposed exactly into a KL self-distillation term that pulls each MTP head toward the model's own next-token prediction (NTP) distribution and improves speculative decoding, and a residual that has a low signal-to-noise ratio and buries the useful KL signal. We introduce the KL gradient-recovery trick: when two distributions share a linear output head, the gradient of their KL divergence can be recovered exactly by combining their cross-entropy gradients through straight-through gradient routing. Unlike minimizing the KL directly, this trick requires no vocabulary-sized logit matrices and is compatible with standard fused cross-entropy kernels. This enables Soft Multi-Token Prediction (Soft-MTP), a one-line code change to MTP that removes the noisy residual and backpropagates only the KL self-distillation signal by reusing the existing NTP and MTP cross-entropy computations. Soft-MTP supports both DeepSeek- and Meta-style MTP, adds no parameters, and incurs no measurable overhead. From 167M to 1.2B parameters, Soft-MTP improves over standard MTP with lower NTP perplexity, faster speculative decoding and higher zero-shot accuracy at every scale, lower MTP perplexity from 689M onward, and stronger math and code reasoning after fine-tuning at 1.2B. Soft-MTP also matches, if not exceeds, direct KL divergence minimization on most metrics. Soft-MTP is, in effect, a free lunch for MTP optimization. Our code can be found at https://github.com/JaydenTeoh/Soft-MTP.

papers.title: SPARSEBLEED: Bypassing Attribute-Inference Defenses via Sparsity Optimizations
papers.abstract: When a model trained on sensitive records is exposed through a prediction API, an attribute-inference attack (AIA) plugs each possible value of a missing field into a partially known record to infer which value belonged to the training record. Current defenses mask confidence scores and hide internal activations. We show that sparsity optimizations, software and hardware routines (sparse kernels) that skip arithmetic and memory fetches on zero activations or weights, reopen attribute inference through the execution footprint. We introduce SparseBleed, the first hardware and execution-based AIA on training data. Training makes neuron firing selective to sensitive attributes, so each candidate value activates a different set of neurons and sparse kernels skip the rest; the candidate value therefore sets how many multiply-accumulate operations execute and which weight columns are read, shifting response time and shared-hardware contention even when only a class label is returned. SparseBleed calibrates each candidate's footprint against reference measurements for that value. Across 11 CPU and GPU sparse libraries (e.g., Intel oneDNN-AMX, NVIDIA cuSPARSE), MLPs, and FT-Transformers up to 1.5B parameters, execution time on TACO varies by up to ~25,000 timer ticks across prediction-confidence levels. The strongest SparseBleed variant gains +16.4 points in mean accuracy over label-only LOMIA and +8.9 over confidence-based CSMIA, up to +32 points over random guessing in a single query on CPU and +15 on GPU, reaches 60.5% mean AUC with 50 calibration records, and widens its margin over output-only attacks from +6.0 to +12.9 points as FT-Transformers scale from 288M to 1.5B. Response-time padding leaves co-resident channels open; thus, privacy requires equalizing executed work and memory access (4.8-13.7% overhead in our patches).

papers.title: Analysis of CONUS+ run 2: Detector performance, background model and CE$ν$NS measurement
papers.abstract: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) provides a uniquely sensitive probe of neutrino properties, but its detection requires pushing energy thresholds to the sub-keV scale while controlling backgrounds. The CONUS+ experiment, located at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, reported the first observation of CE$ν$NS using reactor antineutrinos in 2025. Following a detector upgrade that replaced three of the original 1 kg high-purity germanium detectors with larger 2.42 kg diodes, this paper presents the analysis of the CONUS+ run 2 dataset, including the detector characterization, the background model, the signal prediction and expected sensitivity, and the extraction of the CE$ν$NS signal. The new detectors reach a background level per unit mass reduced by approximately a factor of two relative to the original detectors, while reaching energy thresholds between 140 and 170 eV$_{ee}$. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on and 86 kg$\cdot$days reactor-off, a blind likelihood analysis fitting directly the number of signal counts yields $N_s = 1565 \pm 155$ CE$ν$NS events and a relative precision of 9.9\%. The result is in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events, with $N_s/N_{\mathrm{SM}} = 0.92 \pm 0.14$.

papers.title: Precision measurement of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering at a nuclear reactor by CONUS+
papers.abstract: We report the most precise measurement to date of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) from reactor antineutrinos, using the CONUS+ germanium detectors at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on, a blind likelihood analysis yields a signal with high statistical significance, corresponding to $1565 \pm 155$ CE$ν$NS events, in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events within 0.5 $σ$. The flux-averaged cross section is $(0.57 \pm 0.09)\times10^{-40}$ cm$^{2}$, and the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV is $\sin^2θ_W = 0.226 \pm 0.022$.

papers.title: A Bi-level Co-design Framework for Lunar Monoped with 2D Jump and Landing Control
papers.abstract: Legged robots for lunar exploration must be designed for low gravity, where reduced contact forces and long flight phases make leg morphology and controller choice interdependent. We study this for a planar monoped in lunar gravity (1.625 m/s^2) using a bi-level co-design framework: a differential evolution outer loop searches over link lengths, and each candidate is evaluated on a vertical jump by either a quadratic program based task-space controller (QP-TSC) or a direct-collocation based trajectory optimization. The two controllers yield different optimal link lengths, and trajectory optimization outperforms the QP-TSC across most of the design space, with 17% lower Cost of Transport (COT) at their respective optima. We then extend to a 2D jump, where trajectory optimization with centroidal angular momentum regulation produces stable in-place and forward jumps, and an LQR controller absorbs impact and stabilizes the robot after touchdown. This is demonstrated on a baseline morphology with both links 0.3 m long.

papers.title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. We also obtain some results about the set of all efficient dominating sets in any circulant graph. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained. These results extend some theorems in [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1503--1507], [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1522--1527], and [Des. Codes Cryptogr. 94 (2026), 87].

papers.title: Variational Optimal Control for Diffusion Guidance
papers.abstract: Sampling-time guidance and reward-based post-training act on different variables but share a core geometric objective: realizing an output-space improvement through a generative model. We organize both around a Jacobian pullback evaluated with respect to either the current noisy state or the trainable parameters. Formulating current-state conditional variational optimal control (VOC) yields Variational Optimal Guidance (VOG), which transports a terminal reward proxy into a covariance-weighted sampling correction. Under a linear-subspace denoising model, the exact pullback has no component normal to the data subspace. Distilled Variational Optimal Control (DVOC) realizes the parameter-space counterpart of this local control principle: projected reward ascent constructs a bounded endpoint displacement within a local trust region, and a sparse, forward-pinned Euler surrogate transports it to LoRA parameters. Empirically, VOG reduces DiT-XL/2 FID on ImageNet from 2.27 to 2.04 at 250 sampling steps and from 7.58 to 4.44 at 25 steps. After 20 updates on Z-Image-Turbo, DVOC improves HPSv3++ and four held-out evaluator scores over the untrained model and leads all trained comparators on these five means, while CLIP remains close to the base and DeQA declines across all trained methods. The shared pullback interface cleanly separates the desired output change from the model derivative and the actuation variable.

papers.title: Doubly robust estimation of direct and spillover effects using multiple pre-treatment periods
papers.abstract: Under interference, the treatment of some units affects the outcomes of others, so that the effect on a treated unit consists of a direct and a spillover component. A non-treated comparison group then generally identifies neither component, but the difference between the total effect on the treated and the spillover effect on the comparison units. Under certain identifying assumptions, both components may be identified separately when multiple pre-treatment periods are available, even in the absence of an uncontaminated comparison group. Under a no-anticipation assumption, pre-treatment outcomes are free of both components for every unit. Extrapolating the pre-treatment trend within a group, as in interrupted time-series approaches, therefore identifies the counterfactual outcome in the absence of any treatment, provided that the model used for the extrapolation is correctly specified. Applied to the treated it gives the total effect on them, applied to the non-treated at a given level of exposure the spillover effect on them. Disentangling the two components in addition requires effect homogeneity across treated and non-treated units with the same exposure and covariates, as well as common support in exposure. We derive doubly robust and Neyman-orthogonal expressions for the effects of interest, which permits controlling for possibly high-dimensional covariates by machine learning. A simulation study confirms the root-$n$ consistent behaviour of the estimators and the reliability of the standard errors under specific regularity conditions. We apply the framework to the compulsory licensing of enemy-owned patents in the United States in 1919. Licensing raised patenting in the licensed subclasses and in technologically close ones alike, so that a comparison-group design understates the total effect.

papers.title: Advancement or Acceleration? How Data Curation Improves LLM Training
papers.abstract: While data curation is widely credited with improving large language model training, a basic question remains unresolved: does curation expand what a model can ultimately learn, or reach the same solution faster? In this paper, we formalize this distinction between advancement (improving the attainable performance) and acceleration (reaching the same performance with less data). Through an analytic characterization and real-world LLM experiments, we show that advancement requires a correctable train-target gap. When the baseline training and target objectives coincide, no curation policy improves the endpoint, and its benefit is acceleration. This reframes advancement as a property of the curation task rather than the curation method. Under a common gap-centric view of data mixture and selection, we operationalize this condition as the $Δ$-diagnostic, an observable discrepancy between the uncurated baseline's training and target losses that is computable prior to expensive curation. Across extensive experiments, an appreciably nonzero $Δ$ predicts persistent gains, whereas gains near $Δ=0$ tend to diminish as the training budget grows. Beyond individual methods, our findings recenter data curation on the task itself and point to target-set construction as a promising direction for shaping what curation can achieve.

papers.title: D4GS: Efficient Gaussian Splatting SLAM with Depth Priors
papers.abstract: Achieving high-quality reconstruction and responsive camera tracking remains challenging for monocular RGB Gaussian splatting SLAM under a limited optimization budget. We present an online system that addresses this challenge by combining learned geometric priors with explicit geometric camera tracking, which efficiently performs camera tracking while maintaining the map to keep the predicted depth scale consistent. A frozen depth model serves as a virtual RGB-D sensor, providing depth estimation from monocular video. An explicit geometric solver then estimates camera pose through feature reprojection, and a streaming Gaussian mapper integrates the resulting observations into a dense scene representation. Extensive experiments on indoor and outdoor datasets show that our method significantly improves reconstruction quality over existing approaches, achieving over 10 FPS on a single RTX 4090 and delivering almost twice the throughput of the evaluated fastest prior SLAM systems on the 7-Scenes dataset.

papers.title: Bias Correction and Inference for Panel Quantile Regression
papers.abstract: We develop a large-$n$, large-$T$ theory for the unsmoothed fixed-effects quantile regression estimator that allows for serially correlated panel data. An exact rank-score identity for the profiled criterion, with a convexity argument, delivers the leading incidental parameter bias of the slope estimator, of order $T^{-1}$, in closed form, paralleling Hahn and Newey (2004) for smooth nonlinear panel models. When $n$ and $T$ grow at the same rate, the estimator is asymptotically normal but in general not centred, and conventional intervals are invalid. In stationary panels whose dependence decays geometrically or polynomially, with $n/T$ bounded, serial correlation changes the structure of this bias: the long-run variance of the quantile score enters it, and feedback from past errors to current regressors adds a term that can bias the estimator even at the median. A split-panel jackknife with contiguous half-panels removes the bias, whereas one with interleaved half-panels does not in general, and a cluster-robust variance estimator, clustered by individual, yields valid inference. Under independence over time, the admissible growth of $n$ relative to $T$, up to $n=o(T^3)$, depends on the regularity of the conditional error densities, and the jackknife is valid throughout this range.

papers.title: ObjectTwin: Training-Free Asset Verification for Captured Scenes
papers.abstract: An editable digital twin needs assets that faithfully represent the particular objects captured. Partial observations leave both unseen geometry and asset placement uncertain: several registrations can explain the available views while predicting different surfaces elsewhere. We introduce ObjectTwin, a training-free framework for capture-conditioned asset verification. It retains calibration-compatible alignments, checks observed surfaces and known free space, and carries the resulting range of evidence into acceptance, exclusion, or deferred inspection. Withheld observations evaluate each fixed decision. Across Replica and ScanNet, capture correspondence improves held-out asset selection over registered geometry, reducing mean IoU regret by 55% on shared candidate pairs. Across multiview reconstruction, amodal completion, and scene generation, surface-based selection identifies the best unseen-view candidate for 97.5% of shared test objects. Controlled edits verify sensitivity to visible errors and invariance to unobserved geometry. Compatible alignments also predict different unseen outcomes, while strong single-fit controls distinguish this sensitivity from gains in screening accuracy. Together, these experiments establish capture correspondence as a useful asset-selection signal and provide a reproducible framework for evaluating absolute quality and alignment-dependent decisions.

papers.title: Relative norm averaging property and selflessness of almost periodic actions
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra with a faithful state $σ$ and $G$ be a discrete group. We introduce a property called relative norm averaging property (RNA) for almost periodic $σ$-preserving actions by $G$ on $(D,σ)$. We prove that if an almost periodic $σ$-preserving action $α$ satisfies that $\overline{α(G)} \subseteq \text{Aut}(D,σ)$ is connected and nontrivial, then $α$ satisfies (RNA). As an application, we prove that if $G$ has property PHP of Ozawa and $α:G\curvearrowright (D,σ)$ is an ergodic (i.e. $D^G=\mathbb{C}$) almost periodic $σ$-preserving action with $\overline{α(G)}$ being connected, then $D\rtimes_r G$ is selfless. This includes certain paradoxical isometric actions of $\mathbb{F}_2$ on the sphere. In non-ergodic case, we prove that the relative norm averaging property implies that $D\rtimes_r G$ satisfies the $D^G$-valued selfless, if $G$ satisfies PHP.

papers.title: Synthetic linguistic data
papers.abstract: Synthetic linguistic data have become increasingly prominent in linguistic research, from the analysis of large collections of AI-generated texts to controlled computational experiments investigating grammatical and lexical preferences. This glossary entry extends Bresnan's (2016) distinction between the linguistic garden and the bush by introducing an artificial plant nursery as a metaphor for synthetic data. We distinguish between two complementary forms of synthetic linguistic data according to how they are collected and investigated: synthetic bush-like data, consisting primarily of corpus-like collections of model-generated language, and synthetic garden-like data, in which model outputs are elicited or evaluated under controlled conditions to investigate specific linguistic hypotheses. We argue that synthetic data constitute a distinct object of linguistic investigation; comparing them with natural language data can reveal both shared patterns and divergences, but their interpretation requires careful consideration of the conditions under which they are generated.

papers.title: SWE-Ladder: Learning to Localize, Reproduce, and Patch via Progressive Privileged Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Resolving a repository-level issue typically requires a software-engineering (SWE) agent to localize the faulty code, reproduce the failure, and patch the code. Reinforcement learning trains such agents from a single test result on the final patch, while on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) adds token-level supervision from a teacher with privileged evidence, exposing the full reference patch at every step. Neither provides stage-specific guidance for localization or reproduction. We propose SWE-Ladder, which turns the verified repair of each training instance into stage-specific evidence: the changed files and lines for localization, the fail-to-pass tests for reproduction, and the diff for patching. A rule-based router assigns each step of an end-to-end rollout to a stage based on its tool call, a frozen teacher sees only the matching evidence, and the stages are distilled in repair order while GRPO optimizes the full trajectory. With Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on SWE-bench Verified under the R2E-Gym scaffold, SWE-Ladder improves pass@1 from 9.6% to 16.4%, compared with 10.4% for GRPO and 12.4% for OPSD with the full patch. Under the OpenHands scaffold, it improves pass@1 from 13.0% to 17.6%. Reversing the stage order under R2E-Gym reduces pass@1 to 11.4%.

papers.title: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a closed manifold is regular. On even-dimensional manifolds we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics with trivial isometry group carrying Zoll families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism. In particular, this applies to all even-dimensional manifolds with a Besse family.

papers.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $μ$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(μ)$, then $μ$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.

papers.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.

papers.title: SABLE: Scalable Affine Bayesian Latent-space Exploration
papers.abstract: Complex objects such as engineering designs and proteins are often difficult to optimise because their design spaces exhibit high-dimensional structure and objective evaluations are expensive. Generative models provide continuous latent representations, but their latent spaces can have thousands to tens of thousands of dimensions, creating a regime where the latent dimension $D$ exceeds the evaluation budget. We introduce SABLE, a Bayesian optimisation method for high-dimensional latent spaces with an isotropic distribution and limited budget. SABLE uses a Bayesian affine surrogate for prediction and acquisition, treating higher-order structure as surrogate discrepancy. After $N$ observations, the slope update has dimension at most $N-1$, yielding a decomposition of each query into an in-span component optimised by expected improvement (EI) in at most $N$ dimensions and an off-span component governed by a scalar norm. We show that the off-span norm implicitly selected by affine EI can lead to underexploration, and SABLE instead prescribes it using an exploration schedule, without restricting search to a learned subspace. An efficient recompression scheme reduces information to $\mathcal O(M)$ pseudo-observations, bringing the overall time complexity per step to $\mathcal O(M^2D+M^3+D\log D)$ while keeping parameter inference, prediction, and acquisition decisions to tens of milliseconds. Across synthetic benchmarks and latent-space optimisation tasks, SABLE achieves high sample efficiency and reduces decision time by several orders of magnitude at large budgets.

papers.title: On Lusztig Sheaves for Tame Quivers
papers.abstract: Let $Q$ be a connected quiver of tame type, and let $U_v^-$ be the positive part of the corresponding quantized affine algebra. In Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis of $U_v^-$, the simple perverse sheaves occurring, up to shift, as direct summands of the flag sheaf complexes are given by intersection cohomology complexes $\operatorname{IC}(X(c,m),\mathcal{L}_χ)$. We study the restrictions of these intersection cohomology complexes to the locally closed subsets $Y(c,m)$ obtained by fixing the preprojective, non-homogeneous regular, and preinjective summands in the category $\operatorname{rep} Q$. We prove pointwise purity on the loci where the homogeneous regular part is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic quasi-simple modules, and establish a semisimple decomposition of the restrictions to the corresponding larger strata. The graded multiplicities of the local systems associated with irreducible characters of symmetric groups determine the transition coefficients from the canonical basis to the PBW basis constructed via quiver representations. This gives a geometric explanation of the positivity of these coefficients and the unitriangularity of the transition matrix.

papers.title: Production of the weakly bound $T_{cc}^+$ state combining the coalescence model with its mass spectrum
papers.abstract: We investigate the production of the doubly charmed molecular state $T_{cc}^+$ within the coalescence model. The formation probability is evaluated with the Wigner distribution function. In contrast to previous studies, which usually adopt a Gaussian wave function, we obtain the molecular wave function by numerically solving the coupled-channel Schrödinger equation with the one-boson-exchange potential fitted to the mass spectrum of $T_{cc}^+$. The resulting wave function is the universal form of a weakly bound $S$-wave molecule in momentum space (a Yukawa-type exponential in coordinate space), dressed by the dipole form factor of the OBE interaction, and is thus more suitable for such a state. As the input of the coalescence model, we use the transverse-momentum distributions of the constituent $D$ and $D^*$ mesons fitted to the ALICE and LHCb data, and also generated by PYTHIA for comparison. We compute the transverse-momentum distributions of $T_{cc}^+$ in $pp$ and Pb-Pb collisions. The two collision systems differ in which part of the wave function is probed: for the extended Pb--Pb source the universal pure-Lorentzian form suffices, whereas for the compact $pp$ source the short-distance part of the wave function, captured by the dipole form factor, becomes relevant. These results provide a theoretical reference for future experimental measurements of $T_{cc}^+$.

papers.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established. A series of numerical experiments has been performed to confirm the theoretical results of this paper.

papers.title: VERDICT: Multi-Agent Parallel Modular Verification
papers.abstract: Deductive verification scales to large software systems through modular reasoning, where formal contracts summarize the behavior of individual functions and enable their independent verification. Its central bottleneck is specification synthesis: constructing the contracts required for modular verification. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled automated specification synthesis at unprecedented scale. However, existing approaches remain fundamentally bottom-up, requiring callees to be verified before their callers. This dependency limits parallelism and provides no principled mechanism for resolving interprocedural inconsistencies that propagate across call chains. We present VERDICT, a multi-agent framework for parallelizing modular deductive verification of large-scale programs. VERDICT is built on two key principles. First, assumption-based parallel specification synthesis assigns an agent to each function and allows it to proceed immediately using assumed contracts for its callees, enabling verification to proceed in parallel across the program. Second, bidirectional interprocedural conflict reconciliation resolves the inconsistencies introduced by these assumptions: when a synthesized contract contradicts an assumption, agents propagate the necessary revisions both up and down the call graph until the contracts converge. Experimental results on real-world C programs show that VERDICT synthesizes higher-quality specifications than existing approaches while substantially reducing verification time. In particular, VERDICT is the first approach that scales to the complete 20,000-line X.509 parser, ruling out nearly all the potential runtime errors within hours, whereas prior tools like PREGUSS fall far short even after days of execution.

papers.title: CaPS: A causal world model for out-of-distribution physical parameter shifts
papers.abstract: A world model that serves as a robot's digital twin has to keep working when the robot changes, for example when its links become heavier than anything seen in training. We study this case on the TriFinger robot in CausalWorld, assuming that the link masses and the low-level control law are known. Our model, CaPS (a causal world model for physical parameter shifts), gives each finger a learned energy in which every movable link contributes a term scaled by its measured mass, plus one term that does not depend on mass. Inertia and bias forces both come from this energy, actions pass through the known proportional-derivative controller, and a residual network that never sees the masses accounts for contact. Trained with light links, CaPS forecasts 100 steps open loop on three disjoint test ranges whose mean masses are 1.86, 2.75, and 3.75 times the training mean, with median joint R2 of 0.773, 0.779, and 0.750; an ensemble-residual variant, CaPS-Ens, reaches 0.801, 0.784, and 0.753. Compared with separately trained controls that see only the training-mean mass, the true masses improve both models in all ten runs at every shift. A rigid-body calculation traces the mass-independent term to the fingertips, whose mass is not intervened on, and adding the same term to ModLaNet improves it at every shift.

papers.title: From Predictive Geometry to Action: Learning Complementary Predictive Representations for Embodied Manipulation
papers.abstract: Effective manipulation requires a policy to capture not only about the current scene geometry, but also about how that geometry will evolve under interaction. Existing approaches either augment policies with geometric information from current observations or introduce future prediction as auxiliary supervision, leaving open how predictive geometry should be represented for action generation. Therefore, we propose a two-stage framework, which learns complementary predictive representations from multi-view video clips. During pretraining, a frozen 3D foundation model provides dense geometric features that are compressed into predictive geometric representations and optimized to preserve scene structure and its temporal evolution. Action supervision is then applied to geometric transitions to extract a complementary motor representation that emphasizes action-relevant transitions.
