At 4K, generation is 2.05$\times$ faster for 4B and 2.23$\times$ faster for 8B than unforced 8K decoding in local amortized batch time. Tail-CRC thus enables reliable, efficient budgeted reasoning from a single rollout.

papers.title: A Comparison of Uncertainty in AI and Dynamical Climate Ensembles
papers.abstract: Climate model ensembles and their uncertainty estimates are essential for evaluating risk and designing climate policy. Yet, in the assessment of newly developed AI climate models, evaluating uncertainty is often secondary to diagnosing mean-state climate biases and trends. In this work, we conduct the first systematic comparison of uncertainty representation in ensembles of state-of-the-art AI and dynamical atmospheric climate models. Examining 2-meter temperature, 500 hPa geopotential height, and precipitable water, we find that the AI ensemble exhibits reduced internal variability and model uncertainty across variables relative to the dynamical ensemble. We show that this dampened variability causes the AI ensemble to produce more limited climate extremes and yields underdispersion relative to ERA5. Under a uniform warming scenario, the AI ensemble shows increased model uncertainty. Dynamical models grapple with their own challenges, exhibiting stronger miscalibration (overdispersion) relative to ERA5 and larger climate biases than the AI models. As AI and dynamical climate models are mutually integrated into operational climate prediction, careful consideration of their differences in uncertainty representations is crucial for grounded assessment of climate risk.

papers.title: From Local Errors to System Failures: Modeling and Benchmarking Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.abstract: In multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs), errors can propagate through intermediate messages and compromise final answers. However, outcome-based evaluation obscures how agents amplify, attenuate, or correct these errors. We propose Response-Aware Error Propagation among Agents (REPA), a structural model that connects measured local responses to system-level error propagation. REPA separately estimates input assembly and agent processing across multiple error channels, while theoretical analysis relates local modeling errors to endpoint prediction error. Experiments span three Qwen base models, six MAS workflows, and ten knowledge and reasoning settings in ErrPropBench-10. REPA achieves a mean condition-level Spearman correlation of 0.84 across base models, compared with 0.47 for direct regression. Controlled experiments also demonstrate its utility for targeted recovery. REPA-guided retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves accuracy over no retrieval by an average of 19 percentage points with 16% additional tokens. By linking local agent behavior to system susceptibility, REPA provides an interpretable foundation for studying error propagation and developing targeted optimization in MAS.

papers.title: X-BQSR: Holistic Acceleration of Base Quality Recalibration for Scalable Genomic Analysis
papers.abstract: With the continued decline in sequencing costs, genomics-based precision medicine is gaining increasing importance. The Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) is the standard framework for converting raw genomic data into actionable variants, but one of its most expensive steps is base quality score recalibration (BQSR), which corrects systematic sequencing errors. Despite significant work on accelerating other parts of the variant calling pipeline, BQSR has not been systematically explored on GPUs. In this work, we analyze BQSR to identify computational and I/O bottlenecks and show that simply offloading key stages to an accelerator is insufficient to achieve overall gains. We then present X-BQSR, a holistic redesign of the entire BQSR pipeline, including I/O, compression, and kernel execution, to better leverage GPU parallelism. We implement X-BQSR using portable SYCL kernels for NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs, along with native CUDA and HIP backends for comparison, and we evaluate its performance against previous FPGA work. Our evaluation shows up to 141.7x acceleration compared to standard GATK and 8.7x acceleration compared to a proprietary GPU-accelerated solution.

papers.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.

papers.title: Sharp High-Dimensional Self-Normalized Central Limit Theorems
papers.abstract: We study Gaussian approximation over all coordinate rectangles for coordinatewise self-normalized sums of iid centered random vectors. The Gaussian reference has the population correlation matrix, which may be singular. Under a fixed bound $K>1$ on the standardized marginal third absolute moments, uniform approximation over the corresponding moment class holds exactly when $d=o(\sqrt n)$ under arbitrary coordinate dependence. If $R_{jk}\le1-a$ for $j\ne k$ and a fixed $a\in(0,1]$, the necessary and sufficient condition becomes $\log d=o(n^{1/3})$. For marginal moment order $q\ge3$, we also allow the correlation gap $a_n$ to depend on $n$. For every fixed $0<β<1/3$, uniform approximation over the corresponding class in dimension $d_n=\lfloor e^{n^β}\rfloor$ holds if and only if $a_n\log n\to\infty$. Under arbitrary dependence, we determine the sharp error order $1\wedge\{d/n^{(q-2)/2}\}^{1/q}$ for every $q\ge3$ and $d\ge2$. At a fixed positive gap, we identify, for every $q>2$, the supremum of the decay exponents in uniform error bounds that allow fixed logarithmic factors. The proofs replace observations one at a time, keeping their contributions to both numerator and denominator in the same expansion. The resulting weights depend only on the retained sample, allowing the remainders to be controlled by marginal moments.

papers.title: On the stress-bienergy tensor of conformal immersions and hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study the stress-bienergy tensor $\bar S_2$ of a conformal immersion $ϕ:(M^m,\bar g)\to(N^n,h)$ with conformal factor $λ$, and we compute it, together with its trace and its divergence, in terms of $λ$ and of the second fundamental form of the associated isometric immersion. This gives a characterization of biconservative conformal immersions and, for hypersurfaces, we prove that $\mathrm{div}\,\bar S_2=0$ if and only if the tangent part of the bitension field vanishes. We introduce conformally biconservative hypersurfaces and show that a totally umbilical hypersurface of a space form is conformally biconservative with a non-constant conformal factor if and only if this factor is an isoparametric function satisfying an explicit ordinary differential equation. We illustrate this result with several examples, in which dimension four plays a special role. Finally, we study the equation $\bar S_2=0$: on a compact manifold of dimension $m\neq 4$, it forces the associated isometric immersion to be harmonic.

papers.title: Kushel--Tyaglov's problem, sharp Schoenberg-type inequalities and majorization relations between zeros and critical points
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a purely complex-analytic proof of Schoenberg's conjecture. We also determine the sharp constants in Schoenberg-type inequalities for every real exponent $p>0$ and every degree $n\ge2$, and characterize all corresponding extremal configurations. In particular, we confirm two conjectures posed in \cite{TZ25} and provide a complete solution to a problem of Kushel and Tyaglov. Furthermore, we introduce the tool of weighted weak majorization and establish, under the zero-centroid condition, new weak-majorization relations between the moduli of the critical points and those of the zeros. As consequences of these relations, we obtain refinements of several known results.

papers.title: Dawn of the Gaia Era: Revisiting Cold Jupiters Orbiting M Dwarfs with Astrometry+Doppler Data Joint Analysis
papers.abstract: We perform a joint analysis of ground-based radial velocities (RVs), Hipparcos Intermediate Astrometric Data, and two-epoch Gaia astrometry for known M dwarfs hosting cold Jupiters discovered through long-term spectroscopic monitoring. Among a sample of 25 planets in 19 systems, we derive robust absolute masses and orbital solutions for 13 planets in 11 systems with companion inclination uncertainties lower than 30 degrees. These include first mass measurements for five planets: GJ 328b, GJ 649b, GJ 849b and c, and GJ 9066c. We also reclassify one object, HIP 79431B, as a brown dwarf. We further compare the mass ratios of these 13 cold Jupiter systems with those of giant planets orbiting M stars characterized via transit, microlensing, and direct imaging. Without correcting for detection bias, we find that (1) there is likely a deficiency of high-mass-ratio hot Jupiters around M dwarfs compared with cold Jupiters, and (2) the local cold Jupiters orbiting M stars found by RV observations exhibit a similar mass ratio distribution as the counterparts in the Galactic bulge found by microlensing. Cold Jupiters orbiting stars with masses above $0.65~M_\odot$ tend to be more massive than those around M dwarfs. Our study establishes a sample of local cold Jupiters with precise mass determinations around M dwarfs, and reveal a tip of the iceberg in the upcoming Gaia DR4 and DR5.

papers.title: DKnown-Jev-2: Article-Level Answer-Evidence Classification and Efficient Inference with a Pre-trained Language Model
papers.abstract: Evidence selection in normative knowledge question answering requires determining whether a candidate article contains content that directly supports an answer under the applicable conditions of the question. We present DKnown-Jev-2, an article-level answer evidence classifier designed for evidence integration across multiple paragraphs. The model jointly encodes question conditions, article metadata, and paragraph content, and uses a pointer-style classification head to predict Answer Evidence (AE) and Non-answer Evidence (NE) in a single forward pass. Ona manually annotated test set of 972 evaluation instances, DKnown-Jev-2 achieves 91.77% accuracy and 91.28% macro-F1, outperforming Jev by 2.16 and 2.37 percentage points, respectively, while reducing both evidence misses and non-evidence false positives. The test set contains 317 multi-paragraph instances, with a maximum body length of 9,322 characters. Shared article encoding and non-autoregressive classification support low-latency inference. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for article-level evidence selection in normative knowledge question answering.

papers.title: CAST: A Deployed Speech-to-Text Cascade for Closed Captioning of Entertainment Television
papers.abstract: Despite rapid progress in automatic speech recognition (ASR), caption generation for long-form entertainment video remains challenging for content dense in music and effects, rich in accents, crosstalk, and noise. The transcript quality depends on segmentation and surrounding modules as much as the acoustic model. A single pass voice activity detection (VAD) can miss faint, low-energy voice while forwarding near-silent segments that induce hallucination and repetition in an autoregressive decoder. These competing errors motivate a hierarchical VAD that revisits rejected segments under semantic and acoustic retention checks. We present Captioning ASR Stack for Television (CAST), an integrated speech-to-text pipeline for closed captioning (CC) combining frozen Whisper large-v3 with segmentation, language identification, lyrics routing, and targeted hallucination detection and repair on a single NVIDIA L4 GPU. On 100 in-house assets spanning 60.46 hours, CAST reduces normalized WER from 6.99% to 5.36% and subtitle edit rate from 254.2 to 221.9 min/hour against the WhisperX pipeline, and improves deletion rate by 11% on public datasets. We also present the behavior of each stage in the pipeline. CAST entered the production speech-to-text (STT) stage of our CC pipeline in late August 2026; we report the evaluation evidence and path to full-scale operation.

papers.title: Completing analytical conversion scheme among DH, Hayati, CPC and POE models for manipulator calibration
papers.abstract: Building on Mooring's decomposition of the calibration procedure into four stages - modeling, measurement, identification, and correction - this paper investigates the role of analytical kinematic model conversion algorithms within the calibration framework and their potential to improve calibration performance. Four prominent and widely cited kinematic models: Denavit-Hartenberg (DH), Hayati (HAY), Complete and Parametrically Continuous (CPC), and Product of Exponentials (POE), - are considered. A systematic analysis of the existing conversion relationships reveals that, although most conversions among these models have already been established in the literature, a direct analytical conversion between POE and HAY, and CPC and HAY remains unavailable. Relying instead on a sequential combination of the existing POE-DH and DH-HAY conversions, for example, introduces several limitations. To address this gap, we develop a constructive analytical conversion between POE-HAY and HAY-CPC models based on Lie group theory, formally established through a set of lemmas and propositions. The proposed algorithms are illustrated using an RRRP SCARA robot and an RRHHHH Puma 560 manipulator. The direct POE-HAY conversion is compared with the sequential POE-DH-HAY approach, as well as HAY-CPC in terms of several relevant criteria, demonstrating the advantages of the proposed solution. Finally, we demonstrate the practical significance of the completed analytical conversion framework in an open-loop kinematic calibration experiment on an ABB IRB 1600 manipulator, using an API Radian EMSD3 Laser Tracker for measurements. The experimental results demonstrate that proper model selection combined with completed analytical conversion scheme directly improves calibration accuracy.

papers.title: ReWeave: Emergent Physical Task Topologies for Embodied Harness Optimization and Cross-Task Meta-Distillation
papers.abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks involve physical dependencies that may only become clear through interaction. As task understanding deepens, past trials can reveal new information for adaptation and transfer. However, coarse progress feedback cannot identify which physical preconditions held, leaving search unguided, while task-specific optimization easily overfits to individual scenes, making cross-task transfer brittle. We introduce ReWeave, a framework that jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights. Keeping execution policies and perception frozen, ReWeave co-optimizes coupled context, workflows, and control loops. As new evidence revises the topology, ReWeave reprojects past trials onto the updated task understanding, exposing retained progress, regressions, and bottlenecks that guide parent selection and search width. Across tasks, matching verified local mechanisms to unmet preconditions consolidates 72 specialist units into 44 reusable groups ($0.34\times$ full concatenation) within a compact shared harness capable of continual learning. ReWeave improves held-out success from 89.00% to 98.75% on LIBERO-PRO and from 25.50% to 58.25% on RoboDojo, while uncovering retained progress in 89% of 159 failed RoboDojo development trials and translating stronger offline reasoning into higher online performance. On eight unseen LIBERO-PRO tasks, the shared harness reaches 51.3% success versus 41.3% for direct distillation, rising to 75.0% after continual learning.

papers.title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization
papers.abstract: Recommender systems exhibit popularity bias, often under-serving long-tail and cold-start items with sparse interaction data. We propose a group-specific data augmentation approach that leverages LLMs to generate synthetic interactions, formulated as a constrained optimization problem, maximizing group-specific NDCG@20 and coverage while bounding overall NDCG@20 degradation within an acceptable threshold. Items are partitioned by interaction frequency to find the optimal augmentation strategy for each group. We further study combining the augmentation across groups simultaneously and find that while individual optimal strategies navigate the multi-group augmentation design, they are not simply additive. We further ablate on the LLM-based augmentation itself, comparing LLM scales, augmentation configuration under token constraints, finding that augmentation quality scales with contextual richness, albeit at a proportionally higher cost. Experiments with SASRec demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving over 100% and 60% improvement in group-specific NDCG@20 for extreme and regular long-tail items, respectively, on our industrial dataset, and 40%, 25% for MovieLens-32M, while increasing their coverage without significant overall degradation.

papers.title: Automatic Occupational Coding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Annually 1.9 million deaths and 89.7 million disability-adjusted life years are caused by exposure to agents during work (e.g., welding fumes, silica dust, and noise pollution). To improve worker health, high-quality exposure assessments are crucial. Therefore, free-text job descriptions from large-scale occupational cohorts are manually standardized through occupational classifications and linked to hazardous exposures using Job Exposure Matrices (JEM). However, manual coding is slow, unreliable (i.e., 44-89% inter-coder reliability), and costly, due to i) short, ambiguous free-text job descriptions, ii) classifications containing hundreds to thousands of categories, and iii) the absence of gold standards. With 46%-79% accuracy, state-of-the-art automatic occupational coding tools achieve classification performance on human level. However, their performance drops to 17-26% on out-of-distribution datasets. Furthermore, their supervised architectures limit them to occupational classifications present in the training set. Consequently, JEM using other classifications are incompatible, leaving vital exposure-response associations unexplored. Our Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework, OPERAG, enables classification into any occupational classification without expert-labelled databases. It retrieves coding index information and combines this with Large Language Model-based classification. Validated on AsiaLymph's 36,062 real-world job descriptions, OPERAG achieved 42.6% occupational classification accuracy on the 4th coding level, substantially outperforming existing tools and approaching human coders' 51-56% inter-coder reliability. Using two JEM named ALOHA+ and SHOCK, 89.9-98.6% accuracy was achieved on exposure assessment. OPERAG approaches human-level, universal occupational classification, enabling efficient and effective large-scale exposure assessment to improve worker health.

papers.title: Gradient formula from the sphere for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the gradient property of perturbative renormalisation group flows in $d=d_c-\varepsilon$, with a potential and a metric regular at $\varepsilon=0$ up to logarithms of gauge couplings. We state properties of the renormalised functional with local couplings on the sphere $S^d$: finiteness, a local Weyl anomaly, the Ward identity of a conformal Killing vector, rotation properties and statements on the free theory. From them we derive a Ward identity without anomaly for a combination of the functional and its anomaly. Its first variation is a gradient formula whose symmetric metric contains the two-point function on the sphere and whose potential at fixed points is, in an extended form of the properties, proportional to the sphere free energy $\tilde F$ up to a constant. Sources of relevant operators enter through their Weyl variation, and in a scheme which we construct the gradient formula persists, with a nondegenerate metric if a matrix of the free theory is invertible. For multiscalar $ϕ^4$ theory and for scalars and Dirac fermions with Yukawa and quartic couplings in $d=4-\varepsilon$, for sextic scalars in $d=3-\varepsilon$ and for cubic scalars in $d=6-\varepsilon$, we derive all these properties from a finiteness hypothesis. The gradient formula then holds to all orders for the beta function defined on the sphere. For interacting gauge theories the properties remain assumptions.

papers.title: RoFE: Rotated Frozen Embeddings for Low-Data Multimodal Tabular Learning
papers.abstract: Multimodal tabular learning combines tabular data with images and text, often in settings where labeled data are scarce. Tabular foundation models such as prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) offer a promising solution via in-context learning without task-specific training. However, modern image and text encoders produce embeddings with hundreds or thousands of dimensions, far exceeding the number of features encountered during PFN pretraining. Existing approaches bridge this gap using principal component analysis (PCA) to compress frozen embeddings. Surprisingly, we find that this PCA interface can underperform simple linear classifiers when labeled examples are scarce, even though PFNs are designed for small datasets. We identify the underlying failure mechanism: the PFN's per-column standardization removes the variances of the PCA scores. When the PCA keeps every direction of the labeled examples, the examples collapse into a regular simplex in which all pairwise distances are equal. To address this problem, we propose Rotated Frozen Embeddings (RoFE), a training-free method that rotates PCA scores before PFN inference. We theoretically show that rotation makes the column variances nearly equal, so that standardization approximately preserves the embedding geometry. Across image and text classification tasks, encoders, and tabular foundation models, RoFE improves low-data performance over the PCA interface and outperforms baselines that require task-specific training. The improvements also extend to regression.

papers.title: Distill the Correction, Not the Rewrite: Hindsight Twins for Self-Improving Text-to-Image Models
papers.abstract: Text-to-image models can learn from their own mistakes by distilling a self-teacher conditioned on a vision-language critic's revised prompt. However, such self-teachers barely improve alignment, and both they and their hindsight-contrast variants absorb the critic's unintended additions to the scene, such as lighting or scenery. We attribute this to two factors: (1) the prompt already specifies the desired fix, so a useful revision must go beyond the failed span, often rewriting the entire scene and adding details that overshadow the fix; (2) although the critic localizes the error to a single span, self-teachers condition on the rewrite, entangling the intended fix with unintended additions. Motivated by these insights, we propose Hindsight Twins (HinT), which fills the critic's revision template once with the intended fix and once with the observed error and distills only their velocity difference, anchored at the user's prompt. Because text encoders spread the edit of a single slot to all other tokens, HinT further aligns the twins' token states outside the slot. Across Qwen-Image-2512, SD3.5-M, and FLUX.2-klein, HinT keeps the rate of critic-induced bias at the base-model level while matching or exceeding the alignment gains of prior self-distillation, and it keeps improving over twelve rounds of self-training where contrastive baselines decay.

papers.title: Revealing Geometry under Strong Noise: Spectral Embeddings and Clustering via Random Geometric Graphs
papers.abstract: Modern massive datasets often contain useful low-dimensional nonlinear structures that are hidden by noise. Spectral embedding algorithms rely on meaningful local relationships between observations, but noise accumulated across many coordinates can make the observed distances unreliable. This also complicates clustering when groups have curved or concentric shapes and cannot be distinguished by their centers. In this paper, we develop a new method that denoises pairwise distances before using them to construct spectral embeddings and identify communities. Our approach uses cross-fitted projections to estimate distances between the underlying signals, selects a neighborhood radius from the observed sample, and builds a random geometric graph whose spectral coordinates represent the latent geometric structure. By connecting nearby points, such a geometric graph can distinguish different groups even when their centers coincide. A novel recursive procedure is then proposed to extract clusters from the graph using its spectral embeddings when such clusters exist. On the theoretical side, under a manifold model, we provide guarantees for our spectral embedding algorithm, which can be understood through the eigendecomposition of an integral operator associated with the underlying geometry. We show that the algorithm is robust to noise when the total noise energy is comparable to the total signal energy or, under additional conditions, exceeds it. To our knowledge, this is among the first spectral embedding algorithms that can handle such strong noise in datasets with nonlinear structures. In addition, our proposed clustering algorithm can recover the underlying clusters even when their centers coincide. Numerical studies demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in mitigating noise and revealing geometric structures for both spectral embedding and clustering.

papers.title: Total curvature and area growth of entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space
papers.abstract: We prove that entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ have infinite total curvature. Since their Gauss curvature is negative, this means that their intrinsic area growth is not quadratic, as conjectured by Pérez, Rodríguez and the author. It follows that vertical planes are the only orientable complete stable surfaces with constant mean curvature and quadratic area growth in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$, and this classification is extended to surfaces with critical and supercritical constant mean curvature in the homogeneous spaces $\mathbb{E}(κ,τ)$. We also prove that the height of an entire minimal graph in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ grows at most quadratically, as conjectured by Nelli and the author, whence the extrinsic and cylindrical area growths of such a graph are exactly cubic. Our arguments rely on the conformal Calabi-Lee duality between minimal graphs in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ and spacelike graphs with constant mean curvature $τ$ in the Lorentz-Minkowski space $\mathbb{L}^3$, for which we also get sharp gradient estimates.

papers.title: When Positivity Matters: Maximal Distance Integrals on Curves and Surfaces
papers.abstract: How far apart, on average, can $n$ points in a set $A$ be? As $n\to\infty$ the answer is the $\textit{maximal energy}$ $M^{+}(A)$, the largest possible value of $\mathbb{E}|X-Y|$ when $X$ and $Y$ are independent random points of $A$ with a common distribution. If the distribution is allowed to carry negative mass, we obtain a second constant $M(A)\ge M^{+}(A)$. It is often far easier to compute: when a signed equilibrium measure exists, it is characterized by a $\textit{linear}$ potential equation, whereas the positive problem must also locate the support of the mass. This paper asks when positivity matters, that is, when $M^{+}(A)<M(A)$. For polygons and polyhedra the extremal mass sits on the vertices and closed forms abound. Even so, every hollow convex polygon has $M^{+}<M$, and a simple kite shows how a vertex can be forced out of the support. For smooth curves and surfaces the answer depends on the shape. Circles and spheres have $M^{+}=M$. The ellipse $x^2+4y^2=4$ has $M^{+}=M$ numerically, and we give its value to 50 digits. The ellipses $x^2+9y^2=9$ and $x^2+25y^2=25$ have $M^{+}<M$ numerically, with gaps in the support. For the ellipsoid $10x^2+15y^2+12z^2=15$, studied by Larcher, Schmid and Wolf, we compute 50 digits of $M$ and give strong numerical evidence that $M^{+}<M$. The extremal measure vanishes on two caps around the ends of the shortest axis. Proofs and numerical methods are collected in appendices.

papers.title: Grower-in-the-loop AI for Deployable Precision Fertilisation in Sustainable Agriculture
papers.abstract: In agriculture, typically over half of the applied nitrogen fertiliser is lost to water and to air. Precision fertilisation aims to reduce these losses while maintaining yield and quality, yet existing tools struggle to capture farm-specific challenges in determining optimal nitrogen rates. Static recommendations are common and overlook on-farm constraints, such as delays due to weather or machinery availability, or change in budgets. Each constraint governs when and how growers apply fertiliser in practice. Here we present a grower-in-the-loop framework for winter wheat in England, combining baseline fertilisation planning from a machine learning-derived nitrogen-response curve with in-season adaptation via a large language model. We evaluated the framework using data from long-term experiments (LTEs), replicated field trials, and farm deployments. Retrospective model validation using LTEs confirmed low economic decision-loss across multiple seasons. Using field and farm trials, baseline schedules were shown to match standard-practice yields with less nitrogen, whereas in-season adjusted schedules additionally retained grain quality standards. Given this enhanced performance, in-season adaptation absorbed weather, machinery and budget constraints to keep recommendations executable. The framework therefore shows promise for translating static recommendations into adaptable, grower-informed decisions for sustainable fertiliser management.

papers.title: What Do Sound Event Embeddings Reveal? Auditing Speaker Leakage in Audio Representations
papers.abstract: Pretrained audio embeddings are increasingly used as intermediate representations for sound event detection (SED) and other always-on acoustic sensing tasks. While these representations are selected for their utility on downstream tasks, they may also retain sensitive information unrelated to their intended purpose, creating privacy risks even when raw audio is not exposed. In this work, we present an empirical framework for auditing privacy leakage from pretrained audio embeddings using two complementary approaches. First, we quantify representation-level leakage by measuring statistical dependence between an audio embedding and a representation specialized for encoding sensitive information. Second, we measure attack-level leakage by training lightweight adversarial probes to recover sensitive attributes directly from the embedding. We apply this framework to four widely used audio representations (CLAP, PANNs, AST, and YAMNet) and evaluate leakage of speaker identity and gender. We found that speaker identification balanced accuracy ranges from $0.43$ to $0.72$, while gender information is also strongly recoverable. Moreover, representation-level and attack-based measurements exhibit consistent trends, with CLAP leaking the most and YAMNet leaking the lest speaker identity. These results demonstrate that intermediate audio representations are not inherently privacy-preserving interfaces and motivate privacy leakage as an explicit criterion, alongside downstream utility, when selecting representations for acoustic sensing systems.

papers.title: Degree three unramified cohomology of homogeneous spaces with finite stabilisers
papers.abstract: We provide an explicit formula for the third unramified cohomology group of homogeneous spaces of $\mathrm{SL}_n$ with finite stabilisers and a rational point, valid over an arbitrary field of characteristic prime to the order of the stabilisers. As a concrete application, we compute this group explicitly for every generalised quaternion group over an arbitrary field of characteristic 0, and settle Noether's problem over the rational numbers in the negative for those of order at least 16, thereby generalising a classical result of Serre. Over an algebraically closed field, our formula recovers and sharpens a theorem of Peyre; we further show that universal triviality of unramified cohomology in degree at most three is equivalent to its vanishing in the same degrees. Over the function field of a $p$-adic curve, we extend a result of Harari-Scheiderer-Szamuely. Over a finite field, the formula is effective and yields an algorithm for computing the group explicitly.

papers.title: Closure of averaged Einstein equations by DESI data
papers.abstract: We benchmark the hypothesis that the redshift dependence of postulated dark energy in the standard model, measured by the DESI collaboration, is a natural outcome of dark energy-free models of structure formation in general relativity. We recall fundamental results and the properties of averaged dust cosmologies that suggest to replace the dark energy equation of state through the nonperturbative impact of the inhomogeneous geometry. The relevant mechanism can be phrased in terms of an effective mean field description of inhomogeneities using the fluid analogy of a scalar field (the `morphon'). Without violating energy conditions this effective field exhibits a cross-over to phantom behaviour, compatible with observations. The exact dark energy-free framework needs a single closure condition that we implement in terms of parametrizations of the 3-years data of the DESI team. The resulting redshift dependence of effective cosmological characteristics is then illustrated and subject to physical interpretation. The aim of this paper is to set a benchmark that has to be met by any structure formation model or simulation investigated within general relativity in a flow-orthogonal foliation of spacetime, given the hypothesis.

papers.title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
papers.abstract: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations. Our results show that this moat structure is robust against thermal effects across these relativistic nuclear matter models, providing motivation for future studies of inhomogeneous phases in hot and dense astrophysical matter.

papers.title: Boundedness and $L_p$-estimates for non-local operators with square-Dini continuous coefficients
papers.abstract: We prove the boundedness of the non-local operator $\mathcal{L}^a$ of order $σ\in(0,2)$ with kernel $a(x,y)|y|^{-d-σ}$ from $H^σ_{p,w}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L_{p,w}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for the whole range of $p\in(1,\infty)$, where $w$ is a Muckenhoupt weight. The coefficient $a(x,y)$ is bounded, merely measurable in $y$, and its modulus of continuity $ω$ in $x$ satisfies the square-Dini condition $\int_0^1ω(t)^2t^{-1}dt<\infty$. This condition allows, for instance, $ω(t)=(\log(1/t))^{-1}$, which is not a Dini modulus, and it improves the Hölder continuity assumption in previous work. Using the boundedness result, we obtain global estimates and the unique solvability in weighted $L_p$ spaces, as well as interior $L_p$-estimates, for the corresponding elliptic and parabolic equations. We also show that the square-Dini condition is sharp. By adapting a recent construction of C. Liu, we show that for every regular modulus $ω$ with $\int_0^1ω(t)^2t^{-1}dt=\infty$, there is a coefficient with modulus of continuity $ω$ for which the boundedness, the global estimates, and the interior estimates all fail. In particular, on the scale $ω(t)=(\log(1/t))^{-θ}$, the threshold is $θ=1/2$.

papers.title: Boltz-Flow: Generating High-Quality Robot Action from Boltzmann Machine
papers.abstract: Flow-matching policies integrate a velocity field from a fixed, observation-independent Gaussian source. However, since the source is unimodal and identical across all tasks, the limited representational capacity of Gaussian distributions constrains how far a policy can scale with growing task diversity. Moreover, the source factorizes over time steps and control dimensions, discarding the coordination that manipulation requires. We introduce Boltz-Flow, which replaces Gaussian initialization with a more powerful, observation- and instruction-conditioned Boltzmann source while leaving the base VLA unchanged. Boltz-Flow parameterizes this source with a conditional Boltzmann machine that assigns an energy value to each binary source state. A listwise objective, supervised entirely by offline demonstrations, aligns this energy with the quality of actions produced after frozen flow integration. At inference, the energy defines an Ising instance whose solution is decoded into continuous noise before a single standard integration. We use a physical coherent Ising machine during training. Experiments show that Boltz-Flow improves $π_{0.5}$ across three benchmarks, outperforming the compared strong policy baselines and competing noise optimization methods on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 and ranking second only to LEAP on LIBERO-Plus. Additional experiments show gains under noise-adapted fine-tuning, with action-to-action warm starts, and on the SmolVLA backbone.

papers.title: SurgeCount: A Protocol-Guided Composition Harness for Bimanual Surgical Sponge Counting
papers.abstract: We present SurgeCount, a system for auditable robotic surgical sponge counting that composes learned skills under a written procedural protocol. Retained sponges cause preventable harm, and surgical teams count every sponge before closure to reduce that risk. The robot repeatedly isolates one deformable sponge from a tangled pile and places it in the next numbered counting-tray slot, requiring handling of occluded grasp threads while preserving step order. We train one subtask-conditioned policy on eleven short skills and learn when each skill ends. At each learned boundary, a stateful vision-language model selects the next skill from an operator-authored specification of step order, visual verification, and recovery. This creates temporal commitment to each subtask and enables failures to be recovered by recomposing existing skills rather than using a dedicated recovery policy. We evaluate five methods across 100 real-robot trials using 20 matched layouts. SurgeCount fills 47 of 60 ordered slots and completes 12 of 20 procedures, compared with 27 of 60 and 3 of 20 for the strongest of four end-to-end policies trained on the same data. Replacing the detailed protocol prompt with a minimal prompt reduces performance to 29 of 60 slots and 5 of 20 completed procedures. These results show that long-horizon performance depends not only on visuomotor capacity, but also on how learned skills are committed, verified, and composed. This tabletop proof of concept motivates further evaluation of protocol-guided robotic sponge counting in clinically representative settings.

papers.title: Déjà VAE: When Do Autoencoder Traces Reveal Generated Images?
papers.abstract: A latent diffusion model's output has already passed through its autoencoder, so a second round trip changes it very little. This "déjà vu" underlies reconstruction-based detectors of generated images; we analyse when it reveals a generated image and when it does not. Read by a frozen vision foundation model without training, the trace is strongest in intermediate layers, and, unlike pixel-level reconstruction error, it treats blur as a sign of a real image. It belongs to the generator's exact decoder: on Synthbuster, the exact decoders of Stable Diffusion 1.3, 1.4, 2 and XL are the strongest of eight autoencoders and catch 94-100% of their generators' images at a 5% false-alarm rate (SDXL's version identified post hoc), while near-identical versions catch 7-42%. A detector trained only on real photographs and their autoencoder copies matches one trained on 162k generated images on GenImage (+2.3 points, 95% CI [0.9, 3.7]) and complements it in fusion, but one resize with JPEG re-save, or a mild blur, costs it 19-27 points. Two lessons concern benchmarks. The in-the-wild benchmark Chameleon can be solved from image width alone. And on Synthbuster, how the real photographs are matched to the generated images' size decides whether our detector leads or trails (+4.4 or -9.7 points): the matching protocol alone can reverse a detector comparison. Code and per-image scores: https://github.com/iamsaugatpandey/deja-vae

papers.title: Lyapunov Stability of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by the Kiselev Anisotropic Fluid
papers.abstract: We investigate the geodesic structure and the stability of circular orbits around a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a Kiselev anisotropic fluid, characterised by the equation-of-state parameter $ω$ and the normalisation parameter $N$. We consider six representative values, $ω=-1,-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3$ and $1$, over the admissible range of $N$ determined by the horizon structure, including the corresponding extremal limits. Using the effective potentials for null and timelike geodesics, we determine the photon sphere, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and the outermost stable circular orbit (OSCO), and examine their stability through coordinate-time Lyapunov exponents. The photon sphere is unstable for all values of $ω$ and $N$ considered. Its instability weakens with increasing $N$ for $ω\leq0$ and vanishes at extremality for $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, whereas it varies non-monotonically with $N$ for $ω=1/3$ and strengthens for $ω=1$. For $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, stable circular orbits are confined between the ISCO and the OSCO, which merge at a critical value of $N$ beyond which no stable circular orbits exist. In contrast, for $ω\geq-1/3$ stable circular orbits exist at all radii beyond the ISCO, whose location varies with $N$. We also derive a closed-form expression for the squared coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent $(λ_t^T)^2$, valid for arbitrary $ω$, whose sign changes exactly at the ISCO and OSCO, so that the Lyapunov criterion reproduces the boundaries of stable circular motion. The Schwarzschild--de Sitter, mass-shifted Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström geometries are recovered as special cases, and the results may have implications for black-hole shadows, thin accretion discs and quasi-periodic oscillations.

papers.title: Online Disk Hitting via Two-Point Traces
papers.abstract: In the online hitting set problem for disks, a set $P$ of $n$ points in the plane is given in advance, and disks intersecting $P$ arrive one at a time. After each arrival, the algorithm must maintain a hitting set $X\subseteq P$ for all disks seen so far. The algorithm can only add points to $X$, and the objective is to minimize the final size of $X$. Even and Smorodinsky gave an $O(\log n)$-competitive algorithm for unit disks and asked whether the $O(\log^2 n)$ bound for disks of arbitrary radii could be improved. For arbitrary radii, our randomized algorithm selects $O(k(1+\log(n/k)))$ points in expectation on every fixed request sequence, where $k$ is the size of a minimum hitting set for that sequence. This gives an $O(\log n)$ expected competitive ratio. For every $k$, we prove a matching lower bound on the worst-case expected cost, even on collinear point sets. The algorithm samples priority orders on $P$ in advance. For each arriving disk $D$, it selects the first point of $D\cap P$ in the current order. The same expected cost bound holds for shortest-path balls in graphs excluding a fixed minor, with a matching lower bound on paths.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Auto-formalization for Trustworthy Scientific Computing: Case Studies and Lessons Learned
papers.abstract: Agentic AI tools have recently had success in mathematical reasoning. Both general purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, and specialized mathematics agents such as Aristotle, have been used for formalizing mathematical problems such as Fermat's last theorem, Erdős problems and several IMO level math problems. However, much of these efforts are concentrated in the pure mathematics domain, which benefits from relatively self-contained theorem statements, fixed mathematical representation and extensive support in existing formal libraries. Applied mathematics, on the other hand, presents additional challenges because the source may describe a computational procedure or modeling transformation rather than a declarative theorem. In this work, we present a systematic study of AI-assisted auto-formalization for scientific computing (SC), a domain in applied mathematics central to U.S. Department of Energy applications. Through case studies spanning hierarchical abstraction layers in SC software stack, we evaluate not only whether AI agents can complete numerical proofs, but also where and why they fail across the stack. Our primary contribution is a cross-layer taxonomy of failure modes and an analysis of the form of expert feedback required at each layer to recover mathematical soundness. From these observations, we derive a workflow for recurring proof patterns and practical guidance for using AI agents while preserving mathematical soundness. Our results characterize both the practical value and the current limitations of AI-assisted formalization for trustworthy scientific computing.

papers.title: Black-Box Comparator-Adaptive Network Regret
papers.abstract: We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. To prove this, we construct a two-node counterexample, which shows that gossip-based algorithms can produce exponential regret despite bounded disagreement, resolving a previously open question in the literature. We then introduce a black-box reduction, which uses local learners with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret to obtain sublinear comparator-adaptive network regret. Each node exchanges predictions with its neighbors once per decision round, and a universal choice of edge weights works on every connected undirected graph without graph preprocessing. We also characterize admissible edge weights and show how weights adapted to the graph improve the regret bound. For example, for the complete graph, this improvement is quadratic in the number of nodes. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data illustrate the counterexamples we propose and compare the reduction with decentralized baselines.

papers.title: Tame homotopy theory and the Goodwillie tower of the identity
papers.abstract: The purpose of this note is to provide a modern treatment of Dwyer's tame homotopy theory and extend it to non-simply connected spaces, exploiting a connection with the work of Heuts on the Goodwillie tower of the identity. As an application, we construct spectral Lie algebraic models for Hess's $r$-mild homotopy theory.

papers.title: Accurate Products, Inaccurate Inverse: Emulated FP64 BLAS in Blocked Triangular Inversion
papers.abstract: FP64 emulation on integer tensor units now ships in cuBLAS and GEMMul8, and each emulated matrix product can be checked against an accuracy grade. We ask if a routine built from such products inherits their accuracy, and show that blocked triangular inversion, the core of LAPACK's inverse of a symmetric positive definite matrix, does not. Under fixed-precision emulation every product passes the grade-B error bound of Demmel et al., yet the inverse errs at 7.1e-2, against 2.0e-15 natively. The matrices are well conditioned after diagonal scaling, but the scaling spans 64 binades. The cause is one product, T = X22 L21, whose summed index carries both the diagonal scaling and its inverse, which a grade-B bound does not absorb. Computing those products natively restores native accuracy; leaving any one of them emulated does not. The pattern holds on four GPUs, and on real covariance matrices the fixed-precision routes lose up to about four orders of accuracy. Equilibration, a solve-based association and cuBLAS's automatic dynamic precision avoid the loss, and an exact error recurrence audits a completed run. On an RTX 4090 the fastest accurate emulated inversion takes 0.40 of cuSOLVER's time. Where each product's scaling falls decides if per-product accuracy carries over to a composite routine, and that is what builders of emulated libraries need to check.

papers.title: LeIFF: A localized-electron and ion force field for coupled nuclear and electronic dynamics
papers.abstract: Classical and machine-learned interatomic potentials enable large-scale simulations by replacing electronic structure with an effective energy surface for nuclear motion. This excludes electronic dynamics, electronic excitation and energy exchange between electrons and ions. First-principles electron dynamics can describe these processes, but its computational cost restricts system sizes and simulation times. Electron force fields offer an intermediate description by treating electrons as semiclassical dynamical particles interacting with ions. We introduce the localized-electron and ion force field (LeIFF), a compact physical model for both ground state bonding and excited electron dynamics. Valence electrons are represented by spin-labeled spherical charge distributions with dynamical centers and widths. The energy combines analytic electronic kinetic, Coulomb, and dispersion terms with spline-interpolated short-range interactions fitted to a large molecular data set. The resulting energy surface describes a variety of ground state properties across diverse bonding environments and charge states. It also provides a qualitative description of electronic behavior away from equilibrium. It shows improved robustness, accuracy, and transferability relative to earlier electron force-fields. Without any solid-state training, the same model describes dielectric screening and collective electronic response in silicon. LeIFF thus opens a route to large-scale simulations of nonadiabatic processes in molecules and solids, combining chemical bonding and nonequilibrium electronic motion within a common physical framework.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic interactions of self-propelled tandem flappers with passive pitching
papers.abstract: We simulate two in-line, self-propelled 3D flappers of finite span, driven by sinusoidal heaving motions with a phase difference $Δϕ$. Pitching is passive, governed by fluid--structure interaction and resisted by a torsional spring. We first consider identical spring stiffnesses, set to the value that maximises the propulsive speed of an isolated flapper. We characterise the self-arrangement of the pair. The pair settles into a stable equilibrium for all phase shifts, travelling at a common propulsive speed and maintaining an equilibrium distance that increases approximately linearly with $Δϕ$. The leader is largely unaffected by the presence of the follower and performs similarly to an isolated flapper, whereas the follower requires more power in every case. This additional power outweighs the small increase in propulsive speed, so that the tandem generally provides no efficiency benefit over an isolated flapper, with comparable efficiency reached only at an intermediate phase shift. For equal stiffness, the power penalty of the follower is associated with a reduction of its pitching amplitude by the wake of the leader, while its pitching phase remains nearly unchanged relative to the isolated flapper. Keeping the leader at the stiffness that maximises its isolated propulsive speed, we investigate whether the tandem performance can be improved by independently tuning the follower through the stiffness ratio $\tildeκ$ in the range $0.8 \le \tildeκ \le 1.2$. Reducing the follower stiffness lowers its power requirement and increases the tandem efficiency by an almost phase-independent amount, without affecting the equilibrium distance or propulsive speed significantly. For the softest follower considered, the tandem is more efficient than an isolated flapper across the full range of phase shifts, with gains of about 2--3\% for $Δϕ\ge 90^\circ$

papers.title: ComputeWise: Measuring and Fixing GPU Waste by AI Research Agents
papers.abstract: AI agents are given GPUs to do AI research on their own. Do they use those GPUs well? A busy GPU does not tell us, because it can be busy with work the answer did not need. This matters, because the tokens the agent spends cost almost nothing next to the GPUs its experiments run on, so using those GPUs better has a huge impact. So we built ComputeWise, an open benchmark of research tasks on which this waste can be measured and reduced. For it we developed our own simulated GPU, which replays recorded runs to the agent's code. With no real GPU needed, we ran hundreds of experiments, far more than would be reasonable on real GPUs. With no help, the agents put only 52% of their GPU time into work the answer needed. Another 22% went to work it did not need, and 26% sat idle. Asking the agent to finish the work faster, telling it to keep every GPU busy, or giving it a job scheduler does not fix this. So we built an open-source harness, part prompting and part deterministic code. Across five models, it removed over 80% of the extra time to the answer.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Soft-Constrained AC-OPF in Multiphase Distribution Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a self-supervised learning framework for fast, soft-constrained AC optimal power flow (OPF) in unbalanced multiphase distribution systems. The soft AC-OPF objective balances operating cost, renewable energy curtailment, and penalties for violating operating limits. A neural network predicts distributed energy resource (DER) setpoints conditioned on operating conditions, switch configurations, and objective weights. The predicted setpoints are then processed through a DER projection and differentiable AC power flow to enforce device limits and network equalities. The framework is trained by directly minimizing the AC-OPF objective, without optimal-solution labels. Experiments on 123-, 240-, and 906-bus systems yield mean objective gaps of 0.32%, 0.92%, and 0.56%, respectively, relative to IPOPT, across wide operating ranges. Across these systems and the evaluated high-load/low-generation and low-load/high-generation scenarios, the largest mean gap is 1.04%, with mean speedups of 58-5272 times relative to IPOPT.

papers.title: Token Pruning Needs a Protected Sink Token: Coherent Spatial Aggregation in Vision Transformers
papers.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are a predominant architecture for computer vision, with token reduction emerging as a popular paradigm to improve their efficiency. Prior work compares reduction algorithms, but not how models respond to them, nor how their response changes with model depth. We propose Monte Carlo Token Pruning (MCTP), which estimates each token's impact on the prediction when tokens are explicitly removed during the forward pass. Applying MCTP to recent pretrained models, we observe that most, such as DINOv3, maintain a similar ranking of token importance at every depth (high Coherent Aggregation), while SigLIP 2 does not. This coherence requires predictions to survive pruning, which depends on keeping high-norm "sink" tokens: prefix tokens are kept by design, while prefix-free SigLIP 2 forms them on patch tokens, which pruning may remove. We show that in removing DINOv3's prefix tokens, its predictions and coherence collapse, while protecting only 5 tokens for SigLIP 2 cuts the token impact outside the object's bounding box by up to 62%. Beyond this, MCTP offers a post-hoc method to evaluate how a pretrained ViT responds to pruning, and suggests that token reduction methods should keep "sinks".

papers.title: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
papers.abstract: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g λ_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8π^2/\sqrt{3} + 8π$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.

papers.title: WildAnySplat: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting in the Wild
papers.abstract: We present WildAnySplat, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that enables robust novel-view synthesis from in-the-wild multi-view images. Unlike controlled captures, real-world images often contain multi-view inconsistencies caused by transient occluders, illumination changes, and camera ISP, which degrade the quality of existing feed-forward reconstruction methods. To address this challenge, we introduce a student-teacher framework that learns transient-robust and appearance-consistent 3D representations. A teacher network operates on clean images, while a student processes the corresponding in-the-wild inputs. The teacher provides clean supervision to guide the student toward a consistent canonical representation. Since paired clean and in-the-wild data are scarce, we use a hybrid data strategy, combining real paired captures, synthetic augmentations, and pseudo-clean labels generated from optimization-based reconstructions, bridging the domain gap between synthetic and real-world data. We adopt a transformer architecture with dedicated DPT heads for camera pose, depth, and Gaussian prediction. We additionally predict per-view transient masks to reweight photometric supervision and suppress unreliable Gaussians. To account for cross-view appearance variation, we incorporate a bilateral grid module that models per-image color transformations and enables recovery of a canonical radiance representation. Experiments on challenging in-the-wild benchmarks show that WildAnySplat improves robustness to transient occlusions and appearance variation while retaining the fast inference of feed-forward Gaussian Splatting.

papers.title: OmniV-Bench: Can MLLMs Comprehend Immersive Spatio-temporal Scenes?
papers.abstract: Omnidirectional videos (ODVs) capture dynamic environments with a full $360^\circ$ field of view, providing rich spatial context and temporal dynamics for applications such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and embodied intelligence. Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made great progress in spatial and temporal understanding, yet their ability to comprehend the immersive 360 spatio-temporal information conveyed by ODVs remains largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we first introduce OmniV-Bench, a Benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate the capabilities of MLLMs on spatio-temporal Omnidirectional Video understanding. OmniV-Bench contains 4,123 high-quality ODVs collected from diverse scenes, along with 8,923 human-annotated question-answer pairs spanning 11 fine-grained tasks across three categories, i.e., general, spatial, and spatio-temporal understanding. Extensive benchmark experiments reveal that the spatio-temporal complexity of ODVs poses significant challenges for current MLLMs. To address these limitations, we further propose OmniV-Harness, an agentic harness that enhances ODV understanding through viewpoint-guided evidence initialization and task-relevant evidence acquisition with adaptive tool use. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that OmniV-Harness consistently improves immersive spatio-temporal reasoning ability of MLLMs. Both OmniV-Bench and OmniV-Harness will be released upon publication.

papers.title: Parsing Visual Latents for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning
papers.abstract: Spatial reasoning across multiple views requires inferring the 3D relations between objects and the camera from 2D observations, which depends on cross-view correspondence and scene geometry that vision-language models (VLMs) do not reliably extract. Pretrained vision encoders already capture this information in their latent features, with CLIP linking objects to image regions, DINOv3 matching semantics across views, and VGGT encoding multi-view geometry. However, VLMs do not benefit from these features when we present them directly in context as grayscale feature images. We therefore propose LatentParse, a training-free framework that parses latent features into explicit spatial evidence for VLMs. In LatentParse, an analyst VLM probes the features of all three encoders with predefined tools that locate objects, track them across views, and measure motion between views. It then distills the results into a concise text report, which is provided together with the images to the VLM to answer the question. We evaluate LatentParse on MMSI-Bench, MV-RoboBench and SPAR-Bench, where it improves all five VLMs over the photo-only baseline by 0.7-2.4 percentage points on average. On MMSI-Bench, it raises Qwen3.8-27B from 34.4% to 39.5%, with the largest improvements of 19.2 percentage points on the camera-related questions. These results suggest that latent features become useful for spatial reasoning once they are parsed into relation evidence, without training. Code is available at https://github.com/Harvard-AI-and-Robotics-Lab/LatentParse.

papers.title: Nontrivial Expanding Kähler--Ricci Solitons and Automorphism Groups of Stein Domains
papers.abstract: We study complete nontrivial expanding Kähler--Ricci solitons with complete real holomorphic soliton fields. Let $Ω$ be a relatively compact domain in a complex surface such that a neighborhood of $\overlineΩ$ admits a holomorphic immersion into Euclidean space. We prove that such a soliton exists if and only if $Ω$ is Stein and the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(Ω)$ is noncompact. On such a Stein domain, a complete real holomorphic vector field is the soliton field of a complete nontrivial expander if and only if its flow has noncompact closure in $\operatorname{Aut}(Ω)$. In higher dimensions, we establish existence criteria using the adjoint representation of automorphism groups, boundary geometry, and homogeneous positive closed $(1,1)$-currents. We give sufficient conditions for the holomorphic $\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$-action on the universal globalization of a proper holomorphic $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$-action on a Stein $n$-manifold to be free and proper. Applications include bounded convex and homogeneous domains, domains satisfying weak Kobayashi visibility, and certain finite-type domains.

papers.title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter space is not rigid
papers.abstract: Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines gluing at separated scales with uniform elliptic estimates. An integral condition removes infinitesimal translations of each Schwarzschild model, while a localized tensor source restores solvability of the linearized equation. Matching the local Schwarzschild corrections to a global Green tensor identifies the leading source coefficients. Reflection makes these coefficients equal, and varying the common radial position of the centers makes them vanish. A radial Green function and the heat equation on the sphere determine the angular variation of the lapse and the geometry of its maximum set.

papers.title: DiffSimp: Differentiable Mesh Simplification for Gradient-Based Low-Poly Modeling
papers.abstract: Differentiable mesh extraction enables gradient-based optimization of detailed 3D geometry across diverse tasks. However, compact meshes are commonly obtained through post-processing simplification, leaving simplification-induced errors outside upstream optimization. We introduce DiffSimp, a training-free, drop-in differentiable mesh simplification layer built on QEM-based parallel edge collapse, enabling existing geometry optimization pipelines to optimize their final simplified meshes. We formulate simplification under a fixed collapse history as a locally differentiable collapse map, enabling gradient propagation without relaxing discrete collapse decisions. We combine fast, high-quality parallel simplification with a factorized backward formulation that exploits differentiable vertex quadrics and quadric reduction forests for efficient gradient propagation. Experiments on low-poly mesh reconstruction and inverse rendering demonstrate improved fidelity over post-processing simplification, with additional gains from gradient propagation that increase under tighter vertex budgets. DiffSimp supports diverse geometry optimization frontends, with 1.00-1.25$\times$ the end-to-end runtime of unsimplified baselines in evaluated pipelines.

papers.title: Quotient maps, pliability, and Lusin approximation in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: In Carnot groups, we show that pliability and the Lusin approximation property are preserved by quotient maps, and we deduce several applications. For instance, we show that, in free Carnot groups of step at least 3 with at least $2$ generators, every horizontal direction is non-pliable, the Lusin property fails in a strong sense, and there is a Lipschitz curve that is purely unrectifiable with respect to smooth horizontal curves. We also give a previously unpublished example of a pliable Carnot group, namely, the group of upper triangular, unipotent matrices.

papers.title: CenShaper: Shaping Proxy Traffic for Censorship Circumvention
papers.abstract: Modern commodity DPI systems are capable of analyzing packet sizes, directions, and timings to detect circumvention tools even when those tools use sophisticated obfuscation. The anti-censorship community has called for innovation in traffic shaping and built an ecosystem that facilitates the adoption of new shaping techniques. However, a fundamental gap is halting progress: \textit{what} should circumvention traffic look like? Past experience with traffic shaping has underscored that effective shaping must produce traffic that looks like legitimate Internet traffic while limiting the ability of censors to identify multiple proxies through shared fingerprints. In this paper, we use our access to large-scale real-world TLS traffic at a regional ISP to analyze approximately 12 million connections, finding that individual servers differ substantially from the broader TLS population and that traffic patterns vary across services. Combining these empirical observations with past experience with traffic shaping, we build CenShaper, which shapes each proxy's traffic to look like a selected TLS server. To reproduce these server-specific patterns, CenShaper trains a shared generative model using traffic from TLS connections to many servers and adapts it for each proxy using a small sample of recorded connections to its selected server. Our model evaluation shows that fingerprints learned from known proxies transfer poorly to proxies imitating previously unseen TLS services. In end-to-end testing, CenShaper reduces the detection rate of TLS-over-TLS fingerprinting from over 85\% to approximately 3\% at a 1\% false positive rate. Finally, we show how running CenShaper as a sidecar process simplifies integration with existing circumvention tools, making it a practical defense against increasingly powerful traffic analysis attacks.

papers.title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
papers.abstract: LLMs typically solve complex tasks with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, which is also the main tool for monitoring them for misaligned behavior. However, standard transformers can also solve tasks with complete latent reasoning (CLR), carrying out the whole task internally and outputting only the final answer. Theory bounds the depth of CLR, the number of sequential steps it can carry out, and recent work measured it to be shallow. In this work, we ask whether CLR is deep enough for a model to pursue a hidden objective that requires reasoning. Such a model would generate a CoT that appears to solve the given task, while a latent multi-step computation decides its answer based on the hidden objective. First, we show that a simple auxiliary loss allows models to solve a multi-step task latently at least 5x deeper than previously reported. Then, in two common tasks, decision-making and code generation, we train a model to pursue such a hidden objective, which decides a loan or plants a vulnerability. The model's CoT justifies the output with no trace of the hidden objective, and a strong LLM monitor does not flag it. Finally, using activation patching, we find that the latent computation is completed before the model generates its CoT, which takes no part in it. Altogether, we show that a hidden objective that requires reasoning can go unseen by a monitor that reads only the output.

papers.title: Demographic Encoding is Not Exposure: Fairness and Privacy in Chest X-ray Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Medical foundation models encode patient demographics and can reveal whether a patient was in the training set, and these properties are often treated as one problem. We tested whether they are aligned by measuring demographic encoding, diagnostic fairness gaps and membership-inference vulnerability on the same models. We trained 200 linear or multilayer-perceptron (MLP) heads on frozen BiomedCLIP, DINOv2 and RAD-DINO embeddings, with three seeds, and audited them on CheXpert and NIH ChestX-ray14. Demographic encoding explained almost no variance in patient vulnerability, and all 72 CheXpert associations were statistically equivalent to zero. Erasing linearly decodable demographics left leakage unchanged but reduced age-related underdiagnosis gaps. Leakage depended instead on head capacity and training length. On RAD-DINO, a linear head reached a membership-inference area under the curve (AUC) of 0.694, compared with 0.907 for a 30-epoch MLP, at similar test performance. Fairness and privacy should therefore be audited separately, and linear heads or shorter training reduce leakage with little or no loss of utility. The code is available on GitHub for public use.

papers.title: (n-1)-Dimensional Hausdorff Measure Estimates for Free Boundaries of Infinity Laplace Equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the geometric properties of free boundaries associated with nonnegative viscosity solutions to the infinity Laplace equation with strong absorption $$ Δ_\infty u=λu_+^m, \qquad λ>0,\quad 0<m<3. $$ We first establish a sharp distance-to-free-boundary regularity estimate with an explicit optimal coefficient, which coincides with the constant in the non-degeneracy estimate. This exact matching yields a uniform interior tangent ball property at every sufficiently small scale for every free boundary point. As consequences, we obtain a sharp lower density bound of $1/2$ for the positive phase, a locally finite covering of the free boundary by Lipschitz graphs, and quantitative local estimates for its $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the question raised by Araújo, Leitão, and Teixeira (J. Funct. Anal. {\textbf 270} (2016), no. 6, 2249-2267). The underlying barrier mechanism also suggests possible extensions to more general equations.

papers.title: Triage Accuracy of Jev and Open-Weight System One Decision Models and Their Use for Early Emergency Recognition in Symptom-Assessment Applications
papers.abstract: Laypeople increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for triage advice, but LLMs answer in variable free text, which makes it hard to evaluate them for use in medical devices. Decision models, which assign a probability to each predefined triage category, may be easier to evaluate. To test their triage accuracy, we evaluated 16 decision models (14 open-weight, 2 proprietary) on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, yielding 163,728 total assessments. The best models triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly and agreed with an existing algorithm in 56.1% of real-world cases. They were more promising for recognising emergencies early: given only demographics, chief complaints, risk factors and red-flag answers, the best model reached an AUROC of 0.87. At a 5% error margin, it could decide for or against emergencies for about half of users. Decision models should therefore not replace triage engines but could shorten symptom assessments at setting-specific error margins.

papers.title: Airlock: Robust Sandboxing and Governance of Rogue Agents
papers.abstract: Recent incidents involving agents bypassing sandboxing and network isolation have raised concerns about existing agent harnesses, prompting frontier labs such as OpenAI to reevaluate the security of their training platforms. Incident reviews show that determined agents can escape processes, containers, and VMs, or bypass their isolation through advanced side and covert channels. Follow-up audits also found that some agents concealed their actions by disabling monitoring and tampering with logs. We propose Airlock, an architecture that pairs each agent's VM with an Airlock VM, each running in a separate hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). The Airlock VM fully mediates the agent's interactions with the outside world, including network and storage operations. We modify the firmware layer of Arm's Confidential Computing Architecture, Realm Management Monitor (RMM), and the kernels of both VMs so that the Airlock VM serves the agent VM's IO without involving the host. We adapt OpenShell, an agent runtime supporting sandboxing and governance policies, to this architecture. Airlock keeps network and filesystem policies, and credential protection effective even if the agent VM is fully compromised, and it removes the host from the agent's IO path, reducing opportunities for collusion and covert channels with the host. Finally, we extend the Airlock VM's capabilities to provide tamper-proof auditing of all agent operations, preserving forensic evidence even if the Airlock VM is compromised. We implement and evaluate Airlock on a Radxa development board. Our evaluation shows a loss of filesystem performance and network latency for small messages under 15% and a drop of network bandwidth by half or more, which in practice has a limited effect on typical agent tasks.

papers.title: Origins of City Reputation: Measuring Trust and Bias in Online Reviews Using Agentic AI and NLP
papers.abstract: Online reviews aggregate millions of individual judgments into signals that shape where people eat, stay and travel to, and increasingly read them as evidence of the reputation of places. Nevertheless, whether such reputations really reflect the places or more the instruments used to measure them is unclear. Here we compare two instruments for measuring trust and bias in 100,000 Yelp reviews from ten US cities: a large language model based agentic system including an evaluator critic loop, and a corpus-based tool built on pretrained classifiers, lexicons and rule-based features. Our results show that the two instruments agree on credibility, but not at all on plausibility. They also respond to different use of words and phrases. The corpus-based better flagged complaints and generalizations, whereas the agent better quoted references to social groups. We also found that with five examples, the agent treats ordinary superlatives as bias far more often than with none or one.
