We then scale SPARSEUP with large-scale contrastive pre-training, distillation, and Matryoshka-style training. The resulting SPARSEUP-v2 reaches 57.2 average nDCG@10 on BEIR-15, matching LateOn, the best public retriever under 150M parameters we know of, while being an order of magnitude more efficient.

papers.title: Quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximation for exponential random graphs in the single-phase critical regime
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximations for edge-count fluctuations in dense exponential random graphs at single-phase criticality of any fixed even order $2m_*\ge 4$. The Hamiltonians use injective homomorphism counts of fixed simple graphs, with nonnegative leading coefficients for the higher-order terms. In bounded calibrated windows, edge-density fluctuations on the scale $n^{-1/m_*}$ admit an explicit non-Gaussian approximation with error $O(n^{-1/m_*})$. For parameter perturbations by fixed multiples of $n^{-1}$ with a nonzero first-order drift correction at the critical density, the deterministically centered edge count admits a Gaussian approximation on the scale $n^{(3m_*-2)/(2m_*-1)}$, with error $O(n^{-1/(2m_*-1)})$. Both rates hold in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. The key step is to construct auxiliary kernels for exterior graphs outside an event of exponentially small probability. These kernels contract uniformly on the full row state space and agree with the conditional Gibbs updates on typical row configurations, yielding the conditional cumulant estimates used in Stein's method.

papers.title: Robust Reconstruction of Power Lines from Incomplete Mobile and Aerial LiDAR Data
papers.abstract: Accurate vegetation-encroachment assessment and risk mitigation require electric utilities to accurately locate and characterize distribution-network assets, including poles and power lines, and distinguish among medium-voltage, low-voltage, neutral, and telecommunication lines. Mobile and aerial Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) point clouds provide detailed 3D representations of these assets and their surroundings. However, power-line detection and reconstruction remain challenging because conductor returns are often sparse, incomplete, noisy, or occluded by vegetation. These challenges are especially significant in distribution networks, where lower pole heights and complex line configurations place conductors close to trees. In addition, mobile and aerial LiDAR datasets differ substantially in point density, viewing geometry, spatial coverage, and occlusion patterns. We propose a robust and automated reconstruction method combining scaled density-based clustering, robust polynomial fitting, and iterative fragment merging to recover individual conductors under severe data incompleteness and occlusion. Following semantic classification, the same reconstruction pipeline processes both mobile and aerial LiDAR data without modality-specific code or parameter tuning. The method is evaluated through degradation experiments, benchmarking, parameter sensitivity analysis, and large-scale validation. On the aerial dataset, it achieves 96.87% precision, 96.66% recall, a 96.76% F$_1$-score, and a geometric RMSE of 0.127 m. On the mobile dataset, where conductor-level reference annotations were unavailable, it achieves a point-to-model RMSE of 0.045 m and a reconstruction coverage of 95.27%. Source code, documentation, and evaluation data are publicly available at https://github.com/varen-project.

papers.title: Improving Entrepreneurial Skills by Practicing with AI
papers.abstract: Durable skills like critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration are essential for innovation, yet teaching them remains difficult. In this work, we focus on the entrepreneurial domain, where these skills and others are required, and ask whether AI can be used as a tool for improving entrepreneurial proficiency. As a first step towards this challenge, we present an extension of Vantage, a platform developed at Google Research, adapted to serve as an interactive practice environment for entrepreneurship. Vantage pairs students with simulated AI peers engineered to navigate realistic business scenarios and challenge learners to exercise key skills. In a randomized controlled trial (RCT) embedded in summer entrepreneurship programs run by The Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship (NFTE), students using Vantage scored significantly higher on their Capstone Business Plans than control students with access to standard AI tools. These preliminary findings suggest that orchestrated AI peers can meaningfully support short-term performance on tasks requiring complex, durable skills.

papers.title: An Egorov-type Theorem for Analytic Wick Observables in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: We provide an exact Egorov-type formula, given by a convergent expansion in the semi-classical parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, for the propagation of a certain class of analytic Wick observables with super-exponentially decaying coefficients, under the action of a time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian. This work generalizes a result established by S. Breteaux for polynomial symbols, and includes the spatially cutoff $P(φ)_2$ model, as well as a variant of the Höegh-Krohn model.

papers.title: LatentWeave: Test-Time Latent Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Recent advances in test-time optimization have shown that the multimodal reasoning performance of large multimodal language models (MLLMs) can be improved during inference without modifying backbone model parameters. However, existing approaches primarily operate at the prompt or output level, leaving the latent reasoning process largely uncontrolled and insufficient to prevent error accumulation during autoregressive generation. To address this limitation, we propose LatentWeave, a test-time framework that treats multimodal reasoning as a controllable latent trajectory. LatentWeave performs structured Latent Weaving, progressively refining intermediate hidden states segment-wise to correct emerging deviations, and further introduces Reasoning Anchors via lightweight WEAVE tokens to stabilize reasoning structure and guide answer-oriented generation. These mechanisms are designed to enable fine-grained, step-aware intervention in the latent reasoning process while keeping the main MLLM backbone parameters fixed. Extensive experiments across diverse multimodal reasoning benchmarks report improvements over the evaluated baselines; the contribution of latent optimization, anchor training, and additional test-time computation is analyzed separately in the ablation and efficiency studies.

papers.title: ALADDIN: Adversarial Latent Diffusion Distillation for One-Step Identity Swapping
papers.abstract: Face swapping transfers a source identity onto a target image while preserving the target's pose, expression, hair, and lighting. The most realistic current methods are diffusion-based, but they need many network evaluations per image. GAN-based methods are fast, yet trained from scratch they must learn realism from the adversarial signal alone and produce visibly weaker results. We present ALADDIN (Adversarial Latent Diffusion Distillation for One-Step Identity Swapping), a one-step face swapper obtained by initialising the generator from a pre-trained multi-step flow-matching model and training it adversarially under identity and target-preservation constraints. We expose a controllable trade-off between identity transfer and target-attribute preservation by training a student model with triplet pseudo-label supervision. We additionally identify a bias in the standard evaluation protocol, which favours methods trained against the same identity encoder used to score them, and re-evaluate all baselines with an independent one. ALADDIN is state-of-the-art among one-step methods in realism and target preservation at comparable identity transfer, and matches the best multi-step model with 28 times fewer network evaluations and an order of magnitude fewer training samples.

papers.title: Native Rectangular Linear Assignment with Implicit Rejection: A Jonker-Volgenant Solver without Square Expansion
papers.abstract: Rectangular assignment with a uniform unmatched penalty is often implemented by expanding the cost matrix. We integrate established rectangular Jonker-Volgenant principles and implicit rejection with float64 working arithmetic and reusable workspaces in Rust (JVRUST), hybrid Rust/C++ (JVHYBRID) and C++ (JVCPP). A campaign evaluates laprust/lapcpp 1.2.0 and LAPX 0.13.0 in four Windows/Linux and Python environments. Each environment contains 302 cases: 3,286 complete-call timing conditions with five inputs and three rounds, plus 91 memory conditions with five fresh-process trials. Against the matching compact SciPy reference, all three native implementations exceed a 3% advantage on all 102 required cases; JVRUST and JVCPP do so on 163-165 and 163-166 of 166 optional cases, respectively. Controlled comparisons qualify these gains by representation, initialization, sparsity, batching and orientation. We also assess how solver gains carry over to pedestrian and cell tracking using real-world data and prepared detections. In each Windows environment, the specialized LSAPE code wins 38 of 67 cases against the original Hungarian implementation and all 67 against its unchanged one-sided baseline. The contribution is software integration and reproducible performance characterization. Adverse results are retained; no algorithmic priority, statistical significance or universal solver ranking is claimed. The initialization policy was developed using related workload families, so the campaign is not a held-out test of heuristic optimality.

papers.title: Validating the Comparison, Not Just the Scorer: Why Overall Accuracy Can Mislead in Interactive LLM Evaluation
papers.abstract: Many LLM studies compare how a model responds to different follow-up prompts. A neutral prompt might ask the model to reconsider an answer; a pressure prompt might insist that an invented film really exists. The difference between the two conditions is the quantity the study reports. An automatic scorer then labels each response as making an unsupported factual claim or not, and researchers usually justify the scorer with a single pooled accuracy or $F_1$ score. That pooled number does not validate the comparison. When the scorer's errors differ across prompt conditions, the measured difference can be too large, too small, or point in the wrong direction, even if pooled $F_1$ is high. An audit drawn mostly from difficult responses can also misrepresent performance in the full study. We derive the distortion as the difference in signed error between conditions and study it in a released panel of six models, 180 constructed nonexistent-entity questions, and six prompt conditions. In a balanced audit of 288 responses, pooled $F_1$ was 0.916, yet arm-level false-positive rates ranged from 2.6% to 33.3%. On 300 matched model--item keys, automatic scoring overstated the Certainty-only--Neutral contrast by 7.0 points relative to the primary LLM rater (95% CI 1.3 to 12.8); that contrast fell from an apparent 9.3 points to 2.3 points, and the primary-rater interval included zero. Two other contrasts kept their direction under both raters; a prompt-specific correction remained too uncertain to use. Researchers should validate the exact difference they plan to report: audit both prompts on matched cases and carry scorer and rater uncertainty into the result.

papers.title: HistoLoop: Coarse-to-Fine Spatial Context Integration with a Looped Transformer for Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction
papers.abstract: Inferring spatial gene expression from routine H&E slides requires interpreting local morphology within a tissue organization that spans multiple spatial scales. Existing multi-scale methods, however, compute regional summaries at each scale only once and then combine them across scales, rather than forming finer-scale summaries from representations that have already absorbed coarser-scale context. We propose HistoLoop, a looped Transformer that integrates spatial context progressively from coarse to fine. HistoLoop applies a shared set of modules across recurrent steps at increasingly fine resolutions, and constructs the context at each step from spot states that have already absorbed coarser-scale context. On HEST-1k, a single model trained jointly on six cancer types achieves a macro-averaged HVG50 Pearson correlation of 0.480, compared with 0.435 for the strongest baseline. Ablations show that the multi-resolution loop, the coarse-to-fine schedule, and the dependence of each step on updated spot states each contribute to this performance, and clustering analysis indicates that HistoLoop better preserves the multigene structure of tissue domains. On cancer types held out from training, HistoLoop attains the highest average correlation, although transfer to unseen cancer types remains challenging for all methods.

papers.title: CodecMotion-OAD: Efficient Online Action Detection with Compressed-Domain Motion
papers.abstract: Online action detection (OAD) recognizes ongoing actions in streaming video, often relying on RGB appearance and optical flow. Codec motion vectors (MVs) provide motion information at low computational cost, but directly replacing Flow with MVs can reduce detection accuracy. Our analysis shows that Flow and MVs capture similar dominant motion patterns; fine-grained motion details contribute less after RGB fusion, but motion still provides complementary cues that RGB alone cannot fully capture, helping maintain detection accuracy. The remaining gap between RGB+Flow and RGB+MV narrows substantially for conditional category identity but persists for action presence, where motion-only predictions provide complementary evidence. We propose CodecMotion-OAD to replace Flow with MVs in existing two-stream detectors. To our knowledge, this is the first use of codec MVs as a Flow substitute in frame-level causal OAD. Its unlabeled motion representation adaptation initializes an MV encoder with Flow-pretrained weights and adapts it through feature alignment. It also employs presence-identity routing to improve action presence estimation using complementary motion-only evidence while preserving the joint detector's conditional category distribution. On IPPP-re-encoded THUMOS'14, CodecMotion-OAD with MiniROAD achieves 69.60 mAP versus 70.39 for RGB+Flow, with 1.99-fold GPU and 11.13-fold CPU decoder-to-prediction speedups.

papers.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows
papers.abstract: LLM agentic workflows increasingly employ different models for specialized roles. Users may prefer different trade-offs between task quality and deployment cost, sometimes also considering latency. Finding good assignments incurs a separate search cost from evaluating multiple candidates. We introduce Cost-Coupled Gittins (CC-Gittins), a multi-objective extension of single-objective cost-aware Gittins search for Pareto recommendation. It exploits the coupling between evaluation and deployment costs: assignments that cost more to deploy also cost more to evaluate. The search alternates between seeking higher quality and lower deployment cost, reusing each evaluation to inform both searches. After each batch, CC-Gittins recommends assignments that are nondominated under uncertainty-adjusted estimates of quality and deployment cost. We evaluate CC-Gittins on eight quality--cost matrices from workflows with two to five roles and up to 1,681 candidate assignments. We also evaluate the method with latency as a third objective. Across the eight benchmarks, CC-Gittins recovers a substantial fraction of the true Pareto frontier at roughly 10% of the exhaustive-evaluation cost, and recovers most of the frontier with few false positives by 30%.

papers.title: QIEN: Quantum-Inspired Energy-Neutral UAV Trajectory for WPT-Enabled Industrial HRLLC
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Quantum-Inspired Energy-Neutral (QIEN) UAV Trajectory for WPT-Enabled Industrial HRLLC, a novel framework for mobility-integrated trajectory and resource optimization in solar-powered uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) relay systems supporting autonomous mining robots in post-disaster environments. We formulate a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) that jointly optimizes UAV trajectory, finite blocklength allocation, transmit power, and wireless power transfer (WPT) over discrete time horizons to maximize aggregate data throughput. The system operates under strict extreme hyper-reliable low-latency communication (HRLLC) constraints, energy sustainability requirements via solar harvesting, and continuous robot power delivery. To solve this large-scale optimization problem, QIEN employs a hybrid Cooperative Quantum-behaved Particle Swarm Optimization (Co-QPSO) algorithm using quantum tunneling mechanisms and a heterogeneous swarm architecture. Our simulation results demonstrate that the proposed QIEN framework significantly outperforms benchmark algorithms, achieving successful convergence while maintaining energy-neutral operation and satisfying all reliability, power, and mobility constraints.

papers.title: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
papers.abstract: For all integers $1 \le k < d$ and every $α\in (0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous iterated function system of similarities in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space satisfying the open set condition. The same system is used at every scale. Its attractor $F_{k,α}$ has positive and finite $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Write $A_δ$ for the closed $δ$-neighbourhood of a set $A$. For all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, every orthogonal projection of $(F_{k,α})_δ$ onto a $k$-plane has $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure at most $C_{k,α}(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$. The construction places the product of a planar self-similar set $E_α$ and the unit $(k-1)$-cube in a coordinate $(k+1)$-plane. For every $0 < δ< 1$, the supremum of these projected measures is comparable, up to constants depending only on $k$, to the supremum of the lengths of the orthogonal projections of $(E_α)_δ$ onto lines. We bound this latter supremum by $C_α(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$. We also prove that the analytic capacity $γ((E_α)_δ)$ is comparable to $(\log(1/δ))^{-1/2}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, with constants depending only on $α$. Consequently, the Favard length of $(E_α)_δ$ is at most $C_αγ((E_α)_δ)^{2α}$ for every $0 < δ< 1$. This quantitative Vitushkin inequality is superlinear for $α> 1/2$, and its exponent $2α$ approaches the optimal upper limit of two for this class of self-similar sets as $α$ tends to one.

papers.title: Quantum-classical algorithm interpolation for spatial search
papers.abstract: Quantum-walk algorithms can quadratically reduce the dependence of spatial search on the classical hitting time $\mathrm{HT}$. Realising this speedup using standard quantum-walk algorithms, however, requires deep coherent circuits, limiting their applicability on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum devices. We derive a parameterised family of hybrid quantum-classical spatial search algorithms that continuously interpolates between the classical and fully coherent quantum regimes, trading off circuit depth for total query complexity. For any $γ\in[0,1]$, our algorithms use circuits of depth $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{γ/2})$ and find a marked vertex with constant success probability at total cost $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{1-γ}\mathsf{S} + \mathrm{HT}^{1-γ/2}(\mathsf{U} + \mathsf{C}))$, where $\mathsf{S}$, $\mathsf{U}$, and $\mathsf{C}$ denote the setup, update, and checking costs, respectively. We also derive an optimal continuous depth-query trade-off for fixed-point amplitude amplification, providing a potential building block for other hybrid designs.

papers.title: Flux Compensation as a Prerequisite for Temporal CT: Per-Bundle Cramér-Rao Floors and Estimators That Reach Them
papers.abstract: In Temporal CT (TCT) each detector reading sums the photons of up to three rays. Earlier work measured the resulting per-bundle cost as a Dose Inflation Factor (DIF), using one incident count $N_0$ for all rays and a learned prior trained on one patient; this paper removes both restrictions. N$_0$FC ($N_0$ flux compensation), a bow-tie and tube-current-modulation co-design, approximately equalizes each bundle's detected flux. SNN2 is a bias-corrected, box-projected Gauss-Newton Poisson likelihood iteration. V8c, a neural network trained on 19 patients, corrects SNN2. T2bp, an empirical-Bayes post-processor without trained weights, combines per-bundle Poisson likelihoods with a prior from the patient's own bundles. On 23 non-test volumes, N$_0$FC lowers the per-volume median middle-path Cramér-Rao floor, as a DIF, from 23-48 under a flat-fluence baseline to 3.3-6.3 at 35-62% of the baseline's incident photons, near the equal-attenuation 13/3 and 1.4-1.7 times below GE-type bow-ties. For bundles with $X_2<6$ (83%), SNN2 attains this floor (median MSE ratio 1.02); holding air paths at zero, a box-constrained maximum likelihood estimate lowers the ratio to 0.88, and T2bp$\circ$SNN2 to 0.89 (0.74-1.26); T2bp's per-patient prior adds measurably only in the deeper bins (a median 12-29% over all bins). T2bp$\circ$SNN2 beats T2bp$\circ$V8c on three of four N$_0$FC test cells, but trails or ties it on the four N$_0$FC validation volumes. V8c beats SNN2 in distribution under baseline acquisition, gains at most 9% under N$_0$FC (losing 14% on the largest in-distribution test patient), and fails on a patient acquired outside its corpus's exposure rule. Flux compensation, chiefly the bow-tie, is a prerequisite; classical estimation attains the resulting limit. The remaining 3- to 6-fold gap to single-source CT at equal fluence, and the high-attenuation tail, are targets for inter-bundle priors.

papers.title: Good human thinking populates AI's semantic blind spots
papers.abstract: AI-generated outputs tend to be more similar (homogenized) than human ideas. Does the human heterogeneity that extends beyond AI homogenization reflect valuable thinking that AI misses, or bad human ideas that AI avoids? We quantified how much an individual response expands an idea space beyond recurring clusters of ideas, enabling us to identify human responses located in AI's "semantic blind spots" (regions AI sparsely covers). Across three large samples (college admissions essays, alternative uses of objects, and interpersonal problem solving), human ideas in AI blind spots predicted higher academic achievement and performed as well or better on creativity, quality, and effectiveness. In contrast to humans, when AI expanded idea space, the association with creativity weakened or reversed. AI blind spots persisted across 66 diverse models and were not resolved by human-AI collaboration. Thinking "outside the bots" does not appear to reflect low-performing human variation that AI can safely omit.

papers.title: Gluing Local Contexts into Global Meaning: A Sheaf-Theoretic Decomposition of Transformer Representations
papers.abstract: Prior research into interpretability does not test whether a representation stays consistent under paraphrasing. Each pair of paraphrases can be thought of as a local witness that two activations should be the same. From these local witnesses we can build a cellular sheaf on the paraphrase graph. The question of what is consistent under paraphrasing can be answered by the Laplacian $L_\mathcal{F}$ given a frozen model. No training required. Our kernel $H^0$ gives us a content subspace. We show that with only 20 dims the kernel outperforms the subspace that LEACE retains with all dims on held-out CounterFact fact retrieval by $+17.1$\,pp on average across 8 models. By constraining all paraphrases of a fact together we see an additional increase of $+6.5$\,pp. Our spectral complement shows us where the causal influence is concentrated. Ablating the coordinates that vary the most when paraphrased (which approximates ablating the spectral complement at the coordinate level) leads to $5.6$ to $26.5\times$ larger changes in model outputs compared to ablating coordinates with matched per-coordinate variability. We find this across 9 models from 124M to 13B params. By stacking layers we can create a grid which has $b_1 = N(L-1)$ algebraic 1-cycles. The harmonic mass derived from the model varies by nearly 3 orders of magnitude between the 6 architectures. It also tracks the order of steering fragility (Spearman's $ρ= 0.90$, exact one-sided permutation $p = 0.014$). The kernel, its spectral complement and the harmonic mass all come from the same paraphrase graph. Project page: https://cwru-aism.github.io/gluing-lc-page/.

papers.title: Massive de Sitter Correlators as Finite Mellin-Barnes Integrals
papers.abstract: Using the Mellin-Barnes representation of de Sitter propagators, we reduce tree-level heavy-particle exchange to finite integrals that converge at physical kinematics on mass-independent contours, and one-loop diagrams to the same integrand times a flat-space momentum factor. We compute the complete one-loop triangle at general masses, with its collider signal in closed form to all orders in the squeezed-limit expansion, and give the triple-exchange bispectrum at arbitrary heavy masses as a double series that converges at every physical shape. The loop reduction also applies at strong mixing.

papers.title: Nowhere Locally Metric-Minimising Saddle Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the relation between the saddle property and local metric minimality for smooth surfaces in Euclidean spaces. Anton Petrunin and Stephan Stadler proved that every smooth strictly saddle surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is locally metric-minimising and expressed the expectation that this phenomenon fails in $\mathbb{R}^4$. We confirm this expectation and prove a stronger density result: Every smooth strictly saddle embedding of a closed disc into $\mathbb{R}^4$ can be approximated arbitrarily closely in the $C^\infty$-topology by smooth strictly saddle embeddings that are nowhere locally metric-minimising. In particular, nowhere locally metric-minimising saddle embeddings exist in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for every $d \geq 4$. The main ingredient is the construction of non-trivial infinitesimal isometric deformations of saddle immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$ supported in arbitrarily small discs. We also provide an explicit twisted quadratic surface that is saddle in a neighbourhood of the origin but fails to be locally metric-minimising there, by deriving a necessary condition for metric minimality.

papers.title: Argos: Adapt Rich Geometric Priors for Generalizable Online Scene-Change-Detection
papers.abstract: Robots operating in dynamic environments require reliable detection of how their surroundings change over time. Existing learning-based methods largely rely on pairwise 2D image features, which struggle under large viewpoint changes and occlusions, are sensitive to noise, and show limited generalization across domains, while explicit 3D approaches typically require costly offline optimization. We show that the implicit 3D knowledge of Geometric Foundation Models (GFMs) provides a strong basis for addressing these limitations. We introduce Argos, which adapts GFM features for joint scene change detection and 3D reconstruction. To address data scarcity and take a step toward a foundation model for scene change detection, we introduce a large-scale benchmark comprising two synthetic datasets and one real-world dataset, and train jointly across diverse datasets to improve cross-domain generalization. We further introduce Argos-SLAM, a real-time system designed for robotics, which performs online change detection and change-aware 4D mapping. Across benchmarks, our framework substantially outperforms existing baselines, with gains of up to 42.01% in change IoU and 27.91% in F1, while supporting scalable deployment in changing real-world environments.

papers.title: Fully Interpretable Minimal Transformers: From Geometry to Algorithm
papers.abstract: We present a framework for building and interpreting minimal transformer models. By constraining a transformer's embedding dimension and head size to 2, we enable full two-dimensional visualization of its internal representations. Embeddings, query/key/value transforms, attention outputs, residual streams, and decision boundaries can all be seen directly. Our central claim is that the learned geometry implies an algorithm. The arrangement of points and boundaries in R^2 can be read as a step-by-step procedure. We train a transformer on a simple task where it must produce the most recently observed even number whenever the '+' operator appears in a sequence of digits. Once trained, we visually walk through every step of the transformer's computation. We show how the model embeds the tokens and their respective positions in the sequence, transforms them via the Q, K, and V matrices, uses the dot product between the Q and K representations to form the attention matrix, and uses the attention matrix to select values that move the representation of each input token embedding to the region of the domain of the output layer that will correctly predict the next token. We introduce a suite of interpretability visualizations that make the algorithmic interpretation of this procedure explicit. Our framework offers a pedagogical and experimental testbed to explore how transformers use information geometry to implement next-token prediction.

papers.title: Goal-Oriented Wave Computing for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation
papers.abstract: Programmable metasurfaces are arrays of elements whose electromagnetic response can be tuned electronically. They can process signals as a wave propagates through or reflects off them, an approach known as wave-domain analog computing, or wave computing. The design strategy is typically indirect: the surface is fitted to a prescribed linear operator, such as a discrete Fourier transform (DFT), and the result is read from output power measurements. Using direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation as a canonical benchmark, we study what this indirection costs across three analog computing topologies: reflective reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), beyond-diagonal RIS (BD-RIS), and stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM). We first derive Cramér-Rao bounds for the complete physical estimation chain, including one that accounts for output detectors measuring only intensity. We then formulate a goal-oriented alternative where the surfaces are trained directly through the deployed readout, with no operator target. We observe that goal-oriented training lets sparsely connected or shallower surfaces reach the task performance of their more complex operator-fitted counterparts, despite nearly identical Fisher information. For fully connected BD-RIS and six-layer SIM, the advantage persists under one- and two-bit control. From 16 to 64 elements, the connectivity a beyond-diagonal RIS needs grows with the aperture, and the depth saving of a stacked intelligent metasurface shrinks. Under tuner and per-layer loss, the goal-oriented designs mostly keep their advantage over DFT fits of the same hardware.

papers.title: Beyond ideal cavities: quantifying the impact of cavity dissipation on light-matter strong coupling
papers.abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical cavities promises to reshape molecular reactivity and properties in a non-invasive and tunable way, yet cavity experiments remain notoriously difficult to interpret and reproduce, highlighting the need for accurate theoretical predictions. Significant progress has been made through ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) methods, but these generally assume ideal, lossless cavity fields, an approximation commonly justified by the assumption that cavity losses are negligible and by the need to keep the methods computationally tractable. Here we show that this approximation is far from innocent: incorporating cavity dissipation through the experimentally accessible quality factor Q reduces the Rabi splitting of p-nitroaniline by more than 10% and red-shifts the minimum polaritonic gap by 0.24 eV, even when the system remains firmly in the strong-coupling regime. This implies that convergence towards the ideal-cavity limit requires quality factors substantially larger than those needed to establish strong coupling itself. Our approach, based on a damped harmonic oscillator description of the cavity field and a time-dependent unitary transformation yielding a real Hermitian Hamiltonian, is demonstrated here within the quantum electrodynamics coupled-cluster singles and doubles framework (QED-CCSD). Its general formulation allows straightforward integration into existing ab initio QED frameworks without increasing the computational cost of the underlying methods, providing a practical and efficient route to quantitatively account for realistic cavity conditions in first-principles simulations of molecular systems in cavities.

papers.title: Algebraic Dimension and Reduction of LVMB manifolds
papers.abstract: LVMB manifolds are a large class of compact complex manifolds constructed from an initial combinatorial datum. Most of them are non-algebraic manifolds nor do they support Kähler metrics. All LVMB manifolds are equipped with a canonical holomorphic foliation, whose leaf space is a complex toric quasifold; these spaces constitute the nonrational counterpart of compact toric orbifolds. For an LVMB manifold with no nonzero holomorphic 1-forms, we show that every meromorphic function is a rational function of the Laurent monomials arising from the rational linear relations among the points in the initial datum. It follows that Meersseman's lower bound for the algebraic dimension is attained and that the algebraic reduction is rational. In particular, both conclusions hold for every LVMB manifold with at most two indispensable indices. Under the same vanishing hypothesis, we relate the algebraic dimension of an LVMB manifold to the nonrationality degree of its canonical quasifold leaf space. We give an explicit formula for this invariant recently introduced by Battaglia and Prato.

papers.title: ARCH-B: Architectural Representation, Comprehension and Hierarchy Benchmark
papers.abstract: Multimodal models increasingly interpret visual environments, but their ability to recognize the same building across photographs, floor plans, elevations, sections, and renderings remains poorly characterized. We introduce ARCH-B, a benchmark of 354 four-choice questions across 11 cross-representational archetypes, constructed from a building-linked corpus of 3.9 million architectural images using visually similar distractors, model-guided difficulty screening, and manual validation. We evaluate 25 multimodal models and collect 5,830 responses from non-expert human participants. Model accuracy ranges from 10.45% to 83.90%, compared with a human baseline of 35.35%. Models perform comparatively well on mixed-representation outlier detection and photograph matching, but remain weaker on floorplan-to-photograph correspondence. Human and model difficulty across archetypes is only weakly correlated (Spearman's (ρ=0.33)). Held-out evaluation confirms that the difficulty identified during screening generalizes beyond the curation models. ARCH-B provides a diagnostic evaluation of visual correspondence and representation transfer across architectural media.
authors: Jose Luis Garcia del Castillo y Lopez

papers.title: Maximal first Betti number drop and collapsing RCD spaces
papers.abstract: Let $(X_i,d_i,\mathfrak m_i)$ be compact $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces converging to a space $X$ of rectifiable dimension $m$. Their first Betti numbers can drop by at most $N-m$. When equality holds, the maximal abelian covers have a non-collapsed limit $Y$ carrying a free isometric $\mathbb{R}^{N-m}$-action. We turn this limiting symmetry into fibrations of the approximating spaces. More precisely, after passing to a subsequence, there is an open full-measure set $G\subset X$, containing every regular point, on which $X$ is a topological orbifold and the $X_i$ admit local Seifert fibrations with $(N-m)$-torus fibres. Each finite local group acts on the fibre by translations. If the $X_i$ have no boundary, then $X\setminus G$ has Hausdorff codimension at least two. If $Y$ has no bubbling and $X$ is a smooth closed Riemannian orbifold, the local fibrations may be chosen as restrictions of a single global Seifert fibration. A global orbit coordinate on the smooth manifold cover shows, in addition, that this fibration is the orbit map of a continuous torus action and becomes a product with $\mathbb{T}^{N-m}$ on finite covers of $X_i$ and $X$ of a fixed degree, as Peng, Wang and Wang proved for smooth torus bundles at the Betti number equality. When the base is a closed Riemannian manifold, the maps are principal torus bundles; this confirms a conjecture of Zamora and Zhu for possibly singular $\mathrm{RCD}$ total spaces. The new ingredients are a pointwise linearization of the collapsing action at regular orbits, an invariant harmonic transverse coordinate compatible with finite isotropy, and an exactly equivariant orbit coordinate built from an elementary rounding-and-doubling argument in the collapsing deck group.

papers.title: TwinCheck: Evidence-Grounded Negative-Twin Verification for Stateful Tool Agents
papers.abstract: A single locally plausible tool call can derail an otherwise successful agent trajectory. Suspicion alone does not justify intervention, because the replacement itself can introduce the very failure verification is meant to prevent. We introduce TwinCheck, an inference-time verification policy that considers replacement only when the trace satisfies an evidence condition tied to a local failure hypothesis. It constructs a trace-grounded counterfactual alternative, a negative twin, and replaces the actor's proposal only if the twin passes structural checks and the pairwise verifier prefers it in both candidate orders. For paired evaluation, exact replay holds the actor's parsed responses and actions fixed until the first accepted replacement, separating intervention effects from resampling. On 159 primary BFCL V4 multi-turn tasks, the complete policy raises GPT-5.6 Sol task success from 45.3% to 58.5%, a gain of 13.2 percentage points (95% task-bootstrap CI [8.2, 18.8]), with 21 rescues and no observed success-to-failure regressions. Across the completed primary set and a conditional extension, all 37 rescues follow the same inverse-action repair pattern. The verifier accepts every constructed candidate and adds no filtering on these trajectories. TwinCheck frames execution-boundary repair as a constrained comparison, making the proposed replacement itself the object of verification.

papers.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
papers.abstract: We study gradient descent with predetermined nonnegative stepsizes on smooth strongly convex functions. Let $p_{\mathrm{sil}}=\log_2(1+\sqrt2)$ and $κ$ be the condition number. We prove the iteration lower bound $Ω\left(κ^{\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{sil}}}-o(1)}\log\frac1δ\right)$ for both relative squared distance and relative function error, uniformly over $0<δ<1$ and sufficiently large $κ$. This matches the polynomial exponent of $κ$ for the Silver stepsize schedule established in [Altschuler and Parrilo, 2025].

papers.title: Efficient Cost-Aware LLM Evaluation via Bayesian Bandit Gittins Indices
papers.abstract: Exhaustively evaluating every candidate LLM configuration on every benchmark item to identify a high-performing one is costly. We formulate configuration selection as a cost-aware Bayesian bandit problem and propose GittinsEval, inspired by Bayesian-optimal Gittins-index policies for Markov chain selection. We augment this policy with a separate anytime recommendation rule over both fully and partially evaluated configurations, using an LCB-style score to account for posterior uncertainty. GittinsEval is computationally efficient, requiring only lightweight online updates after offline precomputation. Across tasks with varying numbers of candidates and examples, GittinsEval is consistently competitive, with particularly strong gains over the Bayesian optimization baselines on few-candidate large-example benchmarks and over cost-unaware frequentist baselines on large-candidate tasks. Crucially, GittinsEval often attains near-zero simple regret using only 1%-2% of the exhaustive-evaluation cost; it also offers a stopping rule that typically triggers at 1%-10% with an appropriate cost--quality tradeoff parameter.

papers.title: SAVOR: Score Once, Learn Deeper in On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own samples with token-level scores from a stronger teacher, and it effectively transfers reasoning ability to small language models. Each training step pays for student rollouts and teacher scoring, yet common OPD configurations make a single pass over the scored batch and then discard it. We observe that reusing the batch alone is not enough, because no single fixed teacher target suits every batch. In our runs, a fixed $α$ of 0.3 exceeds a KL envelope at every training step, while 0.2 leaves over a quarter of it unused. We propose SAVOR, which selects for each batch the strongest teacher target inside the KL envelope, freezes the scored batch, and reuses it for a fixed number of student updates without further teacher calls. On five math reasoning benchmarks with a 1.7B student and a 30B-A3B teacher, SAVOR raises macro accuracy over TOP-D from 15.41 to 17.78 with two passes and to 19.36 with three passes at about the same teacher budget. With three passes, SAVOR nearly matches the final accuracy of TOP-D after one third of training while using 67.2% fewer teacher-scored tokens. These results suggest budgeting reuse depth explicitly in OPD.

papers.title: Leveraging Industrial Foundation Models at the Edge of Particle Physics Detectors via Distillation Learning and Hardware Co-design
papers.abstract: Data acquisition (DAQ) systems at future particle physics experiments stand to benefit from the extremes of AI/ML development: large-scale foundation models can enhance the performance of feature extraction algorithms, and small-scale on-detector deployments can enable real-time intelligent data handling. This work provides the first tokenizer fine-tuning of an industrial foundation model for particle physics DAQ. Starting from the backbone of Google Research's TimesFM (Time Series Foundation Model), we address real-time regression tasks for drift chamber trackers and dual-readout calorimeters by jointly training the pretrained tokenizer and a newly initialized residual adapter, then fitting task-specific linear heads while keeping the transformer backbone frozen. Furthermore, the resulting TimesFM teachers can be distilled into students and co-designed with FPGA implementation to support real-time operation at future colliders. The distilled and compressed models achieve competitive performance, while distillation reduces reliance on labeled training data. Further, the pipeline of distillation and model compression from TimesFM is generic and can be easily adapted to a variety of 1D waveform tasks across domains.

papers.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem over quadratic fields
papers.abstract: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic fields $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2),\mathbb Q(\sqrt3),\mathbb Q(\sqrt6)$. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$ with $d\in\{2,3,6\}$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{24}\in K$.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of gas giants accreting via shocks: the role of molecular hydrogen dissociation
papers.abstract: Within the core-accretion framework, gas giants acquire the bulk of their mass through accretion shocks during runaway gas accretion. The shock thermodynamics---governed by radiative cooling efficiency, accretion history, and equation of state (EoS)---sets the post-shock entropy and initial thermal state, strongly influencing both observables and subsequent evolution. We construct a coupled evolutionary model predicting the initial thermodynamic states, intrinsic luminosities, and upper limits on the magnetic field strengths of gas giants across diverse accretion histories. We couple radiation hydrodynamics and $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociation to long-term interior evolution by training a fast physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate model on 1000 first-principles simulations resolving the shock physics. This surrogate model supplies post-shock outer boundary conditions for MESA to evolve the planetary envelope beyond runaway accretion. It yields higher post-shock temperatures than the canonical cold-start model, with the discrepancy widening with planetary mass, while the post-shock entropy jumps sharply when $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociates at $\sim 2000$ K. Gas giants evolved with these boundary conditions attain intrinsic luminosities 4--10 times higher than cold-start models. Under optimistic assumptions, the maximum magnetic field strength at $2\,\mathrm{R_J}$ reaches a few gauss for a $0.3\,\mathrm{M_J}$ planet, $\sim 100$ G for $1\,\mathrm{M_J}$, and $\sim 500$ G for $3\,\mathrm{M_J}$. Incorporating detailed radiation hydrodynamics and realistic thermodynamics into accretion shock models yields higher initial entropies, brighter intrinsic luminosities, and stronger magnetic fields, providing improved constraints on the masses and accretion rates of directly imaged exoplanets.

papers.title: SlotFill: Repairing Lossy SoC Communication Traces for Post-Silicon Validation
papers.abstract: Post-silicon validation relies on traces of messages exchanged by SoC components, but trace buffers and monitors drop messages, often leaving no mark of what was lost. We present SlotFill, which puts each deleted message back in the right gap, with the right type and order. SlotFill gives every gap between the remaining messages a fixed number of slots, and a Transformer-based model fills each slot with a message or leaves it empty when nothing was deleted there, so the input never reveals how much was lost. The model also uses monitor fields (timestamps, transaction IDs, addresses) from surviving messages. On whole-program gem5 traces of 4- and 8-core systems (2.07 billion messages), SlotFill restores up to 97% of deleted messages exactly at 15% loss and up to 87% at 50% loss, and 76-83% at 15% loss when timestamps are coarse.

papers.title: Evolutionary AI Control: Population-Level Safety Under Reproduction, Heredity, and Selection
papers.abstract: An AI agent can satisfy every individual safety check and still give rise to a population that violates a collective safety limit. This risk arises in open multi-agent systems, where agents copy themselves, modify their successors, and change system membership during a run. Selection then shifts the population toward traits outside the developers' optimization targets. We prove conditions under which safety guarantees persist through reproduction, inheritance, and selection, and we characterize how they fail. Four counterexamples illustrate these failures. Unauthorized copies, which violate a specified reproductive restriction, can each leave fewer than one successor on average while their expected number grows without bound under continued production from an expanding authorized population. Two lineages can each decline in isolation yet grow exponentially when they interact. Alternating between reproductive rules can drive growth even when each rule, applied alone, suppresses it. Selection can raise the population's average rate of unauthorized reproduction above a certified limit even though every agent's rate remains fixed. Whereas existing verification methods assume fixed or registered membership, we prove safety certificates, under stated assumptions, for populations whose agents create successors during a run. The main result bounds the expected cumulative harm over a run, including when a scheduler adapts the reproductive rules to the observed history. Further conditions cover every population state reachable through evolution and preserve reproductive restrictions as descendants inherit modifications. Drawing on the mechanisms by which multicellular organisms control cell reproduction, the framework enables developers to specify and verify these controls before deployment.

papers.title: Machine learning for trigger, reconstruction and generation
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly embedded in every stage of the LHC data-processing chain, from event generation to final reconstruction. This contribution reviews the latest ML developments from the ALICE, ATLAS, CMS and LHCb collaborations that were made public in the year preceding LHCP2026, following the workflow of the experiments: event generation and detector simulation, real-time trigger selection, and online/offline reconstruction. Highlights include generative models that accelerate the simulation of specific ALICE detector components by up to six orders of magnitude, the CMS AXOL1TL and ATLAS GELATO unsupervised anomaly- detection triggers now operating in Run 3, a quantised Deep Sets jet tagger for the CMS Phase-2 Level-1 trigger, ML-based jet energy correction and flavour tagging at LHCb, the first empirical scaling laws for transformer-based flavour taggers in ATLAS, and several transformer and graph- based reconstruction algorithms (ATLAS GN3 flavour tagging and MaskFormer tracking, LHCb GarNet, CMS MLPF) developed for HL-LHC operation.

papers.title: Concave Run Budgets and Restart Width
papers.abstract: A source-to-target path in an edge-labelled DAG uses each label in some number of maximal runs, with a label used in \(r\) runs charged according to a nondecreasing concave rational tariff \(f(r)\). We seek a path of total charge at most \(B\), or a shortest such path. We parameterize by restart width \(\wr\), the maximum number of labels that have already appeared and can still begin a new run at some vertex. It is at most live width but can be arbitrarily smaller. Let \(J_f(T)\) denote the number of distinct marginal rates of \(f\) up to horizon \(T\). A lazy-commitment dynamic program solves minimum charge and feasibility in \(J_f(T)^{\wr}\poly(N)\) time, allowing arbitrary per-label tariffs and unbounded charge magnitudes. Thus the problem is FPT whenever \(J_f\) is effectively subpolynomial. Conversely, for every fixed tariff with \(J_f(T)\ge T^δ\) eventually, feasibility is NP-complete and W[1]-hard in \(\wr\), even on planar bipartite DAGs of maximum degree three and treewidth two whose paths have equal length, and admits no \(g(\wr)N^{o(\wr)}\) algorithm under ETH. The reduction uses positive pairwise Jensen-gap charges, requires no denominator assumption, and covers harmonic, geometric, and power-law tariffs. A \(k\)-colour clique instance has width at most \(2k+1\), improved to \(k+1\) for polynomially bounded denominators. We further exhibit arbitrarily close tariffs with opposite parameterized complexity, give an FPT budget-relaxing scheme and accuracy obstruction, establish few-label hardness and W[P]-membership, and identify separate hardness from binary-encoded lengths. Oscillating plan growth and non-effective subpolynomial bounds remain open.

papers.title: Curvature-Orbit Quantization of Gauge-Related Connections and a Radon--Nikodym Route to Lattice Yang--Mills Theory
papers.abstract: We study a four-dimensional gauge construction in which two gauge-related non-abelian connections, $A=B^g$, interact only through the squared difference of their curvatures. Independent kinetic term is absent. The action is an ultralocal functional on a curvature orbit. Its Hessian is a pointwise positive-semidefinite operator whose kernel is the common stabilizer algebra of the curvature components, and its spectrum is given for every compact simple Lie group. At a finite regulator the model is an exact compact-group integral. Integrating out the orbit variable yields a positive, bounded Radon--Nikodym cocycle that relates the induced link measure to a lattice Yang--Mills measure, recasting the existence and mass-gap question as a uniform estimate on this cocycle.

papers.title: A counterexample to the Ho-Hsieh VQCS saturation conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that there exists a 4-qubit state that can be prepared by a variational quantum-classical simulation (VQCS) circuit ansatz containing 3 layers, but not with 2 layers. This disproves the strong form of a conjecture presented by Ho and Hsieh stating that the expressivity of VQCS on $L$ qubits saturates at $L/2$ layers. The weak form of the conjecture concerning the preparation of the ground state remains open.

papers.title: When Successful Collaboration Becomes an Attack Surface: Insider Memory Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Recent Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) increasingly use shared memory to store and reuse successful collaboration records, enabling teams to improve across tasks. However, this memory introduces a new attack surface for malicious insiders. Unlike existing insider attacks that inject misleading information directly into the current collaboration, misinformation stored in shared memory can later appear as successful team experience and gain greater credibility and influence. We propose MIMPA (Multi-Agent Insider Memory Poisoning Attack), which exploits this vulnerability using only normal participation privileges, without direct memory access. During an earlier task, the malicious agent embeds a target-specific payload while helping the team answer correctly, allowing the payload to be retained in a successful collaboration record. When retrieved for a later target task, this poisoned record can steer benign agents toward a designated wrong answer, further amplified by malicious triggering. Across three benchmarks and two LLM backbones, MIMPA substantially outperforms existing insider attacks and remains effective under hierarchical memory management, while auditing only partially mitigates it. These results reveal that shared memory intended to accumulate team experience can become a persistent channel for insider attacks. Our code is available at https://github.com/ahnji0520/MIMPA-code.

papers.title: Set-based comprehensive learning and particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problem
papers.abstract: This paper describes a novel algorithm of set-based comprehensive learning and particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problem. Our algorithm is an approach of searching for the best position in a set by referring to the current position when updating the solution. In order to show the validity of our algorithm, we examine numerical experiments compared to existing algorithms.

papers.title: Differential evolution with perturbation for continuous function optimization
papers.abstract: This paper presents differential evolution with perturbation (DEP) for continuous function optimization. Differential evolution is a simple and efficient algorithm. Perturbation is the phenomenon that the motion by the contribution of the main force is disturbed by the influence subsidiary power. In order to show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, we compare it to existing algorithms by CEC2017 datasets.

papers.title: Beyond Quantum Mechanics: From Nonlinear to Emergent and Solitonic Approaches
papers.abstract: This thesis investigates the role of nonlinearity in approaches beyond standard quantum mechanics, following a path from modifications of quantum dynamics to the possibility of an emergent statistical description. We first examine Weinberg's nonlinear formulation and its implications for the statistical interpretation of quantum states. We then discuss de Broglie-Bohm theory and the Madelung formulation, which provide a framework for comparing guided trajectories with ensemble descriptions involving momentum fluctuations. The Hall-Reginatto exact uncertainty approach identifies the fluctuation energy associated with the quantum potential. We then investigate whether quantum dynamics can emerge from the collective statistics of solitons in a fluctuating background, using a Galilean formulation of the complex sine-Gordon model. Within a weak-noise approximation, we identify a regime in which the statistics of the soliton centres reproduce the Schr{ö}dinger equation, with an effective action scale determined by the background fluctuations. This correspondence is established for Gaussian ensembles and potentials at most quadratic. These results provide a concrete setting for exploring how quantum dynamics can emerge as a statistical description of underlying nonlinear field dynamics.

papers.title: Exact nonstationary heat-excess statistics in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model
papers.abstract: Exact nonstationary large-deviation statistics remain scarce for interacting many-body systems. Here we employ the macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to determine the complete long-time statistics of heat excess produced by an initially localized heat pulse in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model. We find a remarkable nonlocal canonical transformation which maps the weakly asymmetric MFT problem, including its initial and terminal conditions, onto the symmetric problem, previously solved exactly. The resulting rate function is an explicit nonlinear deformation of its symmetric counterpart. We also extend the solution to heat measured beyond an arbitrary observation point.

papers.title: Validating Concurrent Correctness Witnesses with Ghosts by Thread-Modular Abstract Interpretation (Extended Version)
papers.abstract: Concurrent programs are notoriously difficult to write and to reason about, and even tools based on sound theoretical foundations can produce incorrect results due to implementation bugs. Correctness witnesses have been proposed as a way to increase the confidence in the verdicts of software verifiers by enabling independent validation. Recently, correctness witnesses have been extended to the concurrent setting, by introducing ghost variables to allow encoding more expressive invariants. While different approaches to producing witnesses with ghosts exist, validation techniques are still lacking; instead of leveraging the information encoded in the ghosts to guide the validation process, validators merely treat ghost instrumentation and invariants over ghost variables as additional proof obligations. We propose a novel framework for the validation of concurrent correctness witnesses that exploits the semantic information encoded in ghost variables. It combines a checking phase, which establishes the semantic content of the ghost instrumentation, with an exploitation phase making use of this information. Both phases are formulated as thread-modular abstract interpretation. In particular, we consider two different classes of ghost variables and techniques for exploiting them, one based on resource invariants and one based on phases. Phase ghosts guide the degree to which the abstract interpretation considers interleavings instead of always abstracting them coarsely. In this way, the abstract interpreter can validate witnesses containing invariants beyond the reach of unguided thread-modular analysis, while still retaining its scalability benefits. We have implemented our framework in a static analyzer and evaluate it on witnesses encoding resource invariants obtained from a state-of-the-art software verifier, as well as on hand-crafted witnesses encoding phase information.

papers.title: Resilient Federated LQR over Noisy and Lossy Uplinks via Scalar Communication
papers.abstract: This paper studies model-free federated learning of a common LQR controller for a fleet of similar systems that communicate with a server over an uplink subject to limited bandwidth, packet dropout, and additive noise. We propose \textsc{ResiFedLQR}, a scalar communication scheme in which each agent sends one real number per packet, with redundancy, instead of full gradient estimates. The scalars can be gradient coordinates, projections of the gradient onto random directions reproduced at the server from a shared seed, or the rollout costs themselves. For the projection encoding, we prove that, with high probability, every iterate stabilizes all agents and the fleet-average cost converges linearly to a neighborhood of the optimum whose radius separates heterogeneity, sampling, and communication effects, and we derive a rule for choosing the number of transmissions from the channel parameters and the fleet size. We then compare the encodings with full-gradient transmission under the same uplink budget and identify the signal-to-noise regime and power constraint under which each is preferable. Numerical experiments on a heterogeneous fleet \reza{of BlueROV2 underwater vehicles} evaluate stability and convergence under varying noise levels and dropout probabilities.

papers.title: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
papers.abstract: For every \(1<p\le2\), we prove that the optimal universal factor relating the Enflo type \(p\) constant to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant is \(p\), already among finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. Ivanisvili, van Handel, and Volberg [Ann.\ of Math.\ (2) \textbf{192} (2020), 665--678] proved the equivalence with factor \(π/\sqrt{2}\). Areshidze [arXiv:2609.32666v1 (2026)] improved the upper bound to \(p\). Our matching lower bound settles the optimality question posed in that preprint. We also study orthogonal families in a real Banach space \(X\). \begin{list}{}{\setlength{\leftmargin}{\dimexpr24pt+1.8em\relax}\setlength{\rightmargin}{24pt}\setlength{\labelwidth}{1.4em}\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}\setlength{\topsep}{2pt}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}} \item[(a)] For \(1<p<2\), \(X\) has Enflo type \(p\) if and only if the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality holds uniformly over ordered families \((v_i)\) satisfying \[ v_i\perp_B v_j \qquad \text{for all } i<j, \] where \(\perp_B\) denotes Birkhoff--James orthogonality (that is, \(\|v_i+t v_j\|\ge\|v_i\|\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\)). \item[(b)] For \(1<p\le2\), uniform validity of the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality on pairwise isosceles orthogonal families implies that \(X\) has Enflo type \(s\) for every \(1\le s<p\), with a quadratic bound in the restricted type constant at \(s=2p/(p+1)\). \end{list} We also record the subcritical type implication for Pythagorean orthogonality and the sharp factor \(p\) for Roberts orthogonality. {For each \(1<p<2\), as the modulus of roundness \(ν_X(p)\) approaches \(2\), the ratio of the Enflo to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant tends uniformly to \(1\) over real Banach spaces of Rademacher type \(p\). The same limit holds for the ratio of the two constants restricted by mutual Birkhoff--James orthogonality.}

papers.title: RSIBench-Infra: Can Agents Optimize Training and Inference Infrastructure at Production Scale?
papers.abstract: Improving the efficiency of training and inference infrastructure is a practical component of recursive self-improvement. Existing benchmarks for agent-driven optimization largely focus on individual software layers such as kernel, leaving unclear whether agents can deliver end-to-end performance gains under production workloads. We introduce RSIBench-Infra, a benchmark of 20 training and inference tasks spanning diverse model families and modalities, with deployments of up to 32 accelerators on NVIDIA GPUs and Ascend NPUs. Agents start from runnable baselines derived from official recipes and can modify the software stack across engine, kernel, and instruction levels. An OCI image-layer submission protocol captures these changes for reproducible deployment, while independent evaluation measures end-to-end performance under task-specific quality constraints. Across all task results, 66.2% exceed $1.10\times$ validated speedup. These results demonstrate that current agents can improve production-scale training and inference performance, but identifying effective optimization strategies and consistently translating local improvements into end-to-end gains remain challenging.

papers.title: Gravitational Illumination Bodies
papers.abstract: For a given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R ^n$ and $δ>0$, we introduce a new class of bodies, the {\em gravitational illumination bodies} $I^δ(K)$. We show some of their properties and explore their relation to floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. Unexpected phenomena happen and the gravitational illumination bodies exhibit very different behavior than the floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. While the classical bodies are all convex and either contained in $K$ or containing $K$, this is no longer the case for the new bodies. They need not be convex, but they are star shaped and it may happen that $I^δ(K)$ has non-empty intersection with both, $K$ and its complement. Moreover, the containment behavior may change with the dimension. Most surprising is the behavior of a volume derivative, $$ \lim_{δ\to 0} \frac{ |\vol_n(K)-\vol_n(I^δ(K)) |}{δ^\frac{2}{n+1}}. $$ In all dimensions the corresponding volume derivative for the classical bodies results in the equi-affine invariant affine surface area of the body $K$. In the case of the gravitational illumination body, this is also the case in all dimensions, except in dimension $3$. In dimension $3$ the limit is equal to $0$ for all convex bodies. A non-zero derivative is obtained in dimension $3$ if one normalizes by $δ$ instead of $δ^\frac{1}{2}$. The non-zero limit is a new affine invariant involving the {\em affine mean curvature } and the {\em Pick invariant} of the convex body.

papers.title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations
papers.abstract: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Do these differences merely reflect alternative solutions, or do they preserve information about individual learning histories? We tested whether final weights reveal initialization, task order, and earlier trajectory states. Training reorganized the ensemble: initial pairwise distances did not consistently predict final distances. Nevertheless, all 30 trained networks were correctly matched to their initial weights among ten candidates per dataset. Networks sharing an initialization also developed recognizable final hidden representations across different batch schedules, although direct comparisons with initial activity did not recover identity. Learning order remained readable as well. A linear probe decoded the order of two earlier tasks with 100% accuracy on 80 held-out networks after ten epochs of a common final task. Earlier intermediate weight states were partly predictable, but individual initial weights could not be reliably reconstructed. Final weights thus retain selective historical information rather than a complete trajectory record. Perturbed networks recovered classification performance without returning to their unperturbed training paths. This separation persisted across datasets, intervention times, and network layers. Moreover, 2,157 of 2,160 aligned endpoint pairs showed no positive loss barrier at sampled interpolation points, indicating low-loss connections between distinct solutions rather than convergence to one weight vector. Together, these findings show that a shared task constrains networks to related successful solutions without erasing their individual histories. Final weights reflect not only what a network has learned, but also where learning began and how it unfolded.

papers.title: Self-supervised behavior encoders rarely beat a training-free baseline
papers.abstract: Self-supervised encoders of animal and human pose are compared with one another, and rarely with simple summaries of the poses they encode. We propose such a summary that needs no training and no knowledge of the species: each body's keypoints and velocities in its own frame, a small block on the nearest other animals, and the mean, spread and histogram of every number over windows from half a second to the whole clip, reduced by PCA. We compare it with seven encoders on five benchmarks under the standard protocol: frozen representations of equal size, read by a linear classifier. It matches or beats hBehaveMAE and BAMS, the encoders pretrained on each benchmark, on all five: behaviors of mouse pairs and of human motion capture, the movements of a simulated basketball player, the strain and lighting of mouse triplets and group-level traits of flies. It leads hBehaveMAE from about a tenth of the labels. A few dozen plain kinematic measurements in place of the keypoints widen the lead over hBehaveMAE to 3.4 to 5.6 points. With all labels only HiDRA, a forecaster built for pairs of mice, beats the baseline, on mouse pairs; it trails on mouse triplets and cannot run on flies or humans. Two choices carry the baseline, the body's own frame and windows of seconds, and readouts of the frozen embeddings show what the encoders miss: they keep where body parts are, but little of how they move over seconds.

papers.title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields
papers.abstract: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra.

papers.title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square torus
papers.abstract: For each finite $s>1$ we construct a solution of the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square two-torus with initial data in $H^s$ whose $H^s$ norm tends to infinity as $t\to+\infty$. The growth can be arbitrarily slow. More precisely, the squared norm agrees, up to a bounded error at all positive times, with the number of selected axial frequencies $K_j$ for which $K_j^s\le t$. The central construction couples a finite tree of orthogonal frequency pairs to a finite-dimensional family of one-dimensional solutions of the same equation. Each transfer leaves a nonvanishing Fourier coefficient on the horizontal axis. Control on an entire half-line allows successive transfers to retain the coefficients produced earlier. At and above the index two, we match the second-order normal frequency shift separately on each triangle using harmonics of the axial solution. For every fixed $2<s<\infty$ we also obtain a solution for which $\log\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\asymp\sqrt{\log t/\log\log t}$ at every sufficiently large time.

papers.title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen increasing temperature or pressure may either occur gradually or abruptly, via a phase transition. Despite considerable experimental and theoretical efforts, the phase diagram of dense hydrogen at temperatures above solid melting is not precisely known. Here, we perform classical and quantum Path Integral molecular dynamics simulations of dense hydrogen using two machine-learned interatomic potentials both trained on quantum Monte Carlo energies and forces. The resulting phase diagram is constructed using state-of-the-art techniques. Both models show a first-order phase transition from the molecular to the atomic liquid terminating in critical points whose locations were determined using finite-size scaling techniques. Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with the melting curve and should lead to clear signatures in ramp compression experiments.

papers.title: Steering Automated Scientific Discovery via Audited Epistemic Exploration
papers.abstract: Scientific discovery requires revisiting the hypotheses in light of new evidence and identifying promising directions beyond those already explored. However, research agents often make claims that are not supported by their observations, explore a narrow hypothesis space, and retain beliefs despite recognizing conflicting evidence. These failures motivate the search for an explicit epistemic state that captures both beliefs about existing hypotheses and directions for further exploration. To this end, we propose Epistemic Compass (EpiCompass), a plug-and-play scaffold that maintains this state through an epistemic tree linking hypotheses, evidence, beliefs, and revisions. As an investigation progresses, EpiCompass reassesses the hypotheses explored against accumulated evidence and uses unresolved conflicts and unexplored directions to guide hypothesis generation. It selects candidates by anticipated epistemic gain, accounting for both refinement of existing hypotheses and expansion of the hypothesis space, and verifies the final conclusion against the accumulated evidence. Experimental results across three scientific discovery benchmarks and three LLM backbones demonstrate that EpiCompass consistently outperforms baselines, with further analyses showing reductions in errors of unsupported claims and failures to revise beliefs. Our code is available at https://github.com/tianyi-lab/EpiCompass.

papers.title: Embeddable matrix-algebra bundles
papers.abstract: A unital embedding of a bundle of complex matrix algebras in a trivial matrix algebra bundle of coprime multiplicity determines two complementary factors. We recover from them an integral virtual special-unitary bundle of rank one. This gives a proof of the stable classification by $B{\rm SU}_{\otimes}$ that allows torsion in the cohomology of the base. At fixed core rank $k$, the telescope of matrix Grassmannians with complementary ranks $l^N$ is the homotopy fibre of $B{\rm PU}(k)\to B{\rm Aut}(M_k\otimes M_{l^\infty})$. Thus unital UHF triviality detects exactly which cores admit coprime finite-dimensional embeddings. We determine the least stage on even spheres and on four-dimensional Moore spaces. A rank-three example over $S^6$ first embeds in $M_{12}$ and represents a unit whose clutching gives a higher twist over $S^7$.

papers.title: Is Classical Error Control Ready for IMT-2030? Information-Loss Interfaces in Channel Estimation, FEC, CRC, and ARQ for Machine-Type Services
papers.abstract: Fault tolerance and structured error control in mobile communication networks--historically implemented as a modular cascade of pilot-aided channel estimation (CE), forward error correction (FEC), cyclic redundancy check (CRC), and hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ)--remain foundational to 5G New Radio (NR). Although finite-blocklength coding, joint estimation-decoding, and grant-free access have been active academic topics for over a decade, commercial 3GPP specifications up to Release 18 still enforce rigid cross-layer boundaries between these blocks. In short-packet machine-type communications (MTC) for IMT-2030 (6G), inserting separate redundancy for channel training, error correction, and error detection shrinks the net payload entropy resolved per channel slot, while standardized UE processing timelines and HARQ round-trip delays collide with sub-millisecond reliability targets. Combining a multi-user MIMO short-packet simulation with real 3GPP TS 38.214 numerology latency budgets, this article diagnoses the structural bottlenecks of the legacy reliability pipeline and outlines an interoperable roadmap for 3GPP Release 20+--spanning soft-output universal decoding, sensing-assisted priors, grant-free joint detection, and task-oriented error control.

papers.title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with a Matern Kernel
papers.abstract: Gaussian processes (GPs) provide a flexible framework for modeling complex dependence structures through a covariance function, or kernel, whose parameters determine the variability, correlation, and smoothness of the underlying process. The Matérn kernel is among the most popular choices due to its flexibility in modeling different degrees of smoothness. Although the identifiability of Matérn kernel parameters under fixed-domain asymptotics is completely understood, identifiability alone does not establish the consistency or asymptotic behavior of the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs) routinely used in practice. In this paper, we address this gap by developing a sharp asymptotic theory for the joint MLE of Matérn kernel parameters. Since parameter identifiability depends critically on the dimension of the observation domain, we characterize the estimable parameters and establish their convergence rates across different dimensions. We establish joint asymptotic normality and minimax optimality of the convergence rates. In addition, we establish asymptotically valid confidence regions for the estimable parameters. Our results accommodate irregular sampling designs and extend to sub-Gaussian measurement errors. Extensive simulation studies illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: The Coupled Scaled Dirichlet Distribution
papers.abstract: We introduce a coupled scaled Dirichlet distribution for paired compositions that may have different dimensions. Building on the matched Gamma-sharing construction of Trick, Rothkopf, and Jäkel (2023) for ordinary Dirichlet vectors, we allow scaled Dirichlet margins and extend the construction to include crossed sharing between non-corresponding latent components. We propose a signed coupling parameter whose sign selects matched or crossed sharing and whose magnitude controls the strength of sharing. We then develop a time-varying extension in which observed covariates determine this parameter. The model can therefore switch between matched and crossed sharing over time while preserving both scaled Dirichlet margins. We derive the joint mixed moments and use them to estimate dependence after fitting the margins separately. The moments can be evaluated by Monte Carlo simulation or by two-dimensional numerical quadrature, regardless of the dimensions of the compositions. Simulations show that the estimator generally recovers the sharing pattern, although weak crossed sharing is harder to detect.
